title: 黑神駒
author: Anna Sewell 安娜·休厄爾
description: 《Black Beauty》(1877):以一匹馬的第一人稱講述一生遭遇,語言平實、情感動人,是最適合英語初學者的經典小說之一。

chapters.title: Part I · 01 My Early Home 第一部·01 我的早年之家

passages.original: CH The first place that I can well remember was a large pleasant meadow with a pond of clear water in it.
passages.vernacular: 我能清楚記得嘅第一個地方,係一片寬敞宜人嘅草地,裡面有一個清澈嘅池塘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能清楚記得的第一個地方,是一片寬敞宜人的草地,裡面有一個清澈的池塘。

passages.original: Some shady trees leaned over it, and rushes and water-lilies grew at the deep end.
passages.vernacular: 幾棵樹蔭濃密嘅樹斜斜地覆喺上面,池塘深嘅嗰一頭長住蘆葦同瞓蓮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾棵樹蔭濃密的樹斜斜地覆在上面,池塘深的那一頭長著蘆葦和睡蓮。

passages.original: Over the hedge on one side we looked into a plowed field, and on the other we looked over a gate at our master's house, which stood by the roadside; at the top of the meadow was a grove of fir trees, and at the bottom a running brook overhung by a steep bank.
passages.vernacular: 隔住一邊嘅樹籬,我哋可以望見一塊犁過嘅田;另一邊隔住一道柵門,我哋可以望見主人嘅房子,佢就立喺路邊;草地嘅頂端係一片冷杉樹林,底部係一條潺潺嘅小溪,被一道陡坡嘅堤岸遮蔽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隔著一邊的樹籬,我們可以望見一塊犁過的田;另一邊隔著一道柵門,我們可以望見主人的房子,它就立在路邊;草地的頂端是一片冷杉樹林,底部是一條潺潺的小溪,被一道陡坡的堤岸遮蔽著。

passages.original: While I was young I lived upon my mother's milk, as I could not eat grass.
passages.vernacular: 我年紀小嘅時候靠母親嘅奶水生活,因為我仲唔會食草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我年紀小的時候靠母親的奶水生活,因為我還不會吃草。

passages.original: In the daytime I ran by her side, and at night I lay down close by her.
passages.vernacular: 白天我跑喺佢身邊,夜裡我緊挨住佢躺下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白天我跑在她身邊,夜裡我緊挨著她躺下。

passages.original: When it was hot we used to stand by the pond in the shade of the trees, and when it was cold we had a nice warm shed near the grove.
passages.vernacular: 天熱嘅時候,我哋常常站喺池塘邊樹蔭下,天冷嘅時候,我哋喺樹林附近有一間溫暖嘅好棚子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天熱的時候,我們常常站在池塘邊樹蔭下,天冷的時候,我們在樹林附近有一間溫暖的好棚子。

passages.original: As soon as I was old enough to eat grass my mother used to go out to work in the daytime, and come back in the evening.
passages.vernacular: 我一到能食草嘅年紀,母親白天就出去幹活,傍晚才回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一到能吃草的年紀,母親白天就出去幹活,傍晚才回來。

passages.original: There were six young colts in the meadow besides me; they were older than I was; some were nearly as large as grown-up horses.
passages.vernacular: 草地上除咗我仲有六匹小馬駒;佢哋比我大;有嘅幾乎同成年嘅馬一樣大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草地上除了我還有六匹小馬駒;它們比我大;有的幾乎和成年的馬一樣大。

passages.original: I used to run with them, and had great fun; we used to gallop all together round and round the field as hard as we could go.
passages.vernacular: 我常常同佢哋一起跑,玩得好開心;我哋常常一起繞住草地一圈又一圈地拚命奔跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常常和它們一起跑,玩得很開心;我們常常一起繞著草地一圈又一圈地拚命奔跑。

passages.original: Sometimes we had rather rough play, for they would frequently bite and kick as well as gallop.
passages.vernacular: 有時我哋玩得相當粗野,因為佢哋常常又咬又踢,仲要奔跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我們玩得相當粗野,因為它們常常又咬又踢,還要奔跑。

passages.original: One day, when there was a good deal of kicking, my mother whinnied to me to come to her, and then she said:
passages.vernacular: 有一天,踢得特別厲害時,我母親嘶鳴住叫我到佢身邊嚟,然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,踢得特別厲害時,我母親嘶鳴著叫我到她身邊來,然後她說:

passages.original: “I wish you to pay attention to what I am going to say to you.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望你注意聽我要對你講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望你注意聽我要對你說的話。

passages.original: The colts who live here are very good colts, but they are cart-horse colts, and of course they have not learned manners.
passages.vernacular: 住喺呢度嘅小馬駒都係好好嘅小馬駒,不過佢哋係拉車馬嘅小馬駒,當然佢哋冇學過規矩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住在這裡的小馬駒都是很好的小馬駒,可是它們是拉車馬的小馬駒,當然它們沒有學過規矩。

passages.original: You have been well-bred and well-born; your father has a great name in these parts, and your grandfather won the cup two years at the Newmarket races; your grandmother had the sweetest temper of any horse I ever knew, and I think you have never seen me kick or bite.
passages.vernacular: 你出身良好,血統高貴;你父親喺呢一帶名氣好大,你祖父喺紐馬基特賽馬會上連續兩年贏得獎盃;你祖母係我所知道嘅所有馬裡脾氣最溫順嘅,我想你從冇見過我踢人或咬人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你出身良好,血統高貴;你父親在這一帶名氣很大,你祖父在紐馬基特賽馬會上連續兩年贏得獎盃;你祖母是我所知道的所有馬裡脾氣最溫順的,我想你從沒見過我踢人或咬人。

passages.original: I hope you will grow up gentle and good, and never learn bad ways; do your work with a good will, lift your feet up well when you trot, and never bite or kick even in play.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你長大成為溫順善良嘅馬,永遠唔好學壞習慣;幹活要心甘情願,小跑時要把蹄子抬高,即使係玩耍都永遠唔好咬人或踢人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你長大成為溫順善良的馬,永遠不要學壞習慣;幹活要心甘情願,小跑時要把蹄子抬高,即使是玩耍也永遠不要咬人或踢人。」

passages.original: I have never forgotten my mother's advice; I knew she was a wise old horse, and our master thought a great deal of her.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇忘記母親嘅忠告;我知道佢係匹聰明嘅老馬,我哋嘅主人都好睇重佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒忘記母親的忠告;我知道她是匹聰明的老馬,我們的主人也非常看重她。

passages.original: Her name was Duchess, but he often called her Pet.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字叫公爵夫人,但主人常叫佢寶貝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的名字叫公爵夫人,但主人常叫她寶貝。

passages.original: Our master was a good, kind man.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅主人係個善良、和藹嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的主人是個善良、和藹的人。

passages.original: He gave us good food, good lodging, and kind words; he spoke as kindly to us as he did to his little children.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀我哋好嘅食物、好嘅住處同親切嘅話語;佢對我哋講話,同佢對佢嘅小細路哋講話一樣和氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給我們好的食物、好的住處和親切的話語;他對我們說話,和他對他的小孩子們說話一樣和氣。

passages.original: We were all fond of him, and my mother loved him very much.
passages.vernacular: 我哋都鍾意佢,我母親好愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們都喜歡他,我母親非常愛他。

passages.original: When she saw him at the gate she would neigh with joy, and trot up to him.
passages.vernacular: 佢一睇見佢喺門口,就會高興地嘶鳴,小跑到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一看見他在門口,就會高興地嘶鳴,小跑到他身邊。

passages.original: He would pat and stroke her and say, “Well, old Pet, and how is your little Darkie?”
passages.vernacular: 佢會拍拍、撫摸佢,講:「點樣,老寶貝,你嘅小黑黑好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會拍拍、撫摸她,說:「怎麼樣,老寶貝,你的小黑黑好嗎?」

passages.original: I was a dull black, so he called me Darkie; then he would give me a piece of bread, which was very good, and sometimes he brought a carrot for my mother.
passages.vernacular: 我係暗黑色嘅,所以佢叫我黑黑;然後佢會畀我一塊麵包,好好食,有時佢還畀我母親帶一根胡蘿蔔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是暗黑色的,所以他叫我黑黑;然後他會給我一塊麵包,很好吃,有時他還給我母親帶一根胡蘿蔔。

passages.original: All the horses would come to him, but I think we were his favorites.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅馬都會嚟到佢身邊,但我想我哋係佢嘅最愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的馬都會來到他身邊,但我想我們是他的最愛。

passages.original: My mother always took him to the town on a market day in a light gig.
passages.vernacular: 趕集嘅日子,我母親總是用一輛輕便嘅雙輪馬車載佢到城裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 趕集的日子,我母親總是用一輛輕便的雙輪馬車載他到城裡。

passages.original: There was a plowboy, Dick, who sometimes came into our field to pluck blackberries from the hedge.
passages.vernacular: 有個耕地嘅男孩叫迪克,有時佢會到我哋嘅田裡,從樹籬上摘黑莓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個耕地的男孩叫迪克,有時他會到我們的田裡,從樹籬上摘黑莓。

passages.original: When he had eaten all he wanted he would have what he called fun with the colts, throwing stones and sticks at them to make them gallop.
passages.vernacular: 等佢食夠咗佢想食嘅,佢就要同小馬駒哋玩佢所謂嘅樂子,朝佢哋扔石頭同棍子,讓佢哋奔跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他吃夠了他想吃的,他就要和小馬駒們玩他所謂的樂子,朝它們扔石頭和棍子,讓它們奔跑。

passages.original: We did not much mind him, for we could gallop off; but sometimes a stone would hit and hurt us.
passages.vernacular: 我哋不太在意佢,因為我哋可以跑開;不過有時石頭會打中並傷到我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不太在意他,因為我們可以跑開;可是有時石頭會打中並傷到我們。

passages.original: One day he was at this game, and did not know that the master was in the next field; but he was there, watching what was going on; over the hedge he jumped in a snap, and catching Dick by the arm, he gave him such a box on the ear as made him roar with the pain and surprise.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢正玩呢個把戲,唔知道主人就喺隔壁嘅田裡;可佢喺嗰度,睇住發生嘅一切;佢一下子跳過樹籬,一把抓住迪克嘅胳膊,畀咗佢一記耳光,打得佢又疼又驚地大叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天他正玩這個把戲,不知道主人就在隔壁的田裡;可他在那裡,看著發生的一切;他一下子跳過樹籬,一把抓住迪克的胳膊,給了他一記耳光,打得他又疼又驚地大叫。

passages.original: As soon as we saw the master we trotted up nearer to see what went on.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一睇見主人,就小跑住走近啲,睇發生咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一看見主人,就小跑著走近一些,看發生了什麼。

passages.original: “Bad boy!” he said, “bad boy! to chase the colts.
passages.vernacular: 「壞細路!」佢講,「壞細路!竟敢追趕小馬駒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「壞孩子!」他說,「壞孩子!竟敢追趕小馬駒。

passages.original: This is not the first time, nor the second, but it shall be the last.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係第一次,都唔係第二次,但呢個係最後一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是第一次,也不是第二次,但這是最後一次。

passages.original: There--take your money and go home; I shall not want you on my farm again.”
passages.vernacular: 攞住——攞你嘅工錢回家去;我農場裡唔再需要你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿著——拿你的工錢回家去;我農場裡不再需要你。」

passages.original: So we never saw Dick any more.
passages.vernacular: 於是我哋再都冇見過迪克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我們再也沒見過迪克。

passages.original: Old Daniel, the man who looked after the horses, was just as gentle as our master, so we were well off.
passages.vernacular: 照睇馬嘅老丹尼爾,同我哋嘅主人一樣溫和,所以我哋過得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照看馬的老丹尼爾,和我們的主人一樣溫和,所以我們過得很好。

chapters.title: Part I · 02 The Hunt 第一部·02 狩獵

passages.original: CH Before I was two years old a circumstance happened which I have never forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 我兩歲唔到嘅時候,發生咗一件我從未忘記嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我兩歲不到的時候,發生了一件我從未忘記的事。

passages.original: It was early in the spring; there had been a little frost in the night, and a light mist still hung over the woods and meadows.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係早春,夜裡下咗啲霜,一層薄霧仍然籠罩住樹林同草地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是早春,夜裡下了一點霜,一層薄霧仍然籠罩著樹林和草地。

passages.original: I and the other colts were feeding at the lower part of the field when we heard, quite in the distance, what sounded like the cry of dogs.
passages.vernacular: 我同其他小馬駒正在田野嘅下半部食草,忽然聽見遠處傳嚟像係狗叫嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和其他小馬駒正在田野的下半部吃草,忽然聽見遠處傳來像是狗叫的聲音。

passages.original: The oldest of the colts raised his head, pricked his ears, and said, “There are the hounds!” and immediately cantered off, followed by the rest of us to the upper part of the field, where we could look over the hedge and see several fields beyond.
passages.vernacular: 最大嘅嗰匹小馬駒抬起頭,豎起耳朵,講:「獵犬嚟喇!」即刻小跑起嚟,我哋其餘嘅都跟住跑到田野嘅上半部,喺嗰度我哋可以隔住樹籬睇見更遠嘅幾塊田。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最大的那匹小馬駒抬起頭,豎起耳朵,說:「獵犬來了!」立刻小跑起來,我們其餘的都跟著跑到田野的上半部,在那裡我們可以隔著樹籬看見更遠的幾塊田。

passages.original: My mother and an old riding horse of our master's were also standing near, and seemed to know all about it.
passages.vernacular: 我母親同主人嘅一匹老騎馬都站喺附近,似乎對呢一切都好清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親和主人的一匹老騎馬也站在附近,似乎對這一切都很清楚。

passages.original: “They have found a hare,” said my mother, “and if they come this way we shall see the hunt.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋發現咗一隻野兔,」我母親講,「如果佢哋往呢邊嚟,我哋就能睇到狩獵。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們發現了一隻野兔,」我母親說,「如果它們往這邊來,我們就能看到狩獵。」

passages.original: And soon the dogs were all tearing down the field of young wheat next to ours.
passages.vernacular: 不久,狗群就全都衝下我哋隔壁嗰片嫩麥田。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,狗群就全都衝下我們隔壁那片嫩麥田。

passages.original: I never heard such a noise as they made.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇聽過佢哋發出嗰樣嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒聽過它們發出那樣的聲音。

passages.original: They did not bark, nor howl, nor whine, but kept on a “yo! yo, o, o! yo! yo, o, o!” at the top of their voices.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔係吠,都唔係嚎,都唔係嗚咽,而係扯住嗓子不停地「唷!唷,噢,噢!唷!唷,噢,噢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不是吠,也不是嚎,也不是嗚咽,而是扯著嗓子不停地「唷!唷,噢,噢!唷!唷,噢,噢!」

passages.original: After them came a number of men on horseback, some of them in green coats, all galloping as fast as they could.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋後面跟住許多騎馬嘅人,有嘅穿住綠外套,全都拚命飛奔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們後面跟著許多騎馬的人,有的穿著綠外套,全都拚命飛奔。

passages.original: The old horse snorted and looked eagerly after them, and we young colts wanted to be galloping with them, but they were soon away into the fields lower down; here it seemed as if they had come to a stand; the dogs left off barking, and ran about every way with their noses to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 老馬噴住鼻息,急切地望住佢哋,我哋呢啲小馬駒都想同佢哋一起奔跑,不過佢哋好快就進入咗更低處嘅田野;喺嗰度佢哋似乎停咗下嚟;狗不叫喇,鼻子貼住地,四處亂跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老馬噴著鼻息,急切地望著它們,我們這些小馬駒也想和它們一起奔跑,可是它們很快就進入了更低處的田野;在那裡它們似乎停了下來;狗不叫了,鼻子貼著地,四處亂跑。

passages.original: “They have lost the scent,” said the old horse; “perhaps the hare will get off.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋失去咗氣味,」老馬講;「或者野兔能逃脫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們失去了氣味,」老馬說;「也許野兔能逃脫。」

passages.original: “What hare?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢野兔?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼野兔?」

passages.original: I said.
passages.vernacular: 我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問。

passages.original: “Oh!

I don't know what hare; likely enough it may be one of our own hares out of the woods; any hare they can find will do for the dogs and men to run after;” and before long the dogs began their “yo! yo, o, o!” again, and back they came altogether at full speed, making straight for our meadow at the part where the high bank and hedge overhang the brook.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道係乜嘢野兔;好可能係樹林裡我哋自己嘅野兔;任何佢哋能找到嘅野兔都行,狗同人跑住追就係喇;」不久狗又開始「唷!唷,噢,噢!」地叫喇,佢哋全速一起回嚟,徑直衝向我哋草地上高堤同樹籬俯臨小溪嘅嗰一段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道是什麼野兔;很可能是樹林裡我們自己的野兔;任何它們能找到的野兔都行,狗和人跑著追就是了;」不久狗又開始「唷!唷,噢,噢!」地叫了,它們全速一起回來,徑直衝向我們草地上高堤和樹籬俯臨小溪的那一段。

passages.original: “Now we shall see the hare,” said my mother; and just then a hare wild with fright rushed by and made for the woods.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我哋能睇到野兔喇,」我母親講;就喺呢陣,一隻嚇瘋咗嘅野兔飛奔而過,朝樹林跑去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我們能看到野兔了,」我母親說;就在這時,一隻嚇瘋了的野兔飛奔而過,朝樹林跑去。

passages.original: On came the dogs; they burst over the bank, leaped the stream, and came dashing across the field followed by the huntsmen.
passages.vernacular: 狗群衝咗上嚟;佢哋沖過堤岸,跳過小溪,飛快地穿過田野,獵人哋跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗群衝了上來;它們沖過堤岸,跳過小溪,飛快地穿過田野,獵人們跟在後面。

passages.original: Six or eight men leaped their horses clean over, close upon the dogs.
passages.vernacular: 六、八個人騎住馬,一下子跳過去,緊跟喺狗後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六、八個人騎著馬,一下子跳過去,緊跟在狗後面。

passages.original: The hare tried to get through the fence; it was too thick, and she turned sharp round to make for the road, but it was too late; the dogs were upon her with their wild cries; we heard one shriek, and that was the end of her.
passages.vernacular: 野兔想鑽過籬笆;太密喇,佢猛地轉身想跑上大路,不過太遲喇;狗群帶住狂野嘅叫聲撲到咗佢身上;我哋聽見一聲尖叫,佢就完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野兔想鑽過籬笆;太密了,她猛地轉身想跑上大路,可是太遲了;狗群帶著狂野的叫聲撲到了她身上;我們聽見一聲尖叫,她就完了。

passages.original: One of the huntsmen rode up and whipped off the dogs, who would soon have torn her to pieces.
passages.vernacular: 一個獵人騎過去,抽打走咗嗰啲狗,佢哋好快就會把佢撕成碎片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個獵人騎過去,抽打走了那些狗,它們很快就會把她撕成碎片。

passages.original: He held her up by the leg torn and bleeding, and all the gentlemen seemed well pleased.
passages.vernacular: 佢拎住佢嘅腿把佢舉起嚟,佢被撕裂喇,流住血,所有嘅先生哋似乎都好滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拎著她的腿把她舉起來,她被撕裂了,流著血,所有的先生們似乎都很滿意。

passages.original: As for me, I was so astonished that I did not at first see what was going on by the brook; but when I did look there was a sad sight; two fine horses were down, one was struggling in the stream, and the other was groaning on the grass.
passages.vernacular: 至於我,我太驚訝喇,起初冇睇見小溪邊發生嘅事;但我睇去時,嗰個係一幅悲慘嘅景象:兩匹好馬倒下喇,一匹喺溪裡掙扎,另一匹喺草地上呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我,我太驚訝了,起初沒看見小溪邊發生的事;但我看去時,那是一幅悲慘的景象:兩匹好馬倒下了,一匹在溪裡掙扎,另一匹在草地上呻吟。

passages.original: One of the riders was getting out of the water covered with mud, the other lay quite still.
passages.vernacular: 一個騎手正從水裡爬出嚟,渾身係泥,另一個一動不動地躺住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個騎手正從水裡爬出來,渾身是泥,另一個一動不動地躺著。

passages.original: “His neck is broke,” said my mother.
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅脖子斷喇,」我母親講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的脖子斷了,」我母親說。

passages.original: “And serve him right, too,” said one of the colts.
passages.vernacular: 「都係活該,」一匹小馬駒講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也是活該,」一匹小馬駒說。

passages.original: I thought the same, but my mother did not join with us.
passages.vernacular: 我都咁想,不過我母親不贊同我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這麼想,可是我母親不贊同我們。

passages.original: “Well, no,” she said, “you must not say that; but though I am an old horse, and have seen and heard a great deal, I never yet could make out why men are so fond of this sport; they often hurt themselves, often spoil good horses, and tear up the fields, and all for a hare or a fox, or a stag, that they could get more easily some other way; but we are only horses, and don't know.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢講,「你唔能夠咁講;雖然我係匹老馬,見過、聽過好多事,不過我從來弄不明白,點解人咁鍾意呢種運動;佢哋常常傷到自己,常常毀掉好馬,踩壞田地,而呢一切都係為了一隻野兔、一隻狐狸或一頭雄鹿,佢哋用別嘅辦法好容易得到;可我哋只係馬,不懂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」她說,「你不能那麼說;雖然我是匹老馬,見過、聽過很多事,可是我從來弄不明白,為什麼人這麼喜歡這種運動;他們常常傷到自己,常常毀掉好馬,踩壞田地,而這一切都是為了一隻野兔、一隻狐狸或一頭雄鹿,他們用別的辦法很容易得到;可我們只是馬,不懂。」

passages.original: While my mother was saying this we stood and looked on.
passages.vernacular: 我母親講呢啲話時,我哋站住睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親說這些話時,我們站著看。

passages.original: Many of the riders had gone to the young man; but my master, who had been watching what was going on, was the first to raise him.
passages.vernacular: 許多騎手都到嗰個年輕人嗰度去喇;但係一直睇住發生一切嘅我嘅主人,第一個把佢扶起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多騎手都到那個年輕人那裡去了;但是一直看著發生一切的我的主人,第一個把他扶起來。

passages.original: His head fell back and his arms hung down, and every one looked very serious.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅頭向後垂,胳膊耷拉下嚟,每個人都神情嚴肅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的頭向後垂,胳膊耷拉下來,每個人都神情嚴肅。

passages.original: There was no noise now; even the dogs were quiet, and seemed to know that something was wrong.
passages.vernacular: 而家冇聲音喇;連狗都安靜下嚟,似乎知道出事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在沒有聲音了;連狗也安靜下來,似乎知道出事了。

passages.original: They carried him to our master's house.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把佢抬到咗我哋主人嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把他抬到了我們主人的房子。

passages.original: I heard afterward that it was young George Gordon, the squire's only son, a fine, tall young man, and the pride of his family.
passages.vernacular: 我後來聽講,嗰個係年輕嘅喬治·戈登,鄉紳嘅獨生子,一位英俊高大嘅年輕人,係佢哋家嘅驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我後來聽說,那是年輕的喬治·戈登,鄉紳的獨生子,一位英俊高大的年輕人,是他們家的驕傲。

passages.original: There was now riding off in all directions to the doctor's, to the farrier's, and no doubt to Squire Gordon's, to let him know about his son.
passages.vernacular: 而家有人往四面八方騎馬去,去找醫生、馬蹄鐵匠,毫無疑問仲有鄉紳戈登,讓佢知道佢兒子嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在有人往四面八方騎馬去,去找醫生、馬蹄鐵匠,毫無疑問還有鄉紳戈登,讓他知道他兒子的事。

passages.original: When Mr. Bond, the farrier, came to look at the black horse that lay groaning on the grass, he felt him all over, and shook his head; one of his legs was broken.
passages.vernacular: 馬蹄鐵匠邦德先生來睇躺喺草地上呻吟嘅嗰匹黑馬時,佢把佢全身摸咗一遍,搖咗搖頭;佢嘅一條腿斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬蹄鐵匠邦德先生來看躺在草地上呻吟的那匹黑馬時,他把它全身摸了一遍,搖了搖頭;它的一條腿斷了。

passages.original: Then some one ran to our master's house and came back with a gun; presently there was a loud bang and a dreadful shriek, and then all was still; the black horse moved no more.
passages.vernacular: 然後有人跑到我哋主人嘅房子,攞咗一支槍回嚟;不久傳嚟一聲巨響同一聲可怕嘅尖叫,然後一切都靜喇;嗰匹黑馬再都冇動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有人跑到我們主人的房子,拿了一支槍回來;不久傳來一聲巨響和一聲可怕的尖叫,然後一切都靜了;那匹黑馬再也沒動。

passages.original: My mother seemed much troubled; she said she had known that horse for years, and that his name was “Rob Roy”; he was a good horse, and there was no vice in him.
passages.vernacular: 我母親似乎好難過;佢講佢認識嗰匹馬好多年喇,佢嘅名字叫「羅伯·羅伊」;佢係匹好馬,身上冇惡習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親似乎非常難過;她說她認識那匹馬很多年了,它的名字叫「羅伯·羅伊」;它是匹好馬,身上沒有惡習。

passages.original: She never would go to that part of the field afterward.
passages.vernacular: 佢後來再都唔肯去田野嘅嗰個地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她後來再也不肯去田野的那個地方。

passages.original: Not many days after we heard the church-bell tolling for a long time, and looking over the gate we saw a long, strange black coach that was covered with black cloth and was drawn by black horses; after that came another and another and another, and all were black, while the bell kept tolling, tolling.
passages.vernacular: 冇過幾天,我哋聽見教堂嘅鐘敲咗好久,隔住柵門望去,我哋睇見一輛長長嘅、奇怪嘅黑色馬車,蒙住黑布,由黑馬拉住;後面又係一輛、又一輛、又一輛,全都係黑嘅,鐘聲一直敲住、敲住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒過幾天,我們聽見教堂的鐘敲了很久,隔著柵門望去,我們看見一輛長長的、奇怪的黑色馬車,蒙著黑布,由黑馬拉著;後面又是一輛、又一輛、又一輛,全都是黑的,鐘聲一直敲著、敲著。

passages.original: They were carrying young Gordon to the churchyard to bury him.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正把年輕嘅戈登送到墓地去埋葬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們正把年輕的戈登送到墓地去埋葬。

passages.original: He would never ride again.
passages.vernacular: 佢再都唔能夠騎馬喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他再也不能騎馬了。

passages.original: What they did with Rob Roy I never knew; but 'twas all for one little hare.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把羅伯·羅伊點處理喇,我從來唔知道;但呢一切都係為了一隻小小嘅野兔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把羅伯·羅伊怎麼處理了,我從來不知道;但這一切都是為了一隻小小的野兔。

chapters.title: Part I · 03 My Breaking In 第一部·03 我被馴服

passages.original: CH I was now beginning to grow handsome; my coat had grown fine and soft, and was bright black.
passages.vernacular: 我開始長得漂亮喇;我嘅皮毛變得細軟,係明亮嘅黑色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我開始長得漂亮了;我的皮毛變得細軟,是明亮的黑色。

passages.original: I had one white foot and a pretty white star on my forehead.
passages.vernacular: 我有一隻白蹄子,額頭上有一顆好睇嘅白星。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一隻白蹄子,額頭上有一顆好看的白星。

passages.original: I was thought very handsome; my master would not sell me till I was four years old; he said lads ought not to work like men, and colts ought not to work like horses till they were quite grown up.
passages.vernacular: 大家都覺得我好漂亮;我嘅主人喺我四歲前唔肯賣我;佢講年輕人不該像大人嗰樣幹活,小馬駒唔到完全長大,都不該像馬嗰樣幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都覺得我很漂亮;我的主人在我四歲前不肯賣我;他說年輕人不該像大人那樣幹活,小馬駒不到完全長大,也不該像馬那樣幹活。

passages.original: When I was four years old Squire Gordon came to look at me.
passages.vernacular: 我四歲時,鄉紳戈登嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我四歲時,鄉紳戈登來看我。

passages.original: He examined my eyes, my mouth, and my legs; he felt them all down; and then I had to walk and trot and gallop before him.
passages.vernacular: 佢檢查咗我嘅眼睛、嘴巴同腿;佢把佢哋從上到下摸咗一遍;然後我唔得不喺佢面前走、小跑同飛奔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他檢查了我的眼睛、嘴巴和腿;他把它們從上到下摸了一遍;然後我不得不在他面前走、小跑和飛奔。

passages.original: He seemed to like me, and said, “When he has been well broken in he will do very well.”
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎鍾意我,講:「等佢好好馴服喇,佢會好好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他似乎喜歡我,說:「等他好好馴服了,他會很好的。」

passages.original: My master said he would break me in himself, as he should not like me to be frightened or hurt, and he lost no time about it, for the next day he began.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人講佢要自己馴服我,因為佢唔想讓我受驚或受傷,佢都冇耽擱,第二天就開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人說他要自己馴服我,因為他不想讓我受驚或受傷,他也沒有耽擱,第二天就開始了。

passages.original: Every one may not know what breaking in is, therefore I will describe it.
passages.vernacular: 唔係每個人都知道乜嘢係馴服,所以我嚟描述一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是每個人都知道什麼是馴服,所以我來描述一下。

passages.original: It means to teach a horse to wear a saddle and bridle, and to carry on his back a man, woman or child; to go just the way they wish, and to go quietly.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅意思係教一匹馬戴鞍同嚼子,喺背上載男人、女人或細路;完全按照佢哋嘅意願行進,而且安安靜靜地走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的意思是教一匹馬戴鞍和嚼子,在背上載男人、女人或孩子;完全按照他們的意願行進,而且安安靜靜地走。

passages.original: Besides this he has to learn to wear a collar, a crupper, and a breeching, and to stand still while they are put on; then to have a cart or a chaise fixed behind, so that he cannot walk or trot without dragging it after him; and he must go fast or slow, just as his driver wishes.
passages.vernacular: 此外,佢仲得學會戴頸圈、鞦韆同臀帶,並喺呢啲套上去時站住不動;然後讓一輛馬車或雙輪馬車被裝喺後面,咁樣佢不拖住佢走,就唔能夠走都唔能夠跑;佢必須完全照趕車人嘅意願,快或慢地走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,它還得學會戴頸圈、鞦韆和臀帶,並在這些套上去時站著不動;然後讓一輛馬車或雙輪馬車被裝在後面,這樣它不拖著它走,就不能走也不能跑;它必須完全照趕車人的意願,快或慢地走。

passages.original: He must never start at what he sees, nor speak to other horses, nor bite, nor kick, nor have any will of his own; but always do his master's will, even though he may be very tired or hungry; but the worst of all is, when his harness is once on, he may neither jump for joy nor lie down for weariness.
passages.vernacular: 佢絕唔能夠被睇到嘅嘢嚇一跳,唔能夠對別嘅馬講話,唔能夠咬,唔能夠踢,唔能夠有自己嘅意志;而總是照主人嘅意願做,即使佢可能好累或好餓;但最糟嘅係,一旦套上咗挽具,佢既唔能夠高興得跳起嚟,都唔能夠累得躺下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它絕不能被看到的東西嚇一跳,不能對別的馬說話,不能咬,不能踢,不能有自己的意志;而總是照主人的意願做,即使它可能很累或很餓;但最糟的是,一旦套上了挽具,它既不能高興得跳起來,也不能累得躺下。

passages.original: So you see this breaking in is a great thing.
passages.vernacular: 所以你睇,呢種馴服不過件大事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你看,這種馴服可是件大事。

passages.original: I had of course long been used to a halter and a headstall, and to be led about in the fields and lanes quietly, but now I was to have a bit and bridle; my master gave me some oats as usual, and after a good deal of coaxing he got the bit into my mouth, and the bridle fixed, but it was a nasty thing!
passages.vernacular: 當然我早就習慣咗籠頭同頭絡,習慣咗安安靜靜地被牽住走過田野同小路,但而家我要戴上嚼子同轡頭喇;我嘅主人像往常一樣畀咗我啲燕麥,經過一番哄勸,佢把嚼子放進咗我嘴裡,把轡頭固定好,可嗰個係個討厭嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我早就習慣了籠頭和頭絡,習慣了安安靜靜地被牽著走過田野和小路,但現在我要戴上嚼子和轡頭了;我的主人像往常一樣給了我一些燕麥,經過一番哄勸,他把嚼子放進了我嘴裡,把轡頭固定好,可那是個討厭的東西!

passages.original: Those who have never had a bit in their mouths cannot think how bad it feels; a great piece of cold hard steel as thick as a man's finger to be pushed into one's mouth, between one's teeth, and over one's tongue, with the ends coming out at the corner of your mouth, and held fast there by straps over your head, under your throat, round your nose, and under your chin; so that no way in the world can you get rid of the nasty hard thing; it is very bad! yes, very bad! at least I thought so; but I knew my mother always wore one when she went out, and all horses did when they were grown up; and so, what with the nice oats, and what with my master's pats, kind words, and gentle ways, I got to wear my bit and bridle.
passages.vernacular: 冇戴過嚼子嘅人,想唔到佢嘅感覺有多糟;一大塊像人手指咁粗嘅冷硬嘅鋼,要被塞進人嘅嘴裡,放喺牙齒之間,壓喺舌頭上面,兩端從嘴角露出嚟,被頭頂上、喉嚨下、鼻子周圍同下巴下面嘅帶子牢牢固定喺嗰度;咁樣你無論如何都擺脫不掉嗰個討厭嘅硬嘢;佢好糟!係嘅,好糟!至少我係咁覺得;但我知道我母親出門時總戴住一個,所有長大嘅馬都戴;所以,憑住嗰啲好食嘅燕麥,憑住我主人嘅撫摸、親切嘅話語同溫和嘅方式,我學會咗戴嚼子同轡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒戴過嚼子的人,想不到它的感覺有多糟;一大塊像人手指那麼粗的冷硬的鋼,要被塞進人的嘴裡,放在牙齒之間,壓在舌頭上面,兩端從嘴角露出來,被頭頂上、喉嚨下、鼻子周圍和下巴下面的帶子牢牢固定在那裡;這樣你無論如何也擺脫不掉那個討厭的硬東西;它非常糟!是的,非常糟!至少我是這麼覺得;但我知道我母親出門時總戴著一個,所有長大的馬都戴;所以,憑著那些好吃的燕麥,憑著我主人的撫摸、親切的話語和溫和的方式,我學會了戴嚼子和轡頭。

passages.original: Next came the saddle, but that was not half so bad; my master put it on my back very gently, while old Daniel held my head; he then made the girths fast under my body, patting and talking to me all the time; then I had a few oats, then a little leading about; and this he did every day till I began to look for the oats and the saddle.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟係馬鞍,但嗰冇一半咁糟;我嘅主人好輕柔地把佢放喺我背上,老丹尼爾扶住我嘅頭;然後佢把肚帶喺我身體下面繫緊,一直拍住我、對我講話;然後我食咗幾口燕麥,再被牽住走一小段;佢每天咁樣做,直到我開始期待燕麥同馬鞍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來是馬鞍,但那沒有一半那麼糟;我的主人非常輕柔地把它放在我背上,老丹尼爾扶著我的頭;然後他把肚帶在我身體下面繫緊,一直拍著我、對我說話;然後我吃了幾口燕麥,再被牽著走一小段;他每天這樣做,直到我開始期待燕麥和馬鞍。

passages.original: At length, one morning, my master got on my back and rode me round the meadow on the soft grass.
passages.vernacular: 終於,一天早晨,我嘅主人騎到我背上,喺柔軟嘅草地上繞住草場騎咗一圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於,一天早晨,我的主人騎到我背上,在柔軟的草地上繞著草場騎了一圈。

passages.original: It certainly did feel queer; but I must say I felt rather proud to carry my master, and as he continued to ride me a little every day I soon became accustomed to it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰確實感覺奇怪;但我必須講,我覺得載住我嘅主人相當自豪,而且佢每天都騎我一會兒,我好快就習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那確實感覺奇怪;但我必須說,我覺得載著我的主人相當自豪,而且他每天都騎我一會兒,我很快就習慣了。

passages.original: The next unpleasant business was putting on the iron shoes; that too was very hard at first.
passages.vernacular: 下一件不愉快嘅事係釘鐵蹄鐵;一開始嗰都好難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一件不愉快的事是釘鐵蹄鐵;一開始那也很難受。

passages.original: My master went with me to the smith's forge, to see that I was not hurt or got any fright.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人陪我去鐵匠嘅爐子嗰度,睇我不被弄傷或受到驚嚇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人陪我去鐵匠的爐子那裡,看我不被弄傷或受到驚嚇。

passages.original: The blacksmith took my feet in his hand, one after the other, and cut away some of the hoof.
passages.vernacular: 鐵匠一隻接一隻地把我嘅蹄子攞喺手裡,削掉啲蹄角質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐵匠一隻接一隻地把我的蹄子拿在手裡,削掉一些蹄角質。

passages.original: It did not pain me, so I stood still on three legs till he had done them all.
passages.vernacular: 呢個冇讓我疼,所以我站住用三條腿不動,直到佢把四個蹄子都弄完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這沒有讓我疼,所以我站著用三條腿不動,直到他把四個蹄子都弄完。

passages.original: Then he took a piece of iron the shape of my foot, and clapped it on, and drove some nails through the shoe quite into my hoof, so that the shoe was firmly on.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢攞一塊同我蹄子形狀一樣嘅鐵,啪地蓋上去,用釘子穿過蹄鐵釘進我嘅蹄子裡,讓蹄鐵牢牢固定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他拿一塊和我蹄子形狀一樣的鐵,啪地蓋上去,用釘子穿過蹄鐵釘進我的蹄子裡,讓蹄鐵牢牢固定。

passages.original: My feet felt very stiff and heavy, but in time I got used to it.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅蹄子覺得好僵硬沉重,但時間長咗我就習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的蹄子覺得非常僵硬沉重,但時間長了我就習慣了。

passages.original: And now having got so far, my master went on to break me to harness; there were more new things to wear.
passages.vernacular: 而家既然走到咗呢一步,我嘅主人接住訓練我習慣挽具;仲有更多新嘢要穿戴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在既然走到了這一步,我的主人接著訓練我習慣挽具;還有更多新東西要穿戴。

passages.original: First, a stiff heavy collar just on my neck, and a bridle with great side-pieces against my eyes called blinkers, and blinkers indeed they were, for I could not see on either side, but only straight in front of me; next, there was a small saddle with a nasty stiff strap that went right under my tail; that was the crupper.
passages.vernacular: 首先,一個僵硬沉重嘅頸圈就套喺我脖子上,仲有一個轡頭,兩側有緊貼我眼睛嘅大擋板,叫作遮眼罩,佢哋確實係遮眼罩,因為我兩邊都睇唔見,只能睇到正前方;接下嚟,有一個小鞍子,帶住一條討厭嘅硬帶子,一直穿到我尾巴底下;嗰個係鞦韆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,一個僵硬沉重的頸圈就套在我脖子上,還有一個轡頭,兩側有緊貼我眼睛的大擋板,叫作遮眼罩,它們確實是遮眼罩,因為我兩邊都看不見,只能看到正前方;接下來,有一個小鞍子,帶著一條討厭的硬帶子,一直穿到我尾巴底下;那是鞦韆。

passages.original: I hated the crupper; to have my long tail doubled up and poked through that strap was almost as bad as the bit.
passages.vernacular: 我恨鞦韆;我嘅長尾巴被折起嚟塞過嗰條帶子,幾乎同嚼子一樣糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨鞦韆;我的長尾巴被折起來塞過那條帶子,幾乎和嚼子一樣糟。

passages.original: I never felt more like kicking, but of course I could not kick such a good master, and so in time I got used to everything, and could do my work as well as my mother.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇咁想踢過人,不過當然我唔能夠踢咁好嘅主人,所以時間長喇,我習慣咗一切,能同我母親一樣做好我嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒那麼想踢過人,可是當然我不能踢這麼好的主人,所以時間長了,我習慣了一切,能和我母親一樣做好我的工作。

passages.original: I must not forget to mention one part of my training, which I have always considered a very great advantage.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠忘咗提我訓練中嘅一部分,我一直認為佢係個好大嘅好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能忘了提我訓練中的一部分,我一直認為它是個非常大的好處。

passages.original: My master sent me for a fortnight to a neighboring farmer's, who had a meadow which was skirted on one side by the railway.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人把我送到鄰近一個農夫嗰度待咗兩個星期,嗰個農夫有一片草場,一邊靠住鐵路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人把我送到鄰近一個農夫那裡待了兩個星期,那個農夫有一片草場,一邊靠著鐵路。

passages.original: Here were some sheep and cows, and I was turned in among them.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有啲羊同牛,我被放進佢哋中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有一些羊和牛,我被放進它們中間。

passages.original: I shall never forget the first train that ran by.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會忘記第一列駛過嘅火車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會忘記第一列駛過的火車。

passages.original: I was feeding quietly near the pales which separated the meadow from the railway, when I heard a strange sound at a distance, and before I knew whence it came--with a rush and a clatter, and a puffing out of smoke--a long black train of something flew by, and was gone almost before I could draw my breath.
passages.vernacular: 我正安靜地喺把草場同鐵路隔開嘅柵欄附近食草,聽見遠處傳嚟一種奇怪嘅聲音,我仲冇弄清佢係從邊兒嚟嘅——伴住轟隆聲同哐啷聲,噴住煙霧——一長列黑色嘅嘢飛馳而過,我仲冇嚟得及喘口氣,佢就冇影喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正安靜地在把草場和鐵路隔開的柵欄附近吃草,聽見遠處傳來一種奇怪的聲音,我還沒弄清它是從哪兒來的——伴著轟隆聲和哐啷聲,噴著煙霧——一長列黑色的東西飛馳而過,我還沒來得及喘口氣,它就沒影了。

passages.original: I turned and galloped to the further side of the meadow as fast as I could go, and there I stood snorting with astonishment and fear.
passages.vernacular: 我轉身,盡可能快地飛奔到草場嘅遠端,站喺嗰度驚訝而恐懼地噴住鼻息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我轉身,盡可能快地飛奔到草場的遠端,站在那裡驚訝而恐懼地噴著鼻息。

passages.original: In the course of the day many other trains went by, some more slowly; these drew up at the station close by, and sometimes made an awful shriek and groan before they stopped.
passages.vernacular: 嗰一天裡,許多別嘅火車經過,有嘅比較慢;呢啲喺附近嘅車站停下,有時停下之前仲發出可怕嘅尖叫同呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一天裡,許多別的火車經過,有的比較慢;這些在附近的車站停下,有時停下之前還發出可怕的尖叫和呻吟。

passages.original: I thought it very dreadful, but the cows went on eating very quietly, and hardly raised their heads as the black frightful thing came puffing and grinding past.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得好可怕,不過牛卻繼續好安靜地食草,黑色嘅可怕嘢噴住氣、嘎吱嘎吱地經過時,佢哋幾乎冇抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得非常可怕,可是牛卻繼續非常安靜地吃草,黑色的可怕東西噴著氣、嘎吱嘎吱地經過時,它們幾乎沒抬起頭。

passages.original: For the first few days I could not feed in peace; but as I found that this terrible creature never came into the field, or did me any harm, I began to disregard it, and very soon I cared as little about the passing of a train as the cows and sheep did.
passages.vernacular: 頭幾天我唔能夠安心食草;但我發現呢個可怕嘅嘢從不進入田野,都冇傷害我,我就開始不理會佢,好快我就像牛羊一樣,不在乎火車經過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭幾天我不能安心吃草;但我發現這個可怕的東西從不進入田野,也沒有傷害我,我就開始不理會它,很快我就像牛羊一樣,不在乎火車經過了。

passages.original: Since then I have seen many horses much alarmed and restive at the sight or sound of a steam engine; but thanks to my good master's care, I am as fearless at railway stations as in my own stable.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後我見過許多馬一見到或聽到蒸汽機就好驚慌、難以駕馭;不過多虧我好主人嘅悉心照顧,我喺火車站同喺自己嘅馬廄裡一樣無所畏懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後我見過許多馬一見到或聽到蒸汽機就非常驚慌、難以駕馭;可是多虧我好主人的悉心照顧,我在火車站和在自己的馬廄裡一樣無所畏懼。

passages.original: Now if any one wants to break in a young horse well, that is the way.
passages.vernacular: 如果有人想好好馴服一匹小馬,嗰個就係辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有人想好好馴服一匹小馬,那就是辦法。

passages.original: My master often drove me in double harness with my mother, because she was steady and could teach me how to go better than a strange horse.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人常常讓我同我母親一起套雙轅挽具駕車,因為佢沉穩,能比一匹陌生嘅馬更好地教我點走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人常常讓我和我母親一起套雙轅挽具駕車,因為她沉穩,能比一匹陌生的馬更好地教我怎麼走。

passages.original: She told me the better I behaved the better I should be treated, and that it was wisest always to do my best to please my master; “but,” said she, “there are a great many kinds of men; there are good thoughtful men like our master, that any horse may be proud to serve; and there are bad, cruel men, who never ought to have a horse or dog to call their own.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴我,我表現得越好,就會被對待得越好,而且最明智嘅係總是盡力讓我嘅主人高興;「但係,」佢講,「人有好多種;有像我哋主人咁樣善良、體貼嘅人,任何馬為佢哋效勞都會感到自豪;都有壞嘅、殘忍嘅人,佢哋永遠不該擁有一匹馬或一條狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她告訴我,我表現得越好,就會被對待得越好,而且最明智的是總是盡力讓我的主人高興;「但是,」她說,「人有很多種;有像我們主人這樣善良、體貼的人,任何馬為他們效勞都會感到自豪;也有壞的、殘忍的人,他們永遠不該擁有一匹馬或一條狗。

passages.original: Besides, there are a great many foolish men, vain, ignorant, and careless, who never trouble themselves to think; these spoil more horses than all, just for want of sense; they don't mean it, but they do it for all that.
passages.vernacular: 此外,仲有許多愚蠢嘅人,虛榮、無知、粗心,佢哋從不費心去想;呢啲人糟蹋嘅馬比所有人都多,只係因為缺乏頭腦;佢哋唔係故意嘅,不過佢哋定係咁做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,還有許多愚蠢的人,虛榮、無知、粗心,他們從不費心去想;這些人糟蹋的馬比所有人都多,只是因為缺乏頭腦;他們不是故意的,可是他們還是那麼做了。

passages.original: I hope you will fall into good hands; but a horse never knows who may buy him, or who may drive him; it is all a chance for us; but still I say, do your best wherever it is, and keep up your good name.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你能落到好人手裡;但係一匹馬永遠唔知道邊個會買佢,或者邊個會駕馭佢;呢對我哋都係碰運氣;不過我仍然要講,不管喺邊度,都盡你嘅力,保持你嘅好名聲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你能落到好人手裡;但是一匹馬永遠不知道誰會買他,或者誰會駕馭他;這對我們都是碰運氣;可是我仍然要說,不管在哪裡,都盡你的力,保持你的好名聲。」

chapters.title: Part I · 04 Birtwick Park 第一部·04 伯特威克莊園

passages.original: CH At this time I used to stand in the stable and my coat was brushed every day till it shone like a rook's wing.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣我常站喺馬廄裡,每天都有人畀我刷毛,刷得像烏鴉嘅翅膀一樣光亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時我常站在馬廄裡,每天都有人給我刷毛,刷得像烏鴉的翅膀一樣光亮。

passages.original: It was early in May, when there came a man from Squire Gordon's, who took me away to the hall.
passages.vernacular: 五月初嘅時候,有個人從戈登鄉紳嗰度嚟,把我帶到咗莊園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五月初的時候,有個人從戈登鄉紳那裡來,把我帶到了莊園。

passages.original: My master said, “Good-by, Darkie; be a good horse, and always do your best.”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人講:「再見,黑黑;做匹好馬,永遠盡你嘅力。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人說:「再見,黑黑;做匹好馬,永遠盡你的力。」

passages.original: I could not say “good-by”, so I put my nose into his hand; he patted me kindly, and I left my first home.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會講「再見」,所以我把鼻子伸進佢嘅手裡;佢親切地拍咗拍我,我就離開咗我嘅第一個家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會說「再見」,所以我把鼻子伸進他的手裡;他親切地拍了拍我,我就離開了我的第一個家。

passages.original: As I lived some years with Squire Gordon, I may as well tell something about the place.
passages.vernacular: 因為我喺戈登鄉紳嗰度住咗幾年,我不妨講講嗰個地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我在戈登鄉紳那裡住了幾年,我不妨講講那個地方。

passages.original: Squire Gordon's park skirted the village of Birtwick.
passages.vernacular: 戈登鄉紳嘅莊園緊挨住伯特威克村。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戈登鄉紳的莊園緊挨著伯特威克村。

passages.original: It was entered by a large iron gate, at which stood the first lodge, and then you trotted along on a smooth road between clumps of large old trees; then another lodge and another gate, which brought you to the house and the gardens.
passages.vernacular: 你從一道大鐵門進入,門邊係第一座門房,然後你沿住一條平整嘅路,喺一叢叢高大嘅老樹之間小跑;然後係另一座門房同另一道門,佢把你帶到房子同花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從一道大鐵門進入,門邊是第一座門房,然後你沿著一條平整的路,在一叢叢高大的老樹之間小跑;然後是另一座門房和另一道門,它把你帶到房子和花園。

passages.original: Beyond this lay the home paddock, the old orchard, and the stables.
passages.vernacular: 再過去係家庭牧場、老果園同馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再過去是家庭牧場、老果園和馬廄。

passages.original: There was accommodation for many horses and carriages; but I need only describe the stable into which I was taken; this was very roomy, with four good stalls; a large swinging window opened into the yard, which made it pleasant and airy.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度有許多馬同馬車嘅容身之處;但我只需要描述我被帶進嘅嗰間馬廄;佢好寬敞,有四個好馬棚;一扇大嘅擺動窗開向院子,讓佢宜人又通風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡有許多馬和馬車的容身之處;但我只需要描述我被帶進的那間馬廄;它非常寬敞,有四個好馬棚;一扇大的擺動窗開向院子,讓它宜人又通風。

passages.original: The first stall was a large square one, shut in behind with a wooden gate; the others were common stalls, good stalls, but not nearly so large; it had a low rack for hay and a low manger for corn; it was called a loose box, because the horse that was put into it was not tied up, but left loose, to do as he liked.
passages.vernacular: 第一個馬棚係大嘅方形嘅,後面用一道木門關起嚟;其他嘅係普通嘅馬棚,係好馬棚,但遠冇咁大;佢有一個低矮嘅乾草架同一個低矮嘅穀物槽;佢被叫作活動廄,因為被放進去嘅馬不被拴起嚟,而係放開,愛點樣就點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個馬棚是大的方形的,後面用一道木門關起來;其他的是普通的馬棚,是好馬棚,但遠沒有那麼大;它有一個低矮的乾草架和一個低矮的穀物槽;它被叫作活動廄,因為被放進去的馬不被拴起來,而是放開,愛怎麼樣就怎麼樣。

passages.original: It is a great thing to have a loose box.
passages.vernacular: 有一個活動廄係件了不起嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個活動廄是件了不起的事。

passages.original: Into this fine box the groom put me; it was clean, sweet, and airy.
passages.vernacular: 馬夫把我放進咗呢個好廄;佢乾淨、清新、通風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬夫把我放進了這個好廄;它乾淨、清新、通風。

passages.original: I never was in a better box than that, and the sides were not so high but that I could see all that went on through the iron rails that were at the top.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇喺比嗰更好嘅廄裡待過,而且四壁並冇高到讓我睇唔見透過頂上嘅鐵欄杆發生嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒在比那更好的廄裡待過,而且四壁並沒有高到讓我看不見透過頂上的鐵欄杆發生的一切。

passages.original: He gave me some very nice oats, he patted me, spoke kindly, and then went away.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀咗我啲好好嘅燕麥,拍咗拍我,親切地講咗話,然後就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給了我一些很好的燕麥,拍了拍我,親切地說了話,然後就走了。

passages.original: When I had eaten my corn I looked round.
passages.vernacular: 我食完穀物,環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我吃完穀物,環顧四周。

passages.original: In the stall next to mine stood a little fat gray pony, with a thick mane and tail, a very pretty head, and a pert little nose.
passages.vernacular: 喺我隔壁嘅馬棚裡,站住一匹矮胖嘅灰色小馬,鬃毛同尾巴好濃密,頭好漂亮,有一個俏皮嘅小鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我隔壁的馬棚裡,站著一匹矮胖的灰色小馬,鬃毛和尾巴很濃密,頭很漂亮,有一個俏皮的小鼻子。

passages.original: I put my head up to the iron rails at the top of my box, and said, “How do you do?
passages.vernacular: 我把頭伸到廄頂上嘅鐵欄杆邊,講:「你好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把頭伸到廄頂上的鐵欄杆邊,說:「你好嗎?

passages.original: What is your name?”
passages.vernacular: 你叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: He turned round as far as his halter would allow, held up his head, and said, “My name is Merrylegs.
passages.vernacular: 佢儘量轉過身,喺籠頭允許嘅範圍內,抬起頭講:「我叫梅利萊格斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他儘量轉過身,在籠頭允許的範圍內,抬起頭說:「我叫梅利萊格斯。

passages.original: I am very handsome; I carry the young ladies on my back, and sometimes I take our mistress out in the low chair.
passages.vernacular: 我好漂亮;我背住年輕小姐哋,有時我仲拉女主人坐低矮嘅椅式車出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很漂亮;我背著年輕小姐們,有時我還拉女主人坐低矮的椅式車出去。

passages.original: They think a great deal of me, and so does James.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好睇重我,詹姆斯都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們非常看重我,詹姆斯也是。

passages.original: Are you going to live next door to me in the box?”
passages.vernacular: 你要住喺我隔壁嘅廄裡嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要住在我隔壁的廄裡嗎?」

passages.original: I said, “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 我講:「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說:「是的。」

passages.original: “Well, then,” he said, “I hope you are good-tempered; I do not like any one next door who bites.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,」佢講,「我希望你脾氣好;我不鍾意隔壁有咬人嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,」他說,「我希望你脾氣好;我不喜歡隔壁有咬人的。」

passages.original: Just then a horse's head looked over from the stall beyond; the ears were laid back, and the eye looked rather ill-tempered.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,一匹馬嘅頭從嗰邊嘅馬棚探過嚟;耳朵向後貼住,眼神睇起嚟相當壞脾氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,一匹馬的頭從那邊的馬棚探過來;耳朵向後貼著,眼神看起來相當壞脾氣。

passages.original: This was a tall chestnut mare, with a long handsome neck.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一匹高大嘅栗色母馬,有一條長長嘅漂亮脖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一匹高大的栗色母馬,有一條長長的漂亮脖子。

passages.original: She looked across to me and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢睇住我講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看著我說:

passages.original: “So it is you who have turned me out of my box; it is a very strange thing for a colt like you to come and turn a lady out of her own home.”
passages.vernacular: 「原來就係你把我從我嘅廄裡趕出嚟;像你咁樣嘅小馬駒跑嚟把一位女士趕出佢自己嘅家,真係件好奇怪嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「原來就是你把我從我的廄裡趕出來;像你這樣的小馬駒跑來把一位女士趕出她自己的家,真是件非常奇怪的事。」

passages.original: “I beg your pardon,” I said, “I have turned no one out; the man who brought me put me here, and I had nothing to do with it; and as to my being a colt, I am turned four years old and am a grown-up horse.
passages.vernacular: 「對不起,」我講,「我冇趕走邊個;帶我嚟嘅人把我放喺呢度,同我無關;至於我係小馬駒,我已經四歲多喇,係匹成年嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對不起,」我說,「我沒有趕走誰;帶我來的人把我放在這裡,與我無關;至於我是小馬駒,我已經四歲多了,是匹成年的馬。

passages.original: I never had words yet with horse or mare, and it is my wish to live at peace.”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇同邊匹馬、邊匹母馬吵過架,我嘅願望係和平相處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒和哪匹馬、哪匹母馬吵過架,我的願望是和平相處。」

passages.original: “Well,” she said, “we shall see.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」佢講,「我哋走住瞧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」她說,「我們走著瞧。

passages.original: Of course, I do not want to have words with a young thing like you.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,我唔想同你咁樣嘅小傢伙吵架。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,我不想同你這樣的小傢伙吵架。」

passages.original: I said no more.
passages.vernacular: 我冇再講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒再說什麼。

passages.original: In the afternoon, when she went out, Merrylegs told me all about it.
passages.vernacular: 下午佢出去時,梅利萊格斯把呢一切都告訴咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午她出去時,梅利萊格斯把這一切都告訴了我。

passages.original: “The thing is this,” said Merrylegs.
passages.vernacular: 「事情係咁樣嘅,」梅利萊格斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「事情是這樣的,」梅利萊格斯說。

passages.original: “Ginger has a bad habit of biting and snapping; that is why they call her Ginger, and when she was in the loose box she used to snap very much.
passages.vernacular: 「金姐有咬人同亂啃嘅壞習慣;所以佢哋才叫佢金姐,佢喺嗰個活動廄嘅時候經常亂啃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「金姐有咬人和亂啃的壞習慣;所以他們才叫她金姐,她在那個活動廄的時候經常亂啃。

passages.original: One day she bit James in the arm and made it bleed, and so Miss Flora and Miss Jessie, who are very fond of me, were afraid to come into the stable.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢咬咗詹姆斯嘅胳膊,咬出血嚟,所以好鍾意我嘅弗洛拉小姐同潔西小姐,都唔敢進馬廄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天她咬了詹姆斯的胳膊,咬出血來,所以非常喜歡我的弗洛拉小姐和潔西小姐,都不敢進馬廄了。

passages.original: They used to bring me nice things to eat, an apple or a carrot, or a piece of bread, but after Ginger stood in that box they dared not come, and I missed them very much.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋以前常畀我帶好食嘅嘢,蘋果、胡蘿蔔或一塊麵包,不過金姐站喺嗰個廄裡以後,佢哋就唔敢嚟喇,我好想念佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們以前常給我帶好吃的東西,蘋果、胡蘿蔔或一塊麵包,可是金姐站在那個廄裡以後,她們就不敢來了,我非常想念她們。

passages.original: I hope they will now come again, if you do not bite or snap.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望佢哋而家會再嚟,如果你不咬不啃嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望她們現在會再來,如果你不咬不啃的話。」

passages.original: I told him I never bit anything but grass, hay, and corn, and could not think what pleasure Ginger found it.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢我除咗草、乾草同穀物乜嘢都不咬,想不通金姐喺其中找到乜嘢樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他我除了草、乾草和穀物什麼也不咬,想不通金姐在其中找到什麼樂趣。

passages.original: “Well, I don't think she does find pleasure,” says Merrylegs; “it is just a bad habit; she says no one was ever kind to her, and why should she not bite?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想佢並冇找到樂趣,」梅利萊格斯講;「嗰只係個壞習慣;佢講從來冇人對佢好過,佢點解唔能夠咬?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想她並沒有找到樂趣,」梅利萊格斯說;「那只是個壞習慣;她說從來沒人對她好過,她為什麼不能咬?

passages.original: Of course, it is a very bad habit; but I am sure, if all she says be true, she must have been very ill-used before she came here.
passages.vernacular: 當然,呢個係個好壞嘅習慣;但我確信,如果佢講嘅都係真嘅,佢喺嚟呢度之前一定被虐待得好厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,這是個很壞的習慣;但我確信,如果她說的都是真的,她在來這裡之前一定被虐待得很厲害。

passages.original: John does all he can to please her, and James does all he can, and our master never uses a whip if a horse acts right; so I think she might be good-tempered here.
passages.vernacular: 約翰盡佢所能討好佢,詹姆斯盡佢所能,我哋嘅主人只要馬行為正確,就從唔使鞭子;所以我想佢喺呢度可能會脾氣好起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰盡他所能討好她,詹姆斯盡他所能,我們的主人只要馬行為正確,就從不用鞭子;所以我想她在這裡可能會脾氣好起來。

passages.original: You see,” he said, with a wise look, “I am twelve years old; I know a great deal, and I can tell you there is not a better place for a horse all round the country than this.
passages.vernacular: 你睇,」佢帶住聰明嘅神情講,「我十二歲喇;我知道好多事,我可以告訴你,整個鄉下冇比呢度更適合馬嘅好地方喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,」他帶著聰明的神情說,「我十二歲了;我知道很多事,我可以告訴你,整個鄉下沒有比這裡更適合馬的好地方了。

passages.original: John is the best groom that ever was; he has been here fourteen years; and you never saw such a kind boy as James is; so that it is all Ginger's own fault that she did not stay in that box.”
passages.vernacular: 約翰係有史以來最好嘅馬夫;佢喺呢度十四年喇;你從冇見過詹姆斯咁樣善良嘅男孩;所以金姐冇能留喺嗰個廄裡,全係佢自己嘅錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰是有史以來最好的馬夫;他在這裡十四年了;你從沒見過詹姆斯這樣善良的男孩;所以金姐沒能留在那個廄裡,全是她自己的錯。」

chapters.title: Part I · 05 A Fair Start 第一部·05 良好的開端

passages.original: CH The name of the coachman was John Manly; he had a wife and one little child, and they lived in the coachman's cottage, very near the stables.
passages.vernacular: 車夫嘅名字叫約翰·曼利;佢有一個妻子同一個小孩,佢哋住喺馬廄附近嘅車夫小屋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 車夫的名字叫約翰·曼利;他有一個妻子和一個小孩,他們住在馬廄附近的車夫小屋裡。

passages.original: The next morning he took me into the yard and gave me a good grooming, and just as I was going into my box, with my coat soft and bright, the squire came in to look at me, and seemed pleased.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨佢把我帶到院子裡,畀我好好刷咗毛,就喺我皮毛柔軟發亮、正要進我嘅廄時,鄉紳進嚟睇我,似乎好滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨他把我帶到院子裡,給我好好刷了毛,就在我皮毛柔軟發亮、正要進我的廄時,鄉紳進來看我,似乎很滿意。

passages.original: “John,” he said, “I meant to have tried the new horse this morning, but I have other business.
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,」佢講,「我本來打算今日早晨試試呢匹新馬,不過我仲有別嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,」他說,「我本來打算今天早晨試試這匹新馬,可是我還有別的事。

passages.original: You may as well take him around after breakfast; go by the common and the Highwood, and back by the watermill and the river; that will show his paces.”
passages.vernacular: 你不妨食完早飯後帶佢走一圈;經過公地同高林,再從水磨坊同河邊回嚟;呢可以顯示佢嘅步伐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不妨吃完早飯後帶他走一圈;經過公地和高林,再從水磨坊和河邊回來;這可以顯示他的步伐。」

passages.original: “I will, sir,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「係,先生,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,先生,」約翰說。

passages.original: After breakfast he came and fitted me with a bridle.
passages.vernacular: 早飯後佢嚟畀我戴上轡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯後他來給我戴上轡頭。

passages.original: He was very particular in letting out and taking in the straps, to fit my head comfortably; then he brought a saddle, but it was not broad enough for my back; he saw it in a minute and went for another, which fitted nicely.
passages.vernacular: 佢調整帶子嘅鬆緊,好講究,讓佢舒適地適合我嘅頭;然後佢攞嚟一個鞍子,但係對我嘅背唔夠寬;佢一眼就睇出嚟,又去攞咗另一個,正合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他調整帶子的鬆緊,非常講究,讓它舒適地適合我的頭;然後他拿來一個鞍子,但是對我的背不夠寬;他一眼就看出來,又去拿了另一個,正合適。

passages.original: He rode me first slowly, then a trot, then a canter, and when we were on the common he gave me a light touch with his whip, and we had a splendid gallop.
passages.vernacular: 佢先慢慢地騎我,然後小跑,然後跑起嚟,到咗公地上佢輕輕地抽咗我一鞭,我哋痛快地飛奔咗一陣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他先慢慢地騎我,然後小跑,然後跑起來,到了公地上他輕輕地抽了我一鞭,我們痛快地飛奔了一陣。

passages.original: “Ho, ho! my boy,” he said, as he pulled me up, “you would like to follow the hounds, I think.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗬嗬!我嘅細路,」佢勒住我時講,「我想你願意追隨獵犬吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗬嗬!我的孩子,」他勒住我時說,「我想你願意追隨獵犬吧。」

passages.original: As we came back through the park we met the Squire and Mrs. Gordon walking; they stopped, and John jumped off.
passages.vernacular: 我哋穿過莊園回嚟時,遇見鄉紳同戈登太太喺散步;佢哋停咗下嚟,約翰跳下馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們穿過莊園回來時,遇見鄉紳和戈登太太在散步;他們停了下來,約翰跳下馬。

passages.original: “Well, John, how does he go?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,約翰,佢走得點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,約翰,他走得怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “First-rate, sir,” answered John; “he is as fleet as a deer, and has a fine spirit too; but the lightest touch of the rein will guide him.
passages.vernacular: 「一流,先生,」約翰回答;「佢像鹿一樣快,精神都好好;不過韁繩最輕嘅一碰就能引導佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一流,先生,」約翰回答;「他像鹿一樣快,精神也很好;可是韁繩最輕的一碰就能引導他。

passages.original: Down at the end of the common we met one of those traveling carts hung all over with baskets, rugs, and such like; you know, sir, many horses will not pass those carts quietly; he just took a good look at it, and then went on as quiet and pleasant as could be.
passages.vernacular: 喺公地盡頭,我哋遇到一輛旅行嘅小車,上面掛滿咗籃子、毯子之類嘅嘢;您知道,先生,許多馬唔肯安靜地經過嗰種車;佢只係好好睇咗一眼,就又安安靜靜、舒舒服服地走過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在公地盡頭,我們遇到一輛旅行的小車,上面掛滿了籃子、毯子之類的東西;您知道,先生,許多馬不肯安靜地經過那種車;他只是好好看了一眼,就又安安靜靜、舒舒服服地走過去了。

passages.original: They were shooting rabbits near the Highwood, and a gun went off close by; he pulled up a little and looked, but did not stir a step to right or left.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺高林附近打兔子,附近響咗一聲槍;佢稍微停咗停,睇咗睇,但冇向左右挪動一步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在高林附近打兔子,附近響了一聲槍;他稍微停了停,看了看,但沒有向左右挪動一步。

passages.original: I just held the rein steady and did not hurry him, and it's my opinion he has not been frightened or ill-used while he was young.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係穩穩地握住韁繩,冇催佢,我認為佢年輕時冇受過驚嚇或虐待。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是穩穩地握著韁繩,沒有催他,我認為他年輕時沒有受過驚嚇或虐待。」

passages.original: “That's well,” said the squire, “I will try him myself to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好好,」鄉紳講,「聽日我自己試試佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很好,」鄉紳說,「明天我自己試試他。」

passages.original: The next day I was brought up for my master.
passages.vernacular: 第二天我被帶去畀我嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天我被帶去給我的主人。

passages.original: I remembered my mother's counsel and my good old master's, and I tried to do exactly what he wanted me to do.
passages.vernacular: 我記起母親嘅忠告同我好老主人嘅教導,盡力做佢要我做嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記起母親的忠告和我好老主人的教導,盡力做他要我做的一切。

passages.original: I found he was a very good rider, and thoughtful for his horse too.
passages.vernacular: 我發現佢係個好好嘅騎手,對佢嘅馬都好體貼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現他是個非常好的騎手,對他的馬也很體貼。

passages.original: When he came home the lady was at the hall door as he rode up.
passages.vernacular: 佢回家時,夫人喺大廳門口,佢騎咗過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回家時,夫人在大廳門口,他騎了過來。

passages.original: “Well, my dear,” she said, “how do you like him?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,親愛嘅,」佢講,「你覺得佢點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,親愛的,」她說,「你覺得他怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “He is exactly what John said,” he replied; “a pleasanter creature I never wish to mount.
passages.vernacular: 「佢完全像約翰講嘅嗰樣,」佢回答;「我從冇希望騎上比呢更愉快嘅生靈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他完全像約翰說的那樣,」他回答;「我從沒希望騎上比這更愉快的生靈。

passages.original: What shall we call him?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋叫佢乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們叫他什麼?」

passages.original: “Would you like Ebony?” said she; “he is as black as ebony.”
passages.vernacular: 「你鍾意烏木嗎?」佢講;「佢像烏木一樣黑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你喜歡烏木嗎?」她說;「他像烏木一樣黑。」

passages.original: “No, not Ebony.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,唔好烏木。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不要烏木。」

passages.original: “Will you call him Blackbird, like your uncle's old horse?”
passages.vernacular: 「像你叔叔嘅嗰匹老馬,叫佢黑鳥點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像你叔叔的那匹老馬,叫他黑鳥怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “No, he is far handsomer than old Blackbird ever was.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢比老黑鳥好睇得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,他比老黑鳥好看得多。」

passages.original: “Yes,” she said, “he is really quite a beauty, and he has such a sweet, good-tempered face, and such a fine, intelligent eye--what do you say to calling him Black Beauty?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」佢講,「佢真嘅係個十足嘅美人,佢有一張咁甜美、好脾氣嘅臉,同咁好嘅、聰明嘅眼睛——你講叫佢黑神駒點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」她說,「他真的是個十足的美人,他有一張那麼甜美、好脾氣的臉,和那麼好的、聰明的眼睛——你說叫他黑神駒怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “Black Beauty--why, yes, I think that is a very good name.
passages.vernacular: 「黑神駒——嗯,係嘅,我想嗰個係個好好嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黑神駒——嗯,是的,我想那是個很好的名字。

passages.original: If you like it shall be his name;” and so it was.
passages.vernacular: 如果你鍾意,嗰個就係佢嘅名字;」於是就咁樣定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你喜歡,那就是他的名字;」於是就這樣定了。

passages.original: When John went into the stable he told James that master and mistress had chosen a good, sensible English name for me, that meant something; not like Marengo, or Pegasus, or Abdallah.
passages.vernacular: 約翰走進馬廄時,佢告訴詹姆斯,主人同女主人畀我起咗個好嘅、明智嘅英國名字,有意義;不像馬倫戈,或者佩加索斯,或者阿卜杜拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰走進馬廄時,他告訴詹姆斯,主人和女主人給我起了個好的、明智的英國名字,有意義;不像馬倫戈,或者佩加索斯,或者阿卜杜拉。

passages.original: They both laughed, and James said, “If it was not for bringing back the past, I should have named him Rob Roy, for I never saw two horses more alike.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋兩個都笑喇,詹姆斯講:「要唔係會勾起過去,我本來會叫佢羅伯·羅伊,因為我從冇見過兩匹咁像嘅馬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們兩個都笑了,詹姆斯說:「要不是會勾起過去,我本來會叫他羅伯·羅伊,因為我從沒見過兩匹這麼像的馬。」

passages.original: “That's no wonder,” said John; “didn't you know that Farmer Grey's old Duchess was the mother of them both?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢不奇怪,」約翰講;「你唔知道格雷農夫嘅老公爵夫人係佢倆嘅母親嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不奇怪,」約翰說;「你不知道格雷農夫的老公爵夫人是它倆的母親嗎?」

passages.original: I had never heard that before; and so poor Rob Roy who was killed at that hunt was my brother!
passages.vernacular: 我以前從冇聽講過;原來喺嗰次狩獵中被殺嘅可憐羅伯·羅伊係我嘅哥哥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前從沒聽說過;原來在那次狩獵中被殺的可憐羅伯·羅伊是我的哥哥!

passages.original: I did not wonder that my mother was so troubled.
passages.vernacular: 我母親咁難過,我並不奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親那麼難過,我並不奇怪。

passages.original: It seems that horses have no relations; at least they never know each other after they are sold.
passages.vernacular: 睇來馬係冇親戚嘅;至少佢哋被賣掉之後,就再都認不出對方喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看來馬是沒有親戚的;至少它們被賣掉之後,就再也認不出對方了。

passages.original: John seemed very proud of me; he used to make my mane and tail almost as smooth as a lady's hair, and he would talk to me a great deal; of course I did not understand all he said, but I learned more and more to know what he meant, and what he wanted me to do.
passages.vernacular: 約翰似乎為我感到好自豪;佢常把我嘅鬃毛同尾巴梳得幾乎像女士嘅頭髮一樣光滑,而且佢常常同我講話;當然我唔係全都聽得懂佢講嘅,但我越嚟越明白佢嘅意思,以及佢要我做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰似乎為我感到非常自豪;他常把我的鬃毛和尾巴梳得幾乎像女士的頭髮一樣光滑,而且他常常同我說話;當然我不是全都聽得懂他說的,但我越來越明白他的意思,以及他要我做什麼。

passages.original: I grew very fond of him, he was so gentle and kind; he seemed to know just how a horse feels, and when he cleaned me he knew the tender places and the ticklish places; when he brushed my head he went as carefully over my eyes as if they were his own, and never stirred up any ill-temper.
passages.vernacular: 我變得好鍾意佢,佢係咁溫和善良;佢似乎完全知道馬嘅感受,畀我刷洗時佢知道邊啲地方嬌嫩、邊啲地方怕癢;佢畀我刷頭時,小心地刷過我嘅眼睛,好像嗰個係佢自己嘅眼睛,從不激起我嘅壞脾氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我變得非常喜歡他,他是那麼溫和善良;他似乎完全知道馬的感受,給我刷洗時他知道哪些地方嬌嫩、哪些地方怕癢;他給我刷頭時,小心地刷過我的眼睛,好像那是他自己的眼睛,從不激起我的壞脾氣。

passages.original: James Howard, the stable boy, was just as gentle and pleasant in his way, so I thought myself well off.
passages.vernacular: 馬廄男孩詹姆斯·霍華德,以佢嘅方式都一樣溫和愉快,所以我覺得自己過得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬廄男孩詹姆斯·霍華德,以他的方式也一樣溫和愉快,所以我覺得自己過得很好。

passages.original: There was another man who helped in the yard, but he had very little to do with Ginger and me.
passages.vernacular: 院子裡仲有一個人幫忙,但佢同金姐同我幾乎冇乜嘢關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 院子裡還有一個人幫忙,但他同金姐和我幾乎沒有什麼關係。

passages.original: A few days after this I had to go out with Ginger in the carriage.
passages.vernacular: 過咗幾天,我唔得不同金姐一起套車出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了幾天,我不得不同金姐一起套車出去。

passages.original: I wondered how we should get on together; but except laying her ears back when I was led up to her, she behaved very well.
passages.vernacular: 我納悶我哋點相處;但除咗我被牽到佢身邊時佢把耳朵向後貼之外,佢表現得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我納悶我們怎麼相處;但除了我被牽到她身邊時她把耳朵向後貼之外,她表現得很好。

passages.original: She did her work honestly, and did her full share, and I never wish to have a better partner in double harness.
passages.vernacular: 佢老老實實地幹活,盡咗佢全部本分,我從不希望有比佢更好嘅雙轅搭檔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她老老實實地幹活,盡了她全部本分,我從不希望有比她更好的雙轅搭檔。

passages.original: When we came to a hill, instead of slackening her pace, she would throw her weight right into the collar, and pull away straight up.
passages.vernacular: 我哋到咗一座山坡,佢不放慢步子,反而把全身嘅重量壓進頸圈,筆直地往上拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們到了一座山坡,她不放慢步子,反而把全身的重量壓進頸圈,筆直地往上拉。

passages.original: We had both the same sort of courage at our work, and John had oftener to hold us in than to urge us forward; he never had to use the whip with either of us; then our paces were much the same, and I found it very easy to keep step with her when trotting, which made it pleasant, and master always liked it when we kept step well, and so did John.
passages.vernacular: 我哋幹活時有同樣嘅勇氣,約翰更常需要勒住我哋,而唔係催促我哋前進;佢從不需要對我哋任何一個用鞭子;而且我哋嘅步伐都大致相同,我發現小跑時好容易同佢保持步調一致,呢讓人愉快,主人總是鍾意我哋步調一致,約翰都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們幹活時有同樣的勇氣,約翰更常需要勒住我們,而不是催促我們前進;他從不需要對我們任何一個用鞭子;而且我們的步伐也大致相同,我發現小跑時很容易和她保持步調一致,這讓人愉快,主人總是喜歡我們步調一致,約翰也是。

passages.original: After we had been out two or three times together we grew quite friendly and sociable, which made me feel very much at home.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一起出去咗兩三次後,就變得相當友好、合群,呢讓我覺得好有家嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一起出去了兩三次後,就變得相當友好、合群,這讓我覺得很有家的感覺。

passages.original: As for Merrylegs, he and I soon became great friends; he was such a cheerful, plucky, good-tempered little fellow that he was a favorite with every one, and especially with Miss Jessie and Flora, who used to ride him about in the orchard, and have fine games with him and their little dog Frisky.
passages.vernacular: 至於梅利萊格斯,佢同我好快成咗好朋友;佢係個咁快活、有膽量、好脾氣嘅小傢伙,人人都鍾意佢,尤其係潔西小姐同弗洛拉小姐,佢哋常騎住佢喺果園裡轉,同佢同佢哋嘅小狗弗里斯基玩得好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於梅利萊格斯,他和我很快成了好朋友;他是個那麼快活、有膽量、好脾氣的小傢伙,人人都喜歡他,尤其是潔西小姐和弗洛拉小姐,她們常騎著他在果園裡轉,同他和她們的小狗弗里斯基玩得很開心。

passages.original: Our master had two other horses that stood in another stable.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅主人仲有另外兩匹馬,站喺另一個馬廄裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的主人還有另外兩匹馬,站在另一個馬廄裡。

passages.original: One was Justice, a roan cob, used for riding or for the luggage cart; the other was an old brown hunter, named Sir Oliver; he was past work now, but was a great favorite with the master, who gave him the run of the park; he sometimes did a little light carting on the estate, or carried one of the young ladies when they rode out with their father, for he was very gentle and could be trusted with a child as well as Merrylegs.
passages.vernacular: 一匹係賈斯蒂斯,一匹花斑矮腳馬,用嚟騎乘或拉行李車;另一匹係一匹老棕色獵馬,叫奧利弗爵士;佢而家已經唔能夠幹活喇,但係主人好鍾意佢,讓佢喺莊園裡自由活動;佢有時喺莊園裡拉點輕便嘅貨車,或者喺年輕小姐哋同佢哋嘅父親出去騎馬時載一位,因為佢好溫和,可以像梅利萊格斯一樣放心地讓細路騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一匹是賈斯蒂斯,一匹花斑矮腳馬,用來騎乘或拉行李車;另一匹是一匹老棕色獵馬,叫奧利弗爵士;他現在已經不能幹活了,但是主人非常喜歡他,讓他在莊園裡自由活動;他有時在莊園裡拉點輕便的貨車,或者在年輕小姐們同她們的父親出去騎馬時載一位,因為他很溫和,可以像梅利萊格斯一樣放心地讓孩子騎。

passages.original: The cob was a strong, well-made, good-tempered horse, and we sometimes had a little chat in the paddock, but of course I could not be so intimate with him as with Ginger, who stood in the same stable.
passages.vernacular: 嗰匹矮腳馬強壯,體格好,脾氣好,我哋有時喺牧場上聊幾句,但我當然唔能夠同佢像同金姐嗰樣親近,金姐站喺同一個馬廄裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那匹矮腳馬強壯,體格好,脾氣好,我們有時在牧場上聊幾句,但我當然不能和他像和金姐那樣親近,金姐站在同一個馬廄裡。

chapters.title: Part I · 06 Liberty 第一部·06 自由

passages.original: CH I was quite happy in my new place, and if there was one thing that I missed it must not be thought I was discontented; all who had to do with me were good and I had a light airy stable and the best of food.
passages.vernacular: 我喺新地方好快樂,如果有一樣我想念嘅嘢,都不該認為我不滿足;所有同我打交道嘅人都好好,我有一間明亮通風嘅馬廄同最好嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在新地方非常快樂,如果有一樣我想念的東西,也不該認為我不滿足;所有和我打交道的人都很好,我有一間明亮通風的馬廄和最好的食物。

passages.original: What more could I want?
passages.vernacular: 我仲想要乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還想要什麼?

passages.original: Why, liberty!
passages.vernacular: 嗯,自由!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,自由!

passages.original: For three years and a half of my life I had had all the liberty I could wish for; but now, week after week, month after month, and no doubt year after year, I must stand up in a stable night and day except when I am wanted, and then I must be just as steady and quiet as any old horse who has worked twenty years.
passages.vernacular: 我生命中嘅三年半裡,我擁有我所能期望嘅一切自由;可而家,一週又一週,一個月又一個月,毫無疑問仲有一年又一年,我必須日夜站喺馬廄裡,除咗被需要嘅時候,而嗰時我必須像任何幹咗二十年活嘅老馬一樣穩重安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我生命中的三年半裡,我擁有我所能期望的一切自由;可現在,一週又一週,一個月又一個月,毫無疑問還有一年又一年,我必須日夜站在馬廄裡,除了被需要的時候,而那時我必須像任何幹了二十年活的老馬一樣穩重安靜。

passages.original: Straps here and straps there, a bit in my mouth, and blinkers over my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 呢度一條帶子,嗰度一條帶子,嘴裡一個嚼子,眼前一副遮眼罩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡一條帶子,那裡一條帶子,嘴裡一個嚼子,眼前一副遮眼罩。

passages.original: Now, I am not complaining, for I know it must be so.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我唔係喺抱怨,因為我知道必須如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我不是在抱怨,因為我知道必須如此。

passages.original: I only mean to say that for a young horse full of strength and spirits, who has been used to some large field or plain where he can fling up his head and toss up his tail and gallop away at full speed, then round and back again with a snort to his companions--I say it is hard never to have a bit more liberty to do as you like.
passages.vernacular: 我只係想講,對於一匹精力充沛、精神飽滿嘅年輕馬,佢習慣咗某片大田野或平原,喺嗰度佢可以昂起頭、甩起尾巴,全速飛奔而去,然後轉一圈,噴住鼻息回到同伴嗰度——我講,從來冇多啲自由想點樣就點樣,係好難受嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是想說,對於一匹精力充沛、精神飽滿的年輕馬,他習慣了某片大田野或平原,在那裡他可以昂起頭、甩起尾巴,全速飛奔而去,然後轉一圈,噴著鼻息回到同伴那裡——我說,從來沒有多一點自由想怎樣就怎樣,是很難受的。

passages.original: Sometimes, when I have had less exercise than usual, I have felt so full of life and spring that when John has taken me out to exercise I really could not keep quiet; do what I would, it seemed as if I must jump, or dance, or prance, and many a good shake I know I must have given him, especially at the first; but he was always good and patient.
passages.vernacular: 有時,我運動得比平常少,我感到充滿活力同彈性,約翰帶我出去運動時,我真嘅靜不下嚟;不管我點做,似乎我必須跳、跳舞或蹦躂,我知道我一定把佢顛得夠嗆,尤其係剛開始時;但佢總是咁好,咁有耐心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時,我運動得比平常少,我感到充滿活力和彈性,約翰帶我出去運動時,我真的靜不下來;不管我怎麼做,似乎我必須跳、跳舞或蹦躂,我知道我一定把他顛得夠嗆,尤其是剛開始時;但他總是那麼好,那麼有耐心。

passages.original: “Steady, steady, my boy,” he would say; “wait a bit, and we will have a good swing, and soon get the tickle out of your feet.”
passages.vernacular: 「穩住,穩住,我嘅細路,」佢會講;「等一等,我哋好好跑一下,好快就能把你腳上嘅癢癢弄掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「穩住,穩住,我的孩子,」他會說;「等一等,我們好好跑一下,很快就能把你腳上的癢癢弄掉。」

passages.original: Then as soon as we were out of the village, he would give me a few miles at a spanking trot, and then bring me back as fresh as before, only clear of the fidgets, as he called them.
passages.vernacular: 然後我哋一出村子,佢就讓我以疾速小跑跑上幾英里,然後帶我回嚟,像以前一樣精神,只係擺脫咗佢所謂嘅煩躁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我們一出村子,他就讓我以疾速小跑跑上幾英里,然後帶我回來,像以前一樣精神,只是擺脫了他所謂的煩躁。

passages.original: Spirited horses, when not enough exercised, are often called skittish, when it is only play; and some grooms will punish them, but our John did not; he knew it was only high spirits.
passages.vernacular: 精神旺盛嘅馬,運動唔夠時,常被稱為易受驚嘅,其實只係玩耍;有些馬夫會懲罰佢哋,不過我哋嘅約翰冇;佢知道嗰只係精神好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 精神旺盛的馬,運動不夠時,常被稱為易受驚的,其實只是玩耍;有些馬夫會懲罰它們,可是我們的約翰沒有;他知道那只是精神好。

passages.original: Still, he had his own ways of making me understand by the tone of his voice or the touch of the rein.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢有佢自己嘅辦法,通過佢嘅語氣或韁繩嘅觸碰讓我明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他有他自己的辦法,通過他的語氣或韁繩的觸碰讓我明白。

passages.original: If he was very serious and quite determined, I always knew it by his voice, and that had more power with me than anything else, for I was very fond of him.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢好嚴肅,好堅決,我總能從佢嘅聲音裡知道,嗰比乜嘢都更有力量,因為我好鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他非常嚴肅,十分堅決,我總能從他的聲音裡知道,那比什麼都更有力量,因為我非常喜歡他。

passages.original: I ought to say that sometimes we had our liberty for a few hours; this used to be on fine Sundays in the summer-time.
passages.vernacular: 我應該講,有時我哋有幾個小時嘅自由;呢通常喺夏天晴朗嘅星期日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我應該說,有時我們有幾個小時的自由;這通常在夏天晴朗的星期日。

passages.original: The carriage never went out on Sundays, because the church was not far off.
passages.vernacular: 星期日馬車從不出去,因為教堂不遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期日馬車從不出去,因為教堂不遠。

passages.original: It was a great treat to us to be turned out into the home paddock or the old orchard; the grass was so cool and soft to our feet, the air so sweet, and the freedom to do as we liked was so pleasant--to gallop, to lie down, and roll over on our backs, or to nibble the sweet grass.
passages.vernacular: 被放到家庭牧場或老果園裡,對我哋係一大享受;草地對我哋嘅蹄子係咁涼爽柔軟,空氣係咁清甜,可以想點樣就點樣嘅自由係咁愉快——奔跑、躺下、仰面打滾,或者啃甜甜嘅草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被放到家庭牧場或老果園裡,對我們是一大享受;草地對我們的蹄子是那麼涼爽柔軟,空氣是那麼清甜,可以想怎樣就怎樣的自由是那麼愉快——奔跑、躺下、仰面打滾,或者啃甜甜的草。

passages.original: Then it was a very good time for talking, as we stood together under the shade of the large chestnut tree.
passages.vernacular: 嗰都係談話嘅好時候,我哋一起站喺大栗樹嘅樹蔭下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那也是談話的好時候,我們一起站在大栗樹的樹蔭下。

chapters.title: Part I · 07 Ginger 第一部·07 金姐

passages.original: CH One day when Ginger and I were standing alone in the shade, we had a great deal of talk; she wanted to know all about my bringing up and breaking in, and I told her.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,金姐同我單獨站喺樹蔭下,我哋談咗好多;佢想知道我嘅成長同馴服嘅一切,我告訴咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,金姐和我單獨站在樹蔭下,我們談了很多;她想知道我的成長和馴服的一切,我告訴了她。

passages.original: “Well,” said she, “if I had had your bringing up I might have had as good a temper as you, but now I don't believe I ever shall.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」佢講,「如果我有你嗰樣嘅成長環境,我或者會有像你一樣好嘅脾氣,可而家我不相信我會有喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」她說,「如果我有你那樣的成長環境,我也許會有像你一樣好的脾氣,可現在我不相信我會有了。」

passages.original: “Why not?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解唔會?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不會?」

passages.original: I said.
passages.vernacular: 我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說。

passages.original: “Because it has been all so different with me,” she replied.
passages.vernacular: 「因為我嘅一切都咁不同,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為我的一切都那麼不同,」她回答。

passages.original: “I never had any one, horse or man, that was kind to me, or that I cared to please, for in the first place I was taken from my mother as soon as I was weaned, and put with a lot of other young colts; none of them cared for me, and I cared for none of them.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇過任何對我好嘅,無論係馬定係人,或者係我願意取悅嘅,因為首先我一斷奶就被從媽媽身邊帶走,同一大群別嘅年輕小馬駒放喺一起;佢哋冇一個關心我,我都不關心佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒有過任何對我好的,無論是馬還是人,或者是我願意取悅的,因為首先我一斷奶就被從媽媽身邊帶走,和一大群別的年輕小馬駒放在一起;它們沒有一個關心我,我也不關心它們。

passages.original: There was no kind master like yours to look after me, and talk to me, and bring me nice things to eat.
passages.vernacular: 冇像你嘅主人嗰樣嘅好主人照顧我、對我講話、畀我帶好食嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有像你的主人那樣的好主人照顧我、對我說話、給我帶好吃的東西。

passages.original: The man that had the care of us never gave me a kind word in my life.
passages.vernacular: 照管我哋嘅嗰個人,一輩子冇對我講過一句好話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照管我們的那個人,一輩子沒有對我說過一句好話。

passages.original: I do not mean that he ill-used me, but he did not care for us one bit further than to see that we had plenty to eat, and shelter in the winter.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係講佢虐待我,但佢除咗確保我哋有足夠食嘅、冬天有住處之外,啲都不關心我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是說他虐待我,但他除了確保我們有足夠吃的、冬天有住處之外,一點也不關心我們。

passages.original: A footpath ran through our field, and very often the great boys passing through would fling stones to make us gallop.
passages.vernacular: 一條人行小路穿過我哋嘅田野,好多時候路過嘅大男孩會扔石頭讓我哋奔跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條人行小路穿過我們的田野,很多時候路過的大男孩會扔石頭讓我們奔跑。

passages.original: I was never hit, but one fine young colt was badly cut in the face, and I should think it would be a scar for life.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇被打中,但有一匹漂亮嘅小馬駒,臉上被劃得好厲害,我想嗰會係一輩子嘅疤痕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒被打中,但有一匹漂亮的小馬駒,臉上被劃得很厲害,我想那會是一輩子的疤痕。

passages.original: We did not care for them, but of course it made us more wild, and we settled it in our minds that boys were our enemies.
passages.vernacular: 我哋不在乎佢哋,但當然呢使我哋更野喇,我哋心裡認定男孩係我哋嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不在乎他們,但當然這使我們更野了,我們心裡認定男孩是我們的敵人。

passages.original: We had very good fun in the free meadows, galloping up and down and chasing each other round and round the field; then standing still under the shade of the trees.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺自由嘅草地上玩得好開心,上上下下飛奔,繞住田野一圈一圈地追逐;然後喺樹蔭下靜靜站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在自由的草地上玩得很開心,上上下下飛奔,繞著田野一圈一圈地追逐;然後在樹蔭下靜靜站著。

passages.original: But when it came to breaking in, that was a bad time for me; several men came to catch me, and when at last they closed me in at one corner of the field, one caught me by the forelock, another caught me by the nose and held it so tight I could hardly draw my breath; then another took my under jaw in his hard hand and wrenched my mouth open, and so by force they got on the halter and the bar into my mouth; then one dragged me along by the halter, another flogging behind, and this was the first experience I had of men's kindness; it was all force.
passages.vernacular: 不過到咗馴服嘅時候,對我係段糟糕嘅時間;幾個人嚟抓我,最後把我圍喺田野嘅一個角落時,一個人抓住我嘅額毛,另一個人抓住我嘅鼻子,抓得咁緊,我幾乎喘不過氣;然後另一個人用佢堅硬嘅手抓住我嘅下顎,扳開我嘅嘴,就咁樣用蠻力把籠頭同嚼子塞進我嘴裡;然後一個人拽住籠頭拖住我走,另一個喺後面抽打,呢個就係我第一次體會到人嘅好意;全係蠻力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是到了馴服的時候,對我是段糟糕的時間;幾個人來抓我,最後把我圍在田野的一個角落時,一個人抓住我的額毛,另一個人抓住我的鼻子,抓得那麼緊,我幾乎喘不過氣;然後另一個人用他堅硬的手抓住我的下顎,扳開我的嘴,就這樣用蠻力把籠頭和嚼子塞進我嘴裡;然後一個人拽著籠頭拖著我走,另一個在後面抽打,這就是我第一次體會到人的好意;全是蠻力。

passages.original: They did not give me a chance to know what they wanted.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不畀我機會知道佢哋要乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不給我機會知道他們要什麼。

passages.original: I was high bred and had a great deal of spirit, and was very wild, no doubt, and gave them, I dare say, plenty of trouble, but then it was dreadful to be shut up in a stall day after day instead of having my liberty, and I fretted and pined and wanted to get loose.
passages.vernacular: 我血統高貴,精神好足,無疑好野,我敢講畀佢哋添咗好多麻煩,但係被關喺馬棚裡一天又一天,而唔係擁有我嘅自由,係可怕嘅,我焦躁、憔悴,想掙脫出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我血統高貴,精神很足,無疑非常野,我敢說給他們添了很多麻煩,但是被關在馬棚裡一天又一天,而不是擁有我的自由,是可怕的,我焦躁、憔悴,想掙脫出去。

passages.original: You know yourself it's bad enough when you have a kind master and plenty of coaxing, but there was nothing of that sort for me.
passages.vernacular: 你自己知道,即使有好主人同大量嘅哄勸,呢已經夠糟喇,不過對我乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你自己知道,即使有好主人和大量的哄勸,這已經夠糟了,可是對我什麼都沒有。

passages.original: “There was one--the old master, Mr. Ryder--who, I think, could soon have brought me round, and could have done anything with me; but he had given up all the hard part of the trade to his son and to another experienced man, and he only came at times to oversee.
passages.vernacular: 「有一個——老主人,賴德先生——我想佢好快就能把我帶好,能對我做任何事;不過佢把行業裡一切艱苦嘅部分都交畀咗佢兒子同另一個有經驗嘅人,佢只係偶爾嚟監督。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一個——老主人,賴德先生——我想他很快就能把我帶好,能對我做任何事;可是他把行業裡一切艱苦的部分都交給了他兒子和另一個有經驗的人,他只是偶爾來監督。

passages.original: His son was a strong, tall, bold man; they called him Samson, and he used to boast that he had never found a horse that could throw him.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅兒子係個強壯、高大、大膽嘅人;佢哋叫佢參孫,佢常吹噓佢從冇遇到過能把佢摔下嚟嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的兒子是個強壯、高大、大膽的人;他們叫他參孫,他常吹噓他從沒遇到過能把他摔下來的馬。

passages.original: There was no gentleness in him, as there was in his father, but only hardness, a hard voice, a hard eye, a hard hand; and I felt from the first that what he wanted was to wear all the spirit out of me, and just make me into a quiet, humble, obedient piece of horseflesh.
passages.vernacular: 佢身上冇佢父親嗰樣嘅溫和,只有冷酷,冷酷嘅聲音,冷酷嘅眼睛,冷酷嘅手;我從一開始就感覺到,佢要嘅係把我嘅全部精神消磨殆盡,把我變成一塊安靜、謙卑、順從嘅馬肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他身上沒有他父親那樣的溫和,只有冷酷,冷酷的聲音,冷酷的眼睛,冷酷的手;我從一開始就感覺到,他要的是把我的全部精神消磨殆盡,把我變成一塊安靜、謙卑、順從的馬肉。

passages.original: 'Horseflesh'!
passages.vernacular: 『馬肉』!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『馬肉』!

passages.original: Yes, that is all that he thought about,” and Ginger stamped her foot as if the very thought of him made her angry.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,呢個就係佢想嘅全部,」金姐跺咗跺腳,好像想到佢就讓佢生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,這就是他想的全部,」金姐跺了跺腳,好像想到他就讓她生氣。

passages.original: Then she went on:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢繼續講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她繼續說:

passages.original: “If I did not do exactly what he wanted he would get put out, and make me run round with that long rein in the training field till he had tired me out.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我不完全按佢要嘅做,佢就會發火,讓我拖住嗰根長韁繩喺訓練場裡轉圈,直到把我累垮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我不完全按他要的做,他就會發火,讓我拖著那根長韁繩在訓練場裡轉圈,直到把我累垮。

passages.original: I think he drank a good deal, and I am quite sure that the oftener he drank the worse it was for me.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢飲好多酒,我好確定佢飲得越多,對我越糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他喝很多酒,我很確定他喝得越多,對我越糟。

passages.original: One day he had worked me hard in every way he could, and when I lay down I was tired, and miserable, and angry; it all seemed so hard.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,佢用盡一切辦法狠狠地操練我,我躺下時又累又痛苦又氣憤;一切似乎咁艱難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,他用盡一切辦法狠狠地操練我,我躺下時又累又痛苦又氣憤;一切似乎那麼艱難。

passages.original: The next morning he came for me early, and ran me round again for a long time.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨佢一早嚟找我,又讓我轉咗好長時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨他一早來找我,又讓我轉了很長時間。

passages.original: I had scarcely had an hour's rest, when he came again for me with a saddle and bridle and a new kind of bit.
passages.vernacular: 我剛休息咗一小時,佢又嚟找我,帶住鞍子同轡頭同一種新嘅嚼子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛休息了一小時,他又來找我,帶著鞍子和轡頭和一種新的嚼子。

passages.original: I could never quite tell how it came about; he had only just mounted me on the training ground, when something I did put him out of temper, and he chucked me hard with the rein.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇弄明白係點回事;佢剛喺訓練場上騎上我,我做嘅乜嘢事使佢發火喇,佢用韁繩猛地拉我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒弄明白是怎麼回事;他剛在訓練場上騎上我,我做的什麼事使他發火了,他用韁繩猛地拉我。

passages.original: The new bit was very painful, and I reared up suddenly, which angered him still more, and he began to flog me.
passages.vernacular: 新嚼子好疼,我突然豎起前蹄,呢使佢更生氣,佢開始抽打我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新嚼子非常疼,我突然豎起前蹄,這使他更生氣,他開始抽打我。

passages.original: I felt my whole spirit set against him, and I began to kick, and plunge, and rear as I had never done before, and we had a regular fight; for a long time he stuck to the saddle and punished me cruelly with his whip and spurs, but my blood was thoroughly up, and I cared for nothing he could do if only I could get him off.
passages.vernacular: 我感到我嘅全部精神都同佢對立起嚟,我開始踢、猛衝、豎起前蹄,像我從未做過嘅嗰樣,我哋打咗一場真正嘅架;好長一段時間佢緊緊坐喺鞍子上,用鞭子同馬刺殘忍地懲罰我,不過我嘅血已經完全沸騰喇,只要能把佢甩下去,佢做乜嘢我都不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感到我的全部精神都與他對立起來,我開始踢、猛衝、豎起前蹄,像我從未做過的那樣,我們打了一場真正的架;很長一段時間他緊緊坐在鞍子上,用鞭子和馬刺殘忍地懲罰我,可是我的血已經完全沸騰了,只要能把他甩下去,他做什麼我都不在乎。

passages.original: At last after a terrible struggle I threw him off backward.
passages.vernacular: 最後經過一場可怕嘅掙扎,我把佢向後甩咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後經過一場可怕的掙扎,我把他向後甩了下去。

passages.original: I heard him fall heavily on the turf, and without looking behind me, I galloped off to the other end of the field; there I turned round and saw my persecutor slowly rising from the ground and going into the stable.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見佢重重地摔喺草皮上,我頭都不回地飛奔到田野嘅另一端;喺嗰度我轉過身,睇見迫害我嘅人慢慢從地上站起嚟,走進馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見他重重地摔在草皮上,我頭也不回地飛奔到田野的另一端;在那裡我轉過身,看見迫害我的人慢慢從地上站起來,走進馬廄。

passages.original: I stood under an oak tree and watched, but no one came to catch me.
passages.vernacular: 我站喺一棵橡樹下睇住,但冇人嚟抓我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站在一棵橡樹下看著,但沒有人來抓我。

passages.original: The time went on, and the sun was very hot; the flies swarmed round me and settled on my bleeding flanks where the spurs had dug in.
passages.vernacular: 時間過去喇,太陽好熱;蒼蠅成群地圍住我,落喺被馬刺扎出血嘅我嘅兩肋上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間過去了,太陽很熱;蒼蠅成群地圍著我,落在被馬刺扎出血的我的兩肋上。

passages.original: I felt hungry, for I had not eaten since the early morning, but there was not enough grass in that meadow for a goose to live on.
passages.vernacular: 我感到餓喇,因為從清晨起我就冇食嘢,不過嗰片草地裡嘅草連一隻鵝都養不活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感到餓了,因為從清晨起我就沒吃東西,可是那片草地裡的草連一隻鵝都養不活。

passages.original: I wanted to lie down and rest, but with the saddle strapped tightly on there was no comfort, and there was not a drop of water to drink.
passages.vernacular: 我想躺下休息,不過鞍子緊緊綁住,啲都不舒服,而且連一滴水都冇飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想躺下休息,可是鞍子緊緊綁著,一點也不舒服,而且連一滴水都沒有喝。

passages.original: The afternoon wore on, and the sun got low.
passages.vernacular: 下午過去喇,太陽低喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午過去了,太陽低了。

passages.original: I saw the other colts led in, and I knew they were having a good feed.
passages.vernacular: 我睇見別嘅小馬駒被牽進去,我知道佢哋喺飽餐一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見別的小馬駒被牽進去,我知道它們在飽餐一頓。

passages.original: “At last, just as the sun went down, I saw the old master come out with a sieve in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 「最後,就喺太陽落山時,我睇見老主人手裡攞住一個篩子走咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最後,就在太陽落山時,我看見老主人手裡拿著一個篩子走了出來。

passages.original: He was a very fine old gentleman with quite white hair, but his voice was what I should know him by among a thousand.
passages.vernacular: 佢係位好好嘅老先生,頭髮全白喇,但我能喺千人中憑佢嘅聲音認出佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是位很好的老先生,頭髮全白了,但我能在千人中憑他的聲音認出他。

passages.original: It was not high, nor yet low, but full, and clear, and kind, and when he gave orders it was so steady and decided that every one knew, both horses and men, that he expected to be obeyed.
passages.vernacular: 佢不高,都不低,而係飽滿、清晰、和藹,佢下命令時係咁穩定而堅決,以致每個人,無論馬定係人,都知道佢期待被服從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不高,也不低,而是飽滿、清晰、和藹,他下命令時是那麼穩定而堅決,以致每個人,無論馬還是人,都知道他期待被服從。

passages.original: He came quietly along, now and then shaking the oats about that he had in the sieve, and speaking cheerfully and gently to me: 'Come along, lassie, come along, lassie; come along, come along.'
passages.vernacular: 佢安靜地走過嚟,不時搖晃住篩子裡嘅燕麥,和氣溫柔地對我講:『嚟吧,小姑娘,嚟吧,小姑娘;嚟吧,嚟吧。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他安靜地走過來,不時搖晃著篩子裡的燕麥,和氣溫柔地對我說:『來吧,小姑娘,來吧,小姑娘;來吧,來吧。』

passages.original: I stood still and let him come up; he held the oats to me, and I began to eat without fear; his voice took all my fear away.
passages.vernacular: 我站住不動,讓佢走近;佢把燕麥遞畀我,我毫不畏懼地開始食;佢嘅聲音驅散咗我所有嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站著不動,讓他走近;他把燕麥遞給我,我毫不畏懼地開始吃;他的聲音驅散了我所有的恐懼。

passages.original: He stood by, patting and stroking me while I was eating, and seeing the clots of blood on my side he seemed very vexed.
passages.vernacular: 我食嘅時候,佢站喺旁邊拍我、撫摸我,睇見我身側嘅血塊,佢似乎好惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我吃的時候,他站在旁邊拍我、撫摸我,看見我身側的血塊,他似乎非常惱火。

passages.original: 'Poor lassie! it was a bad business, a bad business;' then he quietly took the rein and led me to the stable; just at the door stood Samson.
passages.vernacular: 『可憐嘅小姑娘!呢事辦得糟透喇,糟透喇;』然後佢安靜地攞起韁繩,把我牽到馬廄;就喺門口站住參孫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『可憐的小姑娘!這事辦得糟透了,糟透了;』然後他安靜地拿起韁繩,把我牽到馬廄;就在門口站著參孫。

passages.original: I laid my ears back and snapped at him.
passages.vernacular: 我把耳朵向後貼,朝佢亂啃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把耳朵向後貼,朝他亂啃。

passages.original: 'Stand back,' said the master, 'and keep out of her way; you've done a bad day's work for this filly.'
passages.vernacular: 『站開,』主人講,『別擋佢嘅路;你畀呢匹小母馬幹咗件糟糕嘅事。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『站開,』主人說,『別擋她的路;你給這匹小母馬幹了件糟糕的事。』

passages.original: He growled out something about a vicious brute.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘟囔咗一句乜嘢兇惡畜生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他嘟囔了一句什麼兇惡畜生。

passages.original: 'Hark ye,' said the father, 'a bad-tempered man will never make a good-tempered horse.
passages.vernacular: 『聽住,』父親講,『壞脾氣嘅人永遠訓練不出好脾氣嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『聽著,』父親說,『壞脾氣的人永遠訓練不出好脾氣的馬。

passages.original: You've not learned your trade yet, Samson.'
passages.vernacular: 你仲冇學會你嘅行當,參孫。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還沒學會你的行當,參孫。』

passages.original: Then he led me into my box, took off the saddle and bridle with his own hands, and tied me up; then he called for a pail of warm water and a sponge, took off his coat, and while the stable-man held the pail, he sponged my sides a good while, so tenderly that I was sure he knew how sore and bruised they were.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把我牽進我嘅廄,親手取下鞍子同轡頭,把我拴好;然後佢要咗一桶溫水同一塊海綿,脫掉外衣,馬夫提住桶,佢用海綿畀我擦洗兩側,擦咗好一會兒,咁溫柔,我確信佢知道佢哋多疼多腫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他把我牽進我的廄,親手取下鞍子和轡頭,把我拴好;然後他要了一桶溫水和一塊海綿,脫掉外衣,馬夫提著桶,他用海綿給我擦洗兩側,擦了好一會兒,那麼溫柔,我確信他知道它們多疼多腫。

passages.original: 'Whoa! my pretty one,' he said, 'stand still, stand still.'
passages.vernacular: 『噓!我嘅漂亮寶貝,』佢講,『站住別動,站住別動。』
