passages.original: “Your master never taught you a truer thing,” said John; “there is no religion without love, and people may talk as much as they like about their religion, but if it does not teach them to be good and kind to man and beast it is all a sham--all a sham, James, and it won't stand when things come to be turned inside out.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅老師從冇教過你比呢更真實嘅話,」約翰講;「冇愛就冇宗教,人哋愛點談佢哋嘅宗教都行,但如果佢不教佢哋對人同獸善良,嗰都係假嘅——全係假嘅,詹姆斯,等事情被翻過嚟,佢就站不住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的老師從沒教過你比這更真實的話,」約翰說;「沒有愛就沒有宗教,人們愛怎麼談他們的宗教都行,但如果它不教他們對人和獸善良,那都是假的——全是假的,詹姆斯,等事情被翻過來,它就站不住了。」

chapters.title: Part I · 14 James Howard 第一部·14 詹姆斯·霍華德

passages.original: CH Early one morning in December John had just led me into my box after my daily exercise, and was strapping my cloth on and James was coming in from the corn chamber with some oats, when the master came into the stable.
passages.vernacular: 十二月嘅一天清早,約翰剛喺我每日運動後把我牽進我嘅廄,正在畀我繫上毯子,詹姆斯攞住啲燕麥從穀倉間進嚟,主人走進咗馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二月的一天清早,約翰剛在我每日運動後把我牽進我的廄,正在給我繫上毯子,詹姆斯拿著一些燕麥從穀倉間進來,主人走進了馬廄。

passages.original: He looked rather serious, and held an open letter in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟相當嚴肅,手裡攞住一封打開嘅信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來相當嚴肅,手裡拿著一封打開的信。

passages.original: John fastened the door of my box, touched his cap, and waited for orders.
passages.vernacular: 約翰把我廄嘅門扣上,碰咗碰帽子,等候吩咐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰把我廄的門扣上,碰了碰帽子,等候吩咐。

passages.original: “Good-morning, John,” said the master.
passages.vernacular: 「早安,約翰,」主人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「早安,約翰,」主人說。

passages.original: “I want to know if you have any complaint to make of James.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想知道你對詹姆斯有冇乜嘢不滿。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想知道你對詹姆斯有沒有什麼不滿。」

passages.original: “Complaint, sir?
passages.vernacular: 「不滿,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不滿,先生?

passages.original: No, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 冇,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,先生。」

passages.original: “Is he industrious at his work and respectful to you?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢幹活勤快、對你恭敬嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他幹活勤快、對你恭敬嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir, always.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,一向如此。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,一向如此。」

passages.original: “You never find he slights his work when your back is turned?”
passages.vernacular: 「你從冇發現你背過身時佢敷衍工作嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從沒發現你背過身時他敷衍工作嗎?」

passages.original: “Never, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「從冇,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從沒有,先生。」

passages.original: “That's well; but I must put another question.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好好;不過我必須再問一個問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很好;不過我必須再問一個問題。

passages.original: Have you no reason to suspect, when he goes out with the horses to exercise them or to take a message, that he stops about talking to his acquaintances, or goes into houses where he has no business, leaving the horses outside?”
passages.vernacular: 你有冇理由懷疑,佢帶馬出去運動或傳話嘅時候,會停下嚟同熟人聊天,或者進冇事嘅人家,把馬丟喺外面?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有沒有理由懷疑,他帶馬出去運動或傳話的時候,會停下來同熟人聊天,或者進沒有事的人家,把馬丟在外面?」

passages.original: “No, sir, certainly not; and if anybody has been saying that about James, I don't believe it, and I don't mean to believe it unless I have it fairly proved before witnesses; it's not for me to say who has been trying to take away James' character, but I will say this, sir, that a steadier, pleasanter, honester, smarter young fellow I never had in this stable.
passages.vernacular: 「冇,先生,絕對冇;如果有人咁樣講詹姆斯,我不信,而且除非有證人當面證實,我都不打算信;邊個喺試圖詆毀詹姆斯嘅名譽不該由我講,不過我要講呢一句,先生,我喺呢個馬廄裡從冇過比佢更沉穩、更愉快、更誠實、更機靈嘅年輕人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,先生,絕對沒有;如果有人這樣說詹姆斯,我不信,而且除非有證人當面證實,我也不打算信;誰在試圖詆毀詹姆斯的名譽不該由我說,不過我要說這一句,先生,我在這個馬廄裡從沒有過比他更沉穩、更愉快、更誠實、更機靈的年輕人。

passages.original: I can trust his word and I can trust his work; he is gentle and clever with the horses, and I would rather have them in charge with him than with half the young fellows I know of in laced hats and liveries; and whoever wants a character of James Howard,” said John, with a decided jerk of his head, “let them come to John Manly.”
passages.vernacular: 我信得過佢嘅話,都信得過佢嘅活;佢對馬溫和又機靈,我寧可讓馬交畀佢照管,都唔願交畀我所知嘅半數戴住鑲邊帽、穿住制服嘅年輕人;邊個要詹姆斯·霍華德嘅品行證明,」約翰堅決地一甩頭講,「讓佢哋嚟找約翰·曼利。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我信得過他的話,也信得過他的活;他對馬溫和又機靈,我寧可讓馬交給他照管,也不願交給我所知的半數戴著鑲邊帽、穿著制服的年輕人;誰要詹姆斯·霍華德的品行證明,」約翰堅決地一甩頭說,「讓他們來找約翰·曼利。」

passages.original: The master stood all this time grave and attentive, but as John finished his speech a broad smile spread over his face, and looking kindly across at James, who all this time had stood still at the door, he said, “James, my lad, set down the oats and come here; I am very glad to find that John's opinion of your character agrees so exactly with my own.
passages.vernacular: 主人呢陣一直站住,嚴肅而專注,可約翰講完話時,佢臉上綻開咗一個大大嘅微笑,佢親切地睇住一直站喺門口冇動嘅詹姆斯,講:「詹姆斯,細路,放下燕麥過嚟;我好高興發現約翰對你品行嘅睇法同我嘅完全一致。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主人這時一直站著,嚴肅而專注,可約翰說完話時,他臉上綻開了一個大大的微笑,他親切地看著一直站在門口沒動的詹姆斯,說:「詹姆斯,孩子,放下燕麥過來;我很高興發現約翰對你品行的看法與我的完全一致。

passages.original: John is a cautious man,” he said, with a droll smile, “and it is not always easy to get his opinion about people, so I thought if I beat the bush on this side the birds would fly out, and I should learn what I wanted to know quickly; so now we will come to business.
passages.vernacular: 約翰係個謹慎嘅人,」佢帶住滑稽嘅微笑講,「要得到佢對別人嘅睇法並不總是容易,所以我想,如果我喺呢邊打草,鳥就會飛出嚟,我就能好快知道我想知道嘅;而家我哋談正事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰是個謹慎的人,」他帶著滑稽的微笑說,「要得到他對別人的看法並不總是容易,所以我想,如果我在這邊打草,鳥就會飛出來,我就能很快知道我想知道的;現在我們談正事。

passages.original: I have a letter from my brother-in-law, Sir Clifford Williams, of Clifford Hall.
passages.vernacular: 我收到我姐夫克利福德·威廉斯爵士嘅一封信,佢住喺克利福德莊園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我收到我姐夫克利福德·威廉斯爵士的一封信,他住在克利福德莊園。

passages.original: He wants me to find him a trustworthy young groom, about twenty or twenty-one, who knows his business.
passages.vernacular: 佢要我畀佢找一個可靠嘅年輕馬夫,大約二十或二十一歲,懂行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要我給他找一個可靠的年輕馬夫,大約二十或二十一歲,懂行。

passages.original: His old coachman, who has lived with him thirty years, is getting feeble, and he wants a man to work with him and get into his ways, who would be able, when the old man was pensioned off, to step into his place.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅老車夫喺佢嗰度待咗三十年,漸漸衰弱喇,佢想要一個人同佢一起工作,熟悉佢嘅做法,等老人領退休金後,能夠接替佢嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的老車夫在他那裡待了三十年,漸漸衰弱了,他想要一個人與他一起工作,熟悉他的做法,等老人領退休金後,能夠接替他的位置。

passages.original: He would have eighteen shillings a week at first, a stable suit, a driving suit, a bedroom over the coachhouse, and a boy under him.
passages.vernacular: 開始時佢每週有十八先令,一套馬廄制服、一套駕車制服、一間馬車房上面嘅臥室,仲有一個手下嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 開始時他每週有十八先令,一套馬廄制服、一套駕車制服、一間馬車房上面的臥室,還有一個手下的男孩。

passages.original: Sir Clifford is a good master, and if you could get the place it would be a good start for you.
passages.vernacular: 克利福德爵士係個好主人,如果你能得到呢個位置,對你係個好嘅開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 克利福德爵士是個好主人,如果你能得到這個位置,對你是個好的開始。

passages.original: I don't want to part with you, and if you left us I know John would lose his right hand.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔想讓你走,如果你離開我哋,我知道約翰會失去佢嘅右手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想讓你走,如果你離開我們,我知道約翰會失去他的右手。」

passages.original: “That I should, sir,” said John, “but I would not stand in his light for the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「確實會,先生,」約翰講,「但我無論如何唔會擋佢嘅路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實會,先生,」約翰說,「但我無論如何不會擋他的路。」

passages.original: “How old are you, James?” said master.
passages.vernacular: 「你多大喇,詹姆斯?」主人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你多大了,詹姆斯?」主人說。

passages.original: “Nineteen next May, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「明年五月滿十九,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明年五月滿十九,先生。」

passages.original: “That's young; what do you think, John?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲年輕;你點睇,約翰?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還年輕;你怎麼看,約翰?」

passages.original: “Well, sir, it is young; but he is as steady as a man, and is strong, and well grown, and though he has not had much experience in driving, he has a light firm hand and a quick eye, and he is very careful, and I am quite sure no horse of his will be ruined for want of having his feet and shoes looked after.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,先生,係年輕;但佢像大人一樣沉穩,強壯,長得好,雖然佢駕車嘅經驗不多,但佢有一雙輕而穩嘅手同一雙敏銳嘅眼睛,而且佢好細心,我完全肯定佢嘅馬唔會因為冇照睇蹄子同蹄鐵而被毀掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,先生,是年輕;但他像大人一樣沉穩,強壯,長得好,雖然他駕車的經驗不多,但他有一雙輕而穩的手和一雙敏銳的眼睛,而且他非常細心,我完全肯定他的馬不會因為沒有照看蹄子和蹄鐵而被毀掉。」

passages.original: “Your word will go the furthest, John,” said the master, “for Sir Clifford adds in a postscript, 'If I could find a man trained by your John I should like him better than any other;' so, James, lad, think it over, talk to your mother at dinner-time, and then let me know what you wish.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅話最有分量,約翰,」主人講,「因為克利福德爵士喺附言裡講:『如果我能找到一個你嘅約翰訓練出嚟嘅人,我會比其他任何人都更鍾意佢;』所以,詹姆斯,細路,好好想想,午飯時同你母親談談,然後讓我知道你嘅意願。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的話最有分量,約翰,」主人說,「因為克利福德爵士在附言裡說:『如果我能找到一個你的約翰訓練出來的人,我會比其他任何人都更喜歡他;』所以,詹姆斯,孩子,好好想想,午飯時同你母親談談,然後讓我知道你的意願。」

passages.original: In a few days after this conversation it was fully settled that James should go to Clifford Hall, in a month or six weeks, as it suited his master, and in the meantime he was to get all the practice in driving that could be given to him.
passages.vernacular: 呢次談話幾天後,事情完全定下嚟,詹姆斯將喺一個月或六週後,視佢主人方便,去克利福德莊園,喺此期間佢要盡可能多地練習駕車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次談話幾天後,事情完全定下來,詹姆斯將在一個月或六週後,視他主人方便,去克利福德莊園,在此期間他要盡可能多地練習駕車。

passages.original: I never knew the carriage to go out so often before; when the mistress did not go out the master drove himself in the two-wheeled chaise; but now, whether it was master or the young ladies, or only an errand, Ginger and I were put in the carriage and James drove us.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過馬車咁頻繁地出去;女主人不出門時,主人就自己駕嗰輛兩輪馬車;可而家,不管係主人定係年輕小姐哋,或者只係跑腿,金姐同我都被套進馬車,由詹姆斯駕駛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過馬車這麼頻繁地出去;女主人不出門時,主人就自己駕那輛兩輪馬車;可現在,不管是主人還是年輕小姐們,或者只是跑腿,金姐和我都被套進馬車,由詹姆斯駕駛。

passages.original: At the first John rode with him on the box, telling him this and that, and after that James drove alone.
passages.vernacular: 起初約翰同佢一起坐喺車座上,告訴佢呢個嗰個,之後詹姆斯就自己駕車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初約翰同他一起坐在車座上,告訴他這個那個,之後詹姆斯就自己駕車。

passages.original: Then it was wonderful what a number of places the master would go to in the city on Saturday, and what queer streets we were driven through.
passages.vernacular: 然後奇怪嘅係,主人星期六要去城裡嘅咁多地方,我哋被駕住穿過咁多古怪嘅街道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後奇怪的是,主人星期六要去城裡的那麼多地方,我們被駕著穿過那麼多古怪的街道。

passages.original: He was sure to go to the railway station just as the train was coming in, and cabs and carriages, carts and omnibuses were all trying to get over the bridge together; that bridge wanted good horses and good drivers when the railway bell was ringing, for it was narrow, and there was a very sharp turn up to the station, where it would not have been at all difficult for people to run into each other, if they did not look sharp and keep their wits about them.
passages.vernacular: 佢肯定要喺火車進站嘅時候去火車站,出租馬車同轎車、貨車同公共馬車都想一起過橋;鐵路鈴聲響起時,嗰座橋需要好馬同好車夫,因為佢好窄,通往車站有一個好急嘅彎,如果人哋不留神、不保持頭腦清醒,好容易撞喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他肯定要在火車進站的時候去火車站,出租馬車和轎車、貨車和公共馬車都想一起過橋;鐵路鈴聲響起時,那座橋需要好馬和好車夫,因為它很窄,通往車站有一個非常急的彎,如果人們不留神、不保持頭腦清醒,很容易撞在一起。

chapters.title: Part I · 15 The Old Hostler 第一部·15 老馬夫

passages.original: CH After this it was decided by my master and mistress to pay a visit to some friends who lived about forty-six miles from our home, and James was to drive them.
passages.vernacular: 此後我嘅主人同女主人決定去拜訪啲朋友,佢哋住喺離我哋家約四十六英里嘅地方,詹姆斯駕車載佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後我的主人和女主人決定去拜訪一些朋友,他們住在離我們家約四十六英里的地方,詹姆斯駕車載他們。

passages.original: The first day we traveled thirty-two miles.
passages.vernacular: 第一天我哋走咗三十二英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一天我們走了三十二英里。

passages.original: There were some long, heavy hills, but James drove so carefully and thoughtfully that we were not at all harassed.
passages.vernacular: 有幾座又長又陡嘅山,但詹姆斯駕得咁小心周到,我哋啲都不勞累。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾座又長又陡的山,但詹姆斯駕得那麼小心周到,我們一點也不勞累。

passages.original: He never forgot to put on the brake as we went downhill, nor to take it off at the right place.
passages.vernacular: 我哋下坡時佢從不忘記踩上剎車,都不忘記喺適當嘅地方鬆開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們下坡時他從不忘記踩上剎車,也不忘記在適當的地方鬆開。

passages.original: He kept our feet on the smoothest part of the road, and if the uphill was very long, he set the carriage wheels a little across the road, so as not to run back, and gave us a breathing.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我哋嘅蹄子走喺路最平整嘅部分,如果上坡好長,佢就讓馬車輪子稍微橫喺路上,以免倒退,並讓我哋喘口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他讓我們的蹄子走在路最平整的部分,如果上坡很長,他就讓馬車輪子稍微橫在路上,以免倒退,並讓我們喘口氣。

passages.original: All these little things help a horse very much, particularly if he gets kind words into the bargain.
passages.vernacular: 所有呢啲小事都對馬有好大幫助,尤其係再加上幾句好話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些小事都對馬有很大幫助,尤其是再加上幾句好話。

passages.original: We stopped once or twice on the road, and just as the sun was going down we reached the town where we were to spend the night.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺路上停咗一兩次,就喺太陽落山時,我哋到咗要過夜嘅城鎮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在路上停了一兩次,就在太陽落山時,我們到了要過夜的城鎮。

passages.original: We stopped at the principal hotel, which was in the market-place; it was a very large one; we drove under an archway into a long yard, at the further end of which were the stables and coachhouses.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺主要嘅旅館停下,佢喺市場廣場上;好大;我哋駕車穿過一個拱門,進入一個長院子,盡頭係馬廄同馬車房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在主要的旅館停下,它在市場廣場上;非常大;我們駕車穿過一個拱門,進入一個長院子,盡頭是馬廄和馬車房。

passages.original: Two hostlers came to take us out.
passages.vernacular: 兩個馬夫嚟牽我哋出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個馬夫來牽我們出去。

passages.original: The head hostler was a pleasant, active little man, with a crooked leg, and a yellow striped waistcoat.
passages.vernacular: 首席馬夫係個愉快、活躍嘅小個子,一條腿彎曲,穿住黃條紋背心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首席馬夫是個愉快、活躍的小個子,一條腿彎曲,穿著黃條紋背心。

passages.original: I never saw a man unbuckle harness so quickly as he did, and with a pat and a good word he led me to a long stable, with six or eight stalls in it, and two or three horses.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過邊個解挽具像佢咁快,佢拍住我,講住好話,把我領到一個長馬廄,裡面有六到八個馬棚,有兩三匹馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過誰解挽具像他那麼快,他拍著我,說著好話,把我領到一個長馬廄,裡面有六到八個馬棚,有兩三匹馬。

passages.original: The other man brought Ginger; James stood by while we were rubbed down and cleaned.
passages.vernacular: 另一個人帶嚟金姐;我哋被擦洗乾淨時,詹姆斯站喺一旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個人帶來金姐;我們被擦洗乾淨時,詹姆斯站在一旁。

passages.original: I never was cleaned so lightly and quickly as by that little old man.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇被嗰個小老頭嗰樣輕巧迅速地擦洗過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒被那個小老頭那樣輕巧迅速地擦洗過。

passages.original: When he had done James stepped up and felt me over, as if he thought I could not be thoroughly done, but he found my coat as clean and smooth as silk.
passages.vernacular: 佢擦完後,詹姆斯走上嚟,把我摸咗一遍,好像覺得我唔可能擦洗得徹底,但佢發現我嘅皮毛像絲一樣乾淨光滑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他擦完後,詹姆斯走上來,把我摸了一遍,好像覺得我不可能擦洗得徹底,但他發現我的皮毛像絲一樣乾淨光滑。

passages.original: “Well,” he said, “I thought I was pretty quick, and our John quicker still, but you do beat all I ever saw for being quick and thorough at the same time.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」佢講,「我以為我好快,我哋嘅約翰更快,但你確實超過我見過嘅所有人,既快又徹底。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」他說,「我以為我很快,我們的約翰更快,但你確實超過我見過的所有人,既快又徹底。」

passages.original: “Practice makes perfect,” said the crooked little hostler, “and 'twould be a pity if it didn't; forty years' practice, and not perfect! ha, ha! that would be a pity; and as to being quick, why, bless you! that is only a matter of habit; if you get into the habit of being quick it is just as easy as being slow; easier, I should say; in fact it don't agree with my health to be hulking about over a job twice as long as it need take.
passages.vernacular: 「熟能生巧,」彎腿嘅小馬夫講,「要係唔能夠就可惜喇;四十年嘅練習,仲不完美!哈哈!嗰就可惜喇;至於快,哎呀,保佑你!嗰只係習慣問題;如果你養成咗快嘅習慣,就同慢一樣容易;我該講更容易;事實上,把一件活拖得比需要嘅長一倍,對我嘅健康不合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「熟能生巧,」彎腿的小馬夫說,「要是不能就可惜了;四十年的練習,還不完美!哈哈!那就可惜了;至於快,哎呀,保佑你!那只是習慣問題;如果你養成了快的習慣,就和慢一樣容易;我該說更容易;事實上,把一件活拖得比需要的長一倍,對我的健康不合適。

passages.original: Bless you!
passages.vernacular: 保佑你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你!

passages.original: I couldn't whistle if I crawled over my work as some folks do!
passages.vernacular: 如果我像有些人嗰樣慢吞吞地爬住幹活,我連口哨都吹不響!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我像有些人那樣慢吞吞地爬著幹活,我連口哨都吹不響!

passages.original: You see, I have been about horses ever since I was twelve years old, in hunting stables, and racing stables; and being small, ye see, I was jockey for several years; but at the Goodwood, ye see, the turf was very slippery and my poor Larkspur got a fall, and I broke my knee, and so of course I was of no more use there.
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,我從十二歲起就跟馬打交道,喺獵場馬廄,賽馬馬廄;因為我個子小,你瞧,好幾年我當騎師;但喺古德伍德,你瞧,草皮好滑,我可憐嘅雲雀摔倒喇,我摔斷咗膝蓋,於是當然喺嗰度就冇用喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,我從十二歲起就跟馬打交道,在獵場馬廄,賽馬馬廄;因為我個子小,你瞧,好幾年我當騎師;但在古德伍德,你瞧,草皮非常滑,我可憐的雲雀摔倒了,我摔斷了膝蓋,於是當然在那裡就沒用了。

passages.original: But I could not live without horses, of course I couldn't, so I took to the hotels.
passages.vernacular: 不過我離不開馬,當然離不開,所以我轉到旅館嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我離不開馬,當然離不開,所以我轉到旅館來了。

passages.original: And I can tell ye it is a downright pleasure to handle an animal like this, well-bred, well-mannered, well-cared-for; bless ye!
passages.vernacular: 我可以告訴你,侍弄像咁樣嘅牲口,血統好、禮貌好、照顧得好,真係徹頭徹尾嘅快樂;保佑你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以告訴你,侍弄像這樣的牲口,血統好、禮貌好、照顧得好,真是徹頭徹尾的快樂;保佑你!

passages.original: I can tell how a horse is treated.
passages.vernacular: 我能睇出一匹馬係點被對待嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能看出一匹馬是怎麼被對待的。

passages.original: Give me the handling of a horse for twenty minutes, and I'll tell you what sort of a groom he has had.
passages.vernacular: 讓我侍弄一匹馬二好鐘,我就能告訴你佢有過乜嘢樣嘅馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我侍弄一匹馬二十分鐘,我就能告訴你它有過什麼樣的馬夫。

passages.original: Look at this one, pleasant, quiet, turns about just as you want him, holds up his feet to be cleaned out, or anything else you please to wish; then you'll find another fidgety, fretty, won't move the right way, or starts across the stall, tosses up his head as soon as you come near him, lays his ears, and seems afraid of you; or else squares about at you with his heels.
passages.vernacular: 睇呢一匹,愉快,安靜,你要佢點轉就點轉,抬起蹄子讓你清理,或者你願意嘅任何事;然後你會發現另一匹,煩躁,易怒,唔肯往對嘅方向動,或者橫住衝過馬棚,你一走近就甩頭,貼住耳朵,好像怕你;或者用後蹄對住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看這一匹,愉快,安靜,你要他怎麼轉就怎麼轉,抬起蹄子讓你清理,或者你願意的任何事;然後你會發現另一匹,煩躁,易怒,不肯往對的方向動,或者橫著衝過馬棚,你一走近就甩頭,貼著耳朵,好像怕你;或者用後蹄對著你。

passages.original: Poor things!
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的東西!

passages.original: I know what sort of treatment they have had.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢哋受過乜嘢樣嘅對待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道它們受過什麼樣的對待。

passages.original: If they are timid it makes them start or shy; if they are high-mettled it makes them vicious or dangerous; their tempers are mostly made when they are young.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋膽小,呢使佢哋驚跳或躲閃;如果佢哋性子烈,呢使佢哋凶狠或危險;佢哋嘅脾氣大多係年輕時形成嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它們膽小,這使它們驚跳或躲閃;如果它們性子烈,這使它們凶狠或危險;它們的脾氣大多是年輕時形成的。

passages.original: Bless you! they are like children, train 'em up in the way they should go, as the good book says, and when they are old they will not depart from it, if they have a chance.”
passages.vernacular: 保佑你!佢哋像細路,按好書所講,把佢哋培養喺該走嘅路上,等佢哋老咗就唔會偏離,如果佢哋有機會嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保佑你!它們像孩子,按好書所說,把它們培養在該走的路上,等它們老了就不會偏離,如果它們有機會的話。」

passages.original: “I like to hear you talk,” said James, “that's the way we lay it down at home, at our master's.”
passages.vernacular: 「我愛聽你講話,」詹姆斯講,「我哋喺家,喺我哋主人嗰度,就係咁樣定規矩嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛聽你說話,」詹姆斯說,「我們在家,在我們主人那裡,就是這樣定規矩的。」

passages.original: “Who is your master, young man? if it be a proper question.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅主人係邊個,年輕人?如果呢個係個得當嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的主人是誰,年輕人?如果這是個得當的問題。

passages.original: I should judge he is a good one, from what I see.”
passages.vernacular: 從我所見,我判斷佢係個好主人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我所見,我判斷他是個好主人。」

passages.original: “He is Squire Gordon, of Birtwick Park, the other side the Beacon Hills,” said James.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係伯特威克莊園嘅戈登鄉紳,喺燈塔山嘅另一邊,」詹姆斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是伯特威克莊園的戈登鄉紳,在燈塔山的另一邊,」詹姆斯說。

passages.original: “Ah! so, so, I have heard tell of him; fine judge of horses, ain't he? the best rider in the county.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!咁樣,咁樣,我聽講過佢;馬嘅好行家,唔係嗎?全郡最好嘅騎手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!這樣,這樣,我聽說過他;馬的好行家,不是嗎?全郡最好的騎手。」

passages.original: “I believe he is,” said James, “but he rides very little now, since the poor young master was killed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我相信係,」詹姆斯講,「但自從可憐嘅少爺被殺之後,佢而家騎得好少喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信是,」詹姆斯說,「但自從可憐的少爺被殺之後,他現在騎得很少了。」

passages.original: “Ah! poor gentleman; I read all about it in the paper at the time.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!可憐嘅先生;我當時喺報紙上讀到咗全部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!可憐的先生;我當時在報紙上讀到了全部。

passages.original: A fine horse killed, too, wasn't there?”
passages.vernacular: 一匹好馬都被殺喇,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一匹好馬也被殺了,是不是?」

passages.original: “Yes,” said James; “he was a splendid creature, brother to this one, and just like him.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」詹姆斯講;「嗰個係匹出色嘅生靈,係呢一匹嘅哥哥,跟佢一模一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」詹姆斯說;「那是匹出色的生靈,是這一匹的哥哥,跟他一模一樣。」

passages.original: “Pity! pity!” said the old man; “'twas a bad place to leap, if I remember; a thin fence at top, a steep bank down to the stream, wasn't it?
passages.vernacular: 「可惜!可惜!」老人講;「如果我冇記錯嘅話,嗰個係個好壞嘅跳躍地點;頂上一道薄籬笆,下面一道陡堤直通溪流,唔係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可惜!可惜!」老人說;「如果我沒記錯的話,那是個很壞的跳躍地點;頂上一道薄籬笆,下面一道陡堤直通溪流,不是嗎?

passages.original: No chance for a horse to see where he is going.
passages.vernacular: 馬冇機會睇到自己往邊度去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬沒有機會看到自己往哪裡去。

passages.original: Now, I am for bold riding as much as any man, but still there are some leaps that only a very knowing old huntsman has any right to take.
passages.vernacular: 我同任何人一樣主張勇敢騎行,但係有些跳躍只有好有經驗嘅老獵手才有權去跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和任何人一樣主張勇敢騎行,但是有些跳躍只有很有經驗的老獵手才有權去跳。

passages.original: A man's life and a horse's life are worth more than a fox's tail; at least, I should say they ought to be.”
passages.vernacular: 一個人嘅命同一匹馬嘅命比一條狐狸尾巴更值錢;至少我該講佢哋應當如此。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人的命和一匹馬的命比一條狐狸尾巴更值錢;至少我該說它們應當如此。」

passages.original: During this time the other man had finished Ginger and had brought our corn, and James and the old man left the stable together.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣另一個人已經弄完咗金姐,送嚟咗我哋嘅穀物,詹姆斯同老人一起離開咗馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時另一個人已經弄完了金姐,送來了我們的穀物,詹姆斯和老人一起離開了馬廄。

chapters.title: Part I · 16 The Fire 第一部·16 火災

passages.original: CH Later on in the evening a traveler's horse was brought in by the second hostler, and while he was cleaning him a young man with a pipe in his mouth lounged into the stable to gossip.
passages.vernacular: 晚上稍後,第二個馬夫牽進咗一位旅客嘅馬,佢畀佢刷洗時,一個嘴裡叼住煙斗嘅年輕人懶洋洋地走進馬廄嚟閒聊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚上稍後,第二個馬夫牽進了一位旅客的馬,他給它刷洗時,一個嘴裡叼著煙斗的年輕人懶洋洋地走進馬廄來閒聊。

passages.original: “I say, Towler,” said the hostler, “just run up the ladder into the loft and put some hay down into this horse's rack, will you? only lay down your pipe.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,托勒,」馬夫講,「爬梯子上閣樓,畀呢匹馬嘅草架放點乾草,好嗎?只要放下你嘅煙斗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,托勒,」馬夫說,「爬梯子上閣樓,給這匹馬的草架放點乾草,好嗎?只要放下你的煙斗。」

passages.original: “All right,” said the other, and went up through the trapdoor; and I heard him step across the floor overhead and put down the hay.
passages.vernacular: 「好,」另一個講,從活板門上去喇;我聽見佢喺頭頂嘅地板上走過,放下乾草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」另一個說,從活板門上去了;我聽見他在頭頂的地板上走過,放下乾草。

passages.original: James came in to look at us the last thing, and then the door was locked.
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯最後進嚟睇我哋,然後門就被鎖上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯最後進來看我們,然後門就被鎖上了。

passages.original: I cannot say how long I had slept, nor what time in the night it was, but I woke up very uncomfortable, though I hardly knew why.
passages.vernacular: 我講不上瞓咗多久,都唔知道係夜裡乜嘢時候,但我醒嚟時好不舒服,雖然我幾乎唔知道點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不上睡了多久,也不知道是夜裡什麼時候,但我醒來時非常不舒服,雖然我幾乎不知道為什麼。

passages.original: I got up; the air seemed all thick and choking.
passages.vernacular: 我站起嚟;空氣好像又濃又悶人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站起來;空氣好像又濃又悶人。

passages.original: I heard Ginger coughing and one of the other horses seemed very restless; it was quite dark, and I could see nothing, but the stable seemed full of smoke, and I hardly knew how to breathe.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見金姐喺咳嗽,另一匹馬似乎好不安;一片漆黑,我乜嘢都睇唔見,但馬廄好像充滿咗煙,我幾乎唔知點呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見金姐在咳嗽,另一匹馬似乎非常不安;一片漆黑,我什麼也看不見,但馬廄好像充滿了煙,我幾乎不知怎麼呼吸。

passages.original: The trapdoor had been left open, and I thought that was the place it came through.
passages.vernacular: 活板門一直開住,我想煙就係從嗰度進嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 活板門一直開著,我想煙就是從那裡進來的。

passages.original: I listened, and heard a soft rushing sort of noise and a low crackling and snapping.
passages.vernacular: 我聽住,聽到一種輕輕嘅呼呼聲,同低低嘅劈啪聲、爆裂聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽著,聽到一種輕輕的呼呼聲,和低低的劈啪聲、爆裂聲。

passages.original: I did not know what it was, but there was something in the sound so strange that it made me tremble all over.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道嗰個係乜嘢,但嗰聲音裡有乜嘢嘢咁奇怪,讓我渾身發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道那是什麼,但那聲音裡有什麼東西那麼奇怪,讓我渾身發抖。

passages.original: The other horses were all awake; some were pulling at their halters, others stamping.
passages.vernacular: 其他嘅馬都醒喇;有嘅喺拽籠頭,有嘅喺跺腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他的馬都醒了;有的在拽籠頭,有的在跺腳。

passages.original: At last I heard steps outside, and the hostler who had put up the traveler's horse burst into the stable with a lantern, and began to untie the horses, and try to lead them out; but he seemed in such a hurry and so frightened himself that he frightened me still more.
passages.vernacular: 最後我聽見外面有腳步聲,放旅客馬嘅馬夫提住燈籠闖進馬廄,開始解馬,想把佢哋牽出去;但佢似乎咁匆忙,自己都咁害怕,佢把我嚇得更厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後我聽見外面有腳步聲,放旅客馬的馬夫提著燈籠闖進馬廄,開始解馬,想把它們牽出去;但他似乎那麼匆忙,自己也那麼害怕,他把我嚇得更厲害。

passages.original: The first horse would not go with him; he tried the second and third, and they too would not stir.
passages.vernacular: 第一匹馬唔肯跟佢走;佢試咗第二匹同第三匹,佢哋都一動不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一匹馬不肯跟他走;他試了第二匹和第三匹,它們也一動不動。

passages.original: He came to me next and tried to drag me out of the stall by force; of course that was no use.
passages.vernacular: 佢接住嚟到我呢兒,試圖用力把我拖出馬棚;當然嗰冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他接著來到我這兒,試圖用力把我拖出馬棚;當然那沒用。

passages.original: He tried us all by turns and then left the stable.
passages.vernacular: 佢輪流試咗我哋所有嘅馬,然後離開咗馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他輪流試了我們所有的馬,然後離開了馬廄。

passages.original: No doubt we were very foolish, but danger seemed to be all round, and there was nobody we knew to trust in, and all was strange and uncertain.
passages.vernacular: 毫無疑問我哋好愚蠢,但危險似乎喺四周,冇一個我哋認識嘅人可以信賴,一切都陌生而不確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毫無疑問我們非常愚蠢,但危險似乎在四周,沒有一個我們認識的人可以信賴,一切都陌生而不確定。

passages.original: The fresh air that had come in through the open door made it easier to breathe, but the rushing sound overhead grew louder, and as I looked upward through the bars of my empty rack I saw a red light flickering on the wall.
passages.vernacular: 通過敞開嘅門進嚟嘅新鮮空氣使呼吸容易咗些,但頭頂嘅呼呼聲變大喇,我透過空草架嘅欄杆向上睇時,睇到牆上閃爍住一道紅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通過敞開的門進來的新鮮空氣使呼吸容易了些,但頭頂的呼呼聲變大了,我透過空草架的欄杆向上看時,看到牆上閃爍著一道紅光。

passages.original: Then I heard a cry of “Fire!” outside, and the old hostler quietly and quickly came in; he got one horse out, and went to another, but the flames were playing round the trapdoor, and the roaring overhead was dreadful.
passages.vernacular: 然後我聽到外面有人喊「住火喇!」,老馬夫安靜而迅速地走進嚟;佢牽出一匹馬,又走向另一匹,可火焰正在活板門周圍舞動,頭頂嘅轟鳴聲好可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我聽到外面有人喊「著火了!」,老馬夫安靜而迅速地走進來;他牽出一匹馬,又走向另一匹,可火焰正在活板門周圍舞動,頭頂的轟鳴聲很可怕。

passages.original: The next thing I heard was James' voice, quiet and cheery, as it always was.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟我聽到嘅係詹姆斯嘅聲音,安靜愉快,同往常一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來我聽到的是詹姆斯的聲音,安靜愉快,和往常一樣。

passages.original: “Come, my beauties, it is time for us to be off, so wake up and come along.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,我嘅寶貝哋,係我哋該走嘅時候喇,所以醒醒,跟我嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,我的寶貝們,是我們該走的時候了,所以醒醒,跟我來。」

passages.original: I stood nearest the door, so he came to me first, patting me as he came in.
passages.vernacular: 我站得離門最近,所以佢先嚟到我呢兒,進嚟時拍住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站得離門最近,所以他先來到我這兒,進來時拍著我。

passages.original: “Come, Beauty, on with your bridle, my boy, we'll soon be out of this smother.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,神駒,套上你嘅轡頭,細路,我哋好快就會離開呢濃煙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,神駒,套上你的轡頭,孩子,我們很快就會離開這濃煙。」

passages.original: It was on in no time; then he took the scarf off his neck, and tied it lightly over my eyes, and patting and coaxing he led me out of the stable.
passages.vernacular: 轡頭轉眼就套好喇;然後佢解下脖子上嘅圍巾,輕輕蒙喺我嘅眼睛上,一邊拍住、哄住,把我領出咗馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轡頭轉眼就套好了;然後他解下脖子上的圍巾,輕輕蒙在我的眼睛上,一邊拍著、哄著,把我領出了馬廄。

passages.original: Safe in the yard, he slipped the scarf off my eyes, and shouted, “Here somebody! take this horse while I go back for the other.”
passages.vernacular: 喺院子裡安全喇,佢從我眼睛上攞下圍巾,喊道:「呢度邊個嚟牽呢匹馬!我回去帶另一匹。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在院子裡安全了,他從我眼睛上拿下圍巾,喊道:「這裡誰來牽這匹馬!我回去帶另一匹。」

passages.original: A tall, broad man stepped forward and took me, and James darted back into the stable.
passages.vernacular: 一個又高又壯嘅人走上前嚟牽住我,詹姆斯飛快地跑回馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個又高又壯的人走上前來牽住我,詹姆斯飛快地跑回馬廄。

passages.original: I set up a shrill whinny as I saw him go.
passages.vernacular: 我睇佢走喇,發出一聲尖銳嘅嘶鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看他走了,發出一聲尖銳的嘶鳴。

passages.original: Ginger told me afterward that whinny was the best thing I could have done for her, for had she not heard me outside she would never have had courage to come out.
passages.vernacular: 金姐後來告訴我,嗰聲嘶鳴係我能為佢做嘅最好嘅事,因為如果佢冇聽到我喺外面,佢永遠冇勇氣出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 金姐後來告訴我,那聲嘶鳴是我能為她做的最好的事,因為如果她沒聽到我在外面,她永遠沒有勇氣出來。

passages.original: There was much confusion in the yard; the horses being got out of other stables, and the carriages and gigs being pulled out of houses and sheds, lest the flames should spread further.
passages.vernacular: 院子裡一片混亂;馬被從其他馬廄牽出嚟,馬車同輕便馬車被從屋棚裡拖出嚟,以免火焰蔓延得更遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 院子裡一片混亂;馬被從其他馬廄牽出來,馬車和輕便馬車被從屋棚裡拖出來,以免火焰蔓延得更遠。

passages.original: On the other side the yard windows were thrown up, and people were shouting all sorts of things; but I kept my eye fixed on the stable door, where the smoke poured out thicker than ever, and I could see flashes of red light; presently I heard above all the stir and din a loud, clear voice, which I knew was master's:
passages.vernacular: 院子另一邊嘅窗子被推開,人哋喊住各種各樣嘅話;但我嘅眼睛始終盯住馬廄門,煙冒得比以往任何時候都濃,我能睇到閃爍嘅紅光;不一會兒,我喺所有嘅騷動同喧嚷中聽到一個響亮清晰嘅聲音,我知道係主人嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 院子另一邊的窗子被推開,人們喊著各種各樣的話;但我的眼睛始終盯著馬廄門,煙冒得比以往任何時候都濃,我能看到閃爍的紅光;不一會兒,我在所有的騷動和喧嚷中聽到一個響亮清晰的聲音,我知道是主人的:

passages.original: “James Howard!
passages.vernacular: 「詹姆斯·霍華德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「詹姆斯·霍華德!

passages.original: James Howard!
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯·霍華德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯·霍華德!

passages.original: Are you there?”
passages.vernacular: 你喺嗰度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在那裡嗎?」

passages.original: There was no answer, but I heard a crash of something falling in the stable, and the next moment I gave a loud, joyful neigh, for I saw James coming through the smoke leading Ginger with him; she was coughing violently, and he was not able to speak.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答,但我聽見馬廄裡有乜嘢嘢倒塌嘅響聲,下一刻我發出一聲響亮歡快嘅嘶鳴,因為我睇見詹姆斯穿過煙霧,領住金姐出嚟;佢喺劇烈地咳嗽,佢講不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答,但我聽見馬廄裡有什麼東西倒塌的響聲,下一刻我發出一聲響亮歡快的嘶鳴,因為我看見詹姆斯穿過煙霧,領著金姐出來;她在劇烈地咳嗽,他說不出話。

passages.original: “My brave lad!” said master, laying his hand on his shoulder, “are you hurt?”
passages.vernacular: 「我勇敢嘅細路!」主人把手放喺佢肩上講,「你受傷咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我勇敢的孩子!」主人把手放在他肩上說,「你受傷了嗎?」

passages.original: James shook his head, for he could not yet speak.
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯搖搖頭,因為佢仲講不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯搖搖頭,因為他還說不出話。

passages.original: “Ay,” said the big man who held me; “he is a brave lad, and no mistake.”
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,」牽住我嘅大個子講;「佢係個勇敢嘅細路,冇錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,」牽著我的大個子說;「他是個勇敢的孩子,沒錯。」

passages.original: “And now,” said master, “when you have got your breath, James, we'll get out of this place as quickly as we can,” and we were moving toward the entry, when from the market-place there came a sound of galloping feet and loud rumbling wheels.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,」主人講,「等你喘過氣嚟,詹姆斯,我哋就盡快離開呢個地方,」我哋正朝入口走去,呢陣從市場廣場傳嚟馬蹄飛奔同車輪隆隆嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,」主人說,「等你喘過氣來,詹姆斯,我們就盡快離開這個地方,」我們正朝入口走去,這時從市場廣場傳來馬蹄飛奔和車輪隆隆的聲音。

passages.original: “'Tis the fire-engine! the fire-engine!” shouted two or three voices, “stand back, make way!” and clattering and thundering over the stones two horses dashed into the yard with a heavy engine behind them.
passages.vernacular: 「係消防車!消防車!」兩三個聲音喊道,「讓開,讓路!」兩匹馬拉住一輛沉重嘅救火車,喺石頭路上哐啷哐啷、雷鳴般衝進咗院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是消防車!消防車!」兩三個聲音喊道,「讓開,讓路!」兩匹馬拉著一輛沉重的救火車,在石頭路上哐啷哐啷、雷鳴般衝進了院子。

passages.original: The firemen leaped to the ground; there was no need to ask where the fire was--it was rolling up in a great blaze from the roof.
passages.vernacular: 消防員跳到地上;唔使問火喺邊度——佢正從屋頂上滾滾地冒起一大團火焰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消防員跳到地上;不用問火在哪裡——它正從屋頂上滾滾地冒起一大團火焰。

passages.original: We got out as fast as we could into the broad quiet market-place; the stars were shining, and except the noise behind us, all was still.
passages.vernacular: 我哋盡快出嚟,到咗寬闊安靜嘅市場廣場;星星喺閃耀,除咗我哋身後嘅喧鬧,一切都靜悄悄嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們盡快出來,到了寬闊安靜的市場廣場;星星在閃耀,除了我們身後的喧鬧,一切都靜悄悄的。

passages.original: Master led the way to a large hotel on the other side, and as soon as the hostler came, he said, “James, I must now hasten to your mistress; I trust the horses entirely to you, order whatever you think is needed,” and with that he was gone.
passages.vernacular: 主人領頭走向對面嘅一家大旅館,馬夫一來,佢就講:「詹姆斯,我而家必須趕去見你嘅女主人;我完全把馬託付畀你,你認為需要乜嘢就吩咐乜嘢,」講完佢就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主人領頭走向對面的一家大旅館,馬夫一來,他就說:「詹姆斯,我現在必須趕去見你的女主人;我完全把馬託付給你,你認為需要什麼就吩咐什麼,」說完他就走了。

passages.original: The master did not run, but I never saw mortal man walk so fast as he did that night.
passages.vernacular: 主人冇跑,但我從冇見過邊個凡人走得像佢嗰晚咁快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主人沒有跑,但我從沒見過哪個凡人走得像他那晚那麼快。

passages.original: There was a dreadful sound before we got into our stalls--the shrieks of those poor horses that were left burning to death in the stable--it was very terrible! and made both Ginger and me feel very bad.
passages.vernacular: 我哋進馬棚之前傳嚟一種可怕嘅聲音——嗰啲被留喺馬廄裡活活燒死嘅可憐馬嘅尖叫——太可怕喇!讓金姐同我都好難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們進馬棚之前傳來一種可怕的聲音——那些被留在馬廄裡活活燒死的可憐馬的尖叫——太可怕了!讓金姐和我都很難受。

passages.original: We, however, were taken in and well done by.
passages.vernacular: 不過我哋被接咗進去,受到好好嘅照顧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我們被接了進去,受到很好的照顧。

passages.original: The next morning the master came to see how we were and to speak to James.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,主人嚟睇我哋點樣,並同詹姆斯講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,主人來看我們怎麼樣,並同詹姆斯說話。

passages.original: I did not hear much, for the hostler was rubbing me down, but I could see that James looked very happy, and I thought the master was proud of him.
passages.vernacular: 我冇聽到多少,因為馬夫喺畀我擦洗,但我能睇出詹姆斯好高興,我想主人以佢為榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒聽到多少,因為馬夫在給我擦洗,但我能看出詹姆斯非常高興,我想主人以他為榮。

passages.original: Our mistress had been so much alarmed in the night that the journey was put off till the afternoon, so James had the morning on hand, and went first to the inn to see about our harness and the carriage, and then to hear more about the fire.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅女主人夜裡受咗咁大嘅驚嚇,旅程推遲到下午,所以詹姆斯早晨有空,先去客棧睇我哋嘅挽具同馬車,然後去多聽啲關於火災嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的女主人夜裡受了那麼大的驚嚇,旅程推遲到下午,所以詹姆斯早晨有空,先去客棧看我們的挽具和馬車,然後去多聽一些關於火災的事。

passages.original: When he came back we heard him tell the hostler about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢回嚟時,我哋聽到佢告訴馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回來時,我們聽到他告訴馬夫。

passages.original: At first no one could guess how the fire had been caused, but at last a man said he saw Dick Towler go into the stable with a pipe in his mouth, and when he came out he had not one, and went to the tap for another.
passages.vernacular: 起初冇人能猜出火係點起嘅,但最後有個人講佢睇見迪克·托勒嘴裡叼住煙斗走進馬廄,出嚟時冇煙斗,又去酒吧另攞咗一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初沒人能猜出火是怎麼起的,但最後有個人說他看見迪克·托勒嘴裡叼著煙斗走進馬廄,出來時沒有煙斗,又去酒吧另拿了一個。

passages.original: Then the under hostler said he had asked Dick to go up the ladder to put down some hay, but told him to lay down his pipe first.
passages.vernacular: 然後下面嘅馬夫講佢叫迪克爬梯子去放乾草,但叫佢先放下煙斗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後下面的馬夫說他叫迪克爬梯子去放乾草,但叫他先放下煙斗。

passages.original: Dick denied taking the pipe with him, but no one believed him.
passages.vernacular: 迪克否認帶咗煙斗,但冇人相信佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 迪克否認帶了煙斗,但沒人相信他。

passages.original: I remember our John Manly's rule, never to allow a pipe in the stable, and thought it ought to be the rule everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 我記起我哋約翰·曼利嘅規矩,從不允許馬廄裡有煙斗,我想呢應該係到處嘅規矩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記起我們約翰·曼利的規矩,從不允許馬廄裡有煙斗,我想這應該是到處的規矩。

passages.original: James said the roof and floor had all fallen in, and that only the black walls were standing; the two poor horses that could not be got out were buried under the burnt rafters and tiles.
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯講屋頂同地板全塌喇,只剩下黑黑嘅牆壁仲立住;嗰兩匹冇能弄出嚟嘅可憐嘅馬被埋喺燒焦嘅椽子同瓦片下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯說屋頂和地板全塌了,只剩下黑黑的牆壁還立著;那兩匹沒能弄出來的可憐的馬被埋在燒焦的椽子和瓦片下面。

chapters.title: Part I · 17 John Manly's Talk 第一部·17 約翰·曼利的話

passages.original: CH The rest of our journey was very easy, and a little after sunset we reached the house of my master's friend.
passages.vernacular: 我哋旅程嘅其餘部分好順利,日落後不久,我哋到咗我主人朋友嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們旅程的其餘部分很順利,日落後不久,我們到了我主人朋友的家。

passages.original: We were taken into a clean, snug stable; there was a kind coachman, who made us very comfortable, and who seemed to think a good deal of James when he heard about the fire.
passages.vernacular: 我哋被帶進一間乾淨舒適嘅馬廄;有一個和善嘅車夫,把我哋照顧得好舒服,佢聽講咗火災,似乎好睇重詹姆斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們被帶進一間乾淨舒適的馬廄;有一個和善的車夫,把我們照顧得很舒服,他聽說了火災,似乎很看重詹姆斯。

passages.original: “There is one thing quite clear, young man,” he said, “your horses know who they can trust; it is one of the hardest things in the world to get horses out of a stable when there is either fire or flood.
passages.vernacular: 「有一件事好清楚,年輕人,」佢講,「你嘅馬知道可以信任邊個;喺失火或發洪水時把馬弄出馬廄,係世上最難嘅事之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一件事很清楚,年輕人,」他說,「你的馬知道可以信任誰;在失火或發洪水時把馬弄出馬廄,是世上最難的事之一。

passages.original: I don't know why they won't come out, but they won't--not one in twenty.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢哋點解唔肯出嚟,但佢哋就係唔肯——二十匹裡冇一匹肯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道它們為什麼不肯出來,但它們就是不肯——二十匹裡沒有一匹肯。」

passages.original: We stopped two or three days at this place and then returned home.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺呢度停留咗兩三天,然後回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在這裡停留了兩三天,然後回家。

passages.original: All went well on the journey; we were glad to be in our own stable again, and John was equally glad to see us.
passages.vernacular: 旅途一切順利;我哋好高興回到自己嘅馬廄,約翰見到我哋都同樣高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 旅途一切順利;我們很高興回到自己的馬廄,約翰見到我們也同樣高興。

passages.original: Before he and James left us for the night James said, “I wonder who is coming in my place.”
passages.vernacular: 喺佢同詹姆斯夜裡離開我哋之前,詹姆斯講:「我唔知道邊個要嚟接我嘅位置。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他和詹姆斯夜裡離開我們之前,詹姆斯說:「我不知道誰要來接我的位置。」

passages.original: “Little Joe Green at the lodge,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「門房嗰邊嘅小喬·格林,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「門房那邊的小喬·格林,」約翰說。

passages.original: “Little Joe Green! why, he's a child!”
passages.vernacular: 「小喬·格林!嗨,佢係個細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小喬·格林!嗨,他是個孩子!」

passages.original: “He is fourteen and a half,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「佢十四歲半喇,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他十四歲半了,」約翰說。

passages.original: “But he is such a little chap!”
passages.vernacular: 「可佢係咁小嘅一個傢伙!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可他是那麼小的一個傢伙!」

passages.original: “Yes, he is small, but he is quick and willing, and kind-hearted, too, and then he wishes very much to come, and his father would like it; and I know the master would like to give him the chance.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢個子小,但佢機靈、願意幹,心腸都好,而且佢好想嚟,佢父親都樂意;我知道主人都想畀佢呢個機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,他個子小,但他機靈、願意幹,心腸也好,而且他非常想來,他父親也樂意;我知道主人也想給他這個機會。

passages.original: He said if I thought he would not do he would look out for a bigger boy; but I said I was quite agreeable to try him for six weeks.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果我認為佢不行,佢就另找一個大點嘅男孩;可我講我好樂意試用佢六週。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說如果我認為他不行,他就另找一個大點的男孩;可我說我很樂意試用他六週。」

passages.original: “Six weeks!” said James; “why, it will be six months before he can be of much use!
passages.vernacular: 「六週!」詹姆斯講;「嗨,要六個月佢才能派上大用場!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「六週!」詹姆斯說;「嗨,要六個月他才能派上大用場!

passages.original: It will make you a deal of work, John.”
passages.vernacular: 呢會畀你添好多活,約翰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會給你添很多活,約翰。」

passages.original: “Well,” said John with a laugh, “work and I are very good friends; I never was afraid of work yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」約翰笑住講,「活同我係好朋友;我從冇怕過活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」約翰笑著說,「活和我是好朋友;我從沒怕過活。」

passages.original: “You are a very good man,” said James.
passages.vernacular: 「你係個好好嘅人,」詹姆斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個很好的人,」詹姆斯說。

passages.original: “I wish I may ever be like you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望我有一天能像你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望我有一天能像你。」

passages.original: “I don't often speak of myself,” said John, “but as you are going away from us out into the world to shift for yourself I'll just tell you how I look on these things.
passages.vernacular: 「我不常談自己,」約翰講,「但既然你要離開我哋到外面世界自己謀生,我就告訴你我係點睇呢啲事嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不常談自己,」約翰說,「但既然你要離開我們到外面世界自己謀生,我就告訴你我是怎麼看這些事的。

passages.original: I was just as old as Joseph when my father and mother died of the fever within ten days of each other, and left me and my cripple sister Nelly alone in the world, without a relation that we could look to for help.
passages.vernacular: 我父母喺十天之內相繼死於熱病,留下我同我嘅殘疾妹妹內莉孤零零在世上,冇一個可以指望幫忙嘅親戚,嗰時我同喬瑟夫一樣大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父母在十天之內相繼死於熱病,留下我和我的殘疾妹妹內莉孤零零在世上,沒有一個可以指望幫忙的親戚,那時我和喬瑟夫一樣大。

passages.original: I was a farmer's boy, not earning enough to keep myself, much less both of us, and she must have gone to the workhouse but for our mistress (Nelly calls her her angel, and she has good right to do so).
passages.vernacular: 我係個農場嘅細路,賺嘅錢唔夠養活自己,更唔好講我哋兩個,佢本來必須去濟貧院,但幸虧我哋嘅女主人(內莉叫佢佢嘅天使,佢有充分嘅理由咁叫)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是個農場的孩子,賺的錢不夠養活自己,更別說我們兩個,她本來必須去濟貧院,但幸虧我們的女主人(內莉叫她她的天使,她有充分的理由這麼叫)。

passages.original: She went and hired a room for her with old Widow Mallet, and she gave her knitting and needlework when she was able to do it; and when she was ill she sent her dinners and many nice, comfortable things, and was like a mother to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢去替佢喺老寡婦馬利特嗰度租咗一個房間,佢能做嘅時候,就畀佢編織同針線活;佢生病時,佢畀佢送飯同許多好嘅、舒適嘅嘢,像母親一樣對待佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她去替她在老寡婦馬利特那裡租了一個房間,她能做的時候,就給她編織和針線活;她生病時,她給她送飯和許多好的、舒適的東西,像母親一樣對待她。

passages.original: Then the master he took me into the stable under old Norman, the coachman that was then.
passages.vernacular: 然後主人把我帶進馬廄,跟住當時嘅車夫老諾曼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後主人把我帶進馬廄,跟著當時的車夫老諾曼。

passages.original: I had my food at the house and my bed in the loft, and a suit of clothes, and three shillings a week, so that I could help Nelly.
passages.vernacular: 我喺家裡食飯,喺閣樓上瞓覺,有一套衣服,每週三先令,咁樣我就能幫內莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在家裡吃飯,在閣樓上睡覺,有一套衣服,每週三先令,這樣我就能幫內莉。

passages.original: Then there was Norman; he might have turned round and said at his age he could not be troubled with a raw boy from the plow-tail, but he was like a father to me, and took no end of pains with me.
passages.vernacular: 然後係諾曼;佢本可以轉過身講,佢呢個年紀,唔能夠被一個剛從犁尾巴上下嚟嘅生手煩擾,可佢像父親一樣對我,為我費盡心思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後是諾曼;他本可以轉過身說,他這個年紀,不能被一個剛從犁尾巴上下來的生手煩擾,可他像父親一樣對我,為我費盡心思。

passages.original: When the old man died some years after I stepped into his place, and now of course I have top wages, and can lay by for a rainy day or a sunny day, as it may happen, and Nelly is as happy as a bird.
passages.vernacular: 幾年後老人去世,我接替咗佢嘅位置,而家當然我攞最高工資,可以為下雨天或晴天存些錢,內莉像鳥兒一樣快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾年後老人去世,我接替了他的位置,現在當然我拿最高工資,可以為下雨天或晴天存些錢,內莉像鳥兒一樣快樂。

passages.original: So you see, James, I am not the man that should turn up his nose at a little boy and vex a good, kind master.
passages.vernacular: 所以你睇,詹姆斯,我唔係嗰種該對一個小男孩翹鼻子、惹一位善良好主人煩惱嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你看,詹姆斯,我不是那種該對一個小男孩翹鼻子、惹一位善良好主人煩惱的人。

passages.original: No, no!
passages.vernacular: 不,不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不!

passages.original: I shall miss you very much, James, but we shall pull through, and there's nothing like doing a kindness when 'tis put in your way, and I am glad I can do it.”
passages.vernacular: 我會好想念你,詹姆斯,但我哋會渡過難關,冇乜嘢比碰到機會時做件好事更好,我好高興我能做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會非常想念你,詹姆斯,但我們會渡過難關,沒有什麼比碰到機會時做件好事更好,我很高興我能做。」

passages.original: “Then,” said James, “you don't hold with that saying, 'Everybody look after himself, and take care of number one'?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,」詹姆斯講,「你不贊成嗰句話:『人人顧自己,照顧好第一號』嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,」詹姆斯說,「你不贊成那句話:『人人顧自己,照顧好第一號』嗎?」

passages.original: “No, indeed,” said John, “where should I and Nelly have been if master and mistress and old Norman had only taken care of number one?
passages.vernacular: 「不,確實不,」約翰講,「如果主人、女主人同老諾曼只顧第一號,我同內莉會喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,確實不,」約翰說,「如果主人、女主人和老諾曼只顧第一號,我和內莉會在哪裡?

passages.original: Why, she in the workhouse and I hoeing turnips!
passages.vernacular: 嗨,佢喺濟貧院,我喺鋤蕪菁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,她在濟貧院,我在鋤蕪菁!

passages.original: Where would Black Beauty and Ginger have been if you had only thought of number one? why, roasted to death!
passages.vernacular: 如果你只想第一號,黑神駒同金姐會喺邊度?嗨,被活活燒死!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你只想第一號,黑神駒和金姐會在哪裡?嗨,被活活燒死!

passages.original: No, Jim, no! that is a selfish, heathenish saying, whoever uses it; and any man who thinks he has nothing to do but take care of number one, why, it's a pity but what he had been drowned like a puppy or a kitten, before he got his eyes open; that's what I think,” said John, with a very decided jerk of his head.
passages.vernacular: 不,吉姆,不!無論邊個講呢話,呢都係自私嘅、異教嘅講法;任何認為自己除咗顧第一號就冇別嘅事嘅人,嗨,可惜佢冇像小狗或小貓嗰樣,喺睜開眼睛之前就被淹死;呢個就係我嘅想法,」約翰講,堅決地一甩頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,吉姆,不!無論誰說這話,這都是自私的、異教的說法;任何認為自己除了顧第一號就沒別的事的人,嗨,可惜他沒像小狗或小貓那樣,在睜開眼睛之前就被淹死;這就是我的想法,」約翰說,堅決地一甩頭。

passages.original: James laughed at this; but there was a thickness in his voice when he said, “You have been my best friend except my mother; I hope you won't forget me.”
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯聽咗笑喇;但佢講話時聲音有點哽咽:「除咗我母親,你係我最好嘅朋友;我希望你唔好忘咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯聽了笑了;但他說話時聲音有點哽咽:「除了我母親,你是我最好的朋友;我希望你不要忘了我。」

passages.original: “No, lad, no!” said John, “and if ever I can do you a good turn I hope you won't forget me.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔會,細路,唔會!」約翰講,「如果我能幫你一把,我希望你都唔好忘咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會,孩子,不會!」約翰說,「如果我能幫你一把,我希望你也不要忘了我。」

passages.original: The next day Joe came to the stables to learn all he could before James left.
passages.vernacular: 第二天,喬嚟到馬廄,喺詹姆斯離開前盡量多學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,喬來到馬廄,在詹姆斯離開前盡量多學。

passages.original: He learned to sweep the stable, to bring in the straw and hay; he began to clean the harness, and helped to wash the carriage.
passages.vernacular: 佢學會掃馬廄,搬稻草同乾草;佢開始擦挽具,幫忙洗馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他學會掃馬廄,搬稻草和乾草;他開始擦挽具,幫忙洗馬車。

passages.original: As he was quite too short to do anything in the way of grooming Ginger and me, James taught him upon Merrylegs, for he was to have full charge of him, under John.
passages.vernacular: 因為佢個子太矮,冇法畀金姐同我刷毛,詹姆斯就喺梅利萊格斯身上教佢,佢將喺約翰手下全權照管梅利萊格斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他個子太矮,沒法給金姐和我刷毛,詹姆斯就在梅利萊格斯身上教他,他將在約翰手下全權照管梅利萊格斯。

passages.original: He was a nice little bright fellow, and always came whistling to his work.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個漂亮聰明嘅小傢伙,總是吹住口哨嚟幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個漂亮聰明的小傢伙,總是吹著口哨來幹活。

passages.original: Merrylegs was a good deal put out at being “mauled about,” as he said, “by a boy who knew nothing;” but toward the end of the second week he told me confidentially that he thought the boy would turn out well.
passages.vernacular: 梅利萊格斯對被「一個乜嘢都不懂嘅男孩」「亂擺弄」好惱火,佢咁講;但到第二個星期快結束時,佢私下告訴我,佢認為呢細路會有出息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 梅利萊格斯對被「一個什麼都不懂的男孩」「亂擺弄」非常惱火,他這麼說;但到第二個星期快結束時,他私下告訴我,他認為這孩子會有出息。

passages.original: At last the day came when James had to leave us; cheerful as he always was, he looked quite down-hearted that morning.
passages.vernacular: 終於,詹姆斯唔得不離開我哋嘅嗰一天到喇;佢總是咁快活,可嗰天早晨佢睇起嚟好沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於,詹姆斯不得不離開我們的那一天到了;他總是那麼快活,可那天早晨他看起來很沮喪。

passages.original: “You see,” he said to John, “I am leaving a great deal behind; my mother and Betsy, and you, and a good master and mistress, and then the horses, and my old Merrylegs.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,」佢對約翰講,「我留下嘅太多喇;我母親同貝琪,仲有你,同一位好主人、好女主人,仲有馬,仲有我嘅老梅利萊格斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,」他對約翰說,「我留下的太多了;我母親和貝琪,還有你,和一位好主人、好女主人,還有馬,還有我的老梅利萊格斯。

passages.original: At the new place there will not be a soul that I shall know.
passages.vernacular: 新地方連一個我認識嘅人都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新地方連一個我認識的人都沒有。

passages.original: If it were not that I shall get a higher place, and be able to help my mother better, I don't think I should have made up my mind to it; it is a real pinch, John.”
passages.vernacular: 要唔係我會得到更高嘅職位,能更好地幫助我母親,我想我唔會下呢個決心;呢真讓人難受,約翰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是我會得到更高的職位,能更好地幫助我母親,我想我不會下這個決心;這真讓人難受,約翰。」

passages.original: “Ay, James, lad, so it is; but I should not think much of you if you could leave your home for the first time and not feel it.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,詹姆斯,細路,確實;但如果你第一次離開家而不感到難過,我就唔會把你睇得好重喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,詹姆斯,孩子,確實;但如果你第一次離開家而不感到難過,我就不會把你看得很重了。

passages.original: Cheer up, you'll make friends there; and if you get on well, as I am sure you will, it will be a fine thing for your mother, and she will be proud enough that you have got into such a good place as that.”
passages.vernacular: 振作起嚟,你喺嗰度會交到朋友;如果你幹得好,我確信你會,對你母親會係件好事,佢會好自豪你進咗嗰樣好嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 振作起來,你在那裡會交到朋友;如果你幹得好,我確信你會,對你母親會是件好事,她會很自豪你進了那樣好的地方。」

passages.original: So John cheered him up, but every one was sorry to lose James; as for Merrylegs, he pined after him for several days, and went quite off his appetite.
passages.vernacular: 約翰就咁樣讓佢振作起嚟,但每個人都為失去詹姆斯而難過;至於梅利萊格斯,佢想念佢,幾天裡食慾全無。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰就這樣讓他振作起來,但每個人都為失去詹姆斯而難過;至於梅利萊格斯,他想念他,幾天裡食慾全無。

passages.original: So John took him out several mornings with a leading rein, when he exercised me, and, trotting and galloping by my side, got up the little fellow's spirits again, and he was soon all right.
passages.vernacular: 於是約翰幾個早晨用牽引韁繩帶佢出去,我運動時,佢喺我身邊小跑同飛奔,讓小傢伙又振作起咗精神,佢好快就好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是約翰幾個早晨用牽引韁繩帶他出去,我運動時,他在我身邊小跑和飛奔,讓小傢伙又振作起了精神,他很快就好了。

passages.original: Joe's father would often come in and give a little help, as he understood the work; and Joe took a great deal of pains to learn, and John was quite encouraged about him.
passages.vernacular: 喬嘅父親常嚟幫點忙,因為佢懂呢活;喬好用心地學,約翰對佢好受鼓舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬的父親常來幫點忙,因為他懂這活;喬非常用心地學,約翰對他很受鼓舞。

chapters.title: Part I · 18 Going for the Doctor 第一部·18 去請醫生

passages.original: CH One night, a few days after James had left, I had eaten my hay and was lying down in my straw fast asleep, when I was suddenly roused by the stable bell ringing very loud.
passages.vernacular: 詹姆斯走後幾天嘅一個夜裡,我食完乾草,躺喺稻草上沉瞓,忽然被馬廄嘅鈴聲大響驚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詹姆斯走後幾天的一個夜裡,我吃完乾草,躺在稻草上沉睡,忽然被馬廄的鈴聲大響驚醒。

passages.original: I heard the door of John's house open, and his feet running up to the hall.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見約翰嘅房子門開喇,佢嘅腳步聲跑向莊園大廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見約翰的房子門開了,他的腳步聲跑向莊園大廳。

passages.original: He was back again in no time; he unlocked the stable door, and came in, calling out, “Wake up, Beauty!
passages.vernacular: 佢轉眼就回嚟喇;佢打開馬廄門,走進嚟,喊住:「醒醒,神駒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉眼就回來了;他打開馬廄門,走進來,喊著:「醒醒,神駒!

passages.original: You must go well now, if ever you did;” and almost before I could think he had got the saddle on my back and the bridle on my head.
passages.vernacular: 如果你以前跑得好,而家必須跑得好;」我仲冇嚟得及想,佢已經把鞍子放到我背上,把轡頭套到我頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你以前跑得好,現在必須跑得好;」我還沒來得及想,他已經把鞍子放到我背上,把轡頭套到我頭上。

passages.original: He just ran round for his coat, and then took me at a quick trot up to the hall door.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係跑回去攞外套,然後以快步小跑把我帶到大廳門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只是跑回去拿外套,然後以快步小跑把我帶到大廳門口。

passages.original: The squire stood there, with a lamp in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 鄉紳站喺嗰度,手裡攞住一盞燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鄉紳站在那裡,手裡拿著一盞燈。

passages.original: “Now, John,” he said, “ride for your life--that is, for your mistress' life; there is not a moment to lose.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,約翰,」佢講,「拼命騎——就係為了你女主人嘅命;一刻都唔能夠耽誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,約翰,」他說,「拼命騎——就是為了你女主人的命;一刻也不能耽誤。

passages.original: Give this note to Dr. White; give your horse a rest at the inn, and be back as soon as you can.”
passages.vernacular: 把呢張條子交畀懷特醫生;讓你嘅馬喺客棧休息一下,盡快回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這張條子交給懷特醫生;讓你的馬在客棧休息一下,盡快回來。」

passages.original: John said, “Yes, sir,” and was on my back in a minute.
passages.vernacular: 約翰講:「係,先生,」轉眼就騎喺我背上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰說:「是,先生,」轉眼就騎在我背上。

passages.original: The gardener who lived at the lodge had heard the bell ring, and was ready with the gate open, and away we went through the park, and through the village, and down the hill till we came to the toll-gate.
passages.vernacular: 住喺門房嘅園丁聽見咗鈴聲,已經準備好,把門打開喇,我哋穿過莊園,穿過村子,下山,直到來到收費柵門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住在門房的園丁聽見了鈴聲,已經準備好,把門打開了,我們穿過莊園,穿過村子,下山,直到來到收費柵門。

passages.original: John called very loud and thumped upon the door; the man was soon out and flung open the gate.
passages.vernacular: 約翰大聲喊住,砰砰地敲門;嗰人好快出嚟,把門猛地打開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰大聲喊著,砰砰地敲門;那人很快出來,把門猛地打開。

passages.original: “Now,” said John, “do you keep the gate open for the doctor; here's the money,” and off he went again.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,」約翰講,「你為醫生把門開住;呢個係錢,」講完佢又出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,」約翰說,「你為醫生把門開著;這是錢,」說完他又出發了。

passages.original: There was before us a long piece of level road by the river side; John said to me, “Now, Beauty, do your best,” and so I did; I wanted no whip nor spur, and for two miles I galloped as fast as I could lay my feet to the ground; I don't believe that my old grandfather, who won the race at Newmarket, could have gone faster.
passages.vernacular: 我哋前面係一段沿河邊嘅長長嘅平路;約翰對我講:「而家,神駒,盡你嘅力,」我就咁樣做喇;我唔好鞭子或馬刺,兩英里我盡可能快地把蹄子踏喺地上飛奔;我不相信我喺紐馬基特賽馬中獲勝嘅老祖父能跑得更快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們前面是一段沿河邊的長長的平路;約翰對我說:「現在,神駒,盡你的力,」我就這樣做了;我不要鞭子或馬刺,兩英里我盡可能快地把蹄子踏在地上飛奔;我不相信我在紐馬基特賽馬中獲勝的老祖父能跑得更快。

passages.original: When we came to the bridge John pulled me up a little and patted my neck.
passages.vernacular: 我哋到咗橋邊,約翰把我稍微勒住,拍住我嘅脖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們到了橋邊,約翰把我稍微勒住,拍著我的脖子。

passages.original: “Well done, Beauty! good old fellow,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「幹得好,神駒!好老夥計,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幹得好,神駒!好老夥計,」他說。

passages.original: He would have let me go slower, but my spirit was up, and I was off again as fast as before.
passages.vernacular: 佢本來會讓我慢啲,但我嘅精神上嚟喇,又像之前一樣快地跑起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他本來會讓我慢一點,但我的精神上來了,又像之前一樣快地跑起來。

passages.original: The air was frosty, the moon was bright; it was very pleasant.
passages.vernacular: 空氣中有霜,月亮明亮;好愜意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中有霜,月亮明亮;非常愜意。

passages.original: We came through a village, then through a dark wood, then uphill, then downhill, till after eight miles' run we came to the town, through the streets and into the market-place.
passages.vernacular: 我哋穿過一個村子,然後穿過一片黑暗嘅樹林,然後上坡,然後下坡,直到跑咗八英里後來到城裡,穿過街道,進入市場廣場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們穿過一個村子,然後穿過一片黑暗的樹林,然後上坡,然後下坡,直到跑了八英里後來到城裡,穿過街道,進入市場廣場。

passages.original: It was all quite still except the clatter of my feet on the stones--everybody was asleep.
passages.vernacular: 除咗我嘅蹄子喺石頭上嘅噠噠聲,一切都好安靜——所有人都瞓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了我的蹄子在石頭上的噠噠聲,一切都很安靜——所有人都睡了。

passages.original: The church clock struck three as we drew up at Dr. White's door.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺懷特醫生家門口停下時,教堂嘅鐘敲咗三下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在懷特醫生家門口停下時,教堂的鐘敲了三下。

passages.original: John rang the bell twice, and then knocked at the door like thunder.
passages.vernacular: 約翰按咗兩次門鈴,然後像打雷一樣敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰按了兩次門鈴,然後像打雷一樣敲門。

passages.original: A window was thrown up, and Dr. White, in his nightcap, put his head out and said, “What do you want?”
passages.vernacular: 一扇窗子被推開喇,戴住瞓帽嘅懷特醫生探出頭來講:「你要乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一扇窗子被推開了,戴著睡帽的懷特醫生探出頭來說:「你要什麼?」

passages.original: “Mrs. Gordon is very ill, sir; master wants you to go at once; he thinks she will die if you cannot get there.
passages.vernacular: 「戈登太太病得好重,先生;主人要您即刻去;佢認為如果您去不喇,佢會死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「戈登太太病得很重,先生;主人要您馬上去;他認為如果您去不了,她會死。

passages.original: Here is a note.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一張條子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一張條子。」

passages.original: “Wait,” he said, “I will come.”
passages.vernacular: 「等住,」佢講,「我就嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等著,」他說,「我就來。」

passages.original: He shut the window, and was soon at the door.
passages.vernacular: 佢關上窗子,好快到咗門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他關上窗子,很快到了門口。

passages.original: “The worst of it is,” he said, “that my horse has been out all day and is quite done up; my son has just been sent for, and he has taken the other.
passages.vernacular: 「最糟嘅係,」佢講,「我嘅馬跑咗一整天,已經累壞喇;我兒子剛被叫走,把另一匹都騎走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最糟的是,」他說,「我的馬跑了一整天,已經累壞了;我兒子剛被叫走,把另一匹也騎走了。

passages.original: What is to be done?
passages.vernacular: 點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼辦?

passages.original: Can I have your horse?”
passages.vernacular: 我可以用你嘅馬嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以用你的馬嗎?」

passages.original: “He has come at a gallop nearly all the way, sir, and I was to give him a rest here; but I think my master would not be against it, if you think fit, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢幾乎一路飛奔而嚟,先生,我本來要讓佢喺呢度休息;但我想如果您認為合適,我主人唔會反對嘅,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他幾乎一路飛奔而來,先生,我本來要讓他在這裡休息;但我想如果您認為合適,我主人不會反對的,先生。」

passages.original: “All right,” he said; “I will soon be ready.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,」佢講;「我即刻準備好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」他說;「我馬上準備好。」

passages.original: John stood by me and stroked my neck; I was very hot.
passages.vernacular: 約翰站喺我旁邊撫摸我嘅脖子;我好熱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰站在我旁邊撫摸我的脖子;我很熱。

passages.original: The doctor came out with his riding-whip.
passages.vernacular: 醫生攞住佢嘅馬鞭出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生拿著他的馬鞭出來了。

passages.original: “You need not take that, sir,” said John; “Black Beauty will go till he drops.
passages.vernacular: 「您不需要帶嗰個,先生,」約翰講;「黑神駒會跑到倒下為止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不需要帶那個,先生,」約翰說;「黑神駒會跑到倒下為止。

passages.original: Take care of him, sir, if you can; I should not like any harm to come to him.”
passages.vernacular: 如果可以,請照顧好佢,先生;我唔想讓佢受到任何傷害。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果可以,請照顧好他,先生;我不想讓他受到任何傷害。」

passages.original: “No, no, John,” said the doctor, “I hope not,” and in a minute we had left John far behind.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會,唔會,約翰,」醫生講,「我希望唔會,」轉眼間我哋就把約翰遠遠拋喺咗後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會,不會,約翰,」醫生說,「我希望不會,」轉眼間我們就把約翰遠遠拋在了後面。

passages.original: I will not tell about our way back.
passages.vernacular: 我不講我哋嘅回程喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不講我們的回程了。

passages.original: The doctor was a heavier man than John, and not so good a rider; however, I did my very best.
passages.vernacular: 醫生比約翰重,騎術都不如佢好;不過我盡咗我最大嘅努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生比約翰重,騎術也不如他好;不過我盡了我最大的努力。

passages.original: The man at the toll-gate had it open.
passages.vernacular: 收費柵門嘅人把門開住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收費柵門的人把門開著。

passages.original: When we came to the hill the doctor drew me up.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嚟到山坡時,醫生勒住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們來到山坡時,醫生勒住我。

passages.original: “Now, my good fellow,” he said, “take some breath.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,我嘅好夥計,」佢講,「喘口氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,我的好夥計,」他說,「喘口氣。」

passages.original: I was glad he did, for I was nearly spent, but that breathing helped me on, and soon we were in the park.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興佢咁樣做,因為我幾乎筋疲力盡喇,但喘息幫我繼續,好快我哋就到咗莊園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興他這樣做,因為我幾乎筋疲力盡了,但喘息幫我繼續,很快我們就到了莊園。

passages.original: Joe was at the lodge gate; my master was at the hall door, for he had heard us coming.
passages.vernacular: 喬喺門房門口;我嘅主人喺大廳門口,因為佢聽見我哋嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬在門房門口;我的主人在大廳門口,因為他聽見我們來了。

passages.original: He spoke not a word; the doctor went into the house with him, and Joe led me to the stable.
passages.vernacular: 佢一句話都冇講;醫生同佢進咗屋,喬把我牽到馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一句話也沒說;醫生同他進了屋,喬把我牽到馬廄。

passages.original: I was glad to get home; my legs shook under me, and I could only stand and pant.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興回家;我嘅腿喺我下面發抖,我只能站住喘氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興回家;我的腿在我下面發抖,我只能站著喘氣。

passages.original: I had not a dry hair on my body, the water ran down my legs, and I steamed all over, Joe used to say, like a pot on the fire.
passages.vernacular: 我身上冇一根乾嘅毛,水順住我嘅腿流下嚟,喬常講,我全身冒住熱氣,像火上嘅鍋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我身上沒有一根乾的毛,水順著我的腿流下來,喬常說,我全身冒著熱氣,像火上的鍋。

passages.original: Poor Joe! he was young and small, and as yet he knew very little, and his father, who would have helped him, had been sent to the next village; but I am sure he did the very best he knew.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅喬!佢又年輕又小,到嗰時仲懂得好少,本來能幫佢嘅父親被派到下一個村子去喇;但我確信佢做咗佢所知道嘅最好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的喬!他又年輕又小,到那時還懂得很少,本來能幫他的父親被派到下一個村子去了;但我確信他做了他所知道的最好的。

passages.original: He rubbed my legs and my chest, but he did not put my warm cloth on me; he thought I was so hot I should not like it.
passages.vernacular: 佢擦咗我嘅腿同胸,但冇畀我蓋上暖同嘅毯子;佢認為我咁熱,唔會鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他擦了我的腿和胸,但沒有給我蓋上暖和的毯子;他認為我那麼熱,不會喜歡。

passages.original: Then he gave me a pailful of water to drink; it was cold and very good, and I drank it all; then he gave me some hay and some corn, and thinking he had done right, he went away.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢畀咗我一桶水飲;佢好涼,好好飲,我全飲喇;然後佢畀咗我啲乾草同穀物,以為自己做對喇,就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他給了我一桶水喝;它很涼,很好喝,我全喝了;然後他給了我一些乾草和穀物,以為自己做對了,就走了。

passages.original: Soon I began to shake and tremble, and turned deadly cold; my legs ached, my loins ached, and my chest ached, and I felt sore all over.
passages.vernacular: 不久我開始發抖打顫,冷得要命;我嘅腿疼,我嘅腰疼,我嘅胸疼,我全身難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久我開始發抖打顫,冷得要命;我的腿疼,我的腰疼,我的胸疼,我全身難受。

passages.original: Oh! how I wished for my warm, thick cloth, as I stood and trembled.
passages.vernacular: 哦!我站住發抖,幾咁希望有我溫暖厚實嘅毯子啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦!我站著發抖,多麼希望有我溫暖厚實的毯子啊。

passages.original: I wished for John, but he had eight miles to walk, so I lay down in my straw and tried to go to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 我想念約翰,可佢得走八英里,所以我躺喺稻草上,努力想瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想念約翰,可他得走八英里,所以我躺在稻草上,努力想睡著。

passages.original: After a long while I heard John at the door; I gave a low moan, for I was in great pain.
passages.vernacular: 過咗好久,我聽見約翰喺門口;我低低地呻吟咗一聲,因為我疼得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了很久,我聽見約翰在門口;我低低地呻吟了一聲,因為我疼得厲害。

passages.original: He was at my side in a moment, stooping down by me.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉眼就到咗我身邊,喺我旁邊彎下身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉眼就到了我身邊,在我旁邊彎下身。

passages.original: I could not tell him how I felt, but he seemed to know it all; he covered me up with two or three warm cloths, and then ran to the house for some hot water; he made me some warm gruel, which I drank, and then I think I went to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 我冇法告訴佢我嘅感覺,但佢似乎全都知道;佢畀我蓋上咗兩三條暖同嘅毯子,然後跑到屋裡去攞熱水;佢畀我煮咗些溫熱嘅麥片粥,我飲喇,然後我想我就瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒法告訴他我的感覺,但他似乎全都知道;他給我蓋上了兩三條暖和的毯子,然後跑到屋裡去拿熱水;他給我煮了些溫熱的麥片粥,我喝了,然後我想我就睡著了。

passages.original: John seemed to be very much put out.
passages.vernacular: 約翰似乎好惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰似乎非常惱火。

passages.original: I heard him say to himself over and over again, “Stupid boy! stupid boy! no cloth put on, and I dare say the water was cold, too; boys are no good;” but Joe was a good boy, after all.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見佢一遍又一遍地自言自語:「蠢細路!蠢細路!冇蓋毯子,我敢講水定係涼嘅;男細路冇用;」但喬畢竟係個好細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見他一遍又一遍地自言自語:「蠢孩子!蠢孩子!沒蓋毯子,我敢說水還是涼的;男孩子沒用;」但喬畢竟是個好孩子。

passages.original: I was now very ill; a strong inflammation had attacked my lungs, and I could not draw my breath without pain.
passages.vernacular: 我而家病得好重;嚴重嘅炎症襲擊咗我嘅肺,我吸氣時冇不疼嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在病得很重;嚴重的炎症襲擊了我的肺,我吸氣時沒有不疼的。

passages.original: John nursed me night and day; he would get up two or three times in the night to come to me.
passages.vernacular: 約翰日夜照顧我;佢夜裡會起嚟兩三次嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰日夜照顧我;他夜裡會起來兩三次來看我。

passages.original: My master, too, often came to see me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人都常嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人也常來看我。

passages.original: “My poor Beauty,” he said one day, “my good horse, you saved your mistress' life, Beauty; yes, you saved her life.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可憐嘅神駒,」有一天佢講,「我嘅好馬,你救咗你女主人嘅命,神駒;係嘅,你救咗佢嘅命。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可憐的神駒,」有一天他說,「我的好馬,你救了你女主人的命,神駒;是的,你救了她的命。」

passages.original: I was very glad to hear that, for it seems the doctor had said if we had been a little longer it would have been too late.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興聽到呢個,因為睇來醫生講過,如果我哋再晚啲,就太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興聽到這個,因為看來醫生說過,如果我們再晚一點,就太遲了。

passages.original: John told my master he never saw a horse go so fast in his life.
passages.vernacular: 約翰告訴我嘅主人,佢呢輩子從冇見過馬跑得咁快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰告訴我的主人,他這輩子從沒見過馬跑得這麼快。

passages.original: It seemed as if the horse knew what was the matter.
passages.vernacular: 好像馬知道係點回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像馬知道是怎麼回事。

passages.original: Of course I did, though John thought not; at least I knew as much as this--that John and I must go at the top of our speed, and that it was for the sake of the mistress.
passages.vernacular: 當然我知道,雖然約翰認為我唔知道;至少我知道呢啲——約翰同我必須全速奔跑,呢個係為了女主人嘅緣故。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我知道,雖然約翰認為我不知道;至少我知道這些——約翰和我必須全速奔跑,這是為了女主人的緣故。

chapters.title: Part I · 19 Only Ignorance 第一部·19 只是無知

passages.original: CH I do not know how long I was ill.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道我病咗多久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道我病了多久。

passages.original: Mr. Bond, the horse-doctor, came every day.
passages.vernacular: 馬醫邦德先生每天都嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬醫邦德先生每天都來。

passages.original: One day he bled me; John held a pail for the blood.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢畀我放咗血;約翰攞住一個桶接血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天他給我放了血;約翰拿著一個桶接血。

passages.original: I felt very faint after it and thought I should die, and I believe they all thought so too.
passages.vernacular: 放血後我覺得好虛弱,以為自己要死喇,我相信佢哋都都咁想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放血後我覺得非常虛弱,以為自己要死了,我相信他們也都這麼想。

passages.original: Ginger and Merrylegs had been moved into the other stable, so that I might be quiet, for the fever made me very quick of hearing; any little noise seemed quite loud, and I could tell every one's footstep going to and from the house.
passages.vernacular: 金姐同梅利萊格斯被搬到另一個馬廄,好讓我安靜,因為發燒使我嘅聽覺好靈敏;任何啲小聲音都顯得好響,我能分辨每個人進出房子嘅腳步聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 金姐和梅利萊格斯被搬到另一個馬廄,好讓我安靜,因為發燒使我的聽覺非常靈敏;任何一點小聲音都顯得很響,我能分辨每個人進出房子的腳步聲。

passages.original: I knew all that was going on.
passages.vernacular: 我知道正在發生嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道正在發生的一切。

passages.original: One night John had to give me a draught; Thomas Green came in to help him.
passages.vernacular: 一天夜裡,約翰唔得不畀我灌一劑藥;托馬斯·格林進嚟幫佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天夜裡,約翰不得不給我灌一劑藥;托馬斯·格林進來幫他。

passages.original: After I had taken it and John had made me as comfortable as he could, he said he should stay half an hour to see how the medicine settled.
passages.vernacular: 我食咗藥,約翰盡可能讓我舒服之後,佢講佢要待半小時,睇睇藥點起作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我吃了藥,約翰盡可能讓我舒服之後,他說他要待半小時,看看藥怎麼起作用。

passages.original: Thomas said he would stay with him, so they went and sat down on a bench that had been brought into Merrylegs' stall, and put down the lantern at their feet, that I might not be disturbed with the light.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯講佢陪佢,於是佢哋走過去坐喺一條搬到梅利萊格斯馬棚裡嘅長凳上,把燈籠放喺佢哋腳邊,免得燈光打擾我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯說他陪他,於是他們走過去坐在一條搬到梅利萊格斯馬棚裡的長凳上,把燈籠放在他們腳邊,免得燈光打擾我。

passages.original: For awhile both men sat silent, and then Tom Green said in a low voice:
passages.vernacular: 有一陣子兩人都靜靜地坐住,然後湯姆·格林低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣子兩人都靜靜地坐著,然後湯姆·格林低聲說:

passages.original: “I wish, John, you'd say a bit of a kind word to Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,我希望你對喬講句好話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,我希望你對喬說句好話。

passages.original: The boy is quite broken-hearted; he can't eat his meals, and he can't smile.
passages.vernacular: 嗰細路完全傷心透喇;佢食不下飯,都笑不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那孩子完全傷心透了;他吃不下飯,也笑不出來。

passages.original: He says he knows it was all his fault, though he is sure he did the best he knew, and he says if Beauty dies no one will ever speak to him again.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢知道呢都係佢嘅錯,雖然佢確信佢盡咗佢所知道嘅最好嘅,佢講如果神駒死喇,就再都冇人同佢講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他知道這都是他的錯,雖然他確信他盡了他所知道的最好的,他說如果神駒死了,就再也沒有人同他說話了。

passages.original: It goes to my heart to hear him.
passages.vernacular: 我聽住心都碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽著心都碎了。

passages.original: I think you might give him just a word; he is not a bad boy.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你可以對佢講一句話;佢唔係壞細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你可以對他說一句話;他不是壞孩子。」

passages.original: After a short pause John said slowly, “You must not be too hard upon me, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 短暫停頓之後,約翰慢慢地講:「你唔好對我太苛刻,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 短暫停頓之後,約翰慢慢地說:「你不要對我太苛刻,湯姆。

passages.original: I know he meant no harm, I never said he did; I know he is not a bad boy.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢唔係故意嘅,我從冇講佢係;我知道佢唔係壞細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道他不是故意的,我從沒說他是;我知道他不是壞孩子。

passages.original: But you see, I am sore myself; that horse is the pride of my heart, to say nothing of his being such a favorite with the master and mistress; and to think that his life may be flung away in this manner is more than I can bear.
passages.vernacular: 但你睇,我自己都傷心;嗰匹馬係我心中嘅驕傲,更唔好講佢深受主人同女主人喜愛;一想到佢嘅命可能就咁樣白白丟掉,我就受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你看,我自己也傷心;那匹馬是我心中的驕傲,更別說他深受主人和女主人喜愛;一想到他的命可能就這樣白白丟掉,我就受不了。

passages.original: But if you think I am hard on the boy I will try to give him a good word to-morrow--that is, I mean if Beauty is better.”
passages.vernacular: 不過如果你認為我對嗰細路苛刻,我聽日會試住對佢講句好話——我係講,如果神駒好些喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過如果你認為我對那孩子苛刻,我明天會試著對他說句好話——我是說,如果神駒好些了。」

passages.original: “Well, John, thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,約翰,謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,約翰,謝謝你。

passages.original: I knew you did not wish to be too hard, and I am glad you see it was only ignorance.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道你唔想太苛刻,我好高興你睇到嗰只係無知。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道你不想太苛刻,我很高興你看到那只是無知。」

passages.original: John's voice almost startled me as he answered:
passages.vernacular: 約翰回答時嘅聲音幾乎嚇咗我一跳:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰回答時的聲音幾乎嚇了我一跳:

passages.original: “Only ignorance! only ignorance! how can you talk about only ignorance?
passages.vernacular: 「只係無知!只係無知!你點能講只係無知?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是無知!只是無知!你怎麼能說只是無知?

passages.original: Don't you know that it is the worst thing in the world, next to wickedness?--and which does the most mischief heaven only knows.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道佢係世上僅次於邪惡嘅最糟嘅事嗎?——邊一個造成嘅禍害更大,只有天知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道它是世上僅次於邪惡的最糟的事嗎?——哪一個造成的禍害更大,只有天知道。

passages.original: If people can say, 'Oh!
passages.vernacular: 如果人哋可以講:『哦!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果人們可以說:『哦!

passages.original: I did not know, I did not mean any harm,' they think it is all right.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道,我唔係有意傷害,』佢哋就覺得冇事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道,我不是有意傷害,』他們就覺得沒事了。

passages.original: I suppose Martha Mulwash did not mean to kill that baby when she dosed it with Dalby and soothing syrups; but she did kill it, and was tried for manslaughter.”
passages.vernacular: 我想瑪莎·穆爾沃什畀嗰嬰兒灌達爾比合劑同鎮靜糖漿時,並唔想殺死嗰個細路;但佢確實殺死喇,並且因過失殺人受審。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想瑪莎·穆爾沃什給那嬰兒灌達爾比合劑和鎮靜糖漿時,並不想殺死那個孩子;但她確實殺死了,並且因過失殺人受審。」

passages.original: “And serve her right, too,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「都係活該,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也是活該,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “A woman should not undertake to nurse a tender little child without knowing what is good and what is bad for it.”
passages.vernacular: 「一個女人不該喺唔知道乜嘢對嬌嫩嘅小孩好、乜嘢不好嘅情況下照料佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個女人不該在不知道什麼對嬌嫩的小孩好、什麼不好的情況下照料他。」

passages.original: “Bill Starkey,” continued John, “did not mean to frighten his brother into fits when he dressed up like a ghost and ran after him in the moonlight; but he did; and that bright, handsome little fellow, that might have been the pride of any mother's heart is just no better than an idiot, and never will be, if he lives to be eighty years old.
passages.vernacular: 「比爾·斯塔基,」約翰接住講,「穿得像鬼喺月光下追佢弟弟時,並唔想把佢弟弟嚇得抽筋;但佢嚇成喇;嗰個聰明漂亮嘅小傢伙,本來可以成為任何母親心中嘅驕傲,而家不過係個白痴,如果佢活到八十歲,都永遠係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「比爾·斯塔基,」約翰接著說,「穿得像鬼在月光下追他弟弟時,並不想把他弟弟嚇得抽筋;但他嚇成了;那個聰明漂亮的小傢伙,本來可以成為任何母親心中的驕傲,現在不過是個白痴,如果他活到八十歲,也永遠是這樣。

passages.original: You were a good deal cut up yourself, Tom, two weeks ago, when those young ladies left your hothouse door open, with a frosty east wind blowing right in; you said it killed a good many of your plants.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,兩個星期前,嗰啲年輕小姐讓你嘅暖房門開住,冰冷嘅東風直吹進去,你自己都好心疼;你講佢凍死咗你許多植物。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,兩個星期前,那些年輕小姐讓你的暖房門開著,冰冷的東風直吹進去,你自己也很心疼;你說它凍死了你許多植物。」

passages.original: “A good many!” said Tom; “there was not one of the tender cuttings that was not nipped off.
passages.vernacular: 「許多!」湯姆講;「冇一棵嫩插條冇被凍壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「許多!」湯姆說;「沒有一棵嫩插條沒被凍壞。

passages.original: I shall have to strike all over again, and the worst of it is that I don't know where to go to get fresh ones.
passages.vernacular: 我得全部重新扦插,最糟嘅係我唔知道去邊度弄新嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得全部重新扦插,最糟的是我不知道去哪裡弄新的。

passages.original: I was nearly mad when I came in and saw what was done.”
passages.vernacular: 我進去睇到被弄成嗰樣時,幾乎氣瘋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我進去看到被弄成那樣時,幾乎氣瘋了。」

passages.original: “And yet,” said John, “I am sure the young ladies did not mean it; it was only ignorance.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,」約翰講,「我確信年輕小姐哋唔係有意嘅;嗰只係無知。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,」約翰說,「我確信年輕小姐們不是有意的;那只是無知。」

passages.original: I heard no more of this conversation, for the medicine did well and sent me to sleep, and in the morning I felt much better; but I often thought of John's words when I came to know more of the world.
passages.vernacular: 呢場談話我冇再聽到乜嘢,因為藥效好好,讓我瞓住喇,早晨我覺得好多喇;但後來我多了解世界啲後,常常想起約翰嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這場談話我沒再聽到什麼,因為藥效很好,讓我睡著了,早晨我覺得好多了;但後來我多了解世界一點後,常常想起約翰的話。

chapters.title: Part I · 20 Joe Green 第一部·20 喬·格林

passages.original: CH Joe Green went on very well; he learned quickly, and was so attentive and careful that John began to trust him in many things; but as I have said, he was small of his age, and it was seldom that he was allowed to exercise either Ginger or me; but it so happened one morning that John was out with Justice in the luggage cart, and the master wanted a note to be taken immediately to a gentleman's house, about three miles distant, and sent his orders for Joe to saddle me and take it, adding the caution that he was to ride steadily.
passages.vernacular: 喬·格林幹得好好;佢學得快,又咁專心謹慎,約翰開始喺許多事上信任佢;但正如我講過嘅,佢年紀雖小,好少被允許運動金姐或我;不過有一天早晨碰巧約翰駕住賈斯蒂斯拉行李車出去喇,主人要一張條子立即送到大約三英里外一位先生家,就吩咐喬畀我備鞍送去,並叮囑佢要穩穩地騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬·格林幹得很好;他學得快,又那麼專心謹慎,約翰開始在許多事上信任他;但正如我說過的,他年紀雖小,很少被允許運動金姐或我;可是有一天早晨碰巧約翰駕著賈斯蒂斯拉行李車出去了,主人要一張條子立即送到大約三英里外一位先生家,就吩咐喬給我備鞍送去,並叮囑他要穩穩地騎。

passages.original: The note was delivered, and we were quietly returning when we came to the brick-field.
passages.vernacular: 條子送到喇,我哋安靜地往回走,嚟到磚廠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 條子送到了,我們安靜地往回走,來到磚廠。

passages.original: Here we saw a cart heavily laden with bricks; the wheels had stuck fast in the stiff mud of some deep ruts, and the carter was shouting and flogging the two horses unmercifully.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,我哋睇見一輛裝滿磚嘅重載車;車輪陷喺深轍嘅硬泥裡喇,車夫正大叫並無情地抽打嗰兩匹馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,我們看見一輛裝滿磚的重載車;車輪陷在深轍的硬泥裡了,車夫正大叫並無情地抽打那兩匹馬。

passages.original: Joe pulled up.
passages.vernacular: 喬勒住咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬勒住了我。

passages.original: It was a sad sight.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係令人傷心嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是令人傷心的景象。

passages.original: There were the two horses straining and struggling with all their might to drag the cart out, but they could not move it; the sweat streamed from their legs and flanks, their sides heaved, and every muscle was strained, while the man, fiercely pulling at the head of the fore horse, swore and lashed most brutally.
passages.vernacular: 兩匹馬正使出全身力氣掙扎著想把車拖出嚟,不過佢哋拖不動;汗水順住佢哋嘅腿同兩肋流下嚟,肋部起伏,每塊肌肉都繃緊喇,而嗰人兇狠地拉住前面嗰匹馬嘅頭,咒罵並極其殘暴地抽打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩匹馬正使出全身力氣掙扎著想把車拖出來,可是它們拖不動;汗水順著它們的腿和兩肋流下來,肋部起伏,每塊肌肉都繃緊了,而那人兇狠地拉著前面那匹馬的頭,咒罵並極其殘暴地抽打。

passages.original: “Hold hard,” said Joe; “don't go on flogging the horses like that; the wheels are so stuck that they cannot move the cart.”
passages.vernacular: 「住手,」喬講;「唔好再嗰樣抽馬喇;車輪陷得太緊,佢哋拉不動車。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「住手,」喬說;「別再那樣抽馬了;車輪陷得太緊,它們拉不動車。」

passages.original: The man took no heed, but went on lashing.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人不理睬,繼續抽打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人不理睬,繼續抽打。

passages.original: “Stop! pray stop!” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「停下!請停下!」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「停下!請停下!」喬說。

passages.original: “I'll help you to lighten the cart; they can't move it now.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嚟幫你把車卸輕啲;佢哋而家拉不動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我來幫你把車卸輕一些;它們現在拉不動。」

passages.original: “Mind your own business, you impudent young rascal, and I'll mind mine!”
passages.vernacular: 「少管閒事,你呢個無禮嘅小混蛋,我管我嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「少管閒事,你這個無禮的小混蛋,我管我的!」

passages.original: The man was in a towering passion and the worse for drink, and laid on the whip again.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人正在暴怒中,又飲咗酒,又揮起咗鞭子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人正在暴怒中,又喝了酒,又揮起了鞭子。

passages.original: Joe turned my head, and the next moment we were going at a round gallop toward the house of the master brick-maker.
passages.vernacular: 喬掉轉我嘅頭,下一刻我哋就以飛奔嘅快步朝磚廠老闆嘅房子奔去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬掉轉我的頭,下一刻我們就以飛奔的快步朝磚廠老闆的房子奔去。

passages.original: I cannot say if John would have approved of our pace, but Joe and I were both of one mind, and so angry that we could not have gone slower.
passages.vernacular: 我講不上約翰係咪贊成我哋嘅速度,但喬同我想嘅一樣,而且氣得咁厲害,我哋唔可能跑得更慢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不上約翰是否贊成我們的速度,但喬和我想的一樣,而且氣得那麼厲害,我們不可能跑得更慢了。

passages.original: The house stood close by the roadside.
passages.vernacular: 房子就喺路邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子就在路邊。

passages.original: Joe knocked at the door, and shouted, “Halloo!
passages.vernacular: 喬敲住門喊:「喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬敲著門喊:「喂!

passages.original: Is Mr. Clay at home?”
passages.vernacular: 克萊先生喺家嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 克萊先生在家嗎?」

passages.original: The door was opened, and Mr. Clay himself came out.
passages.vernacular: 門開喇,克萊先生親自出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門開了,克萊先生親自出來。

passages.original: “Halloo, young man!
passages.vernacular: 「喂,年輕人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,年輕人!

passages.original: You seem in a hurry; any orders from the squire this morning?”
passages.vernacular: 你睇起嚟好住急;今日早晨鄉紳有乜嘢吩咐嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看起來很著急;今天早晨鄉紳有什麼吩咐嗎?」

passages.original: “No, Mr. Clay, but there's a fellow in your brick-yard flogging two horses to death.
passages.vernacular: 「冇,克萊先生,不過您嘅磚場裡有個傢伙正把兩匹馬抽打致死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,克萊先生,可是您的磚場裡有個傢伙正把兩匹馬抽打致死。

passages.original: I told him to stop, and he wouldn't; I said I'd help him to lighten the cart, and he wouldn't; so I have come to tell you.
passages.vernacular: 我叫佢停下,佢唔肯;我講我嚟幫佢把車卸輕,佢唔肯;所以我嚟告訴您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫他停下,他不肯;我說我來幫他把車卸輕,他不肯;所以我來告訴您。

passages.original: Pray, sir, go.”
passages.vernacular: 請您去吧,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請您去吧,先生。」

passages.original: Joe's voice shook with excitement.
passages.vernacular: 喬嘅聲音因激動而顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬的聲音因激動而顫抖。

passages.original: “Thank ye, my lad,” said the man, running in for his hat; then pausing for a moment, “Will you give evidence of what you saw if I should bring the fellow up before a magistrate?”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,細路,」嗰人講,跑進去攞帽子;然後停咗一下,「如果我把嗰傢伙帶到治安官面前,你願意為你睇見嘅作證嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,孩子,」那人說,跑進去拿帽子;然後停了一下,「如果我把那傢伙帶到治安官面前,你願意為你看見的作證嗎?」

passages.original: “That I will,” said Joe, “and glad too.”
passages.vernacular: 「我願意,」喬講,「而且好樂意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我願意,」喬說,「而且很樂意。」

passages.original: The man was gone, and we were on our way home at a smart trot.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人走喇,我哋以輕快嘅小跑回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人走了,我們以輕快的小跑回家。

passages.original: “Why, what's the matter with you, Joe?
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,你點喇,喬?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,你怎麼了,喬?

passages.original: You look angry all over,” said John, as the boy flung himself from the saddle.
passages.vernacular: 你渾身睇起嚟都喺生氣,」約翰講,男孩從鞍子上一躍而下。
