passages.original: As the sound came nearer and nearer I was almost sure I could distinguish Ginger's step; a little nearer still, and I could tell she was in the dog-cart.
passages.vernacular: 隨住聲音越嚟越近,我幾乎確信我能分辨出金姐嘅步伐;再近啲,我能聽出佢係拉住狗車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著聲音越來越近,我幾乎確信我能分辨出金姐的步伐;再近一點,我能聽出她是拉著狗車。

passages.original: I neighed loudly, and was overjoyed to hear an answering neigh from Ginger, and men's voices.
passages.vernacular: 我大聲嘶鳴,好高興聽到金姐嘅回應嘶鳴同男人哋嘅講話聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我大聲嘶鳴,很高興聽到金姐的回應嘶鳴和男人們的說話聲。

passages.original: They came slowly over the stones, and stopped at the dark figure that lay upon the ground.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋慢慢走過石頭路,喺躺喺地上嘅黑影旁停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們慢慢走過石頭路,在躺在地上的黑影旁停下。

passages.original: One of the men jumped out, and stooped down over it.
passages.vernacular: 其中一人跳下嚟,俯身睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一人跳下來,俯身看著它。

passages.original: “It is Reuben,” he said, “and he does not stir!”
passages.vernacular: 「係呂本,」佢講,「佢一動不動!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是呂本,」他說,「他一動不動!」

passages.original: The other man followed, and bent over him.
passages.vernacular: 另一人跟咗過去,俯身睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一人跟了過去,俯身看他。

passages.original: “He's dead,” he said; “feel how cold his hands are.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢死喇,」佢講;「摸摸佢嘅手多冷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他死了,」他說;「摸摸他的手多冷。」

passages.original: They raised him up, but there was no life, and his hair was soaked with blood.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把佢扶起嚟,但已冇生命,佢嘅頭髮被血浸透喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把他扶起來,但已沒有生命,他的頭髮被血浸透了。

passages.original: They laid him down again, and came and looked at me.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又把佢放下,過嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又把他放下,過來看我。

passages.original: They soon saw my cut knees.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好快睇見咗我受傷嘅膝蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們很快看見了我受傷的膝蓋。

passages.original: “Why, the horse has been down and thrown him!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,呢匹馬摔倒喇,把佢甩咗出去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,這匹馬摔倒了,把他甩了出去!

passages.original: Who would have thought the black horse would have done that?
passages.vernacular: 邊個能想到黑馬會咁樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰能想到黑馬會這樣?

passages.original: Nobody thought he could fall.
passages.vernacular: 冇人想過佢會摔倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人想過他會摔倒。

passages.original: Reuben must have been lying here for hours!
passages.vernacular: 呂本一定喺呢度躺咗好幾個小時喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呂本一定在這裡躺了好幾個小時了!

passages.original: Odd, too, that the horse has not moved from the place.”
passages.vernacular: 仲有奇怪嘅係,馬一步都冇離開嗰個地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有奇怪的是,馬一步也沒離開那個地方。」

passages.original: Robert then attempted to lead me forward.
passages.vernacular: 羅伯特然後試圖牽我向前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅伯特然後試圖牽我向前。

passages.original: I made a step, but almost fell again.
passages.vernacular: 我邁咗一步,幾乎又摔倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我邁了一步,幾乎又摔倒。

passages.original: “Halloo! he's bad in his foot as well as his knees.
passages.vernacular: 「喂!佢腳都壞喇,膝蓋都壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂!他腳也壞了,膝蓋也壞了。

passages.original: Look here--his hoof is cut all to pieces; he might well come down, poor fellow!
passages.vernacular: 睇呢兒——佢嘅蹄子被劃得一塌糊塗;佢難怪會摔倒,可憐嘅傢伙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看這兒——他的蹄子被劃得一塌糊塗;他難怪會摔倒,可憐的傢伙!

passages.original: I tell you what, Ned, I'm afraid it hasn't been all right with Reuben.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你,內德,我怕呂本呢事不太對勁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你,內德,我怕呂本這事不太對勁。

passages.original: Just think of his riding a horse over these stones without a shoe!
passages.vernacular: 想想佢騎住一匹冇蹄鐵嘅馬走過呢啲石頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想他騎著一匹沒有蹄鐵的馬走過這些石頭!

passages.original: Why, if he had been in his right senses he would just as soon have tried to ride him over the moon.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,如果佢神志清醒,佢寧可試住騎佢到月亮上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,如果他神志清醒,他寧可試著騎他到月亮上去。

passages.original: I'm afraid it has been the old thing over again.
passages.vernacular: 我怕又係老毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕又是老毛病。

passages.original: Poor Susan! she looked awfully pale when she came to my house to ask if he had not come home.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅蘇珊!佢到我家問佢回嚟咗冇,臉色可怕地蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的蘇珊!她到我家問他回來了沒有,臉色可怕地蒼白。

passages.original: She made believe she was not a bit anxious, and talked of a lot of things that might have kept him.
passages.vernacular: 佢假裝啲都不擔心,談咗許多可能耽擱佢嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她假裝一點也不擔心,談了許多可能耽擱他的事。

passages.original: But for all that she begged me to go and meet him.
passages.vernacular: 但儘管如此,佢懇求我去接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但儘管如此,她懇求我去接他。

passages.original: But what must we do?
passages.vernacular: 不過我哋該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我們該怎麼辦?

passages.original: There's the horse to get home as well as the body, and that will be no easy matter.”
passages.vernacular: 馬要弄回家,屍體都要,嗰可唔容易。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬要弄回家,屍體也要,那可不容易。」

passages.original: Then followed a conversation between them, till it was agreed that Robert, as the groom, should lead me, and that Ned must take the body.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋商量咗一番,商定羅伯特作為馬夫牽我,內德負責屍體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們商量了一番,商定羅伯特作為馬夫牽我,內德負責屍體。

passages.original: It was a hard job to get it into the dog-cart, for there was no one to hold Ginger; but she knew as well as I did what was going on, and stood as still as a stone.
passages.vernacular: 把佢弄進狗車好費勁,因為冇人扶住金姐;但佢同我一樣清楚正在發生乜嘢,站得像石頭一樣不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把它弄進狗車很費勁,因為沒人扶著金姐;但她和我一樣清楚正在發生什麼,站得像石頭一樣不動。

passages.original: I noticed that, because, if she had a fault, it was that she was impatient in standing.
passages.vernacular: 我注意到呢啲,因為如果佢有缺點,就係站住時不耐煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我注意到這一點,因為如果她有缺點,就是站著時不耐煩。

passages.original: Ned started off very slowly with his sad load, and Robert came and looked at my foot again; then he took his handkerchief and bound it closely round, and so he led me home.
passages.vernacular: 內德載住佢悲傷嘅貨物好慢地出發喇,羅伯特過嚟又睇咗睇我嘅腳;然後佢攞出手帕緊緊裹住,就咁樣牽我回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內德載著他悲傷的貨物非常慢地出發了,羅伯特過來又看了看我的腳;然後他拿出手帕緊緊裹住,就這樣牽我回家。

passages.original: I shall never forget that night walk; it was more than three miles.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會忘記嗰次夜路;有三英里多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會忘記那次夜路;有三英里多。

passages.original: Robert led me on very slowly, and I limped and hobbled on as well as I could with great pain.
passages.vernacular: 羅伯特好慢地牽住我,我帶住劇痛盡我所能一瘸一拐地走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅伯特非常慢地牽著我,我帶著劇痛盡我所能一瘸一拐地走。

passages.original: I am sure he was sorry for me, for he often patted and encouraged me, talking to me in a pleasant voice.
passages.vernacular: 我確信佢為我難過,因為佢常拍我、鼓勵我,用愉快嘅聲音同我講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信他為我難過,因為他常拍我、鼓勵我,用愉快的聲音和我說話。

passages.original: At last I reached my own box, and had some corn; and after Robert had wrapped up my knees in wet cloths, he tied up my foot in a bran poultice, to draw out the heat and cleanse it before the horse-doctor saw it in the morning, and I managed to get myself down on the straw, and slept in spite of the pain.
passages.vernacular: 最後我到咗自己嘅廄,食咗些穀物;羅伯特把我嘅膝蓋用濕布裹好後,又用麩皮膏藥包紮我嘅腳,以便喺早晨馬醫睇之前把熱氣拔出嚟並清潔,我設法躺倒喺稻草上,不顧疼痛瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後我到了自己的廄,吃了些穀物;羅伯特把我的膝蓋用濕布裹好後,又用麩皮膏藥包紮我的腳,以便在早晨馬醫看之前把熱氣拔出來並清潔,我設法躺倒在稻草上,不顧疼痛睡著了。

passages.original: The next day after the farrier had examined my wounds, he said he hoped the joint was not injured; and if so, I should not be spoiled for work, but I should never lose the blemish.
passages.vernacular: 第二天,馬蹄鐵匠檢查咗我嘅傷口,講佢希望關節冇受傷;如果係嗰樣,我唔會幹不咗活,但永遠會有疤痕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,馬蹄鐵匠檢查了我的傷口,說他希望關節沒有受傷;如果是那樣,我不會幹不了活,但永遠會有疤痕。

passages.original: I believe they did the best to make a good cure, but it was a long and painful one.
passages.vernacular: 我相信佢哋盡力要治好,但嗰個係漫長而痛苦嘅過程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信他們盡力要治好,但那是漫長而痛苦的過程。

passages.original: Proud flesh, as they called it, came up in my knees, and was burned out with caustic; and when at last it was healed, they put a blistering fluid over the front of both knees to bring all the hair off; they had some reason for this, and I suppose it was all right.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅膝蓋長出咗佢哋所講嘅「壞肉」,用腐蝕劑燒掉喇;等佢終於癒合,佢哋喺兩個膝蓋前面塗上起泡藥水,把毛全弄掉;佢哋咁樣做有理由,我想都冇錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的膝蓋長出了他們所說的「壞肉」,用腐蝕劑燒掉了;等它終於癒合,他們在兩個膝蓋前面塗上起泡藥水,把毛全弄掉;他們這樣做有理由,我想都沒錯。

passages.original: As Smith's death had been so sudden, and no one was there to see it, there was an inquest held.
passages.vernacular: 由於史密斯嘅死好突然,又冇人在場目睹,舉行咗驗屍調查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由於史密斯的死很突然,又沒人在場目睹,舉行了驗屍調查。

passages.original: The landlord and hostler at the White Lion, with several other people, gave evidence that he was intoxicated when he started from the inn.
passages.vernacular: 白獅客棧嘅店主同馬夫,仲有其他幾個人,作證講佢離開客棧時飲醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白獅客棧的店主和馬夫,還有其他幾個人,作證說他離開客棧時喝醉了。

passages.original: The keeper of the toll-gate said he rode at a hard gallop through the gate; and my shoe was picked up among the stones, so that the case was quite plain to them, and I was cleared of all blame.
passages.vernacular: 收費柵門嘅睇守講佢以飛快嘅速度飛奔住穿過柵門;而我嘅蹄鐵喺石頭中被撿到,所以案情對佢哋好清楚,我被免於一切責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收費柵門的看守說他以飛快的速度飛奔著穿過柵門;而我的蹄鐵在石頭中被撿到,所以案情對他們很清楚,我被免於一切責備。

passages.original: Everybody pitied Susan.
passages.vernacular: 人人都同情蘇珊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人人都同情蘇珊。

passages.original: She was nearly out of her mind; she kept saying over and over again, “Oh! he was so good--so good!
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎神志不清;佢一遍又一遍地講:「哦!佢係咁好——咁好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她幾乎神志不清;她一遍又一遍地說:「哦!他是那麼好——那麼好!

passages.original: It was all that cursed drink; why will they sell that cursed drink?
passages.vernacular: 都係嗰該死嘅酒;佢哋點解要賣嗰該死嘅酒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都是那該死的酒;他們為什麼要賣那該死的酒?

passages.original: Oh Reuben, Reuben!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,呂本,呂本!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,呂本,呂本!」

passages.original: So she went on till after he was buried; and then, as she had no home or relations, she, with her six little children, was obliged once more to leave the pleasant home by the tall oak-trees, and go into that great gloomy Union House.
passages.vernacular: 佢就咁樣直到佢被埋葬;然後,因為佢冇家都冇親戚,佢帶住六個小孩,唔得唔再次離開高大橡樹旁嘅嗰個宜人嘅家,搬進嗰座巨大陰暗嘅濟貧院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就這樣直到他被埋葬;然後,因為她沒有家也沒有親戚,她帶著六個小孩,不得不再次離開高大橡樹旁的那個宜人的家,搬進那座巨大陰暗的濟貧院。

chapters.title: Part II · 27 Ruined and Going Downhill 第二部·27 被毀與走下坡

passages.original: CH As soon as my knees were sufficiently healed I was turned into a small meadow for a month or two; no other creature was there; and though I enjoyed the liberty and the sweet grass, yet I had been so long used to society that I felt very lonely.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅膝蓋一好得差不多,我就被放進一小片草地待咗一兩個月;嗰度冇別嘅生靈;雖然我享受自由同甜草,但我已習慣咗咁長時間嘅社交,感到好孤獨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的膝蓋一好得差不多,我就被放進一小片草地待了一兩個月;那裡沒有別的生靈;雖然我享受自由和甜草,但我已習慣了那麼長時間的社交,感到很孤獨。

passages.original: Ginger and I had become fast friends, and now I missed her company extremely.
passages.vernacular: 金姐同我成咗好朋友,而家我極其想念佢嘅陪伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 金姐和我成了好朋友,現在我極其想念她的陪伴。

passages.original: I often neighed when I heard horses' feet passing in the road, but I seldom got an answer; till one morning the gate was opened, and who should come in but dear old Ginger.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見馬蹄聲從路上經過時常常嘶鳴,但好少得到回答;直到有一天早晨柵門開喇,進嚟嘅唔係別人,正是親愛嘅老金姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見馬蹄聲從路上經過時常常嘶鳴,但很少得到回答;直到有一天早晨柵門開了,進來的不是別人,正是親愛的老金姐。

passages.original: The man slipped off her halter, and left her there.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人解下佢嘅籠頭,把佢留喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人解下她的籠頭,把她留在那裡。

passages.original: With a joyful whinny I trotted up to her; we were both glad to meet, but I soon found that it was not for our pleasure that she was brought to be with me.
passages.vernacular: 我高興地嘶鳴住小跑到佢身邊;我哋倆見面都好高興,但我好快發現,把佢帶嚟同我喺一起並唔係為了我哋嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高興地嘶鳴著小跑到她身邊;我們倆見面都很高興,但我很快發現,把她帶來和我在一起並不是為了我們的快樂。

passages.original: Her story would be too long to tell, but the end of it was that she had been ruined by hard riding, and was now turned off to see what rest would do.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅故事太長喇,但結果係,佢被過度騎行毀喇,而家被趕出嚟睇休息能有乜嘢作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的故事太長了,但結果是,她被過度騎行毀了,現在被趕出來看休息能有什麼作用。

passages.original: Lord George was young and would take no warning; he was a hard rider, and would hunt whenever he could get the chance, quite careless of his horse.
passages.vernacular: 喬治勳爵年輕,不聽警告;佢係個猛騎者,一有機會就去打獵,完全不顧佢嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬治勳爵年輕,不聽警告;他是個猛騎者,一有機會就去打獵,完全不顧他的馬。

passages.original: Soon after I left the stable there was a steeplechase, and he determined to ride.
passages.vernacular: 我離開馬廄不久,有一場障礙賽馬,佢決心參加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我離開馬廄不久,有一場障礙賽馬,他決心參加。

passages.original: Though the groom told him she was a little strained, and was not fit for the race, he did not believe it, and on the day of the race urged Ginger to keep up with the foremost riders.
passages.vernacular: 雖然馬夫告訴佢佢有點勞損,不適合比賽,佢不信,比賽嗰天催金姐跟上最前面嘅騎手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然馬夫告訴他她有點勞損,不適合比賽,他不信,比賽那天催金姐跟上最前面的騎手。

passages.original: With her high spirit, she strained herself to the utmost; she came in with the first three horses, but her wind was touched, besides which he was too heavy for her, and her back was strained.
passages.vernacular: 憑住佢嘅高昂精神,佢拚盡咗全力;佢同前三匹馬一起到達,但佢嘅呼吸受咗損傷,此外佢對佢太重,佢嘅背都勞損喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑著她的高昂精神,她拚盡了全力;她與前三匹馬一起到達,但她的呼吸受了損傷,此外他對她太重,她的背也勞損了。

passages.original: “And so,” she said, “here we are, ruined in the prime of our youth and strength, you by a drunkard, and I by a fool; it is very hard.”
passages.vernacular: 「所以,」佢講,「我哋喺呢度,喺青春力壯嘅年紀被毀喇,你被一個酒鬼,我被一個傻瓜;呢太難受喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以,」她說,「我們在這裡,在青春力壯的年紀被毀了,你被一個酒鬼,我被一個傻瓜;這太難受了。」

passages.original: We both felt in ourselves that we were not what we had been.
passages.vernacular: 我哋倆都覺得自己已唔係以前嘅樣子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們倆都覺得自己已不是以前的樣子了。

passages.original: However, that did not spoil the pleasure we had in each other's company; we did not gallop about as we once did, but we used to feed, and lie down together, and stand for hours under one of the shady lime-trees with our heads close to each other; and so we passed our time till the family returned from town.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢並冇破壞我哋相伴嘅樂趣;我哋唔再像以前嗰樣飛奔,但我哋一起食草、躺下、頭挨住頭喺一棵蔭涼嘅椴樹下一站就係幾個小時;我哋就咁樣打發時間,直到家人從城裡回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這並沒有破壞我們相伴的樂趣;我們不再像以前那樣飛奔,但我們一起吃草、躺下、頭挨著頭在一棵蔭涼的椴樹下一站就是幾個小時;我們就這樣打發時間,直到家人從城裡回來。

passages.original: One day we saw the earl come into the meadow, and York was with him.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,我哋睇見伯爵走進草地,約克同佢喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,我們看見伯爵走進草地,約克和他在一起。

passages.original: Seeing who it was, we stood still under our lime-tree, and let them come up to us.
passages.vernacular: 睇出係邊個,我哋站喺椴樹下冇動,讓佢哋走到我哋跟前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看出是誰,我們站在椴樹下沒動,讓他們走到我們跟前。

passages.original: They examined us carefully.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仔細地檢查咗我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們仔細地檢查了我們。

passages.original: The earl seemed much annoyed.
passages.vernacular: 伯爵似乎好惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伯爵似乎很惱火。

passages.original: “There is three hundred pounds flung away for no earthly use,” said he; “but what I care most for is that these horses of my old friend, who thought they would find a good home with me, are ruined.
passages.vernacular: 「三百英鎊白白扔掉,毫無用處,」佢講;「但我最在意嘅係,我老朋友嘅呢啲馬,佢仲以為佢哋會喺我呢兒得到一個好地方,卻被毀喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「三百英鎊白白扔掉,毫無用處,」他說;「但我最在意的是,我老朋友的這些馬,他還以為它們會在我這兒得到一個好地方,卻被毀了。

passages.original: The mare shall have a twelve-month's run, and we shall see what that will do for her; but the black one, he must be sold; 'tis a great pity, but I could not have knees like these in my stables.”
passages.vernacular: 母馬要有十二個月嘅放牧,睇睇嗰能對佢有乜嘢效果;但黑嘅,必須賣掉;好可惜,但我嘅馬廄裡唔能夠有咁樣嘅膝蓋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母馬要有十二個月的放牧,看看那能對她有什麼效果;但黑的,必須賣掉;很可惜,但我的馬廄裡不能有這樣的膝蓋。」

passages.original: “No, my lord, of course not,” said York; “but he might get a place where appearance is not of much consequence, and still be well treated.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,大人,當然唔能夠,」約克講;「不過佢或者能得到一個不太在意外表嘅地方,仍然被好好對待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,大人,當然不能,」約克說;「不過他也許能得到一個不太在意外表的地方,仍然被好好對待。

passages.original: I know a man in Bath, the master of some livery stables, who often wants a good horse at a low figure; I know he looks well after his horses.
passages.vernacular: 我認識巴思嘅一個人,係啲出租馬廄嘅主人,佢常以低價找好馬;我知道佢好照顧佢嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認識巴思的一個人,是一些出租馬廄的主人,他常以低價找好馬;我知道他很照顧他的馬。

passages.original: The inquest cleared the horse's character, and your lordship's recommendation, or mine, would be sufficient warrant for him.”
passages.vernacular: 驗屍調查洗清咗呢匹馬嘅名譽,大人您嘅推薦或我嘅推薦,足夠為佢作保。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驗屍調查洗清了這匹馬的名譽,大人您的推薦或我的推薦,足夠為他作保。」

passages.original: “You had better write to him, York.
passages.vernacular: 「你最好畀佢寫信,約克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最好給他寫信,約克。

passages.original: I should be more particular about the place than the money he would fetch.”
passages.vernacular: 我更睇重呢個地方,而唔係佢能賣多少錢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我更看重這個地方,而不是他能賣多少錢。」

passages.original: After this they left us.
passages.vernacular: 此後佢哋離開咗我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後他們離開了我們。

passages.original: “They'll soon take you away,” said Ginger, “and I shall lose the only friend I have, and most likely we shall never see each other again.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋好快會把你帶走,」金姐講,「我將失去我唯一嘅朋友,好可能我哋永遠唔會再見面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們很快會把你帶走,」金姐說,「我將失去我唯一的朋友,很可能我們永遠不會再見面。

passages.original: 'Tis a hard world!”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個艱難嘅世界!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個艱難的世界!」

passages.original: About a week after this Robert came into the field with a halter, which he slipped over my head, and led me away.
passages.vernacular: 大約一星期後,羅伯特攞住一個籠頭進咗田野,套喺我頭上,把我牽走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約一星期後,羅伯特拿著一個籠頭進了田野,套在我頭上,把我牽走。

passages.original: There was no leave-taking of Ginger; we neighed to each other as I was led off, and she trotted anxiously along by the hedge, calling to me as long as she could hear the sound of my feet.
passages.vernacular: 冇同金姐告別;我被牽走時我哋互相嘶鳴,佢焦急地沿住樹籬小跑,只要聽得到我嘅蹄聲,佢就一直呼喚我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有同金姐告別;我被牽走時我們互相嘶鳴,她焦急地沿著樹籬小跑,只要聽得到我的蹄聲,她就一直呼喚我。

passages.original: Through the recommendation of York, I was bought by the master of the livery stables.
passages.vernacular: 憑住約克嘅推薦,我被出租馬廄嘅老闆買下喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑著約克的推薦,我被出租馬廄的老闆買下了。

passages.original: I had to go by train, which was new to me, and required a good deal of courage the first time; but as I found the puffing, rushing, whistling, and, more than all, the trembling of the horse-box in which I stood did me no real harm, I soon took it quietly.
passages.vernacular: 我得坐火車去,呢對我係新鮮事,第一次需要不少勇氣;但我發現噴氣、衝撞、鳴笛,尤其係我所站嘅運馬車廂嘅顫動,並冇真正傷害我,我好快就安靜下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得坐火車去,這對我是新鮮事,第一次需要不少勇氣;但我發現噴氣、衝撞、鳴笛,尤其是我所站的運馬車廂的顫動,並沒有真正傷害我,我很快就安靜下來了。

passages.original: When I reached the end of my journey I found myself in a tolerably comfortable stable, and well attended to.
passages.vernacular: 旅程到達終點時,我發現自己喺一個仲算舒適嘅馬廄裡,被照料得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 旅程到達終點時,我發現自己在一個還算舒適的馬廄裡,被照料得很好。

passages.original: These stables were not so airy and pleasant as those I had been used to.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲馬廄不如我習慣嘅嗰啲通風愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些馬廄不如我習慣的那些通風愉快。

passages.original: The stalls were laid on a slope instead of being level, and as my head was kept tied to the manger, I was obliged always to stand on the slope, which was very fatiguing.
passages.vernacular: 馬棚係傾斜嘅,而唔係水平嘅,我嘅頭被拴喺槽上,我唔得不總是站喺斜坡上,呢個好累。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬棚是傾斜的,而不是水平的,我的頭被拴在槽上,我不得不總是站在斜坡上,這非常累。

passages.original: Men do not seem to know yet that horses can do more work if they can stand comfortably and can turn about; however, I was well fed and well cleaned, and, on the whole, I think our master took as much care of us as he could.
passages.vernacular: 人哋似乎仲唔知道,馬如果能舒適地站立、能轉身,就能多幹活;不過,我食得好、洗得乾淨,總嘅來講,我認為我哋嘅主人盡力照顧我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們似乎還不知道,馬如果能舒適地站立、能轉身,就能多幹活;不過,我吃得好、洗得乾淨,總的來說,我認為我們的主人盡力照顧我們。

passages.original: He kept a good many horses and carriages of different kinds for hire.
passages.vernacular: 佢養咗好多出租嘅馬同各種馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他養了很多出租的馬和各種馬車。

passages.original: Sometimes his own men drove them; at others, the horse and chaise were let to gentlemen or ladies who drove themselves.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢自己嘅人駕駛;有時馬同輕便馬車租畀自己駕駛嘅先生或女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他自己的人駕駛;有時馬和輕便馬車租給自己駕駛的先生或女士。

chapters.title: Part II · 28 A Job Horse and His Drivers 第二部·28 臨時馬與牠的駕車人

passages.original: CH Hitherto I had always been driven by people who at least knew how to drive; but in this place I was to get my experience of all the different kinds of bad and ignorant driving to which we horses are subjected; for I was a “job horse”, and was let out to all sorts of people who wished to hire me; and as I was good-tempered and gentle, I think I was oftener let out to the ignorant drivers than some of the other horses, because I could be depended upon.
passages.vernacular: 到此為止,我一直被至少會駕車嘅人駕駛;但喺呢個地方,我要經歷我哋馬所遭受嘅各種各樣嘅壞嘅、無知嘅駕駛;因為我係「臨時馬」,被租畀各種想雇我嘅人;而且因為我脾氣好又溫順,我想比其他啲馬更常被租畀無知嘅駕車人,因為我可以信賴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到此為止,我一直被至少會駕車的人駕駛;但在這個地方,我要經歷我們馬所遭受的各種各樣的壞的、無知的駕駛;因為我是「臨時馬」,被租給各種想雇我的人;而且因為我脾氣好又溫順,我想比其他一些馬更常被租給無知的駕車人,因為我可以信賴。

passages.original: It would take a long time to tell of all the different styles in which I was driven, but I will mention a few of them.
passages.vernacular: 要把我被駕駛嘅所有不同方式都講完要好久,但我要提幾種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要把我被駕駛的所有不同方式都講完要很久,但我要提幾種。

passages.original: First, there were the tight-rein drivers--men who seemed to think that all depended on holding the reins as hard as they could, never relaxing the pull on the horse's mouth, or giving him the least liberty of movement.
passages.vernacular: 首先係緊韁繩嘅駕車人——呢啲人似乎認為一切都取決於盡可能緊地握住韁繩,從不放鬆對馬嘴嘅拉力,或畀馬啲活動自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先是緊韁繩的駕車人——這些人似乎認為一切都取決於盡可能緊地握住韁繩,從不放鬆對馬嘴的拉力,或給馬一點活動自由。

passages.original: They are always talking about “keeping the horse well in hand”, and “holding a horse up”, just as if a horse was not made to hold himself up.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是講「把馬控制好」同「把馬撐住」,好像馬唔係生來就能自己撐住自己似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們總是說「把馬控制好」和「把馬撐住」,好像馬不是生來就能自己撐住自己似的。

passages.original: Some poor, broken-down horses, whose mouths have been made hard and insensible by just such drivers as these, may, perhaps, find some support in it; but for a horse who can depend upon his own legs, and who has a tender mouth and is easily guided, it is not only tormenting, but it is stupid.
passages.vernacular: 啲可憐嘅、垮掉嘅馬,佢哋嘅嘴被咁樣嘅駕車人弄得又硬又麻木,或者能喺其中找到啲支撐;但對於一匹能依靠自己嘅腿、嘴嬌嫩、容易引導嘅馬,呢不僅係折磨,而且係愚蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些可憐的、垮掉的馬,它們的嘴被這樣的駕車人弄得又硬又麻木,也許能在其中找到一些支撐;但對於一匹能依靠自己的腿、嘴嬌嫩、容易引導的馬,這不僅是折磨,而且是愚蠢。

passages.original: Then there are the loose-rein drivers, who let the reins lie easily on our backs, and their own hand rest lazily on their knees.
passages.vernacular: 然後有鬆韁繩嘅駕車人,讓韁繩輕鬆地搭喺我哋背上,自己嘅手懶洋洋地擱喺膝蓋上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有鬆韁繩的駕車人,讓韁繩輕鬆地搭在我們背上,自己的手懶洋洋地擱在膝蓋上。

passages.original: Of course, such gentlemen have no control over a horse, if anything happens suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 當然,咁樣嘅先生一旦出咗突發嘅事,對馬就毫無控制力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,這樣的先生一旦出了突發的事,對馬就毫無控制力。

passages.original: If a horse shies, or starts, or stumbles, they are nowhere, and cannot help the horse or themselves till the mischief is done.
passages.vernacular: 如果馬驚跳、受驚或絆倒,佢哋就無能為力,直到禍已造成,才能幫馬或幫自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果馬驚跳、受驚或絆倒,他們就無能為力,直到禍已造成,才能幫馬或幫自己。

passages.original: Of course, for myself I had no objection to it, as I was not in the habit either of starting or stumbling, and had only been used to depend on my driver for guidance and encouragement.
passages.vernacular: 當然,就我自己來講,我對此冇異議,因為我冇受驚或絆倒嘅習慣,只習慣依靠我嘅駕車人畀予引導同鼓勵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,就我自己來說,我對此沒有異議,因為我沒有受驚或絆倒的習慣,只習慣依靠我的駕車人給予引導和鼓勵。

passages.original: Still, one likes to feel the rein a little in going downhill, and likes to know that one's driver is not gone to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 不過,人哋定係鍾意下坡時感覺到啲韁繩,鍾意知道自己嘅駕車人冇瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,人們還是喜歡下坡時感覺到一點韁繩,喜歡知道自己的駕車人沒有睡著。

passages.original: Besides, a slovenly way of driving gets a horse into bad and often lazy habits, and when he changes hands he has to be whipped out of them with more or less pain and trouble.
passages.vernacular: 此外,邋遢嘅駕車方式使馬養成壞嘅、常常係懶惰嘅習慣,當佢換咗手時,必須用或多或少嘅痛苦同麻煩把佢哋鞭打出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,邋遢的駕車方式使馬養成壞的、常常是懶惰的習慣,當他換了手時,必須用或多或少的痛苦和麻煩把他們鞭打出來。

passages.original: Squire Gordon always kept us to our best paces and our best manners.
passages.vernacular: 戈登鄉紳總是讓我哋保持最好嘅步伐同最好嘅風度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戈登鄉紳總是讓我們保持最好的步伐和最好的風度。

passages.original: He said that spoiling a horse and letting him get into bad habits was just as cruel as spoiling a child, and both had to suffer for it afterward.
passages.vernacular: 佢講糟蹋一匹馬、讓佢染上壞習慣,同寵壞一個細路一樣殘忍,兩者之後都要為此受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說糟蹋一匹馬、讓他染上壞習慣,和寵壞一個孩子一樣殘忍,兩者之後都要為此受苦。

passages.original: Besides, these drivers are often careless altogether, and will attend to anything else more than their horses.
passages.vernacular: 此外,呢啲駕車人往往完全粗心,對別嘅事比對馬仲要留意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,這些駕車人往往完全粗心,對別的事比對馬還要留意。

passages.original: I went out in the phaeton one day with one of them; he had a lady and two children behind.
passages.vernacular: 有一天我同其中一個坐四輪敞篷馬車出去;佢後面有一位女士同兩個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我同其中一個坐四輪敞篷馬車出去;他後面有一位女士和兩個孩子。

passages.original: He flopped the reins about as we started, and of course gave me several unmeaning cuts with the whip, though I was fairly off.
passages.vernacular: 我哋出發時,佢把韁繩甩嚟甩去,當然仲毫無意義地抽咗我幾鞭,雖然我已經喺正常出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們出發時,他把韁繩甩來甩去,當然還毫無意義地抽了我幾鞭,雖然我已經在正常出發。

passages.original: There had been a good deal of road-mending going on, and even where the stones were not freshly laid down there were a great many loose ones about.
passages.vernacular: 有好多修路嘅活動,即使石頭唔係剛鋪嘅,周圍都有好多鬆動嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有很多修路的活動,即使石頭不是剛鋪的,周圍也有很多鬆動的。

passages.original: My driver was laughing and joking with the lady and the children, and talking about the country to the right and the left; but he never thought it worth while to keep an eye on his horse or to drive on the smoothest parts of the road; and so it easily happened that I got a stone in one of my fore feet.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅駕車人同女士同細路哋講笑,談論左右兩邊嘅鄉間;但佢從不覺得值得留意佢嘅馬,或者喺路面最平整嘅地方駕駛;所以好容易地我嘅一隻前蹄裡進咗一塊石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的駕車人同女士和孩子們說笑,談論左右兩邊的鄉間;但他從不覺得值得留意他的馬,或者在路面最平整的地方駕駛;所以很容易地我的一隻前蹄裡進了一塊石頭。

passages.original: Now, if Mr. Gordon or John, or in fact any good driver, had been there, he would have seen that something was wrong before I had gone three paces.
passages.vernacular: 而家,如果戈登先生或約翰,或者實際上任何好嘅駕車人喺嗰度,佢喺我走咗三步之前就會睇出有乜嘢不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,如果戈登先生或約翰,或者實際上任何好的駕車人在那裡,他在我走了三步之前就會看出有什麼不對。

passages.original: Or even if it had been dark a practiced hand would have felt by the rein that there was something wrong in the step, and they would have got down and picked out the stone.
passages.vernacular: 或者即使天黑喇,有經驗嘅手都會從韁繩上感到步伐裡有乜嘢不對,佢哋會下嚟把石頭挑出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者即使天黑了,有經驗的手也會從韁繩上感到步伐裡有什麼不對,他們會下來把石頭挑出去。

passages.original: But this man went on laughing and talking, while at every step the stone became more firmly wedged between my shoe and the frog of my foot.
passages.vernacular: 但呢個人一邊笑一邊講話,而每走一步,嗰塊石頭就更牢地楔喺我嘅蹄鐵同蹄叉之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這個人一邊笑一邊說話,而每走一步,那塊石頭就更牢地楔在我的蹄鐵和蹄叉之間。

passages.original: The stone was sharp on the inside and round on the outside, which, as every one knows, is the most dangerous kind that a horse can pick up, at the same time cutting his foot and making him most liable to stumble and fall.
passages.vernacular: 石頭裡面尖銳,外面圓滑,呢個係人人都知道嘅馬可能撿到嘅最危險嘅一種,同時割傷佢嘅腳,使佢最容易絆倒摔跤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 石頭裡面尖銳,外面圓滑,這是人人都知道的馬可能撿到的最危險的一種,同時割傷他的腳,使他最容易絆倒摔跤。

passages.original: Whether the man was partly blind or only very careless I can't say, but he drove me with that stone in my foot for a good half-mile before he saw anything.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人係眼睛有點瞎定係只係好粗心,我講不上,但佢讓我帶住嗰塊石頭走咗足足半英里才睇出乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人是眼睛有點瞎還是只是非常粗心,我說不上,但他讓我帶著那塊石頭走了足足半英里才看出什麼。

passages.original: By that time I was going so lame with the pain that at last he saw it, and called out, “Well, here's a go!
passages.vernacular: 嗰時我痛得瘸得咁厲害,佢終於睇到喇,喊道:「哎呀,呢下好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時我痛得瘸得那麼厲害,他終於看到了,喊道:「哎呀,這下好了!

passages.original: Why, they have sent us out with a lame horse!
passages.vernacular: 嗨,佢哋畀我哋派咗一匹瘸馬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,他們給我們派了一匹瘸馬!

passages.original: What a shame!”
passages.vernacular: 真丟人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真丟人!」

passages.original: He then chucked the reins and flipped about with the whip, saying, “Now, then, it's no use playing the old soldier with me; there's the journey to go, and it's no use turning lame and lazy.”
passages.vernacular: 佢然後猛拉韁繩,用鞭子亂抽,講:「而家,別對我裝老兵喇;仲有路程要走,瘸咗同偷懶都冇用。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他然後猛拉韁繩,用鞭子亂抽,說:「現在,別對我裝老兵了;還有路程要走,瘸了和偷懶都沒用。」

passages.original: Just at this time a farmer came riding up on a brown cob.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,一個農夫騎住一匹棕色矮腳馬過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,一個農夫騎著一匹棕色矮腳馬過來。

passages.original: He lifted his hat and pulled up.
passages.vernacular: 佢舉起帽子,勒住咗馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他舉起帽子,勒住了馬。

passages.original: “I beg your pardon, sir,” he said, “but I think there is something the matter with your horse; he goes very much as if he had a stone in his shoe.
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒,先生,」佢講,「但我想您嘅馬有點問題;佢走起嚟好像蹄鐵裡有塊石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒,先生,」他說,「但我想您的馬有點問題;他走起來很像蹄鐵裡有塊石頭。

passages.original: If you will allow me I will look at his feet; these loose scattered stones are confounded dangerous things for the horses.”
passages.vernacular: 如果您允許,我嚟睇睇佢嘅蹄子;呢啲鬆散嘅石頭對馬係糟透咗嘅危險嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您允許,我來看看他的蹄子;這些鬆散的石頭對馬是糟透了的危險東西。」

passages.original: “He's a hired horse,” said my driver.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係租嚟嘅馬,」我嘅駕車人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是租來的馬,」我的駕車人說。

passages.original: “I don't know what's the matter with him, but it is a great shame to send out a lame beast like this.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道佢點喇,但派出咁樣一匹瘸牲口,真丟人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道他怎麼了,但派出這樣一匹瘸牲口,真丟人。」

passages.original: The farmer dismounted, and slipping his rein over his arm at once took up my near foot.
passages.vernacular: 農夫下咗馬,把韁繩套喺胳膊上,即刻抬起咗我嘅近側前蹄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農夫下了馬,把韁繩套在胳膊上,立刻抬起了我的近側前蹄。

passages.original: “Bless me, there's a stone!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,有一塊石頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,有一塊石頭!

passages.original: Lame!
passages.vernacular: 瘸喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瘸了!

passages.original: I should think so!”
passages.vernacular: 我想係啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想是啊!」

passages.original: At first he tried to dislodge it with his hand, but as it was now very tightly wedged he drew a stone-pick out of his pocket, and very carefully and with some trouble got it out.
passages.vernacular: 起初佢試住用手把佢弄出嚟,但而家佢楔得好緊,佢從口袋裡掏出一把挑石器,好小心、費咗些力氣把佢挑咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初他試著用手把它弄出來,但現在它楔得很緊,他從口袋裡掏出一把挑石器,非常小心、費了些力氣把它挑了出來。

passages.original: Then holding it up he said, “There, that's the stone your horse had picked up.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把佢舉起來講:「瞧,呢個就係你嘅馬撿到嘅石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他把它舉起來說:「瞧,這就是你的馬撿到的石頭。

passages.original: It is a wonder he did not fall down and break his knees into the bargain!”
passages.vernacular: 佢冇跌倒摔斷膝蓋,真係奇蹟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有跌倒摔斷膝蓋,真是奇蹟!」

passages.original: “Well, to be sure!” said my driver; “that is a queer thing!
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真嘅!」我嘅駕車人講;「呢真係怪事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真的!」我的駕車人說;「這真是怪事!

passages.original: I never knew that horses picked up stones before.”
passages.vernacular: 我從唔知道馬會撿到石頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從不知道馬會撿到石頭。」

passages.original: “Didn't you?” said the farmer rather contemptuously; “but they do, though, and the best of them will do it, and can't help it sometimes on such roads as these.
passages.vernacular: 「唔知道嗎?」農夫相當輕蔑地講;「不過佢哋會,最好嘅馬都會,喺咁樣嘅路上有時避免不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知道嗎?」農夫相當輕蔑地說;「不過它們會,最好的馬也會,在這樣的路上有時避免不了。

passages.original: And if you don't want to lame your horse you must look sharp and get them out quickly.
passages.vernacular: 如果你唔想讓你嘅馬瘸,你就必須眼睛銳利,趕快把佢哋弄出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你不想讓你的馬瘸,你就必須眼睛銳利,趕快把它們弄出來。

passages.original: This foot is very much bruised,” he said, setting it gently down and patting me.
passages.vernacular: 呢隻蹄子被擠壓得好厲害,」佢講,輕輕把佢放下,拍住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這隻蹄子被擠壓得很厲害,」他說,輕輕把它放下,拍著我。

passages.original: “If I might advise, sir, you had better drive him gently for awhile; the foot is a good deal hurt, and the lameness will not go off directly.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我可以建議,先生,您最好慢慢地駕佢一陣;蹄子傷得好厲害,瘸唔會即刻好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我可以建議,先生,您最好慢慢地駕他一陣;蹄子傷得很厲害,瘸不會馬上好。」

passages.original: Then mounting his cob and raising his hat to the lady he trotted off.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢騎上矮腳馬,向女士舉帽致意,小跑住走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他騎上矮腳馬,向女士舉帽致意,小跑著走了。

passages.original: When he was gone my driver began to flop the reins about and whip the harness, by which I understood that I was to go on, which of course I did, glad that the stone was gone, but still in a good deal of pain.
passages.vernacular: 佢走後,我嘅駕車人開始甩動韁繩,抽打挽具,我明白我該繼續走,我當然走喇,石頭冇咗好高興,但定係相當痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走後,我的駕車人開始甩動韁繩,抽打挽具,我明白我該繼續走,我當然走了,石頭沒了很高興,但還是相當痛。

passages.original: This was the sort of experience we job horses often came in for.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我哋臨時馬常遇到嘅嗰種經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我們臨時馬常遇到的那種經歷。

chapters.title: Part II · 29 Cockneys 第二部·29 倫敦佬

passages.original: CH Then there is the steam-engine style of driving; these drivers were mostly people from towns, who never had a horse of their own and generally traveled by rail.
passages.vernacular: 仲有蒸汽機式嘅駕駛;呢啲駕車人大多係城裡人,從冇過自己嘅馬,通常乘火車旅行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有蒸汽機式的駕駛;這些駕車人大多是城裡人,從沒有過自己的馬,通常乘火車旅行。

passages.original: They always seemed to think that a horse was something like a steam-engine, only smaller.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋似乎總認為馬有點像蒸汽機,只係小啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們似乎總認為馬有點像蒸汽機,只是小一些。

passages.original: At any rate, they think that if only they pay for it a horse is bound to go just as far and just as fast and with just as heavy a load as they please.
passages.vernacular: 總之,佢哋認為只要付咗錢,馬就一定要走佢哋想要嘅咁遠、咁快、載咁重嘅貨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,他們認為只要付了錢,馬就一定要走他們想要的那麼遠、那麼快、載那麼重的貨。

passages.original: And be the roads heavy and muddy, or dry and good; be they stony or smooth, uphill or downhill, it is all the same--on, on, on, one must go, at the same pace, with no relief and no consideration.
passages.vernacular: 不管路係泥濘難行,定係乾燥良好;係石頭路定係平路,上坡定係下坡,都一樣——走,走,走,必須以同樣嘅速度前進,冇喘息,冇體諒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管路是泥濘難行,還是乾燥良好;是石頭路還是平路,上坡還是下坡,都一樣——走,走,走,必須以同樣的速度前進,沒有喘息,沒有體諒。

passages.original: These people never think of getting out to walk up a steep hill.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人從唔想下車步行上陡坡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人從不想下車步行上陡坡。

passages.original: Oh, no, they have paid to ride, and ride they will!
passages.vernacular: 哦,不,佢哋付咗錢要坐車,就要坐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,不,他們付了錢要坐車,就要坐!

passages.original: The horse?
passages.vernacular: 馬?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬?

passages.original: Oh, he's used to it!
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢習慣喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,他習慣了!

passages.original: What were horses made for, if not to drag people uphill?
passages.vernacular: 馬生來係幹乜嘢嘅,如果唔係拖人上坡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬生來是幹什麼的,如果不是拖人上坡?

passages.original: Walk!
passages.vernacular: 走路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走路!

passages.original: A good joke indeed!
passages.vernacular: 真係個好笑話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真是個好笑話!

passages.original: And so the whip is plied and the rein is chucked and often a rough, scolding voice cries out, “Go along, you lazy beast!”
passages.vernacular: 於是鞭子揮舞,韁繩猛拉,常常一個粗暴責罵嘅聲音大喊:「走啊,你呢懶畜生!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是鞭子揮舞,韁繩猛拉,常常一個粗暴責罵的聲音大喊:「走啊,你這懶畜生!」

passages.original: And then another slash of the whip, when all the time we are doing our very best to get along, uncomplaining and obedient, though often sorely harassed and down-hearted.
passages.vernacular: 然後又係一鞭抽下嚟,而我哋一直盡力前進,不抱怨,順從,雖然常常極其煩惱同沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又是一鞭抽下來,而我們一直盡力前進,不抱怨,順從,雖然常常極其煩惱和沮喪。

passages.original: This steam-engine style of driving wears us up faster than any other kind.
passages.vernacular: 呢種蒸汽機式嘅駕駛比其他任何一種都更快地磨損我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種蒸汽機式的駕駛比其他任何一種都更快地磨損我們。

passages.original: I would far rather go twenty miles with a good considerate driver than I would go ten with some of these; it would take less out of me.
passages.vernacular: 我寧可同一個好嘅、體諒嘅駕車人走二十英里,都唔願同其中啲人走十英里;嗰樣對我嘅消耗要小。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧可同一個好的、體諒的駕車人走二十英里,也不願同其中一些人走十英里;那樣對我的消耗要小。

passages.original: Another thing, they scarcely ever put on the brake, however steep the downhill may be, and thus bad accidents sometimes happen; or if they do put it on, they often forget to take it off at the bottom of the hill, and more than once I have had to pull halfway up the next hill, with one of the wheels held by the brake, before my driver chose to think about it; and that is a terrible strain on a horse.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一件事,佢哋幾乎從不踩剎車,不論下坡多陡,因此有時發生嚴重事故;或者即使佢哋踩喇,佢哋往往忘咗喺山腳下鬆開,我不止一次唔得不喺一個輪子被剎車抱住嘅情況下,拉上下一座山嘅一半,我嘅駕車人才想到;嗰對馬係可怕嘅勞損。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一件事,他們幾乎從不踩剎車,不論下坡多陡,因此有時發生嚴重事故;或者即使他們踩了,他們往往忘了在山腳下鬆開,我不止一次不得不在一個輪子被剎車抱住的情況下,拉上下一座山的一半,我的駕車人才想到;那對馬是可怕的勞損。

passages.original: Then these cockneys, instead of starting at an easy pace, as a gentleman would do, generally set off at full speed from the very stable-yard; and when they want to stop, they first whip us, and then pull up so suddenly that we are nearly thrown on our haunches, and our mouths jagged with the bit--they call that pulling up with a dash; and when they turn a corner they do it as sharply as if there were no right side or wrong side of the road.
passages.vernacular: 然後呢啲倫敦佬,不像紳士嗰樣以輕鬆嘅步伐出發,而通常係從馬廄院子就全速出發;要停嘅時候,佢哋先抽我哋,然後突然勒住,我哋幾乎被甩到臀部上,嘴被嚼子磨傷——佢哋管嗰叫「瀟灑地停車」;轉彎時,佢哋轉得咁急,好像路上冇左邊右邊之分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後這些倫敦佬,不像紳士那樣以輕鬆的步伐出發,而通常是從馬廄院子就全速出發;要停的時候,他們先抽我們,然後突然勒住,我們幾乎被甩到臀部上,嘴被嚼子磨傷——他們管那叫「瀟灑地停車」;轉彎時,他們轉得那麼急,好像路上沒有左邊右邊之分。

passages.original: I well remember one spring evening I and Rory had been out for the day.
passages.vernacular: 我清楚地記得一個春天嘅傍晚,我同羅里出去咗一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我清楚地記得一個春天的傍晚,我和羅里出去了一天。

passages.original: (Rory was the horse that mostly went with me when a pair was ordered, and a good honest fellow he was.)
passages.vernacular: (羅里係要求駕一對時通常同我一起嘅馬,係個誠實嘅好夥計。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (羅里是要求駕一對時通常同我一起的馬,是個誠實的好夥計。)

passages.original: We had our own driver, and as he was always considerate and gentle with us, we had a very pleasant day.
passages.vernacular: 我哋有自己嘅駕車人,佢對我哋總是體貼溫和,所以我哋過咗愉快嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們有自己的駕車人,他對我們總是體貼溫和,所以我們過了愉快的一天。

passages.original: We were coming home at a good smart pace, about twilight.
passages.vernacular: 黃昏時分,我哋以相當快嘅步伐回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黃昏時分,我們以相當快的步伐回家。

passages.original: Our road turned sharp to the left; but as we were close to the hedge on our own side, and there was plenty of room to pass, our driver did not pull us in.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅路向左急轉;但因為我哋靠近自己一側嘅樹籬,有好多地方讓人通過,我哋嘅駕車人冇把我哋拉進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的路向左急轉;但因為我們靠近自己一側的樹籬,有很多地方讓人通過,我們的駕車人沒有把我們拉進。

passages.original: As we neared the corner I heard a horse and two wheels coming rapidly down the hill toward us.
passages.vernacular: 我哋走近拐角時,我聽到一匹馬同一輛兩輪車從山上急速向我哋衝下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們走近拐角時,我聽到一匹馬和一輛兩輪車從山上急速向我們衝下來。

passages.original: The hedge was high, and I could see nothing, but the next moment we were upon each other.
passages.vernacular: 樹籬好高,我乜嘢都睇唔見,但下一刻我哋就撞喺一起喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樹籬很高,我什麼也看不見,但下一刻我們就撞在一起了。

passages.original: Happily for me, I was on the side next the hedge.
passages.vernacular: 對我來講幸運嘅係,我喺靠近樹籬嘅一側。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說幸運的是,我在靠近樹籬的一側。

passages.original: Rory was on the left side of the pole, and had not even a shaft to protect him.
passages.vernacular: 羅里喺車轅嘅左側,連一根轅桿都冇保護佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅里在車轅的左側,連一根轅桿也沒有保護他。

passages.original: The man who was driving was making straight for the corner, and when he came in sight of us he had no time to pull over to his own side.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個駕車人正直衝拐角,佢睇到我哋時,嚟不及拉到自己嗰一側。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個駕車人正直衝拐角,他看到我們時,來不及拉到自己那一側。

passages.original: The whole shock came upon Rory.
passages.vernacular: 整個衝擊都落喺羅里身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個衝擊都落在羅里身上。

passages.original: The gig shaft ran right into the chest, making him stagger back with a cry that I shall never forget.
passages.vernacular: 輕便馬車嘅轅桿直插進胸部,使佢踉蹌後退,發出一聲我永遠唔會忘記嘅叫聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕便馬車的轅桿直插進胸部,使他踉蹌後退,發出一聲我永遠不會忘記的叫聲。

passages.original: The other horse was thrown upon his haunches and one shaft broken.
passages.vernacular: 另一匹馬被甩到臀部上,一根轅桿斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一匹馬被甩到臀部上,一根轅桿斷了。

passages.original: It turned out that it was a horse from our own stables, with the high-wheeled gig that the young men were so fond of.
passages.vernacular: 結果嗰個係我哋自己馬廄裡嘅一匹馬,拉住年輕人咁鍾意嘅高輪輕便馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果那是我們自己馬廄裡的一匹馬,拉著年輕人那麼喜歡的高輪輕便馬車。

passages.original: The driver was one of those random, ignorant fellows, who don't even know which is their own side of the road, or, if they know, don't care.
passages.vernacular: 駕車人係嗰種隨意、無知嘅傢伙,佢哋連自己係路嘅邊一邊都唔知道,或者,如果知道,都不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 駕車人是那種隨意、無知的傢伙,他們連自己是路的哪一邊都不知道,或者,如果知道,也不在乎。

passages.original: And there was poor Rory with his flesh torn open and bleeding, and the blood streaming down.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅羅里,肉被撕開,流住血,血流如注。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的羅里,肉被撕開,流著血,血流如注。

passages.original: They said if it had been a little more to one side it would have killed him; and a good thing for him, poor fellow, if it had.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講如果再偏啲點,就會要咗佢嘅命;如果嗰樣,對佢係好事,可憐嘅傢伙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說如果再偏一點點,就會要了他的命;如果那樣,對他是好事,可憐的傢伙。

passages.original: As it was, it was a long time before the wound healed, and then he was sold for coal-carting; and what that is, up and down those steep hills, only horses know.
passages.vernacular: 結果,傷口好久才癒合,然後佢被賣去拉煤車;喺嗰啲陡坡上上下下拉煤車係點回事,只有馬才知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果,傷口很久才癒合,然後他被賣去拉煤車;在那些陡坡上上下下拉煤車是怎麼回事,只有馬才知道。

passages.original: Some of the sights I saw there, where a horse had to come downhill with a heavily loaded two-wheel cart behind him, on which no brake could be placed, make me sad even now to think of.
passages.vernacular: 我喺嗰度睇到嘅啲景象,一匹馬要下坡,後面拖著重載嘅兩輪車,唔能夠裝剎車,想起嚟至今仍讓我難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在那裡看到的一些景象,一匹馬要下坡,後面拖著重載的兩輪車,不能裝剎車,想起來至今仍讓我難過。

passages.original: After Rory was disabled I often went in the carriage with a mare named Peggy, who stood in the next stall to mine.
passages.vernacular: 羅里殘廢後,我常同一匹叫佩吉嘅母馬一起拉車,佢站喺我隔壁嘅馬棚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅里殘廢後,我常同一匹叫佩吉的母馬一起拉車,她站在我隔壁的馬棚。

passages.original: She was a strong, well-made animal, of a bright dun color, beautifully dappled, and with a dark-brown mane and tail.
passages.vernacular: 佢係匹強壯、體格好嘅牲口,係明亮嘅灰褐色,斑紋漂亮,有深棕色嘅鬃毛同尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是匹強壯、體格好的牲口,是明亮的灰褐色,斑紋漂亮,有深棕色的鬃毛和尾巴。

passages.original: There was no high breeding about her, but she was very pretty and remarkably sweet-tempered and willing.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇高貴血統,但好漂亮,脾氣特別溫順、肯幹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒有高貴血統,但很漂亮,脾氣特別溫順、肯幹。

passages.original: Still, there was an anxious look about her eye, by which I knew that she had some trouble.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢眼睛裡有一種焦慮嘅神色,我由此知道佢有心事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她眼睛裡有一種焦慮的神色,我由此知道她有心事。

passages.original: The first time we went out together I thought she had a very odd pace; she seemed to go partly a trot, partly a canter, three or four paces, and then a little jump forward.
passages.vernacular: 我哋第一次一起出去時,我覺得佢嘅步伐好奇怪;佢似乎一半小跑、一半跑,三四步,然後向前小小地一跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們第一次一起出去時,我覺得她的步伐很奇怪;她似乎一半小跑、一半跑,三四步,然後向前小小地一跳。

passages.original: It was very unpleasant for any horse who pulled with her, and made me quite fidgety.
passages.vernacular: 呢對任何同佢一起拉車嘅馬都好不舒服,讓我好不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對任何同她一起拉車的馬都很不舒服,讓我非常不安。

passages.original: When we got home I asked her what made her go in that odd, awkward way.
passages.vernacular: 我哋回家後,我問佢係乜嘢使佢走得嗰樣古怪、笨拙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們回家後,我問她是什麼使她走得那樣古怪、笨拙。

passages.original: “Ah,” she said in a troubled manner, “I know my paces are very bad, but what can I do?
passages.vernacular: 「啊,」佢不安地講,「我知道我嘅步伐好糟,但我能點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,」她不安地說,「我知道我的步伐很糟,但我能怎麼辦?

passages.original: It really is not my fault; it is just because my legs are so short.
passages.vernacular: 呢真唔係我嘅錯;只係因為我嘅腿太短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這真不是我的錯;只是因為我的腿太短。

passages.original: I stand nearly as high as you, but your legs are a good three inches longer above your knee than mine, and of course you can take a much longer step and go much faster.
passages.vernacular: 我站得幾乎同你一樣高,但你嘅腿膝蓋以上足足比我長三英寸,當然你能邁大得多嘅步子,走得快得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站得幾乎和你一樣高,但你的腿膝蓋以上足足比我長三英寸,當然你能邁大得多的步子,走得快得多。

passages.original: You see I did not make myself.
passages.vernacular: 你睇,我唔係我自己造嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,我不是我自己造的。

passages.original: I wish I could have done so; I would have had long legs then.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我能自己造;嗰樣我就會有長腿喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我能自己造;那樣我就會有長腿了。

passages.original: All my troubles come from my short legs,” said Peggy, in a desponding tone.
passages.vernacular: 我所有嘅煩惱都來自我嘅短腿,」佩吉用沮喪嘅語氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所有的煩惱都來自我的短腿,」佩吉用沮喪的語氣說。

passages.original: “But how is it,” I said, “when you are so strong and good-tempered and willing?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過點會咁樣呢,」我講,「你咁強壯、脾氣好又肯幹?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是怎麼會這樣呢,」我說,「你那麼強壯、脾氣好又肯幹?」

passages.original: “Why, you see,” said she, “men will go so fast, and if one can't keep up to other horses it is nothing but whip, whip, whip, all the time.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,你睇,」佢講,「人哋要走得咁快,如果你跟不上別嘅馬,就一直只有鞭子、鞭子、鞭子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,你看,」她說,「人們要走得那麼快,如果你跟不上別的馬,就一直只有鞭子、鞭子、鞭子。

passages.original: And so I have had to keep up as I could, and have got into this ugly shuffling pace.
passages.vernacular: 所以我唔得不盡我所能跟上,就養成咗呢種難睇嘅拖拽步伐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我不得不盡我所能跟上,就養成了這種難看的拖拽步伐。

passages.original: It was not always so; when I lived with my first master I always went a good regular trot, but then he was not in such a hurry.
passages.vernacular: 並不總是咁樣;我同我嘅第一個主人喺一起時,我總是走好好嘅規律小跑,但佢冇咁住急。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並不總是這樣;我同我的第一個主人在一起時,我總是走很好的規律小跑,但他沒那麼著急。

passages.original: He was a young clergyman in the country, and a good, kind master he was.
passages.vernacular: 佢係鄉下嘅一位年輕牧師,係個善良嘅好主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是鄉下的一位年輕牧師,是個善良的好主人。

passages.original: He had two churches a good way apart, and a great deal of work, but he never scolded or whipped me for not going faster.
passages.vernacular: 佢有兩座離得好遠嘅教堂,有好多工作,但佢從不因為我走得不快而罵我或抽我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有兩座離得很遠的教堂,有很多工作,但他從不因為我走得不快而罵我或抽我。

passages.original: He was very fond of me.
passages.vernacular: 佢好鍾意我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常喜歡我。

passages.original: I only wish I was with him now; but he had to leave and go to a large town, and then I was sold to a farmer.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望而家仲同佢喺一起;但佢得離開去大城市,然後我被賣畀咗一個農夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望現在還同他在一起;但他得離開去大城市,然後我被賣給了一個農夫。

passages.original: “Some farmers, you know, are capital masters; but I think this one was a low sort of man.
passages.vernacular: 「有些農夫,你知道,係絕好嘅主人;但我覺得呢個係個下等嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有些農夫,你知道,是絕好的主人;但我覺得這個是個下等的人。

passages.original: He cared nothing about good horses or good driving; he only cared for going fast.
passages.vernacular: 佢完全不在乎好馬或好嘅駕駛;佢只在乎走得快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他完全不在乎好馬或好的駕駛;他只在乎走得快。

passages.original: I went as fast as I could, but that would not do, and he was always whipping; so I got into this way of making a spring forward to keep up.
passages.vernacular: 我盡我所能快地走,但嗰不行,佢總是喺抽;所以我就養成咗呢種往前一跳以跟上嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我盡我所能快地走,但那不行,他總是在抽;所以我就養成了這種往前一跳以跟上的方式。

passages.original: On market nights he used to stay very late at the inn, and then drive home at a gallop.
passages.vernacular: 趕集嘅夜裡佢常喺客棧待到好晚,然後飛奔住駕車回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 趕集的夜裡他常在客棧待到很晚,然後飛奔著駕車回家。

passages.original: “One dark night he was galloping home as usual, when all of a sudden the wheel came against some great heavy thing in the road, and turned the gig over in a minute.
passages.vernacular: 「一個黑夜,佢像往常一樣飛奔回家,忽然車輪撞到路上一個又大又重嘅嘢,一下子把輕便馬車翻咗過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個黑夜,他像往常一樣飛奔回家,忽然車輪撞到路上一個又大又重的東西,一下子把輕便馬車翻了過來。

passages.original: He was thrown out and his arm broken, and some of his ribs, I think.
passages.vernacular: 佢被甩咗出去,胳膊斷喇,我想仲有幾根肋骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他被甩了出去,胳膊斷了,我想還有幾根肋骨。

passages.original: At any rate, it was the end of my living with him, and I was not sorry.
passages.vernacular: 總之,呢結束咗我同佢嘅生活,我不覺得遺憾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,這結束了我同他的生活,我不覺得遺憾。

passages.original: But you see it will be the same everywhere for me, if men must go so fast.
passages.vernacular: 但你睇,如果人哋一定要走得咁快,對我來講到處都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你看,如果人們一定要走得這麼快,對我來說到處都一樣。

passages.original: I wish my legs were longer!”
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我嘅腿更長!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我的腿更長!」

passages.original: Poor Peggy!
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅佩吉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的佩吉!

passages.original: I was very sorry for her, and I could not comfort her, for I knew how hard it was upon slow-paced horses to be put with fast ones; all the whipping comes to their share, and they can't help it.
passages.vernacular: 我為佢好難過,又冇法安慰佢,因為我知道,慢步嘅馬被同快嘅馬放喺一起有多難;所有嘅鞭打都落喺佢哋身上,佢哋都冇辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為她非常難過,又沒法安慰她,因為我知道,慢步的馬被同快的馬放在一起有多難;所有的鞭打都落在他們身上,他們也沒辦法。

passages.original: She was often used in the phaeton, and was very much liked by some of the ladies, because she was so gentle; and some time after this she was sold to two ladies who drove themselves, and wanted a safe, good horse.
passages.vernacular: 佢常被用喺四輪敞篷馬車上,被啲女士好鍾意,因為佢咁溫順;此後過咗一段時間,佢被賣畀咗兩位自己駕車、想要一匹安全嘅好馬嘅女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她常被用在四輪敞篷馬車上,被一些女士非常喜歡,因為她那麼溫順;此後過了一段時間,她被賣給了兩位自己駕車、想要一匹安全的好馬的女士。

passages.original: I met her several times out in the country, going a good steady pace, and looking as gay and contented as a horse could be.
passages.vernacular: 我喺鄉下遇見佢好幾次,以穩穩嘅好步伐走住,睇起嚟像馬所能有嘅嗰樣快活同滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在鄉下遇見她好幾次,以穩穩的好步伐走著,看起來像馬所能有的那樣快活和滿足。

passages.original: I was very glad to see her, for she deserved a good place.
passages.vernacular: 我見到佢好高興,因為佢應得一個好地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我見到她很高興,因為她應得一個好地方。

passages.original: After she left us another horse came in her stead.
passages.vernacular: 佢離開我哋之後,另一匹馬嚟接替佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她離開我們之後,另一匹馬來接替她。

passages.original: He was young, and had a bad name for shying and starting, by which he had lost a good place.
passages.vernacular: 佢年輕,以驚躍同受驚而名聲不好,因此丟咗一個好地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他年輕,以驚躍和受驚而名聲不好,因此丟了一個好地方。

passages.original: I asked him what made him shy.
passages.vernacular: 我問佢係乜嘢使佢驚躍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問他是什麼使他驚躍。

passages.original: “Well, I hardly know,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我幾乎唔知道,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我幾乎不知道,」他說。

passages.original: “I was timid when I was young, and was a good deal frightened several times, and if I saw anything strange I used to turn and look at it--you see, with our blinkers one can't see or understand what a thing is unless one looks round--and then my master always gave me a whipping, which of course made me start on, and did not make me less afraid.
passages.vernacular: 「我年輕時膽小,有好幾次受咗好大嘅驚嚇,如果我睇到乜嘢奇怪嘅嘢,我會轉身去睇——你知道,戴住遮眼罩,除非轉過頭睇,一個人睇唔見都不明白嗰個係乜嘢——然後我嘅主人總是抽我一頓,呢當然使我往前竄,並冇使我少害怕啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我年輕時膽小,有好幾次受了很大的驚嚇,如果我看到什麼奇怪的東西,我會轉身去看——你知道,戴著遮眼罩,除非轉過頭看,一個人看不見也不明白那是什麼——然後我的主人總是抽我一頓,這當然使我往前竄,並沒有使我少害怕一點。

passages.original: I think if he would have let me just look at things quietly, and see that there was nothing to hurt me, it would have been all right, and I should have got used to them.
passages.vernacular: 我想如果佢讓我安靜地睇睇嘢,睇出冇乜嘢會傷害我,就會冇事,我會習慣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想如果他讓我安靜地看看東西,看出沒有什麼會傷害我,就會沒事,我會習慣的。

passages.original: One day an old gentleman was riding with him, and a large piece of white paper or rag blew across just on one side of me.
passages.vernacular: 有一天一位老先生同佢一起騎馬,一大張白紙或破布吹過,正好喺我一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天一位老先生同他一起騎馬,一大張白紙或破布吹過,正好在我一邊。

passages.original: I shied and started forward.
passages.vernacular: 我驚躍並往前竄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我驚躍並往前竄。

passages.original: My master as usual whipped me smartly, but the old man cried out, 'You're wrong! you're wrong!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人像往常一樣狠狠地抽我,但老人喊道:『你錯喇!你錯喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人像往常一樣狠狠地抽我,但老人喊道:『你錯了!你錯了!

passages.original: You should never whip a horse for shying; he shies because he is frightened, and you only frighten him more and make the habit worse.'
passages.vernacular: 你永遠不該因為馬驚躍而抽佢;佢驚躍係因為害怕,你只會嚇得佢更厲害,使習慣更糟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你永遠不該因為馬驚躍而抽它;它驚躍是因為害怕,你只會嚇得它更厲害,使習慣更糟。』

passages.original: So I suppose all men don't do so.
passages.vernacular: 所以我想唔係所有人都嗰樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我想不是所有人都那樣做。

passages.original: I am sure I don't want to shy for the sake of it; but how should one know what is dangerous and what is not, if one is never allowed to get used to anything?
passages.vernacular: 我確信我唔係為了驚躍而想驚躍;但如果從不被允許習慣任何事,一個人點知道乜嘢危險、乜嘢不危險?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信我不是為了驚躍而想驚躍;但如果從不被允許習慣任何事,一個人怎麼知道什麼危險、什麼不危險?

passages.original: I am never afraid of what I know.
passages.vernacular: 我從不怕我知道嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從不怕我知道的東西。

passages.original: Now I was brought up in a park where there were deer; of course I knew them as well as I did a sheep or a cow, but they are not common, and I know many sensible horses who are frightened at them, and who kick up quite a shindy before they will pass a paddock where there are deer.”
passages.vernacular: 而家我係喺一個有鹿嘅莊園裡長大嘅;當然我認識佢哋,就像我認識羊或牛一樣,但佢哋不常見,我知道許多明智嘅馬被佢哋嚇到,喺經過有鹿嘅牧場之前會大鬧一場。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我是在一個有鹿的莊園裡長大的;當然我認識它們,就像我認識羊或牛一樣,但它們不常見,我知道許多明智的馬被它們嚇到,在經過有鹿的牧場之前會大鬧一場。」

passages.original: I knew what my companion said was true, and I wished that every young horse had as good masters as Farmer Grey and Squire Gordon.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我嘅同伴講嘅係真嘅,我希望每匹年輕嘅馬都有像格雷農夫同戈登鄉紳嗰樣嘅好主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我的同伴說的是真的,我希望每匹年輕的馬都有像格雷農夫和戈登鄉紳那樣的好主人。

passages.original: Of course we sometimes came in for good driving here.
passages.vernacular: 當然我哋有時喺呢度都遇到好嘅駕駛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我們有時在這裡也遇到好的駕駛。

passages.original: I remember one morning I was put into the light gig, and taken to a house in Pulteney Street.
passages.vernacular: 我記得一天早晨,我被套進輕便嘅敞篷馬車,帶到普爾特尼街嘅一座房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得一天早晨,我被套進輕便的敞篷馬車,帶到普爾特尼街的一座房子。

passages.original: Two gentlemen came out; the taller of them came round to my head; he looked at the bit and bridle, and just shifted the collar with his hand, to see if it fitted comfortably.
passages.vernacular: 兩位先生出嚟;高個子嘅走到我頭前;佢睇咗睇嚼子同轡頭,用手挪咗挪頸圈,睇佢係咪舒適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位先生出來;高個子的走到我頭前;他看了看嚼子和轡頭,用手挪了挪頸圈,看它是否舒適。

passages.original: “Do you consider this horse wants a curb?” he said to the hostler.
passages.vernacular: 「你認為呢匹馬需要一條鏈嚼子嗎?」佢問馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你認為這匹馬需要一條鏈嚼子嗎?」他問馬夫。

passages.original: “Well,” said the man, “I should say he would go just as well without; he has an uncommon good mouth, and though he has a fine spirit he has no vice; but we generally find people like the curb.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」嗰人講,「我該講冇都一樣好;佢嘴特別好,雖然佢精神旺盛,但冇惡習;不過我哋通常發現人哋鍾意鏈嚼子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」那人說,「我該說沒有也一樣好;他嘴特別好,雖然他精神旺盛,但沒有惡習;不過我們通常發現人們喜歡鏈嚼子。」

passages.original: “I don't like it,” said the gentleman; “be so good as to take it off, and put the rein in at the cheek.
passages.vernacular: 「我不鍾意,」嗰位先生講;「請你把佢取下嚟,把韁繩穿到臉頰嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不喜歡,」那位先生說;「請你把它取下來,把韁繩穿到臉頰那邊。

passages.original: An easy mouth is a great thing on a long journey, is it not, old fellow?” he said, patting my neck.
passages.vernacular: 輕柔嘅嘴喺長途旅行中係件大好事,係吧,老夥計?」佢拍住我嘅脖子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕柔的嘴在長途旅行中是件大好事,是吧,老夥計?」他拍著我的脖子說。

passages.original: Then he took the reins, and they both got up.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢攞起韁繩,佢哋兩個都上咗車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他拿起韁繩,他們兩個都上了車。

passages.original: I can remember now how quietly he turned me round, and then with a light feel of the rein, and drawing the whip gently across my back, we were off.
passages.vernacular: 我而家仲能記得佢幾咁平靜地把我轉過嚟,然後輕輕地感覺住韁繩,鞭子輕輕劃過我嘅背,我哋出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在還能記得他多麼平靜地把我轉過來,然後輕輕地感覺著韁繩,鞭子輕輕劃過我的背,我們出發了。

passages.original: I arched my neck and set off at my best pace.
passages.vernacular: 我拱起脖子,以我最好嘅步伐出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拱起脖子,以我最好的步伐出發。

passages.original: I found I had some one behind me who knew how a good horse ought to be driven.
passages.vernacular: 我發現我身後有一個知道好馬該點樣被駕駛嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現我身後有一個知道好馬該怎樣被駕駛的人。

passages.original: It seemed like old times again, and made me feel quite gay.
passages.vernacular: 好像又回到咗從前,讓我覺得好快活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像又回到了從前,讓我覺得很快活。

passages.original: This gentleman took a great liking to me, and after trying me several times with the saddle he prevailed upon my master to sell me to a friend of his, who wanted a safe, pleasant horse for riding.
passages.vernacular: 呢位先生好鍾意我,又試騎咗我幾次後,佢講服咗我嘅主人把我賣畀佢嘅一個朋友,嗰人想要一匹安全、愉快嘅馬騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位先生非常喜歡我,又試騎了我幾次後,他說服了我的主人把我賣給他的一個朋友,那人想要一匹安全、愉快的馬騎。

passages.original: And so it came to pass that in the summer I was sold to Mr. Barry.
passages.vernacular: 於是夏天,我被賣畀咗巴里先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夏天,我被賣給了巴里先生。

chapters.title: Part II · 30 A Thief 第二部·30 小偷

passages.original: CH My new master was an unmarried man.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅新主人係個未婚男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的新主人是個未婚男人。

passages.original: He lived at Bath, and was much engaged in business.
passages.vernacular: 佢住喺巴思,事務繁忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他住在巴思,事務繁忙。

passages.original: His doctor advised him to take horse exercise, and for this purpose he bought me.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅醫生建議佢騎馬運動,為此佢買咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的醫生建議他騎馬運動,為此他買了我。

passages.original: He hired a stable a short distance from his lodgings, and engaged a man named Filcher as groom.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺離佢住處不遠嘅地方租咗一間馬廄,雇咗一個叫菲爾徹嘅人當馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在離他住處不遠的地方租了一間馬廄,雇了一個叫菲爾徹的人當馬夫。

passages.original: My master knew very little about horses, but he treated me well, and I should have had a good and easy place but for circumstances of which he was ignorant.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人對馬懂得好少,但佢對我好好,若唔係佢唔知道嘅啲情況,我本應有個好而輕鬆嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人對馬懂得很少,但他對我很好,若不是他不知道的一些情況,我本應有個好而輕鬆的地方。

passages.original: He ordered the best hay with plenty of oats, crushed beans, and bran, with vetches, or rye grass, as the man might think needful.
passages.vernacular: 佢吩咐用最好嘅乾草,加足夠嘅燕麥、碎豆同麩皮,仲有野豌豆或黑麥草,按嗰人認為需要嘅量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他吩咐用最好的乾草,加足夠的燕麥、碎豆和麩皮,還有野豌豆或黑麥草,按那人認為需要的量。

passages.original: I heard the master give the order, so I knew there was plenty of good food, and I thought I was well off.
passages.vernacular: 我聽到主人下命令,所以知道有足夠嘅好食物,我以為自己過得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到主人下命令,所以知道有足夠的好食物,我以為自己過得很好。

passages.original: For a few days all went on well.
passages.vernacular: 頭幾天一切順利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭幾天一切順利。

passages.original: I found that my groom understood his business.
passages.vernacular: 我發現我嘅馬夫懂佢嘅行當。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現我的馬夫懂他的行當。

passages.original: He kept the stable clean and airy, and he groomed me thoroughly; and was never otherwise than gentle.
passages.vernacular: 佢保持馬廄乾淨通風,把我刷洗得好徹底;從來都好溫和。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他保持馬廄乾淨通風,把我刷洗得很徹底;從來都很溫和。

passages.original: He had been an hostler in one of the great hotels in Bath.
passages.vernacular: 佢曾係巴思一家大旅館嘅馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他曾是巴思一家大旅館的馬夫。

passages.original: He had given that up, and now cultivated fruit and vegetables for the market, and his wife bred and fattened poultry and rabbits for sale.
passages.vernacular: 佢放棄咗嗰個,而家為市場種水果同蔬菜,佢嘅妻子養殖並育肥家禽同兔子出售。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他放棄了那個,現在為市場種水果和蔬菜,他的妻子養殖並育肥家禽和兔子出售。

passages.original: After awhile it seemed to me that my oats came very short; I had the beans, but bran was mixed with them instead of oats, of which there were very few; certainly not more than a quarter of what there should have been.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一陣子,我覺得我嘅燕麥好唔夠;我有豆子,但摻嘅係麩皮而唔係燕麥,燕麥好少;肯定唔到應有量嘅四分之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一陣子,我覺得我的燕麥很不夠;我有豆子,但摻的是麩皮而不是燕麥,燕麥很少;肯定不到應有量的四分之一。

passages.original: In two or three weeks this began to tell upon my strength and spirits.
passages.vernacular: 兩三個星期後,呢開始影響我嘅力氣同精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩三個星期後,這開始影響我的力氣和精神。

passages.original: The grass food, though very good, was not the thing to keep up my condition without corn.
passages.vernacular: 草料雖然好好,但冇穀物,保持不咗我嘅狀態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草料雖然很好,但沒有穀物,保持不了我的狀態。

passages.original: However, I could not complain, nor make known my wants.
passages.vernacular: 然而,我唔能夠抱怨,都無法表達我嘅需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,我不能抱怨,也無法表達我的需要。

passages.original: So it went on for about two months; and I wondered that my master did not see that something was the matter.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣持續咗大約兩個月;我納悶我嘅主人點冇睇出有乜嘢不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣持續了大約兩個月;我納悶我的主人怎麼沒看出有什麼不對。

passages.original: However, one afternoon he rode out into the country to see a friend of his, a gentleman farmer, who lived on the road to Wells.
passages.vernacular: 不過,一天下午,佢騎馬到鄉下去睇佢嘅一位朋友,一位紳士農場主,住喺去韋爾斯嘅路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,一天下午,他騎馬到鄉下去看他的一位朋友,一位紳士農場主,住在去韋爾斯的路上。

passages.original: This gentleman had a very quick eye for horses; and after he had welcomed his friend he said, casting his eye over me:
passages.vernacular: 呢位紳士對馬有好敏銳嘅眼光;佢歡迎佢嘅朋友之後,佢瞥咗我一眼,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位紳士對馬有很敏銳的眼光;他歡迎他的朋友之後,他瞥了我一眼,說:

passages.original: “It seems to me, Barry, that your horse does not look so well as he did when you first had him; has he been well?”
passages.vernacular: 「巴里,喺我睇來,你嘅馬睇起嚟不像你剛有佢時咁好喇;佢一直好好嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里,在我看來,你的馬看起來不像你剛有他時那麼好了;他一直好好的嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I believe so,” said my master; “but he is not nearly so lively as he was; my groom tells me that horses are always dull and weak in the autumn, and that I must expect it.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我相信,」我嘅主人講;「但佢不像以前咁活潑喇;我嘅馬夫告訴我,馬喺秋天總是呆滯虛弱,我得預料到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我相信,」我的主人說;「但他不像以前那麼活潑了;我的馬夫告訴我,馬在秋天總是呆滯虛弱,我得預料到。」

passages.original: “Autumn, fiddlesticks!” said the farmer.
passages.vernacular: 「秋天,胡扯!」農場主講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「秋天,胡扯!」農場主說。

passages.original: “Why, this is only August; and with your light work and good food he ought not to go down like this, even if it was autumn.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,呢才八月;就憑你嘅輕活同好食物,即使係秋天佢都不該咁樣消瘦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,這才八月;就憑你的輕活和好食物,即使是秋天他也不該這樣消瘦。

passages.original: How do you feed him?”
passages.vernacular: 你點餵佢嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼餵他的?」

passages.original: My master told him.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人告訴咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人告訴了他。

passages.original: The other shook his head slowly, and began to feel me over.
passages.vernacular: 另一個人慢慢搖頭,開始把我摸咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個人慢慢搖頭,開始把我摸了一遍。

passages.original: “I can't say who eats your corn, my dear fellow, but I am much mistaken if your horse gets it.
passages.vernacular: 「我講不上係邊個食咗你嘅穀物,我親愛嘅夥計,但如果你嘅馬得到喇,嗰我就大錯特錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說不上是誰吃了你的穀物,我親愛的夥計,但如果你的馬得到了,那我就大錯特錯了。

passages.original: Have you ridden very fast?”
passages.vernacular: 你騎得好快嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你騎得很快嗎?」

passages.original: “No, very gently.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,好慢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,很慢。」

passages.original: “Then just put your hand here,” said he, passing his hand over my neck and shoulder; “he is as warm and damp as a horse just come up from grass.
passages.vernacular: 「咁把手放呢兒,」佢講,佢嘅手劃過我嘅脖子同肩膀;「佢又熱又濕,像剛從草地上上嚟嘅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼把手放這兒,」他說,他的手劃過我的脖子和肩膀;「他又熱又濕,像剛從草地上上來的馬。

passages.original: I advise you to look into your stable a little more.
passages.vernacular: 我勸你多留意你嘅馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我勸你多留意你的馬廄。

passages.original: I hate to be suspicious, and, thank heaven, I have no cause to be, for I can trust my men, present or absent; but there are mean scoundrels, wicked enough to rob a dumb beast of his food.
passages.vernacular: 我討厭疑神疑鬼,感謝上天,我冇理由咁樣,因為我信得過我嘅人,不管喺不喺;但有些卑鄙嘅惡棍,邪惡到會搶劫一頭啞巴牲口嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我討厭疑神疑鬼,感謝上天,我沒有理由這樣,因為我信得過我的人,不管在不在;但有些卑鄙的惡棍,邪惡到會搶劫一頭啞巴牲口的食物。

passages.original: You must look into it.”
passages.vernacular: 你必須查一查。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你必須查一查。」

passages.original: And turning to his man, who had come to take me, “Give this horse a right good feed of bruised oats, and don't stint him.”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢轉向前嚟牽我嘅人講:「畀呢匹馬好好餵一頓碾碎嘅燕麥,唔好吝嗇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他轉向前來牽我的人說:「給這匹馬好好餵一頓碾碎的燕麥,不要吝嗇。」

passages.original: “Dumb beasts!”
passages.vernacular: 「啞巴牲口!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啞巴牲口!」

passages.original: Yes, we are; but if I could have spoken I could have told my master where his oats went to.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,我哋係;但如果我能講話,我可以告訴我嘅主人佢嘅燕麥去邊兒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,我們是;但如果我能說話,我可以告訴我的主人他的燕麥去哪兒了。

passages.original: My groom used to come every morning about six o'clock, and with him a little boy, who always had a covered basket with him.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅馬夫每天早晨六點左右嚟,仲帶住一個小男孩,佢總帶一個有蓋嘅籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的馬夫每天早晨六點左右來,還帶著一個小男孩,他總帶一個有蓋的籃子。

passages.original: He used to go with his father into the harness-room, where the corn was kept, and I could see them, when the door stood ajar, fill a little bag with oats out of the bin, and then he used to be off.
passages.vernacular: 佢常同佢父親進馬具室,穀物就放喺嗰度,我能睇見,門半開時,佢哋把一個小袋子從箱子裡裝滿燕麥,然後男孩就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他常和他父親進馬具室,穀物就放在那裡,我能看見,門半開時,他們把一個小袋子從箱子裡裝滿燕麥,然後男孩就走了。

passages.original: Five or six mornings after this, just as the boy had left the stable, the door was pushed open, and a policeman walked in, holding the child tight by the arm; another policeman followed, and locked the door on the inside, saying, “Show me the place where your father keeps his rabbits' food.”
passages.vernacular: 呢之後五六個早晨,就喺男孩剛離開馬廄時,門被推開喇,一個警察走咗進嚟,緊緊抓住細路嘅胳膊;另一個警察跟住,從裡面鎖上門,講:「帶我睇睇你父親放兔子飼料嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這之後五六個早晨,就在男孩剛離開馬廄時,門被推開了,一個警察走了進來,緊緊抓著孩子的胳膊;另一個警察跟著,從裡面鎖上門,說:「帶我看看你父親放兔子飼料的地方。」

passages.original: The boy looked very frightened and began to cry; but there was no escape, and he led the way to the corn-bin.
passages.vernacular: 男孩顯得好害怕,開始哭;但無路可逃,佢領住去咗穀物箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩顯得非常害怕,開始哭;但無路可逃,他領著去了穀物箱。

passages.original: Here the policeman found another empty bag like that which was found full of oats in the boy's basket.
passages.vernacular: 警察喺呢度找到咗另一個空袋子,同喺男孩籃子裡發現嘅裝滿燕麥嘅嗰個一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 警察在這裡找到了另一個空袋子,和在男孩籃子裡發現的裝滿燕麥的那個一樣。

passages.original: Filcher was cleaning my feet at the time, but they soon saw him, and though he blustered a good deal they walked him off to the “lock-up”, and his boy with him.
passages.vernacular: 菲爾徹嗰時正在畀我清理蹄子,但佢哋好快睇見咗佢,雖然佢大吵大嚷,佢哋定係把佢押走咗到「拘留所」,男孩都跟住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲爾徹那時正在給我清理蹄子,但他們很快看見了他,雖然他大吵大嚷,他們還是把他押走了到「拘留所」,男孩也跟著他。

passages.original: I heard afterward that the boy was not held to be guilty, but the man was sentenced to prison for two months.
passages.vernacular: 我後來聽講男孩被認為無罪,但嗰人被判處兩個月監禁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我後來聽說男孩被認為無罪,但那人被判處兩個月監禁。

chapters.title: Part II · 31 A Humbug 第二部·31 騙子

passages.original: CH My master was not immediately suited, but in a few days my new groom came.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人冇即刻找到合適嘅人,但幾天後我嘅新馬夫嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人沒有馬上找到合適的人,但幾天後我的新馬夫來了。

passages.original: He was a tall, good-looking fellow enough; but if ever there was a humbug in the shape of a groom Alfred Smirk was the man.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個高個子、相當好睇嘅傢伙;但如果有一個以馬夫面目出現嘅騙子,艾爾弗雷德·斯默克就係嗰個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高個子、相當好看的傢伙;但如果有一個以馬夫面目出現的騙子,艾爾弗雷德·斯默克就是那個人。

passages.original: He was very civil to me, and never used me ill; in fact, he did a great deal of stroking and patting when his master was there to see it.
passages.vernacular: 佢對我好客氣,從不虐待我;事實上,佢主人在場睇得見時,佢就大量撫摸同拍我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對我非常客氣,從不虐待我;事實上,他主人在場看得見時,他就大量撫摸和拍我。

passages.original: He always brushed my mane and tail with water and my hoofs with oil before he brought me to the door, to make me look smart; but as to cleaning my feet or looking to my shoes, or grooming me thoroughly, he thought no more of that than if I had been a cow.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是喺把我牽到門口前,用水刷我嘅鬃毛同尾巴,用油擦我嘅蹄子,讓我顯得漂亮;但至於清理我嘅蹄子、查睇我嘅蹄鐵,或徹底畀我刷洗,佢想都唔想,好像我係一頭母牛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是在把我牽到門口前,用水刷我的鬃毛和尾巴,用油擦我的蹄子,讓我顯得漂亮;但至於清理我的蹄子、查看我的蹄鐵,或徹底給我刷洗,他想都不想,好像我是一頭母牛。

passages.original: He left my bit rusty, my saddle damp, and my crupper stiff.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我嘅嚼子生鏽,我嘅鞍子潮濕,我嘅鞦韆僵硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他讓我的嚼子生鏽,我的鞍子潮濕,我的鞦韆僵硬。

passages.original: Alfred Smirk considered himself very handsome; he spent a great deal of time about his hair, whiskers and necktie, before a little looking-glass in the harness-room.
passages.vernacular: 艾爾弗雷德·斯默克自認為好英俊;佢喺馬具室嘅一面小鏡子前,花大量時間整理佢嘅頭髮、鬢角同領帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾爾弗雷德·斯默克自認為非常英俊;他在馬具室的一面小鏡子前,花大量時間整理他的頭髮、鬢角和領帶。

passages.original: When his master was speaking to him it was always, “Yes, sir; yes, sir”--touching his hat at every word; and every one thought he was a very nice young man and that Mr. Barry was very fortunate to meet with him.
passages.vernacular: 佢主人同佢講話時,佢總是講:「係,先生;係,先生」——每講一個字就碰一下帽子;人人都認為佢係個好好嘅年輕人,巴里先生遇到佢好幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他主人同他說話時,他總是說:「是,先生;是,先生」——每說一個字就碰一下帽子;人人都認為他是個很好的年輕人,巴里先生遇到他很幸運。

passages.original: I should say he was the laziest, most conceited fellow I ever came near.
passages.vernacular: 我該講,佢係我見過最懶、最自負嘅傢伙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該說,他是我見過最懶、最自負的傢伙。

passages.original: Of course, it was a great thing not to be ill-used, but then a horse wants more than that.
passages.vernacular: 當然,不被虐待係件大事,但馬需要嘅比呢更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,不被虐待是件大事,但馬需要的比這更多。

passages.original: I had a loose box, and might have been very comfortable if he had not been too indolent to clean it out.
passages.vernacular: 我有一個活動廄,本來可以好舒服,只係佢太懶,唔肯打掃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一個活動廄,本來可以很舒服,只是他太懶,不肯打掃。

passages.original: He never took all the straw away, and the smell from what lay underneath was very bad; while the strong vapors that rose made my eyes smart and inflame, and I did not feel the same appetite for my food.
passages.vernacular: 佢從不把所有稻草都清走,下面稻草嘅氣味好難聞;升起嘅濃烈氣體讓我嘅眼睛刺痛、發炎,我對食物嘅胃口都不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從不把所有稻草都清走,下面稻草的氣味很難聞;升起的濃烈氣體讓我的眼睛刺痛、發炎,我對食物的胃口也不一樣了。

passages.original: One day his master came in and said, “Alfred, the stable smells rather strong; should not you give that stall a good scrub and throw down plenty of water?”
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢嘅主人進來講:「艾爾弗雷德,馬廄嘅氣味相當濃;你不該好好刷洗一下嗰個馬棚,多潑點水嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天他的主人進來說:「艾爾弗雷德,馬廄的氣味相當濃;你不該好好刷洗一下那個馬棚,多潑點水嗎?」

passages.original: “Well, sir,” he said, touching his cap, “I'll do so if you please, sir; but it is rather dangerous, sir, throwing down water in a horse's box; they are very apt to take cold, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,先生,」佢碰住帽子講,「您要係願意,我就做,先生;但喺馬廄裡潑水相當危險,先生,佢哋好容易住涼,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,先生,」他碰著帽子說,「您要是願意,我就做,先生;但在馬廄裡潑水相當危險,先生,它們很容易著涼,先生。

passages.original: I should not like to do him an injury, but I'll do it if you please, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔願意傷害佢,但您要係願意,我就做,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願意傷害他,但您要是願意,我就做,先生。」

passages.original: “Well,” said his master, “I should not like him to take cold; but I don't like the smell of this stable.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」佢主人講,「我唔想讓佢住涼;但我不鍾意呢間馬廄嘅氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」他主人說,「我不想讓他著涼;但我不喜歡這間馬廄的氣味。

passages.original: Do you think the drains are all right?”
passages.vernacular: 你認為下水道都冇問題嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認為下水道都沒問題嗎?」

passages.original: “Well, sir, now you mention it, I think the drain does sometimes send back a smell; there may be something wrong, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,先生,既然您提起,我想下水道有時確實返味;可能有乜嘢地方出咗毛病,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,先生,既然您提起,我想下水道有時確實返味;可能有什麼地方出了毛病,先生。」

passages.original: “Then send for the bricklayer and have it seen to,” said his master.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就叫泥水匠嚟查一下,」佢主人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就叫泥水匠來查一下,」他主人說。

passages.original: “Yes, sir, I will.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,先生,我去叫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,先生,我去叫。」

passages.original: The bricklayer came and pulled up a great many bricks, but found nothing amiss; so he put down some lime and charged the master five shillings, and the smell in my box was as bad as ever.
passages.vernacular: 泥水匠嚟喇,撬起咗好多磚,但冇發現乜嘢毛病;就撒咗些石灰,向主人收咗五先令,我廄裡嘅氣味定係一樣糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 泥水匠來了,撬起了很多磚,但沒發現什麼毛病;就撒了些石灰,向主人收了五先令,我廄裡的氣味還是一樣糟。

passages.original: But that was not all: standing as I did on a quantity of moist straw my feet grew unhealthy and tender, and the master used to say:
passages.vernacular: 但呢仲唔係全部:我一直站喺大量潮濕嘅稻草上,蹄子變得不健康、嬌嫩,主人常講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這還不是全部:我一直站在大量潮濕的稻草上,蹄子變得不健康、嬌嫩,主人常說:

passages.original: “I don't know what is the matter with this horse; he goes very fumble-footed.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道呢匹馬點喇;佢走起路嚟好笨拙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道這匹馬怎麼了;他走起路來很笨拙。

passages.original: I am sometimes afraid he will stumble.”
passages.vernacular: 我有時怕佢會絆倒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有時怕他會絆倒。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir,” said Alfred, “I have noticed the same myself, when I have exercised him.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,」艾爾弗雷德講,「我騎佢運動嘅時候,自己都注意到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,」艾爾弗雷德說,「我騎他運動的時候,自己也注意到了。」

passages.original: Now the fact was that he hardly ever did exercise me, and when the master was busy I often stood for days together without stretching my legs at all, and yet being fed just as high as if I were at hard work.
passages.vernacular: 事實係佢幾乎從冇畀我運動過,主人忙嘅時候,我常常一連幾天站住,腿根本冇伸展過,卻照樣被餵得像喺重活一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實是他幾乎從沒給我運動過,主人忙的時候,我常常一連幾天站著,腿根本沒伸展過,卻照樣被餵得像在重活一樣好。

passages.original: This often disordered my health, and made me sometimes heavy and dull, but more often restless and feverish.
passages.vernacular: 呢常常擾亂我嘅健康,使我有時沉重呆滯,但更多時候係焦躁發燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這常常擾亂我的健康,使我有時沉重呆滯,但更多時候是焦躁發燒。

passages.original: He never even gave me a meal of green food or a bran mash, which would have cooled me, for he was altogether as ignorant as he was conceited; and then, instead of exercise or change of food, I had to take horse balls and draughts; which, beside the nuisance of having them poured down my throat, used to make me feel ill and uncomfortable.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至從冇畀我一頓青飼料或麩皮糊,嗰本可以讓我降溫,因為佢既無知又自負;然後不畀運動或換食物,而係讓我食馬丸同灌藥;呢除咗被灌進喉嚨嘅討厭之外,仲使我覺得不適同難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他甚至從沒給我一頓青飼料或麩皮糊,那本可以讓我降溫,因為他既無知又自負;然後不給運動或換食物,而是讓我吃馬丸和灌藥;這除了被灌進喉嚨的討厭之外,還使我覺得不適和難受。

passages.original: One day my feet were so tender that, trotting over some fresh stones with my master on my back, I made two such serious stumbles that, as he came down Lansdown into the city, he stopped at the farrier's, and asked him to see what was the matter with me.
passages.vernacular: 有一天我嘅蹄子嬌嫩得好,主人騎住我喺啲新石頭上小跑時,我連續兩次嚴重絆倒,佢沿朗斯當進城時,喺馬蹄鐵匠嗰度停下,請佢睇睇我點喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我的蹄子嬌嫩得很,主人騎著我在一些新石頭上小跑時,我連續兩次嚴重絆倒,他沿朗斯當進城時,在馬蹄鐵匠那裡停下,請他看看我怎麼了。

passages.original: The man took up my feet one by one and examined them; then standing up and dusting his hands one against the other, he said:
passages.vernacular: 嗰人一隻一隻地抬起我嘅蹄子檢查;然後站起嚟,把兩手互相拍去灰,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人一隻一隻地抬起我的蹄子檢查;然後站起來,把兩手互相拍去灰,說:

passages.original: “Your horse has got the 'thrush', and badly, too; his feet are very tender; it is fortunate that he has not been down.
passages.vernacular: 「您嘅馬得咗『蹄叉腐爛』,而且好嚴重;佢嘅蹄子好嬌嫩;佢冇摔倒真係幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您的馬得了『蹄叉腐爛』,而且很嚴重;他的蹄子很嬌嫩;他沒有摔倒真是幸運。

passages.original: I wonder your groom has not seen to it before.
passages.vernacular: 我奇怪您嘅馬夫以前點冇處理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我奇怪您的馬夫以前怎麼沒處理。

passages.original: This is the sort of thing we find in foul stables, where the litter is never properly cleaned out.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我哋喺骯髒嘅馬廄裡發現嘅嗰種事,嗰度嘅墊草從不好好清理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我們在骯髒的馬廄裡發現的那種事,那裡的墊草從不好好清理。

passages.original: If you will send him here to-morrow I will attend to the hoof, and I will direct your man how to apply the liniment which I will give him.”
passages.vernacular: 如果您聽日送佢嚟呢度,我嚟處理蹄子,並指導您嘅人點塗我畀佢嘅搽劑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您明天送他來這裡,我來處理蹄子,並指導您的人怎麼塗我給他的搽劑。」

passages.original: The next day I had my feet thoroughly cleansed and stuffed with tow soaked in some strong lotion; and an unpleasant business it was.
passages.vernacular: 第二天我嘅蹄子被徹底清洗,塞進咗用強藥水浸過嘅麻絮;嗰個係件不愉快嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天我的蹄子被徹底清洗,塞進了用強藥水浸過的麻絮;那是件不愉快的事。

passages.original: The farrier ordered all the litter to be taken out of my box day by day, and the floor kept very clean.
passages.vernacular: 馬蹄鐵匠吩咐每天把我廄裡嘅墊草全清走,地板保持好乾淨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬蹄鐵匠吩咐每天把我廄裡的墊草全清走,地板保持非常乾淨。

passages.original: Then I was to have bran mashes, a little green food, and not so much corn, till my feet were well again.
passages.vernacular: 然後我要食麩皮糊、啲青飼料,少食穀物,直到蹄子好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我要吃麩皮糊、一點青飼料,少吃穀物,直到蹄子好了。

passages.original: With this treatment I soon regained my spirits; but Mr. Barry was so much disgusted at being twice deceived by his grooms that he determined to give up keeping a horse, and to hire when he wanted one.
passages.vernacular: 經過咁樣嘅治療,我好快恢復咗精神;但巴里先生因兩次被佢嘅馬夫欺騙而好惱怒,決定唔再養馬,需要時就租。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過這樣的治療,我很快恢復了精神;但巴里先生因兩次被他的馬夫欺騙而非常惱怒,決定不再養馬,需要時就租。

passages.original: I was therefore kept till my feet were quite sound, and was then sold again.
passages.vernacular: 於是我被留到蹄子完全好喇,然後又被賣掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我被留到蹄子完全好了,然後又被賣掉。

chapters.title: Part III · 32 A Horse Fair 第三部·32 馬市

passages.original: CH No doubt a horse fair is a very amusing place to those who have nothing to lose; at any rate, there is plenty to see.
passages.vernacular: 馬市對嗰啲冇乜嘢可失去嘅人來講,無疑係個好有趣嘅地方;總之,有好多嘢可睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬市對那些沒什麼可失去的人來說,無疑是個非常有趣的地方;總之,有很多東西可看。

passages.original: Long strings of young horses out of the country, fresh from the marshes; and droves of shaggy little Welsh ponies, no higher than Merrylegs; and hundreds of cart horses of all sorts, some of them with their long tails braided up and tied with scarlet cord; and a good many like myself, handsome and high-bred, but fallen into the middle class, through some accident or blemish, unsoundness of wind, or some other complaint.
passages.vernacular: 一長串一長串從鄉下嚟嘅小馬,剛離開沼澤;一群群毛茸茸嘅威爾士小矮馬,不比梅利萊格斯高;幾百匹各種各樣嘅拉車馬,有嘅把長尾巴編起嚟,用猩紅色繩子紮住;仲有不少像我咁樣,漂亮、血統高貴,卻因某次意外或瑕疵、呼吸不健全或其他毛病淪為中等嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一長串一長串從鄉下來的小馬,剛離開沼澤;一群群毛茸茸的威爾士小矮馬,不比梅利萊格斯高;幾百匹各種各樣的拉車馬,有的把長尾巴編起來,用猩紅色繩子紮著;還有不少像我這樣,漂亮、血統高貴,卻因某次意外或瑕疵、呼吸不健全或其他毛病淪為中等的。

passages.original: There were some splendid animals quite in their prime, and fit for anything; they were throwing out their legs and showing off their paces in high style, as they were trotted out with a leading rein, the groom running by the side.
passages.vernacular: 有些出色嘅牲口正值盛年,乜嘢都適合;被牽住韁繩小跑時,馬夫喺旁邊跑,佢哋揚住腿,炫耀佢哋嘅步伐,好有派頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些出色的牲口正值盛年,什麼都適合;被牽著韁繩小跑時,馬夫在旁邊跑,它們揚著腿,炫耀它們的步伐,很有派頭。

passages.original: But round in the background there were a number of poor things, sadly broken down with hard work, with their knees knuckling over and their hind legs swinging out at every step, and there were some very dejected-looking old horses, with the under lip hanging down and the ears lying back heavily, as if there were no more pleasure in life, and no more hope; there were some so thin you might see all their ribs, and some with old sores on their backs and hips.
passages.vernacular: 但喺後面嘅背景處,有啲可憐嘅馬,因辛苦勞動垮喇,膝蓋彎曲,每走一步後腿都晃出去,仲有啲睇起嚟好沮喪嘅老馬,下唇耷拉住,耳朵沉重地向後貼,好像生命中再冇快樂,都冇希望;有些瘦得能睇見所有肋骨,有些背上同臀部有舊瘡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在後面的背景處,有一些可憐的馬,因辛苦勞動垮了,膝蓋彎曲,每走一步後腿都晃出去,還有一些看起來非常沮喪的老馬,下唇耷拉著,耳朵沉重地向後貼,好像生命中再沒有快樂,也沒有希望;有些瘦得能看見所有肋骨,有些背上和臀部有舊瘡。
