passages.original: These were sad sights for a horse to look upon, who knows not but he may come to the same state.
passages.vernacular: 對一匹自己唔知道會唔會落到同樣境地嘅馬來講,呢個係可悲嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對一匹自己不知道會不會落到同樣境地的馬來說,這是可悲的景象。

passages.original: There was a great deal of bargaining, of running up and beating down; and if a horse may speak his mind so far as he understands, I should say there were more lies told and more trickery at that horse fair than a clever man could give an account of.
passages.vernacular: 有好多討價仲價,抬價同壓價;如果馬可以就佢所理解嘅暢所欲言,我該講,喺嗰個馬市上講嘅謊言同耍嘅花招,比一個聰明人能講清楚嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有很多討價還價,抬價和壓價;如果馬可以就他所理解的暢所欲言,我該說,在那個馬市上說的謊言和耍的花招,比一個聰明人能說清楚的還多。

passages.original: I was put with two or three other strong, useful-looking horses, and a good many people came to look at us.
passages.vernacular: 我被同兩三匹別嘅強壯、睇起嚟有用嘅馬放喺一起,好多人嚟睇我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被同兩三匹別的強壯、看起來有用的馬放在一起,很多人來看我們。

passages.original: The gentlemen always turned from me when they saw my broken knees; though the man who had me swore it was only a slip in the stall.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋睇見我受傷嘅膝蓋總是轉身走開;雖然帶我嚟嘅人發誓嗰只係喺馬棚裡滑咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們看見我受傷的膝蓋總是轉身走開;雖然帶我來的人發誓那只是在馬棚裡滑了一下。

passages.original: The first thing was to pull my mouth open, then to look at my eyes, then feel all the way down my legs, and give me a hard feel of the skin and flesh, and then try my paces.
passages.vernacular: 首先係扳開我嘅嘴,然後睇我嘅眼睛,然後沿住我嘅腿一路摸下去,使勁摸摸我嘅皮同肉,然後試我嘅步伐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先是扳開我的嘴,然後看我的眼睛,然後沿著我的腿一路摸下去,使勁摸摸我的皮和肉,然後試我的步伐。

passages.original: It was wonderful what a difference there was in the way these things were done.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲事做嘅方式差別之大,令人驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些事做的方式差別之大,令人驚奇。

passages.original: Some did it in a rough, offhand way, as if one was only a piece of wood; while others would take their hands gently over one's body, with a pat now and then, as much as to say, “By your leave.”
passages.vernacular: 有些人以粗暴隨便嘅方式做,好像人只係一塊木頭;而另啲人會輕輕地用手撫過人嘅身體,時不時拍一下,好像喺講:「請原諒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人以粗暴隨便的方式做,好像人只是一塊木頭;而另一些人會輕輕地用手撫過人的身體,時不時拍一下,好像在說:「請原諒。」

passages.original: Of course I judged a good deal of the buyers by their manners to myself.
passages.vernacular: 當然我好大程度上從買主對我嘅態度嚟判斷佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我很大程度上從買主對我的態度來判斷他們。

passages.original: There was one man, I thought, if he would buy me, I should be happy.
passages.vernacular: 有一個人,我想,如果佢買我,我會好快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個人,我想,如果他買我,我會很快樂。

passages.original: He was not a gentleman, nor yet one of the loud, flashy sort that call themselves so.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係紳士,都唔係嗰種自稱紳士嘅大聲花哨之徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是紳士,也不是那種自稱紳士的大聲花哨之徒。

passages.original: He was rather a small man, but well made, and quick in all his motions.
passages.vernacular: 佢個子相當小,但體格好,動作迅速。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他個子相當小,但體格好,動作迅速。

passages.original: I knew in a moment by the way he handled me, that he was used to horses; he spoke gently, and his gray eye had a kindly, cheery look in it.
passages.vernacular: 我從佢碰我嘅方式即刻知道佢習慣於馬;佢講話溫和,灰色眼睛裡有親切、愉快嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從他碰我的方式立刻知道他習慣於馬;他說話溫和,灰色眼睛裡有親切、愉快的神情。

passages.original: It may seem strange to say--but it is true all the same--that the clean, fresh smell there was about him made me take to him; no smell of old beer and tobacco, which I hated, but a fresh smell as if he had come out of a hayloft.
passages.vernacular: 講起嚟或者奇怪——但確實如此——佢身上有一股乾淨清新嘅氣味,使我鍾意上佢;冇我討厭嘅陳啤酒同煙草嘅氣味,而係像剛從乾草棚出嚟嘅清新氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說起來也許奇怪——但確實如此——他身上有一股乾淨清新的氣味,使我喜歡上他;沒有我討厭的陳啤酒和煙草的氣味,而是像剛從乾草棚出來的清新氣味。

passages.original: He offered twenty-three pounds for me, but that was refused, and he walked away.
passages.vernacular: 佢出價二十三英鎊買我,但被拒絕喇,佢走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出價二十三英鎊買我,但被拒絕了,他走開了。

passages.original: I looked after him, but he was gone, and a very hard-looking, loud-voiced man came.
passages.vernacular: 我目送佢,但佢唔見喇,嚟咗一個樣子好凶、嗓門好大嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我目送他,但他不見了,來了一個樣子很凶、嗓門很大的人。

passages.original: I was dreadfully afraid he would have me; but he walked off.
passages.vernacular: 我好害怕佢會買我;但佢走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常害怕他會買我;但他走開了。

passages.original: One or two more came who did not mean business.
passages.vernacular: 又嚟咗一兩個並唔係真想買嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又來了一兩個並不是真想買的人。

passages.original: Then the hard-faced man came back again and offered twenty-three pounds.
passages.vernacular: 然後嗰個臉好凶嘅人又回嚟喇,出價二十三英鎊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後那個臉很凶的人又回來了,出價二十三英鎊。

passages.original: A very close bargain was being driven, for my salesman began to think he should not get all he asked, and must come down; but just then the gray-eyed man came back again.
passages.vernacular: 正在進行一場好緊張嘅討價仲價,因為我嘅賣主開始覺得佢得唔到要嘅全部價錢,必須降價;但就喺呢陣,灰眼睛嘅人又回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正在進行一場非常緊張的討價還價,因為我的賣主開始覺得他得不到要的全部價錢,必須降價;但就在這時,灰眼睛的人又回來了。

passages.original: I could not help reaching out my head toward him.
passages.vernacular: 我忍不住把頭向佢伸去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忍不住把頭向他伸去。

passages.original: He stroked my face kindly.
passages.vernacular: 佢親切地撫摸我嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他親切地撫摸我的臉。

passages.original: “Well, old chap,” he said, “I think we should suit each other.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,老夥計,」佢講,「我想我哋合得嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,老夥計,」他說,「我想我們合得來。

passages.original: I'll give twenty-four for him.”
passages.vernacular: 我出二十四英鎊買佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我出二十四英鎊買他。」

passages.original: “Say twenty-five and you shall have him.”
passages.vernacular: 「講二十五,佢就係你嘅喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說二十五,他就是你的了。」

passages.original: “Twenty-four ten,” said my friend, in a very decided tone, “and not another sixpence--yes or no?”
passages.vernacular: 「二十四鎊十先令,」我嘅朋友用好堅決嘅語氣講,「再多一分錢都不畀——行定係不行?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「二十四鎊十先令,」我的朋友用非常堅決的語氣說,「再多一分錢也不給——行還是不行?」

passages.original: “Done,” said the salesman; “and you may depend upon it there's a monstrous deal of quality in that horse, and if you want him for cab work he's a bargain.”
passages.vernacular: 「成交,」賣主講;「你可以放心,嗰匹馬有極高嘅品質,如果你要佢拉出租馬車,呢個係筆便宜買賣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「成交,」賣主說;「你可以放心,那匹馬有極高的品質,如果你要他拉出租馬車,這是筆便宜買賣。」

passages.original: The money was paid on the spot, and my new master took my halter, and led me out of the fair to an inn, where he had a saddle and bridle ready.
passages.vernacular: 錢當場付清,我嘅新主人攞起我嘅籠頭,領我離開馬市去到一家客棧,喺嗰度佢已準備好咗鞍子同轡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錢當場付清,我的新主人拿起我的籠頭,領我離開馬市去到一家客棧,在那裡他已準備好了鞍子和轡頭。

passages.original: He gave me a good feed of oats and stood by while I ate it, talking to himself and talking to me.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀咗我一頓好燕麥,站喺旁邊睇我食,自言自語,都同我講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給了我一頓好燕麥,站在旁邊看我吃,自言自語,也同我說話。

passages.original: Half an hour after we were on our way to London, through pleasant lanes and country roads, until we came into the great London thoroughfare, on which we traveled steadily, till in the twilight we reached the great city.
passages.vernacular: 半小時後,我哋動身往倫敦走,經過愉快嘅小路同鄉間道路,直到我哋進入倫敦嘅大幹道,我哋喺上面穩步前進,黃昏時分到咗呢座大城市。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半小時後,我們動身往倫敦走,經過愉快的小路和鄉間道路,直到我們進入倫敦的大幹道,我們在上面穩步前進,黃昏時分到了這座大城市。

passages.original: The gas lamps were already lighted; there were streets to the right, and streets to the left, and streets crossing each other, for mile upon mile.
passages.vernacular: 煤氣燈已經點亮;有向右嘅街道,有向左嘅街道,有交叉嘅街道,連綿幾英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 煤氣燈已經點亮;有向右的街道,有向左的街道,有交叉的街道,連綿幾英里。

passages.original: I thought we should never come to the end of them.
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋永遠走唔到頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們永遠走不到頭。

passages.original: At last, in passing through one, we came to a long cab stand, when my rider called out in a cheery voice, “Good-night, governor!”
passages.vernacular: 最後,經過其中一條街時,我哋嚟到一個長長嘅出租馬車停靠站,我嘅騎手用愉快嘅聲音喊道:「晚安,老大!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,經過其中一條街時,我們來到一個長長的出租馬車停靠站,我的騎手用愉快的聲音喊道:「晚安,老大!」

passages.original: “Halloo!” cried a voice.
passages.vernacular: 「喂!」一個聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂!」一個聲音喊道。

passages.original: “Have you got a good one?”
passages.vernacular: 「你弄到好嘅咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你弄到好的了嗎?」

passages.original: “I think so,” replied my owner.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅,」我嘅主人回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的,」我的主人回答。

passages.original: “I wish you luck with him.”
passages.vernacular: 「祝你運氣好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「祝你運氣好。」

passages.original: “Thank you, governor,” and he rode on.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,老大,」講完佢繼續騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,老大,」說完他繼續騎。

passages.original: We soon turned up one of the side streets, and about halfway up that we turned into a very narrow street, with rather poor-looking houses on one side, and what seemed to be coach-houses and stables on the other.
passages.vernacular: 我哋好快轉上一條側街,大約走到一半,我哋拐進一條好窄嘅街,一邊係相當破舊嘅房子,另一邊似乎係馬車房同馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們很快轉上一條側街,大約走到一半,我們拐進一條很窄的街,一邊是相當破舊的房子,另一邊似乎是馬車房和馬廄。

passages.original: My owner pulled up at one of the houses and whistled.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人喺其中一座房子前勒住我,吹咗一聲口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人在其中一座房子前勒住我,吹了一聲口哨。

passages.original: The door flew open, and a young woman, followed by a little girl and boy, ran out.
passages.vernacular: 門猛地打開,一個年輕女人跑出嚟,後面跟住一個小女孩同一個小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門猛地打開,一個年輕女人跑出來,後面跟著一個小女孩和一個小男孩。

passages.original: There was a very lively greeting as my rider dismounted.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅騎手下馬時,有一場好熱烈嘅歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的騎手下馬時,有一場非常熱烈的歡迎。

passages.original: “Now, then, Harry, my boy, open the gates, and mother will bring us the lantern.”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,哈里,我嘅細路,打開大門,媽媽會畀我哋攞燈籠嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,哈里,我的孩子,打開大門,媽媽會給我們拿燈籠來。」

passages.original: The next minute they were all standing round me in a small stable-yard.
passages.vernacular: 下一分鐘,佢哋都站喺一個小馬廄院子裡圍住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一分鐘,他們都站在一個小馬廄院子裡圍著我。

passages.original: “Is he gentle, father?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢溫和嗎,爸爸?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他溫和嗎,爸爸?」

passages.original: “Yes, Dolly, as gentle as your own kitten; come and pat him.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,多麗,像你嘅小貓一樣溫和;嚟拍拍佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,多麗,像你的小貓一樣溫和;來拍拍他。」

passages.original: At once the little hand was patting about all over my shoulder without fear.
passages.vernacular: 即刻嗰隻小手毫不畏懼地喺我肩上到處撫摸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻那隻小手毫不畏懼地在我肩上到處撫摸。

passages.original: How good it felt!
passages.vernacular: 嗰感覺多好啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那感覺多好啊!

passages.original: “Let me get him a bran mash while you rub him down,” said the mother.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我畀佢弄一份麩皮糊,你畀佢擦洗,」母親講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我給他弄一份麩皮糊,你給他擦洗,」母親說。

passages.original: “Do, Polly, it's just what he wants; and I know you've got a beautiful mash ready for me.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,波麗,呢正是佢需要嘅;我知道你畀我準備咗一份美味嘅糊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,波麗,這正是他需要的;我知道你給我準備了一份美味的糊。」

passages.original: “Sausage dumpling and apple turnover!” shouted the boy, which set them all laughing.
passages.vernacular: 「香腸餃子同蘋果卷!」男孩喊道,逗得佢哋都笑起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「香腸餃子和蘋果卷!」男孩喊道,逗得他們都笑起來。

passages.original: I was led into a comfortable, clean-smelling stall, with plenty of dry straw, and after a capital supper I lay down, thinking I was going to be happy.
passages.vernacular: 我被領進一個舒適、氣味乾淨嘅馬棚,有大量乾稻草,一頓極好嘅晚餐後,我躺下,想住我要快樂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被領進一個舒適、氣味乾淨的馬棚,有大量乾稻草,一頓極好的晚餐後,我躺下,想著我要快樂了。

chapters.title: Part III · 33 A London Cab Horse 第三部·33 倫敦出租車馬

passages.original: CH Jeremiah Barker was my new master's name, but as every one called him Jerry, I shall do the same.
passages.vernacular: 我新主人嘅名字叫傑里米亞·巴克,但因為人人都叫佢傑瑞,我都咁樣叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我新主人的名字叫傑里米亞·巴克,但因為人人都叫他傑瑞,我也這樣叫。

passages.original: Polly, his wife, was just as good a match as a man could have.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅妻子波麗,係一個人所能有嘅最好嘅配偶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的妻子波麗,是一個人所能有的最好的配偶。

passages.original: She was a plump, trim, tidy little woman, with smooth, dark hair, dark eyes, and a merry little mouth.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個豐滿、整潔、乾淨嘅小個子女人,有光滑嘅黑髮、黑眼睛同一張快樂嘅小嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個豐滿、整潔、乾淨的小個子女人,有光滑的黑髮、黑眼睛和一張快樂的小嘴。

passages.original: The boy was twelve years old, a tall, frank, good-tempered lad; and little Dorothy (Dolly they called her) was her mother over again, at eight years old.
passages.vernacular: 男孩十二歲,係個高個子、坦率、脾氣好嘅小夥子;小多蘿西(佢哋叫佢多麗)八歲,係佢母親嘅翻版。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩十二歲,是個高個子、坦率、脾氣好的小夥子;小多蘿西(他們叫她多麗)八歲,是她母親的翻版。

passages.original: They were all wonderfully fond of each other; I never knew such a happy, merry family before or since.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋彼此都深愛對方;我從冇見過咁樣幸福快樂嘅家庭,以前冇,以後都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們彼此都深愛對方;我從沒見過這樣幸福快樂的家庭,以前沒有,以後也沒有。

passages.original: Jerry had a cab of his own, and two horses, which he drove and attended to himself.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞有自己嘅一輛出租馬車同兩匹馬,佢自己駕車並照料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞有自己的一輛出租馬車和兩匹馬,他自己駕車並照料。

passages.original: His other horse was a tall, white, rather large-boned animal called “Captain”.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅另一匹馬係一匹高大、白色、骨架相當大嘅牲口,叫「船長」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的另一匹馬是一匹高大、白色、骨架相當大的牲口,叫「船長」。

passages.original: He was old now, but when he was young he must have been splendid; he had still a proud way of holding his head and arching his neck; in fact, he was a high-bred, fine-mannered, noble old horse, every inch of him.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家老喇,但年輕時一定好出色;佢仍有驕傲地昂頭、拱頸嘅姿態;事實上,佢係匹血統高貴、風度優雅、高尚嘅老馬,每一寸都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在老了,但年輕時一定很出色;他仍有驕傲地昂頭、拱頸的姿態;事實上,他是匹血統高貴、風度優雅、高尚的老馬,每一寸都是。

passages.original: He told me that in his early youth he went to the Crimean War; he belonged to an officer in the cavalry, and used to lead the regiment.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴我,佢年輕時去過克里米亞戰爭;佢屬於一位騎兵軍官,常帶領團隊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他告訴我,他年輕時去過克里米亞戰爭;他屬於一位騎兵軍官,常帶領團隊。

passages.original: I will tell more of that hereafter.
passages.vernacular: 呢我以後再講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這我以後再講。

passages.original: The next morning, when I was well-groomed, Polly and Dolly came into the yard to see me and make friends.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,我被刷洗好之後,波麗同多麗嚟到院子裡睇我,同我交朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,我被刷洗好之後,波麗和多麗來到院子裡看我,和我交朋友。

passages.original: Harry had been helping his father since the early morning, and had stated his opinion that I should turn out a “regular brick”.
passages.vernacular: 哈里從清早就一直喺幫佢父親,並表示佢嘅意見,我會變成一個「真正嘅好貨」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里從清早就一直在幫他父親,並表示他的意見,我會變成一個「真正的好貨」。

passages.original: Polly brought me a slice of apple, and Dolly a piece of bread, and made as much of me as if I had been the “Black Beauty” of olden time.
passages.vernacular: 波麗畀我帶嚟一片蘋果,多麗帶嚟一塊麵包,對我疼愛有加,好像我係舊時代嘅「黑神駒」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗給我帶來一片蘋果,多麗帶來一塊麵包,對我疼愛有加,好像我是舊時代的「黑神駒」。

passages.original: It was a great treat to be petted again and talked to in a gentle voice, and I let them see as well as I could that I wished to be friendly.
passages.vernacular: 再次被寵愛並被溫和嘅聲音講話,係一大享受,我盡我所能讓佢哋睇出我願意友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再次被寵愛並被溫和的聲音說話,是一大享受,我盡我所能讓他們看出我願意友好。

passages.original: Polly thought I was very handsome, and a great deal too good for a cab, if it was not for the broken knees.
passages.vernacular: 波麗覺得我好漂亮,拉出租車太屈才,如果唔係因為膝蓋受傷嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗覺得我很漂亮,拉出租車太屈才,如果不是因為膝蓋受傷的話。

passages.original: “Of course there's no one to tell us whose fault that was,” said Jerry, “and as long as I don't know I shall give him the benefit of the doubt; for a firmer, neater stepper I never rode.
passages.vernacular: 「當然冇人能告訴我哋呢個係邊個嘅錯,」傑瑞講,「既然我唔知道,我就畀佢以疑點利益;因為我從冇騎過更穩、更乾淨利落嘅步伐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然沒人能告訴我們這是誰的錯,」傑瑞說,「既然我不知道,我就給他以疑點利益;因為我從沒騎過更穩、更乾淨利落的步伐。

passages.original: We'll call him 'Jack', after the old one--shall we, Polly?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋就叫佢『傑克』,隨嗰匹老嘅——好嗎,波麗?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們就叫他『傑克』,隨那匹老的——好嗎,波麗?」

passages.original: “Do,” she said, “for I like to keep a good name going.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,」佢講,「因為我鍾意讓一個好名字延續下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」她說,「因為我喜歡讓一個好名字延續下去。」

passages.original: Captain went out in the cab all the morning.
passages.vernacular: 船長整個早晨都拉住馬車出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 船長整個早晨都拉著馬車出去。

passages.original: Harry came in after school to feed me and give me water.
passages.vernacular: 哈里放學後來餵我並畀我水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里放學後來餵我並給我水。

passages.original: In the afternoon I was put into the cab.
passages.vernacular: 下午我被套進咗出租車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午我被套進了出租車。

passages.original: Jerry took as much pains to see if the collar and bridle fitted comfortably as if he had been John Manly over again.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞花咗好多力氣查睇頸圈同轡頭係咪舒適合身,好像佢就係約翰·曼利再世。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞花了很多力氣查看頸圈和轡頭是否舒適合身,好像他就是約翰·曼利再世。

passages.original: When the crupper was let out a hole or two it all fitted well.
passages.vernacular: 鞦韆放鬆一兩個孔後,一切都好合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鞦韆放鬆一兩個孔後,一切都很合適。

passages.original: There was no check-rein, no curb, nothing but a plain ring snaffle.
passages.vernacular: 冇止韁繩,冇鏈嚼子,只有一個普通嘅環形嚼子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有止韁繩,沒有鏈嚼子,只有一個普通的環形嚼子。

passages.original: What a blessing that was!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係多大嘅福氣啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是多大的福氣啊!

passages.original: After driving through the side street we came to the large cab stand where Jerry had said “Good-night”.
passages.vernacular: 穿過側街,我哋嚟到傑瑞講過「晚安」嘅大型出租車站。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿過側街,我們來到傑瑞說過「晚安」的大型出租車站。

passages.original: On one side of this wide street were high houses with wonderful shop fronts, and on the other was an old church and churchyard, surrounded by iron palisades.
passages.vernacular: 呢條寬街嘅一側係高房子,有奇妙嘅商店櫥窗,另一側係一座古老嘅教堂同墓地,周圍有鐵柵欄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這條寬街的一側是高房子,有奇妙的商店櫥窗,另一側是一座古老的教堂和墓地,周圍有鐵柵欄。

passages.original: Alongside these iron rails a number of cabs were drawn up, waiting for passengers; bits of hay were lying about on the ground; some of the men were standing together talking; some were sitting on their boxes reading the newspaper; and one or two were feeding their horses with bits of hay, and giving them a drink of water.
passages.vernacular: 沿住呢啲鐵欄杆停住許多出租馬車,等乘客;地上散落住幾片乾草;有些人站喺一起聊天;有些人坐喺車座上睇報紙;有一兩個人正用幾片乾草餵佢哋嘅馬,畀佢哋水飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沿著這些鐵欄杆停著許多出租馬車,等乘客;地上散落著幾片乾草;有些人站在一起聊天;有些人坐在車座上看報紙;有一兩個人正用幾片乾草餵他們的馬,給它們水喝。

passages.original: We pulled up in the rank at the back of the last cab.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺最後一輛馬車後面排進隊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在最後一輛馬車後面排進隊。

passages.original: Two or three men came round and began to look at me and pass their remarks.
passages.vernacular: 有兩三個人走過嚟睇我,並發表意見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有兩三個人走過來看我,並發表意見。

passages.original: “Very good for a funeral,” said one.
passages.vernacular: 「做殯葬車好不錯,」一個講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「做殯葬車很不錯,」一個說。

passages.original: “Too smart-looking,” said another, shaking his head in a very wise way; “you'll find out something wrong one of these fine mornings, or my name isn't Jones.”
passages.vernacular: 「太漂亮喇,」另一個講,聰明地搖住頭;「你呢啲好日子裡有一天會發現佢有乜嘢毛病,否則我就不叫瓊斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太漂亮了,」另一個說,聰明地搖著頭;「你這些好日子裡有一天會發現他有什麼毛病,否則我就不叫瓊斯。」

passages.original: “Well,” said Jerry pleasantly, “I suppose I need not find it out till it finds me out, eh?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」傑瑞愉快地講,「我想喺毛病找上我之前,我唔使去找佢,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」傑瑞愉快地說,「我想在毛病找上我之前,我不必去找它,是吧?

passages.original: And if so, I'll keep up my spirits a little longer.”
passages.vernacular: 如果係咁樣,我會把精神再保持久啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是這樣,我會把精神再保持久一點。」

passages.original: Then there came up a broad-faced man, dressed in a great gray coat with great gray cape and great white buttons, a gray hat, and a blue comforter loosely tied round his neck; his hair was gray, too; but he was a jolly-looking fellow, and the other men made way for him.
passages.vernacular: 然後走嚟一個臉寬寬嘅人,穿住一件灰色大外套,帶灰色大披肩同白色大扣子,戴灰帽子,脖子上鬆鬆繫住一條藍圍巾;佢嘅頭髮都係灰嘅;但佢睇起嚟係個快活嘅傢伙,其他人都畀佢讓路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後走來一個臉寬寬的人,穿著一件灰色大外套,帶灰色大披肩和白色大扣子,戴灰帽子,脖子上鬆鬆繫著一條藍圍巾;他的頭髮也是灰的;但他看起來是個快活的傢伙,其他人都給他讓路。

passages.original: He looked me all over, as if he had been going to buy me; and then straightening himself up with a grunt, he said, “He's the right sort for you, Jerry; I don't care what you gave for him, he'll be worth it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢把我從頭到腳睇咗一遍,好像要買我似嘅;然後哼咗一聲站直身子講:「佢係適合你嘅嗰種,傑瑞;我不在乎你花多少錢買嘅,佢值。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把我從頭到腳看了一遍,好像要買我似的;然後哼了一聲站直身子說:「他是適合你的那種,傑瑞;我不在乎你花多少錢買的,他值。」

passages.original: Thus my character was established on the stand.
passages.vernacular: 於是我嘅名聲就喺停靠站上確立喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我的名聲就在停靠站上確立了。

passages.original: This man's name was Grant, but he was called “Gray Grant”, or “Governor Grant”.
passages.vernacular: 呢個人叫格蘭特,但人哋叫佢「灰格蘭特」或「老大格蘭特」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個人叫格蘭特,但人們叫他「灰格蘭特」或「老大格蘭特」。

passages.original: He had been the longest on that stand of any of the men, and he took it upon himself to settle matters and stop disputes.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺呢個停靠站待得比所有人都久,佢自己擔負起解決事情、制止爭吵嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在這個停靠站待得比所有人都久,他自己擔負起解決事情、制止爭吵的責任。

passages.original: He was generally a good-humored, sensible man; but if his temper was a little out, as it was sometimes when he had drunk too much, nobody liked to come too near his fist, for he could deal a very heavy blow.
passages.vernacular: 佢通常係個脾氣好、明理嘅人;但如果佢脾氣有點不好,像有時飲多咗酒嗰樣,冇人願意靠近佢嘅拳頭,因為佢能打出好重嘅一拳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他通常是個脾氣好、明理的人;但如果他脾氣有點不好,像有時喝多了酒那樣,沒有人願意靠近他的拳頭,因為他能打出很重的一拳。

passages.original: The first week of my life as a cab horse was very trying.
passages.vernacular: 我作為出租車馬嘅生活嘅第一個星期好難熬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我作為出租車馬的生活的第一個星期非常難熬。

passages.original: I had never been used to London, and the noise, the hurry, the crowds of horses, carts, and carriages that I had to make my way through made me feel anxious and harassed; but I soon found that I could perfectly trust my driver, and then I made myself easy and got used to it.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇習慣過倫敦,必須穿過嘅噪音、匆忙、成群嘅馬、貨車同馬車,讓我覺得焦慮同煩惱;但我好快發現我完全可以信任我嘅駕車人,於是我放鬆下嚟,習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒習慣過倫敦,必須穿過的噪音、匆忙、成群的馬、貨車和馬車,讓我覺得焦慮和煩惱;但我很快發現我完全可以信任我的駕車人,於是我放鬆下來,習慣了。

passages.original: Jerry was as good a driver as I had ever known, and what was better, he took as much thought for his horses as he did for himself.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞係我所知最好嘅駕車人之一,更好嘅係,佢為佢嘅馬著想同為自己著想一樣多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞是我所知最好的駕車人之一,更好的是,他為他的馬著想和為自己著想一樣多。

passages.original: He soon found out that I was willing to work and do my best, and he never laid the whip on me unless it was gently drawing the end of it over my back when I was to go on; but generally I knew this quite well by the way in which he took up the reins, and I believe his whip was more frequently stuck up by his side than in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢好快發現我願意幹活並盡力而為,佢從不對我用鞭子,除非係喺我該繼續走時把鞭梢輕輕喺我背上劃過;不過通常我從佢攞起韁繩嘅方式就完全知道,我相信佢嘅鞭子更多時候係插喺身邊而唔係攞喺手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很快發現我願意幹活並盡力而為,他從不對我用鞭子,除非是在我該繼續走時把鞭梢輕輕在我背上劃過;不過通常我從他拿起韁繩的方式就完全知道,我相信他的鞭子更多時候是插在身邊而不是拿在手裡。

passages.original: In a short time I and my master understood each other as well as horse and man can do.
passages.vernacular: 不久,我同我嘅主人彼此了解,就像馬同人能做到嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,我和我的主人彼此了解,就像馬和人能做到的那樣。

passages.original: In the stable, too, he did all that he could for our comfort.
passages.vernacular: 喺馬廄裡,佢都盡其所能讓我哋舒適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在馬廄裡,他也盡其所能讓我們舒適。

passages.original: The stalls were the old-fashioned style, too much on the slope; but he had two movable bars fixed across the back of our stalls, so that at night, and when we were resting, he just took off our halters and put up the bars, and thus we could turn about and stand whichever way we pleased, which is a great comfort.
passages.vernacular: 馬棚都係老式嘅,傾斜得太厲害;但佢喺我哋馬棚後面固定咗兩根可移動嘅橫桿,咁樣晚上同我哋休息時,佢只要取下我哋嘅籠頭,放上橫桿,我哋就可以轉身,愛朝邊邊站就朝邊邊站,呢個係好大嘅舒適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬棚也是老式的,傾斜得太厲害;但他在我們馬棚後面固定了兩根可移動的橫桿,這樣晚上和我們休息時,他只要取下我們的籠頭,放上橫桿,我們就可以轉身,愛朝哪邊站就朝哪邊站,這是很大的舒適。

passages.original: Jerry kept us very clean, and gave us as much change of food as he could, and always plenty of it; and not only that, but he always gave us plenty of clean fresh water, which he allowed to stand by us both night and day, except of course when we came in warm.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞保持我哋好乾淨,盡可能多地畀我哋換食物,而且總是好充足;不僅如此,佢總是畀我哋足夠乾淨新鮮嘅水,日夜放喺我哋身邊,當然我哋熱住回嚟時除外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞保持我們非常乾淨,盡可能多地給我們換食物,而且總是很充足;不僅如此,他總是給我們足夠乾淨新鮮的水,日夜放在我們身邊,當然我們熱著回來時除外。

passages.original: Some people say that a horse ought not to drink all he likes; but I know if we are allowed to drink when we want it we drink only a little at a time, and it does us a great deal more good than swallowing down half a bucketful at a time, because we have been left without till we are thirsty and miserable.
passages.vernacular: 有些人講馬不該隨心所欲地飲水;但我知道,如果允許我哋想飲時就飲,我哋一次只飲啲,呢比我哋被渴得難受後一次吞下半桶好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人說馬不該隨心所欲地喝水;但我知道,如果允許我們想喝時就喝,我們一次只喝一點,這比我們被渴得難受後一次吞下半桶好得多。

passages.original: Some grooms will go home to their beer and leave us for hours with our dry hay and oats and nothing to moisten them; then of course we gulp down too much at once, which helps to spoil our breathing and sometimes chills our stomachs.
passages.vernacular: 有些馬夫會回家飲啤酒,把我哋留幾個小時,只有乾乾嘅草料同燕麥,冇嘢潤濕;嗰我哋當然一次吞太多,呢會破壞我哋嘅呼吸,有時仲會使胃受涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些馬夫會回家喝啤酒,把我們留幾個小時,只有乾乾的草料和燕麥,沒有東西潤濕;那我們當然一次吞太多,這會破壞我們的呼吸,有時還會使胃受涼。

passages.original: But the best thing we had here was our Sundays for rest; we worked so hard in the week that I do not think we could have kept up to it but for that day; besides, we had then time to enjoy each other's company.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋喺呢度最好嘅係我哋星期日嘅休息;我哋一週幹活咁辛苦,我想冇嗰一天我哋撐不住;而且,嗰時我哋有時間享受彼此嘅陪伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們在這裡最好的是我們星期日的休息;我們一週幹活那麼辛苦,我想沒有那一天我們撐不住;而且,那時我們有時間享受彼此的陪伴。

passages.original: It was on these days that I learned my companion's history.
passages.vernacular: 正是喺呢啲日子裡,我知道咗我同伴嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是在這些日子裡,我知道了我同伴的經歷。

chapters.title: Part III · 34 An Old War Horse 第三部·34 一匹老戰馬

passages.original: CH Captain had been broken in and trained for an army horse; his first owner was an officer of cavalry going out to the Crimean war.
passages.vernacular: 船長被馴服同訓練成咗軍馬;佢嘅第一個主人係一個將去克里米亞戰爭嘅騎兵軍官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 船長被馴服和訓練成了軍馬;他的第一個主人是一個將去克里米亞戰爭的騎兵軍官。

passages.original: He said he quite enjoyed the training with all the other horses, trotting together, turning together, to the right hand or the left, halting at the word of command, or dashing forward at full speed at the sound of the trumpet or signal of the officer.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢好鍾意同所有其他馬一起嘅訓練,一起小跑,一起向右或向左轉,聽到口令就停住,或聽到號角聲或軍官信號就全速衝上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他非常喜歡同所有其他馬一起的訓練,一起小跑,一起向右或向左轉,聽到口令就停住,或聽到號角聲或軍官信號就全速衝上去。

passages.original: He was, when young, a dark, dappled iron-gray, and considered very handsome.
passages.vernacular: 佢年輕時係深色嘅斑紋鐵灰色,被認為好漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他年輕時是深色的斑紋鐵灰色,被認為非常漂亮。

passages.original: His master, a young, high-spirited gentleman, was very fond of him, and treated him from the first with the greatest care and kindness.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅主人,一個年輕、精神旺盛嘅紳士,好鍾意佢,從一開始就畀予佢最大嘅照顧和善意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的主人,一個年輕、精神旺盛的紳士,非常喜歡他,從一開始就給予他最大的照顧和善意。

passages.original: He told me he thought the life of an army horse was very pleasant; but when it came to being sent abroad over the sea in a great ship, he almost changed his mind.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴我佢認為軍馬嘅生活好愉快;但輪到被一艘大船運到海外時,佢幾乎改變咗主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他告訴我他認為軍馬的生活非常愉快;但輪到被一艘大船運到海外時,他幾乎改變了主意。

passages.original: “That part of it,” said he, “was dreadful!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一部分,」佢講,「太可怕喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一部分,」他說,「太可怕了!

passages.original: Of course we could not walk off the land into the ship; so they were obliged to put strong straps under our bodies, and then we were lifted off our legs in spite of our struggles, and were swung through the air over the water, to the deck of the great vessel.
passages.vernacular: 當然我哋唔能夠從陸地走進船裡;所以佢哋唔得不把結實嘅帶子套喺我哋身體下面,然後不顧我哋嘅掙扎把我哋提離腿,喺水上方嘅空中擺盪住送到大船嘅甲板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我們不能從陸地走進船裡;所以他們不得不把結實的帶子套在我們身體下面,然後不顧我們的掙扎把我們提離腿,在水上方的空中擺盪著送到大船的甲板上。

passages.original: There we were placed in small close stalls, and never for a long time saw the sky, or were able to stretch our legs.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰度我哋被放喺狹小密閉嘅馬棚裡,好長時間再都睇唔見天空,都無法伸展腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那裡我們被放在狹小密閉的馬棚裡,很長時間再也看不見天空,也無法伸展腿。

passages.original: The ship sometimes rolled about in high winds, and we were knocked about, and felt bad enough.
passages.vernacular: 大風中船有時會搖晃,我哋被撞嚟撞去,難受得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大風中船有時會搖晃,我們被撞來撞去,難受得很。

passages.original: “However, at last it came to an end, and we were hauled up, and swung over again to the land; we were very glad, and snorted and neighed for joy, when we once more felt firm ground under our feet.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,終於結束喇,我哋又被拉起嚟,擺盪住回到陸地;我哋好高興,當我哋再次感到腳下堅實嘅地面時,高興得噴住鼻息、嘶鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,終於結束了,我們又被拉起來,擺盪著回到陸地;我們很高興,當我們再次感到腳下堅實的地面時,高興得噴著鼻息、嘶鳴。

passages.original: “We soon found that the country we had come to was very different from our own and that we had many hardships to endure besides the fighting; but many of the men were so fond of their horses that they did everything they could to make them comfortable in spite of snow, wet, and all things out of order.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋好快發現我哋嚟到嘅國家同我哋自己嘅好不同,除咗打仗,我哋仲要忍受許多艱難;但許多人咁鍾意佢哋嘅馬,不顧雪、潮濕同一切亂糟糟,佢哋盡一切所能讓佢哋舒適。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們很快發現我們來到的國家同我們自己的非常不同,除了打仗,我們還要忍受許多艱難;但許多人那麼喜歡他們的馬,不顧雪、潮濕和一切亂糟糟,他們盡一切所能讓它們舒適。」

passages.original: “But what about the fighting?” said I, “was not that worse than anything else?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過打仗呢?」我講,「嗰唔係比乜嘢都糟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是打仗呢?」我說,「那不是比什麼都糟嗎?」

passages.original: “Well,” said he, “I hardly know; we always liked to hear the trumpet sound, and to be called out, and were impatient to start off, though sometimes we had to stand for hours, waiting for the word of command; and when the word was given we used to spring forward as gayly and eagerly as if there were no cannon balls, bayonets, or bullets.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」佢講,「我幾乎唔知道;我哋總是鍾意聽到號角響起,被叫出去,迫不及待地要出發,雖然有時我哋要站幾個小時等口令;口令一下,我哋就快活、急切地向前躍出,好像冇炮彈、刺刀或子彈似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」他說,「我幾乎不知道;我們總是喜歡聽到號角響起,被叫出去,迫不及待地要出發,雖然有時我們要站幾個小時等口令;口令一下,我們就快活、急切地向前躍出,好像沒有炮彈、刺刀或子彈似的。

passages.original: I believe so long as we felt our rider firm in the saddle, and his hand steady on the bridle, not one of us gave way to fear, not even when the terrible bomb-shells whirled through the air and burst into a thousand pieces.
passages.vernacular: 我相信只要我哋感到騎手喺鞍子上穩穩坐住,手喺轡頭上穩定,我哋就冇一個屈服於恐懼,即使可怕嘅炸彈呼嘯住穿過空中,炸成一千片都不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信只要我們感到騎手在鞍子上穩穩坐著,手在轡頭上穩定,我們就沒有一個屈服於恐懼,即使可怕的炸彈呼嘯著穿過空中,炸成一千片也不。

passages.original: “I, with my noble master, went into many actions together without a wound; and though I saw horses shot down with bullets, pierced through with lances, and gashed with fearful saber-cuts; though we left them dead on the field, or dying in the agony of their wounds, I don't think I feared for myself.
passages.vernacular: 「我同我高貴嘅主人一起經歷咗許多戰鬥,冇受傷;雖然我睇見馬被子彈打倒,被長矛刺穿,被可怕嘅馬刀砍開;雖然我哋把佢哋留喺戰場上死去,或喺傷口嘅痛苦中垂死,我想我都不為自己害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同我高貴的主人一起經歷了許多戰鬥,沒有受傷;雖然我看見馬被子彈打倒,被長矛刺穿,被可怕的馬刀砍開;雖然我們把它們留在戰場上死去,或在傷口的痛苦中垂死,我想我也不為自己害怕。

passages.original: My master's cheery voice, as he encouraged his men, made me feel as if he and I could not be killed.
passages.vernacular: 我主人鼓勵佢嘅部下時愉快嘅聲音,讓我覺得佢同我唔可能被殺死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我主人鼓勵他的部下時愉快的聲音,讓我覺得他和我不可能被殺死。

passages.original: I had such perfect trust in him that while he was guiding me I was ready to charge up to the very cannon's mouth.
passages.vernacular: 我咁完全地信任佢,佢引導我時,我準備好衝到炮口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那麼完全地信任他,他引導我時,我準備好衝到炮口。

passages.original: I saw many brave men cut down, many fall mortally wounded from their saddles.
passages.vernacular: 我睇見許多勇敢嘅人被砍倒,許多人致命地受傷從鞍子上掉下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見許多勇敢的人被砍倒,許多人致命地受傷從鞍子上掉下來。

passages.original: I had heard the cries and groans of the dying, I had cantered over ground slippery with blood, and frequently had to turn aside to avoid trampling on wounded man or horse, but, until one dreadful day, I had never felt terror; that day I shall never forget.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽過垂死者嘅哭喊同呻吟,我喺血滑嘅地面上小跑過,常唔得不轉向一邊,以免踩到受傷嘅人或馬,但喺一個可怕嘅日子之前,我從未感到恐懼;嗰一天我永遠唔會忘記。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽過垂死者的哭喊和呻吟,我在血滑的地面上小跑過,常不得不轉向一邊,以免踩到受傷的人或馬,但在一個可怕的日子之前,我從未感到恐懼;那一天我永遠不會忘記。」

passages.original: Here old Captain paused for awhile and drew a long breath; I waited, and he went on.
passages.vernacular: 講到呢度,老船長停咗一會兒,深深吸咗一口氣;我等住,佢繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到這裡,老船長停了一會兒,深深吸了一口氣;我等著,他繼續說。

passages.original: “It was one autumn morning, and as usual, an hour before daybreak our cavalry had turned out, ready caparisoned for the day's work, whether it might be fighting or waiting.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係一個秋天嘅早晨,像往常一樣,黎明前一小時,我哋嘅騎兵已經出動,披掛整齊,準備好一天嘅任務,不論係戰鬥定係等待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是一個秋天的早晨,像往常一樣,黎明前一小時,我們的騎兵已經出動,披掛整齊,準備好一天的任務,不論是戰鬥還是等待。

passages.original: The men stood by their horses waiting, ready for orders.
passages.vernacular: 人哋站喺馬旁等候,準備接受命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們站在馬旁等候,準備接受命令。

passages.original: As the light increased there seemed to be some excitement among the officers; and before the day was well begun we heard the firing of the enemy's guns.
passages.vernacular: 隨住天色漸亮,軍官哋之間似乎有些激動;天剛亮不久,我哋聽到敵人炮火嘅射擊聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著天色漸亮,軍官們之間似乎有些激動;天剛亮不久,我們聽到敵人炮火的射擊聲。

passages.original: “Then one of the officers rode up and gave the word for the men to mount, and in a second every man was in his saddle, and every horse stood expecting the touch of the rein, or the pressure of his rider's heels, all animated, all eager; but still we had been trained so well that, except by the champing of our bits, and the restive tossing of our heads from time to time, it could not be said that we stirred.
passages.vernacular: 「然後一個軍官騎過嚟,下令士兵上馬,轉眼間每個人都喺鞍子上,每匹馬都站住等待韁繩嘅觸碰或騎手腳跟嘅壓力,全都精神振奮、急切;但我哋定係訓練得咁好,除咗咬嚼子嘅聲音同時不時不安地甩頭之外,唔能夠講我哋動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後一個軍官騎過來,下令士兵上馬,轉眼間每個人都在鞍子上,每匹馬都站著等待韁繩的觸碰或騎手腳跟的壓力,全都精神振奮、急切;但我們還是訓練得那麼好,除了咬嚼子的聲音和時不時不安地甩頭之外,不能說我們動了。

passages.original: “My dear master and I were at the head of the line, and as all sat motionless and watchful, he took a little stray lock of my mane which had turned over on the wrong side, laid it over on the right, and smoothed it down with his hand; then patting my neck, he said, 'We shall have a day of it to-day, Bayard, my beauty; but we'll do our duty as we have done.'
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅主人同我喺隊伍前頭,大家坐住一動不動、警惕觀望時,佢把我嘅鬃毛中一綹翻到錯誤一邊嘅散毛撥到右邊,用手撫平;然後拍住我嘅脖子講:『今日我哋要經歷一天,拜亞德,我嘅寶貝;但我哋會像以前一樣盡職。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的主人和我在隊伍前頭,大家坐著一動不動、警惕觀望時,他把我的鬃毛中一綹翻到錯誤一邊的散毛撥到右邊,用手撫平;然後拍著我的脖子說:『今天我們要經歷一天,拜亞德,我的寶貝;但我們會像以前一樣盡職。』

passages.original: He stroked my neck that morning more, I think, than he had ever done before; quietly on and on, as if he were thinking of something else.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天早晨佢撫摸我嘅脖子,我想比以往任何時候都多;安靜地一下又一下,好像喺想別嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天早晨他撫摸我的脖子,我想比以往任何時候都多;安靜地一下又一下,好像在想別的事。

passages.original: I loved to feel his hand on my neck, and arched my crest proudly and happily; but I stood very still, for I knew all his moods, and when he liked me to be quiet, and when gay.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意感覺佢嘅手喺我脖子上,驕傲而快樂地拱起我嘅鬃頂;但我站得好靜,因為我知道佢所有嘅心情,知道佢乜嘢時候鍾意我安靜,乜嘢時候鍾意我活潑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡感覺他的手在我脖子上,驕傲而快樂地拱起我的鬃頂;但我站得很靜,因為我知道他所有的心情,知道他什麼時候喜歡我安靜,什麼時候喜歡我活潑。

passages.original: “I cannot tell all that happened on that day, but I will tell of the last charge that we made together; it was across a valley right in front of the enemy's cannon.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰天發生嘅一切我講不完,但我要講我哋一起做嘅最後一次衝鋒;嗰個係穿過一個山谷,正對住敵人嘅大炮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那天發生的一切我說不完,但我要講我們一起做的最後一次衝鋒;那是穿過一個山谷,正對著敵人的大炮。

passages.original: By this time we were well used to the roar of heavy guns, the rattle of musket fire, and the flying of shot near us; but never had I been under such a fire as we rode through on that day.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣我哋已經好習慣重炮嘅轟鳴、步槍火力嘅噼啪同飛彈喺我哋附近嘅呼嘯;但我從未處喺像我哋嗰天騎過嘅嗰樣嘅炮火下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時我們已經很習慣重炮的轟鳴、步槍火力的噼啪和飛彈在我們附近的呼嘯;但我從未處在像我們那天騎過的那樣的炮火下。

passages.original: From the right, from the left, and from the front, shot and shell poured in upon us.
passages.vernacular: 從右邊、左邊同前面,炮彈同炮火傾瀉喺我哋身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從右邊、左邊和前面,炮彈和炮火傾瀉在我們身上。

passages.original: Many a brave man went down, many a horse fell, flinging his rider to the earth; many a horse without a rider ran wildly out of the ranks; then terrified at being alone, with no hand to guide him, came pressing in among his old companions, to gallop with them to the charge.
passages.vernacular: 許多勇敢嘅人倒下,許多馬摔倒,把騎手摔到地上;許多冇騎手嘅馬瘋狂地跑出隊列;然後因獨自一個、冇手引導而驚恐,擠回到佢哋嘅老夥伴中間,同佢哋一起衝鋒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多勇敢的人倒下,許多馬摔倒,把騎手摔到地上;許多沒有騎手的馬瘋狂地跑出隊列;然後因獨自一個、沒有手引導而驚恐,擠回到它們的老夥伴中間,與它們一起衝鋒。

passages.original: “Fearful as it was, no one stopped, no one turned back.
passages.vernacular: 「雖然可怕,冇人停下,冇人回頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雖然可怕,沒有人停下,沒有人回頭。

passages.original: Every moment the ranks were thinned, but as our comrades fell, we closed in to keep them together; and instead of being shaken or staggered in our pace our gallop became faster and faster as we neared the cannon.
passages.vernacular: 每一刻隊伍都喺變稀,但我哋嘅同伴倒下時,我哋合攏以保持喺一起;我哋冇被動搖或步伐踉蹌,而係隨住接近大炮,我哋嘅奔跑越嚟越快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一刻隊伍都在變稀,但我們的同伴倒下時,我們合攏以保持在一起;我們沒有被動搖或步伐踉蹌,而是隨著接近大炮,我們的奔跑越來越快。

passages.original: “My master, my dear master was cheering on his comrades with his right arm raised on high, when one of the balls whizzing close to my head struck him.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅主人,我親愛嘅主人正揮起右臂鼓舞佢嘅戰友,呢陣一顆炮彈呼嘯住擦過我嘅頭,擊中咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的主人,我親愛的主人正揮起右臂鼓舞他的戰友,這時一顆炮彈呼嘯著擦過我的頭,擊中了他。

passages.original: I felt him stagger with the shock, though he uttered no cry; I tried to check my speed, but the sword dropped from his right hand, the rein fell loose from the left, and sinking backward from the saddle he fell to the earth; the other riders swept past us, and by the force of their charge I was driven from the spot.
passages.vernacular: 我感到佢因衝擊而搖晃,雖然佢冇喊叫;我試圖減速,可劍從佢嘅右手掉落,韁繩從左手鬆開,佢從鞍子上向後倒下,落到地上;其他騎手從我哋身邊掃過,衝鋒嘅力量把我從嗰度推開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感到他因衝擊而搖晃,雖然他沒有喊叫;我試圖減速,可劍從他的右手掉落,韁繩從左手鬆開,他從鞍子上向後倒下,落到地上;其他騎手從我們身邊掃過,衝鋒的力量把我從那裡推開了。

passages.original: “I wanted to keep my place by his side and not leave him under that rush of horses' feet, but it was in vain; and now without a master or a friend I was alone on that great slaughter ground; then fear took hold on me, and I trembled as I had never trembled before; and I too, as I had seen other horses do, tried to join in the ranks and gallop with them; but I was beaten off by the swords of the soldiers.
passages.vernacular: 「我想留喺佢身邊,不把佢留喺嗰群馬蹄嘅洶湧中,但係徒勞;而家冇主人都冇朋友,我獨自在嗰個巨大嘅屠殺場上;然後恐懼抓住咗我,我顫抖得前所未有;我都,像我睇到嘅其他馬一樣,試圖加入隊伍同佢哋一起奔跑;但我被士兵嘅劍趕開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想留在他身邊,不把他留在那群馬蹄的洶湧中,但是徒勞;現在沒有主人也沒有朋友,我獨自在那個巨大的屠殺場上;然後恐懼抓住了我,我顫抖得前所未有;我也,像我看到的其他馬一樣,試圖加入隊伍同它們一起奔跑;但我被士兵的劍趕開了。

passages.original: Just then a soldier whose horse had been killed under him caught at my bridle and mounted me, and with this new master I was again going forward; but our gallant company was cruelly overpowered, and those who remained alive after the fierce fight for the guns came galloping back over the same ground.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,一個坐騎被打死嘅士兵抓住我嘅轡頭,騎上咗我,有咗呢個新主人,我又向前進;但我哋英勇嘅隊伍被殘酷地壓倒喇,喺爭奪大炮嘅激烈戰鬥後倖存嘅人,又沿住同一塊地面飛奔回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,一個坐騎被打死的士兵抓住我的轡頭,騎上了我,有了這個新主人,我又向前進;但我們英勇的隊伍被殘酷地壓倒了,在爭奪大炮的激烈戰鬥後倖存的人,又沿著同一塊地面飛奔回來。

passages.original: Some of the horses had been so badly wounded that they could scarcely move from the loss of blood; other noble creatures were trying on three legs to drag themselves along, and others were struggling to rise on their fore feet, when their hind legs had been shattered by shot.
passages.vernacular: 有些馬傷得咁重,因為失血幾乎動彈唔得;其他高貴嘅生靈試圖用三條腿拖住自己走,仲有些後腿被炮彈打碎,試圖用前腿站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些馬傷得那麼重,因為失血幾乎動彈不得;其他高貴的生靈試圖用三條腿拖著自己走,還有些後腿被炮彈打碎,試圖用前腿站起來。

passages.original: After the battle the wounded men were brought in and the dead were buried.”
passages.vernacular: 戰鬥後,傷員被抬進嚟,死者被埋葬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戰鬥後,傷員被抬進來,死者被埋葬。」

passages.original: “And what about the wounded horses?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰受傷嘅馬呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那受傷的馬呢?」

passages.original: I said; “were they left to die?”
passages.vernacular: 我講;「佢哋被留下等死嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說;「它們被留下等死嗎?」

passages.original: “No, the army farriers went over the field with their pistols and shot all that were ruined; some that had only slight wounds were brought back and attended to, but the greater part of the noble, willing creatures that went out that morning never came back!
passages.vernacular: 「不,軍隊嘅蹄鐵匠帶著手槍走遍戰場,把所有無法挽救嘅都槍斃喇;啲傷勢輕嘅被帶回去治療,但嗰天早晨出去嘅大部分高貴、願意嘅生靈再都冇回嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,軍隊的蹄鐵匠帶著手槍走遍戰場,把所有無法挽救的都槍斃了;一些傷勢輕的被帶回去治療,但那天早晨出去的大部分高貴、願意的生靈再也沒有回來!

passages.original: In our stables there was only about one in four that returned.
passages.vernacular: 喺我哋嘅馬廄裡,只有大約四分之一回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我們的馬廄裡,只有大約四分之一回來了。

passages.original: “I never saw my dear master again.
passages.vernacular: 「我再都冇見到我親愛嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也沒有見到我親愛的主人。

passages.original: I believe he fell dead from the saddle.
passages.vernacular: 我相信佢從鞍子上死去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信他從鞍子上死去了。

passages.original: I never loved any other master so well.
passages.vernacular: 我再都冇咁愛過任何別嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再也沒有那麼愛過任何別的主人。

passages.original: I went into many other engagements, but was only once wounded, and then not seriously; and when the war was over I came back again to England, as sound and strong as when I went out.”
passages.vernacular: 我又經歷咗許多其他戰鬥,但只受過一次傷,而且不嚴重;戰爭結束後,我回到英國,像出去時一樣健康強壯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我又經歷了許多其他戰鬥,但只受過一次傷,而且不嚴重;戰爭結束後,我回到英國,像出去時一樣健康強壯。」

passages.original: I said, “I have heard people talk about war as if it was a very fine thing.”
passages.vernacular: 我講:「我聽到人哋談論戰爭,好像嗰個係件好了不起嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說:「我聽到人們談論戰爭,好像那是件很了不起的事。」

passages.original: “Ah!” said he, “I should think they never saw it.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!」佢講,「我想佢哋從冇見過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!」他說,「我想他們從沒見過。

passages.original: No doubt it is very fine when there is no enemy, when it is just exercise and parade and sham fight.
passages.vernacular: 無疑,當冇敵人時,只係演習、閱兵同假戰時,係好了不起嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無疑,當沒有敵人時,只是演習、閱兵和假戰時,是很了不起的。

passages.original: Yes, it is very fine then; but when thousands of good brave men and horses are killed or crippled for life, it has a very different look.”
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,嗰時係好了不起;但當成千上萬嘅好勇士同馬被殺死或終身殘廢時,就完全係另一副面貌喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,那時是很了不起;但當成千上萬的好勇士和馬被殺死或終身殘廢時,就完全是另一副面貌了。」

passages.original: “Do you know what they fought about?” said I.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道佢哋係點解打仗嗎?」我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道他們是為什麼打仗嗎?」我說。

passages.original: “No,” he said, “that is more than a horse can understand, but the enemy must have been awfully wicked people, if it was right to go all that way over the sea on purpose to kill them.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔知道,」佢講,「嗰超出咗一匹馬所能理解嘅,但如果有必要專程跨海去殺佢哋,敵人一定係極其邪惡嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知道,」他說,「那超出了一匹馬所能理解的,但如果有必要專程跨海去殺他們,敵人一定是極其邪惡的人。」

chapters.title: Part III · 35 Jerry Barker 第三部·35 傑瑞·巴克

passages.original: CH I never knew a better man than my new master.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過比我嘅新主人更好嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過比我的新主人更好的人。

passages.original: He was kind and good, and as strong for the right as John Manly; and so good-tempered and merry that very few people could pick a quarrel with him.
passages.vernacular: 佢善良,正直,像約翰·曼利一樣堅定地支持正義;而且咁好脾氣、快活,好少有人能同佢吵得起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他善良,正直,像約翰·曼利一樣堅定地支持正義;而且那麼好脾氣、快活,很少有人能同他吵得起來。

passages.original: He was very fond of making little songs, and singing them to himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢好鍾意編小歌,自己唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常喜歡編小歌,自己唱。

passages.original: One he was very fond of was this:
passages.vernacular: 佢特別鍾意嘅一首係咁樣嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他特別喜歡的一首是這樣的:

passages.original: “Come, father and mother, And sister and brother, Come, all of you, turn to And help one another.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟吧,爸爸同媽媽,仲有姐妹同兄弟,嚟吧,大家都動手,彼此互相幫忙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來吧,爸爸和媽媽,還有姐妹和兄弟,來吧,大家都動手,彼此互相幫忙。」

passages.original: And so they did; Harry was as clever at stable-work as a much older boy, and always wanted to do what he could.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都咁樣做;哈里喺馬廄活上同比佢大得多嘅男孩一樣機靈,而且總想盡佢所能做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們也這樣做;哈里在馬廄活上和比他大得多的男孩一樣機靈,而且總想盡他所能做。

passages.original: Then Polly and Dolly used to come in the morning to help with the cab--to brush and beat the cushions, and rub the glass, while Jerry was giving us a cleaning in the yard, and Harry was rubbing the harness.
passages.vernacular: 波麗同多麗常喺早晨嚟幫忙整理馬車——刷、拍墊子,擦玻璃,傑瑞喺院子裡畀我哋刷洗,哈里喺擦挽具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗和多麗常在早晨來幫忙整理馬車——刷、拍墊子,擦玻璃,傑瑞在院子裡給我們刷洗,哈里在擦挽具。

passages.original: There used to be a great deal of laughing and fun between them, and it put Captain and me in much better spirits than if we had heard scolding and hard words.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋之間常有好多笑聲同樂趣,呢使船長同我嘅精神比聽到責罵同難聽嘅話好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們之間常有很多笑聲和樂趣,這使船長和我的精神比聽到責罵和難聽的話好得多。

passages.original: They were always early in the morning, for Jerry would say:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋早晨總是好早,因為傑瑞會講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們早晨總是很早,因為傑瑞會說:

passages.original: “If you in the morning Throw minutes away, You can't pick them up In the course of a day.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你早晨把分鐘浪費,一天之內都撿不回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你早晨把分鐘浪費,一天之內也撿不回來。

passages.original: You may hurry and scurry, And flurry and worry, You've lost them forever, Forever and aye.”
passages.vernacular: 你可以匆忙、慌張、焦急、擔憂,你永遠失去咗佢哋,永永遠遠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以匆忙、慌張、焦急、擔憂,你永遠失去了它們,永永遠遠。」

passages.original: He could not bear any careless loitering and waste of time; and nothing was so near making him angry as to find people, who were always late, wanting a cab horse to be driven hard, to make up for their idleness.
passages.vernacular: 佢受不了任何馬虎嘅閒逛同浪費時間;最讓佢幾乎生氣嘅,係發現總是遲到嘅人,想讓出租馬車馬拚命趕,嚟彌補佢哋嘅懶散。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他受不了任何馬虎的閒逛和浪費時間;最讓他幾乎生氣的,是發現總是遲到的人,想讓出租馬車馬拚命趕,來彌補他們的懶散。

passages.original: One day two wild-looking young men came out of a tavern close by the stand, and called Jerry.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,兩個睇起嚟放蕩嘅年輕人從停靠站附近嘅一間酒館出嚟,叫傑瑞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,兩個看起來放蕩的年輕人從停靠站附近的一間酒館出來,叫傑瑞。

passages.original: “Here, cabby! look sharp, we are rather late; put on the steam, will you, and take us to the Victoria in time for the one o'clock train?
passages.vernacular: 「呢度,車夫!快點,我哋有點晚喇;加快速度,好嗎?送我哋及時趕到維多利亞站坐啲鐘嘅火車?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡,車夫!快點,我們有點晚了;加快速度,好嗎?送我們及時趕到維多利亞站坐一點鐘的火車?

passages.original: You shall have a shilling extra.”
passages.vernacular: 你可以多得一先令。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以多得一先令。」

passages.original: “I will take you at the regular pace, gentlemen; shillings don't pay for putting on the steam like that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會以正常嘅速度送你哋,先生哋;一先令唔夠為嗰樣加快速度付出。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會以正常的速度送你們,先生們;一先令不夠為那樣加快速度付出。」

passages.original: Larry's cab was standing next to ours; he flung open the door, and said, “I'm your man, gentlemen! take my cab, my horse will get you there all right;” and as he shut them in, with a wink toward Jerry, said, “It's against his conscience to go beyond a jog-trot.”
passages.vernacular: 拉里嘅馬車停喺我哋旁邊;佢猛地打開車門,講:「我就係你哋要嘅人,先生哋!坐我嘅車,我嘅馬會把你哋準時送到;」佢把佢哋關進車裡,朝傑瑞眨咗眨眼,講:「超過慢跑對佢嘅良心係不許可嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉里的馬車停在我們旁邊;他猛地打開車門,說:「我就是你們要的人,先生們!坐我的車,我的馬會把你們準時送到;」他把他們關進車裡,朝傑瑞眨了眨眼,說:「超過慢跑對他的良心是不許可的。」

passages.original: Then slashing his jaded horse, he set off as hard as he could.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢抽打佢疲憊嘅馬,盡可能快地出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他抽打他疲憊的馬,盡可能快地出發了。

passages.original: Jerry patted me on the neck: “No, Jack, a shilling would not pay for that sort of thing, would it, old boy?”
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞拍住我嘅脖子:「不,傑克,一先令唔夠為嗰種事付出,對吧,老夥計?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞拍著我的脖子:「不,傑克,一先令不夠為那種事付出,對吧,老夥計?」

passages.original: Although Jerry was determinedly set against hard driving, to please careless people, he always went a good fair pace, and was not against putting on the steam, as he said, if only he knew why.
passages.vernacular: 雖然傑瑞堅決反對為了討好粗心嘅人而拚命駕車,佢總是以不錯嘅合理速度行進,只要佢知道點解,佢並不反對加快速度,佢咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然傑瑞堅決反對為了討好粗心的人而拚命駕車,他總是以不錯的合理速度行進,只要他知道為什麼,他並不反對加快速度,他這麼說。

passages.original: I well remember one morning, as we were on the stand waiting for a fare, that a young man, carrying a heavy portmanteau, trod on a piece of orange peel which lay on the pavement, and fell down with great force.
passages.vernacular: 我清楚地記得一天早晨,我哋喺停靠站等乘客,一個年輕人提住一個沉重嘅旅行皮箱,踩到咗人行道上嘅一塊橙子皮,猛烈地摔倒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我清楚地記得一天早晨,我們在停靠站等乘客,一個年輕人提著一個沉重的旅行皮箱,踩到了人行道上的一塊橙子皮,猛烈地摔倒了。

passages.original: Jerry was the first to run and lift him up.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞係第一個跑去把佢扶起嚟嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞是第一個跑去把他扶起來的人。

passages.original: He seemed much stunned, and as they led him into a shop he walked as if he were in great pain.
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎暈得好厲害,佢哋把佢領進一家商店時,佢走路像好痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他似乎暈得很厲害,他們把他領進一家商店時,他走路像很痛。

passages.original: Jerry of course came back to the stand, but in about ten minutes one of the shopmen called him, so we drew up to the pavement.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞當然回到咗停靠站,但大約好鐘後,一個店員叫佢,於是我哋靠到人行道旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞當然回到了停靠站,但大約十分鐘後,一個店員叫他,於是我們靠到人行道旁。

passages.original: “Can you take me to the South-Eastern Railway?” said the young man; “this unlucky fall has made me late, I fear; but it is of great importance that I should not lose the twelve o'clock train.
passages.vernacular: 「您能送我去東南鐵路車站嗎?」年輕人講;「呢次倒楣嘅摔倒我怕讓我晚喇;但我唔能夠錯過十二點嘅火車,呢個好重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您能送我去東南鐵路車站嗎?」年輕人說;「這次倒楣的摔倒我怕讓我晚了;但我不能錯過十二點的火車,這非常重要。

passages.original: I should be most thankful if you could get me there in time, and will gladly pay you an extra fare.”
passages.vernacular: 如果您能及時送我到,我會好感激,並樂意多付車費。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您能及時送我到,我會非常感激,並樂意多付車費。」

passages.original: “I'll do my very best,” said Jerry heartily, “if you think you are well enough, sir,” for he looked dreadfully white and ill.
passages.vernacular: 「我會盡我最大嘅努力,」傑瑞誠懇地講,「如果您認為您嘅身體夠好,先生,」因為佢睇起嚟可怕地蒼白,有病容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會盡我最大的努力,」傑瑞誠懇地說,「如果您認為您的身體夠好,先生,」因為他看起來可怕地蒼白,有病容。

passages.original: “I must go,” he said earnestly, “please to open the door, and let us lose no time.”
passages.vernacular: 「我必須去,」佢懇切地講,「請開門,我哋別耽擱時間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須去,」他懇切地說,「請開門,我們別耽擱時間。」

passages.original: The next minute Jerry was on the box; with a cheery chirrup to me, and a twitch of the rein that I well understood.
passages.vernacular: 下一分鐘傑瑞已喺車座上;佢愉快地對我吆飲咗一聲,抖咗抖我熟悉嘅韁繩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一分鐘傑瑞已在車座上;他愉快地對我吆喝了一聲,抖了抖我熟悉的韁繩。

passages.original: “Now then, Jack, my boy,” said he, “spin along, we'll show them how we can get over the ground, if we only know why.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,傑克,我嘅細路,」佢講,「飛奔吧,我哋讓佢哋睇睇我哋點樣趕路,只要我哋知道點解。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,傑克,我的孩子,」他說,「飛奔吧,我們讓他們看看我們怎樣趕路,只要我們知道為什麼。」

passages.original: It is always difficult to drive fast in the city in the middle of the day, when the streets are full of traffic, but we did what could be done; and when a good driver and a good horse, who understand each other, are of one mind, it is wonderful what they can do.
passages.vernacular: 中午喺城裡,街道上擠滿咗車輛,要快跑總是困難嘅,但我哋做咗能做嘅;當一個好嘅駕車人同一匹好馬,彼此了解,同心協力時,佢哋能做嘅事真係奇妙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午在城裡,街道上擠滿了車輛,要快跑總是困難的,但我們做了能做的;當一個好的駕車人和一匹好馬,彼此了解,同心協力時,他們能做的事真是奇妙。

passages.original: I had a very good mouth--that is I could be guided by the slightest touch of the rein; and that is a great thing in London, among carriages, omnibuses, carts, vans, trucks, cabs, and great wagons creeping along at a walking pace; some going one way, some another, some going slowly, others wanting to pass them; omnibuses stopping short every few minutes to take up a passenger, obliging the horse that is coming behind to pull up too, or to pass, and get before them; perhaps you try to pass, but just then something else comes dashing in through the narrow opening, and you have to keep in behind the omnibus again; presently you think you see a chance, and manage to get to the front, going so near the wheels on each side that half an inch nearer and they would scrape.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅嘴好好——就係講我能被韁繩最輕微嘅觸碰引導;呢喺倫敦係件大事,喺馬車、公共汽車、貨車、廂式車、卡車、出租車同以步行速度爬行嘅大馬車之間;有嘅往呢邊,有嘅往嗰邊,有嘅慢,有嘅想超過佢哋;公共汽車每隔幾分鐘就突然停下接乘客,迫使後面嘅馬都得停下,或者超過佢哋,趕到佢哋前面;或者你試住超過,但正在嗰時有別嘅乜嘢嘢從狹窄嘅空隙猛衝進嚟,你唔得唔再次跟喺公共汽車後面;不久你想你睇到機會喇,設法到咗前面,兩邊離輪子咁近,再近半英寸就會刮到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的嘴很好——就是說我能被韁繩最輕微的觸碰引導;這在倫敦是件大事,在馬車、公共汽車、貨車、廂式車、卡車、出租車和以步行速度爬行的大馬車之間;有的往這邊,有的往那邊,有的慢,有的想超過它們;公共汽車每隔幾分鐘就突然停下接乘客,迫使後面的馬也得停下,或者超過它們,趕到它們前面;也許你試著超過,但正在那時有別的什麼東西從狹窄的空隙猛衝進來,你不得不再次跟在公共汽車後面;不久你想你看到機會了,設法到了前面,兩邊離輪子那麼近,再近半英寸就會刮到。

passages.original: Well, you get along for a bit, but soon find yourself in a long train of carts and carriages all obliged to go at a walk; perhaps you come to a regular block-up, and have to stand still for minutes together, till something clears out into a side street, or the policeman interferes; you have to be ready for any chance--to dash forward if there be an opening, and be quick as a rat-dog to see if there be room and if there be time, lest you get your own wheels locked or smashed, or the shaft of some other vehicle run into your chest or shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 好,你走咗一會兒,但好快發現自己處喺一長串貨車同馬車嘅隊伍裡,全都唔得不步行;或者你遇到真正嘅堵塞,唔得不一動不動站好幾分鐘,直到乜嘢嘢清走進咗側街,或警察干預;你必須準備好抓住任何機會——有空隙就衝上去,要像捕鼠犬一樣敏捷地睇有冇空間,有冇時間,以免你自己嘅輪子被卡住或撞碎,或某個別嘅車輛嘅轅桿撞進你嘅胸或肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你走了一會兒,但很快發現自己處在一長串貨車和馬車的隊伍裡,全都不得不步行;也許你遇到真正的堵塞,不得不一動不動站好幾分鐘,直到什麼東西清走進了側街,或警察干預;你必須準備好抓住任何機會——有空隙就衝上去,要像捕鼠犬一樣敏捷地看有沒有空間,有沒有時間,以免你自己的輪子被卡住或撞碎,或某個別的車輛的轅桿撞進你的胸或肩。

passages.original: All this is what you have to be ready for.
passages.vernacular: 所有呢啲都係你必須準備好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些都是你必須準備好的。

passages.original: If you want to get through London fast in the middle of the day it wants a deal of practice.
passages.vernacular: 如果你想喺中午快速穿過倫敦,需要大量練習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你想在中午快速穿過倫敦,需要大量練習。

passages.original: Jerry and I were used to it, and no one could beat us at getting through when we were set upon it.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞同我習慣喇,我哋要穿過去時,冇人能勝過我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞和我習慣了,我們要穿過去時,沒有人能勝過我們。

passages.original: I was quick and bold and could always trust my driver; Jerry was quick and patient at the same time, and could trust his horse, which was a great thing too.
passages.vernacular: 我快速、大膽,又總是能信任我嘅駕車人;傑瑞快速又有耐心,同時都能信任佢嘅馬,呢都係件大事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我快速、大膽,又總是能信任我的駕車人;傑瑞快速又有耐心,同時也能信任他的馬,這也是件大事。

passages.original: He very seldom used the whip; I knew by his voice, and his click, click, when he wanted to get on fast, and by the rein where I was to go; so there was no need for whipping; but I must go back to my story.
passages.vernacular: 佢好少用鞭子;我從佢嘅聲音同佢嘅吆飲聲「喀、喀」知道佢想快走,從韁繩知道我該往邊度走;所以不需要抽打;但我得回到我嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很少用鞭子;我從他的聲音和他的吆喝聲「喀、喀」知道他想快走,從韁繩知道我該往哪裡走;所以不需要抽打;但我得回到我的故事。

passages.original: The streets were very full that day, but we got on pretty well as far as the bottom of Cheapside, where there was a block for three or four minutes.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天街道好擁擠,但我哋走得相當好,直到齊普賽街嘅底部,嗰度堵塞咗三四分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天街道很擁擠,但我們走得相當好,直到齊普賽街的底部,那裡堵塞了三四分鐘。

passages.original: The young man put his head out and said anxiously, “I think I had better get out and walk; I shall never get there if this goes on.”
passages.vernacular: 年輕人探出頭,焦急地講:「我想我最好下車走;如果咁樣下去,我永遠到不喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕人探出頭,焦急地說:「我想我最好下車走;如果這樣下去,我永遠到不了。」

passages.original: “I'll do all that can be done, sir,” said Jerry; “I think we shall be in time.
passages.vernacular: 「我會做一切能做嘅,先生,」傑瑞講;「我想我哋會及時嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會做一切能做的,先生,」傑瑞說;「我想我們會及時的。

passages.original: This block-up cannot last much longer, and your luggage is very heavy for you to carry, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 呢堵塞唔會持續太久,而且您嘅行李對您太重喇,先生,您攞不動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這堵塞不會持續太久,而且您的行李對您太重了,先生,您拿不動。」

passages.original: Just then the cart in front of us began to move on, and then we had a good turn.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,我哋前面嘅貨車開始走動,然後我哋輪到咗好時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,我們前面的貨車開始走動,然後我們輪到了好時候。

passages.original: In and out, in and out we went, as fast as horseflesh could do it, and for a wonder had a good clear time on London Bridge, for there was a whole train of cabs and carriages all going our way at a quick trot, perhaps wanting to catch that very train.
passages.vernacular: 我哋穿梭進出,以馬所能做到嘅最快速度,奇蹟般地喺倫敦橋上有一段暢通嘅時間,因為有一整列出租車同馬車都以快步小跑朝我哋呢個方向走,或者想趕嗰同一班火車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們穿梭進出,以馬所能做到的最快速度,奇蹟般地在倫敦橋上有一段暢通的時間,因為有一整列出租車和馬車都以快步小跑朝我們這個方向走,也許想趕那同一班火車。

passages.original: At any rate, we whirled into the station with many more, just as the great clock pointed to eight minutes to twelve o'clock.
passages.vernacular: 總之,我哋同許多別嘅車一起風馳電掣地進咗車站,正好嗰個大鐘指向十二點差八分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,我們同許多別的車一起風馳電掣地進了車站,正好那個大鐘指向十二點差八分。

passages.original: “Thank God! we are in time,” said the young man, “and thank you, too, my friend, and your good horse.
passages.vernacular: 「感謝上帝!我哋趕上喇,」年輕人講,「都感謝你,我嘅朋友,同你嘅好馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「感謝上帝!我們趕上了,」年輕人說,「也感謝你,我的朋友,和你的好馬。

passages.original: You have saved me more than money can ever pay for.
passages.vernacular: 你救咗我,係多少錢都報答不咗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你救了我,是多少錢也報答不了的。

passages.original: Take this extra half-crown.”
passages.vernacular: 收下呢額外嘅半克朗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收下這額外的半克朗。」

passages.original: “No, sir, no, thank you all the same; so glad we hit the time, sir; but don't stay now, sir, the bell is ringing.
passages.vernacular: 「不,先生,不,謝謝您;趕上時間我哋真高興,先生;但而家別停留,先生,鈴喺響喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,先生,不,謝謝您;趕上時間我們真高興,先生;但現在別停留,先生,鈴在響了。

passages.original: Here, porter! take this gentleman's luggage--Dover line twelve o'clock train--that's it,” and without waiting for another word Jerry wheeled me round to make room for other cabs that were dashing up at the last minute, and drew up on one side till the crush was past.
passages.vernacular: 呢度,搬運工!攞呢位先生嘅行李——多佛線十二點嘅火車——就係嗰個,」傑瑞冇等再講一個字,就把我調轉,為最後一刻衝過嚟嘅其他馬車讓出地方,靠到一邊,直到擁擠過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡,搬運工!拿這位先生的行李——多佛線十二點的火車——就是那個,」傑瑞沒等再說一個字,就把我調轉,為最後一刻衝過來的其他馬車讓出地方,靠到一邊,直到擁擠過去。

passages.original: “'So glad!' he said, 'so glad!'
passages.vernacular: 「『太高興喇!』佢講,『太高興喇!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『太高興了!』他說,『太高興了!』

passages.original: Poor young fellow!
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅年輕人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的年輕人!

passages.original: I wonder what it was that made him so anxious!”
passages.vernacular: 我納悶係乜嘢使佢咁焦急!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我納悶是什麼使他那麼焦急!」

passages.original: Jerry often talked to himself quite loud enough for me to hear when we were not moving.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇動時,傑瑞常自言自語,聲音大得足夠我聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒動時,傑瑞常自言自語,聲音大得足夠我聽見。

passages.original: On Jerry's return to the rank there was a good deal of laughing and chaffing at him for driving hard to the train for an extra fare, as they said, all against his principles, and they wanted to know how much he had pocketed.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞回到隊列,許多人笑佢、取笑佢為了額外車費拚命趕火車,佢哋講,呢同佢嘅原則完全相反,佢哋想知道佢裝進咗多少錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞回到隊列,許多人笑他、取笑他為了額外車費拚命趕火車,他們說,這與他的原則完全相反,他們想知道他裝進了多少錢。

passages.original: “A good deal more than I generally get,” said he, nodding slyly; “what he gave me will keep me in little comforts for several days.”
passages.vernacular: 「比我通常得到嘅多得多,」佢講,狡猾地點頭;「佢畀我嘅會讓我享受小小嘅舒適好幾天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「比我通常得到的多得多,」他說,狡猾地點頭;「他給我的會讓我享受小小的舒適好幾天。」

passages.original: “Gammon!” said one.
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!」一個講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!」一個說。

passages.original: “He's a humbug,” said another; “preaching to us and then doing the same himself.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個騙子,」另一個講;「向我哋講教,然後自己做同樣嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是個騙子,」另一個說;「向我們說教,然後自己做同樣的事。」

passages.original: “Look here, mates,” said Jerry; “the gentleman offered me half a crown extra, but I didn't take it; 'twas quite pay enough for me to see how glad he was to catch that train; and if Jack and I choose to have a quick run now and then to please ourselves, that's our business and not yours.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,夥計哋,」傑瑞講;「嗰位先生講要多畀我半克朗,我冇收;睇到佢趕上嗰班火車咁高興,對我來講已經夠報酬喇;如果傑克同我選擇偶爾為了自己高興跑快啲,嗰個係我哋嘅事,唔係你哋嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,夥計們,」傑瑞說;「那位先生說要多給我半克朗,我沒收;看到他趕上那班火車那麼高興,對我來說已經夠報酬了;如果傑克和我選擇偶爾為了自己高興跑快一點,那是我們的事,不是你們的。」

passages.original: “Well,” said Larry, “you'll never be a rich man.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」拉里講,「你永遠唔會成為富人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」拉里說,「你永遠不會成為富人。」

passages.original: “Most likely not,” said Jerry; “but I don't know that I shall be the less happy for that.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能唔會,」傑瑞講;「但我唔知道我會因此少快樂啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能不會,」傑瑞說;「但我不知道我會因此少快樂一點。

passages.original: I have heard the commandments read a great many times and I never noticed that any of them said, 'Thou shalt be rich'; and there are a good many curious things said in the New Testament about rich men that I think would make me feel rather queer if I was one of them.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽過十誡被讀咗好多次,我從冇注意到其中任何一條講『你應當富有』;新約裡關於富人講咗許多奇怪嘅事,我想如果我係其中一個,會讓我覺得相當不自在。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽過十誡被讀了很多次,我從沒注意到其中任何一條說『你應當富有』;新約裡關於富人說了許多奇怪的事,我想如果我是其中一個,會讓我覺得相當不自在。」

passages.original: “If you ever do get rich,” said Governor Gray, looking over his shoulder across the top of his cab, “you'll deserve it, Jerry, and you won't find a curse come with your wealth.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你有一天真嘅發財喇,」灰老大講,從佢馬車頂上回頭睇,「你配得上,傑瑞,而且你唔會發現你嘅財富帶嚟詛咒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你有一天真的發財了,」灰老大說,從他馬車頂上回頭看,「你配得上,傑瑞,而且你不會發現你的財富帶來詛咒。

passages.original: As for you, Larry, you'll die poor; you spend too much in whipcord.”
passages.vernacular: 至於你,拉里,你會窮死;你花喺鞭繩上嘅太多喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於你,拉里,你會窮死;你花在鞭繩上的太多了。」

passages.original: “Well,” said Larry, “what is a fellow to do if his horse won't go without it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」拉里講,「如果馬冇佢就唔肯走,一個人能點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」拉里說,「如果馬沒有它就不肯走,一個人能怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “You never take the trouble to see if he will go without it; your whip is always going as if you had the St. Vitus' dance in your arm, and if it does not wear you out it wears your horse out; you know you are always changing your horses; and why?
passages.vernacular: 「你從不費心睇睇冇佢佢會唔會走;你嘅鞭子總是喺揮舞,好像你胳膊有聖維特斯舞蹈症,如果佢冇把你累垮,佢就把你嘅馬累垮;你知道你總是喺換馬;點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從不費心看看沒有它他會不會走;你的鞭子總是在揮舞,好像你胳膊有聖維特斯舞蹈症,如果它沒把你累垮,它就把你的馬累垮;你知道你總是在換馬;為什麼?

passages.original: Because you never give them any peace or encouragement.”
passages.vernacular: 因為你從不畀佢哋安寧或鼓勵。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你從不給它們安寧或鼓勵。」

passages.original: “Well, I have not had good luck,” said Larry, “that's where it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我運氣不好,」拉里講,「就係咁回事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我運氣不好,」拉里說,「就是這麼回事。」

passages.original: “And you never will,” said the governor.
passages.vernacular: 「你永遠唔會好,」老大講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你永遠不會好,」老大說。

passages.original: “Good Luck is rather particular who she rides with, and mostly prefers those who have got common sense and a good heart; at least that is my experience.”
passages.vernacular: 「好運挺挑剔佢同邊個騎馬,大多鍾意有常識、有好心腸嘅人;至少呢個係我嘅經驗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好運挺挑剔她同誰騎馬,大多喜歡有常識、有好心腸的人;至少這是我的經驗。」

passages.original: Governor Gray turned round again to his newspaper, and the other men went to their cabs.
passages.vernacular: 灰老大又轉回去睇佢嘅報紙,其他人回到咗各自嘅馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 灰老大又轉回去看他的報紙,其他人回到了各自的馬車。

chapters.title: Part III · 36 The Sunday Cab 第三部·36 星期日的出租車

passages.original: CH One morning, as Jerry had just put me into the shafts and was fastening the traces, a gentleman walked into the yard.
passages.vernacular: 一天早晨,傑瑞剛把我套進轅桿,正在繫挽繩,一位紳士走進院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天早晨,傑瑞剛把我套進轅桿,正在繫挽繩,一位紳士走進院子。

passages.original: “Your servant, sir,” said Jerry.
passages.vernacular: 「為您效勞,先生,」傑瑞講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為您效勞,先生,」傑瑞說。

passages.original: “Good-morning, Mr. Barker,” said the gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 「早安,巴克先生,」嗰位紳士講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「早安,巴克先生,」那位紳士說。

passages.original: “I should be glad to make some arrangements with you for taking Mrs. Briggs regularly to church on Sunday mornings.
passages.vernacular: 「我想同你作些安排,定期星期日早晨送布里格斯太太去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想同你作些安排,定期星期日早晨送布里格斯太太去教堂。

passages.original: We go to the New Church now, and that is rather further than she can walk.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家去新教堂,嗰比佢能走嘅路遠啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在去新教堂,那比她能走的路遠一些。」

passages.original: “Thank you, sir,” said Jerry, “but I have only taken out a six-days' license,* and therefore I could not take a fare on a Sunday; it would not be legal.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝您,先生,」傑瑞講,「但我只領咗六天嘅執照,*所以我星期日唔能夠接客;嗰個係不合法嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝您,先生,」傑瑞說,「但我只領了六天的執照,*所以我星期日不能接客;那是不合法的。」

passages.original: * A few years since the annual charge for a cab license was very much reduced, and the difference between the six and seven days' cabs was abolished.
passages.vernacular: * 幾年前,出租馬車執照嘅年費大大降低,六天同七天出租車嘅區別被取消喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: * 幾年前,出租馬車執照的年費大大降低,六天和七天出租車的區別被取消了。

passages.original: “Oh!” said the other, “I did not know yours was a six-days' cab; but of course it would be very easy to alter your license.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!」另一個講,「我唔知道你嘅係六天嘅車;不過當然改你嘅執照好容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!」另一個說,「我不知道你的是六天的車;不過當然改你的執照非常容易。

passages.original: I would see that you did not lose by it; the fact is, Mrs. Briggs very much prefers you to drive her.”
passages.vernacular: 我會保證你不食虧;事實係,布里格斯太太好鍾意你為佢駕車。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會保證你不吃虧;事實是,布里格斯太太非常喜歡你為她駕車。」

passages.original: “I should be glad to oblige the lady, sir, but I had a seven-days' license once, and the work was too hard for me, and too hard for my horses.
passages.vernacular: 「我好樂意為女士效勞,先生,但我曾經領過七天嘅執照,嗰工作對我太辛苦,對我嘅馬都太辛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很樂意為女士效勞,先生,但我曾經領過七天的執照,那工作對我太辛苦,對我的馬也太辛苦。

passages.original: Year in and year out, not a day's rest, and never a Sunday with my wife and children; and never able to go to a place of worship, which I had always been used to do before I took to the driving box.
passages.vernacular: 一年到頭,冇一天休息,從唔能夠喺星期日同我嘅妻子細路喺一起;都從唔能夠去禮拜嘅地方,喺我登上駕駛座之前我一直習慣去嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一年到頭,沒有一天休息,從不能在星期日同我的妻子孩子在一起;也從不能去禮拜的地方,在我登上駕駛座之前我一直習慣去的。

passages.original: So for the last five years I have only taken a six-days' license, and I find it better all the way round.”
passages.vernacular: 所以最近五年我只領六天嘅執照,我發現佢從各方面都更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以最近五年我只領六天的執照,我發現它從各方面都更好。」

passages.original: “Well, of course,” replied Mr. Briggs, “it is very proper that every person should have rest, and be able to go to church on Sundays, but I should have thought you would not have minded such a short distance for the horse, and only once a day; you would have all the afternoon and evening for yourself, and we are very good customers, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當然,」布里格斯先生回答,「每個人都應該休息,能喺星期日去教堂,呢個係好對嘅,但我本以為你唔會介意咁短嘅距離,對馬來講,而且一天一次;你整個下午同晚上都屬於自己,你知道,我哋係好好嘅顧客。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當然,」布里格斯先生回答,「每個人都應該休息,能在星期日去教堂,這是很對的,但我本以為你不會介意這麼短的距離,對馬來說,而且一天一次;你整個下午和晚上都屬於自己,你知道,我們是很好的顧客。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir, that is true, and I am grateful for all favors, I am sure; and anything that I could do to oblige you, or the lady, I should be proud and happy to do; but I can't give up my Sundays, sir, indeed I can't.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,呢個係真嘅,我確信我感激一切恩惠;凡是我能做嘅嚟取悅您或女士嘅,我都會好驕傲、好高興地做;但我唔能夠放棄我嘅星期日,先生,確實唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,這是真的,我確信我感激一切恩惠;凡是我能做的來取悅您或女士的,我都會很驕傲、很高興地做;但我不能放棄我的星期日,先生,確實不能。

passages.original: I read that God made man, and he made horses and all the other beasts, and as soon as He had made them He made a day of rest, and bade that all should rest one day in seven; and I think, sir, He must have known what was good for them, and I am sure it is good for me; I am stronger and healthier altogether, now that I have a day of rest; the horses are fresh too, and do not wear up nearly so fast.
passages.vernacular: 我讀到,上帝造咗人,造咗馬同所有其他嘅獸,祂一造出佢哋,就造咗一個休息日,並命令所有生靈七天休息一天;我想,先生,祂一定知道乜嘢對佢哋好,我確信呢對我係好嘅;而家有一天休息,我整個人更強壯、更健康;馬都精神,磨損都冇咁快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讀到,上帝造了人,造了馬和所有其他的獸,祂一造出它們,就造了一個休息日,並命令所有生靈七天休息一天;我想,先生,祂一定知道什麼對它們好,我確信這對我是好的;現在有一天休息,我整個人更強壯、更健康;馬也精神,磨損也沒有那麼快。

passages.original: The six-day drivers all tell me the same, and I have laid by more money in the savings bank than ever I did before; and as for the wife and children, sir, why, heart alive! they would not go back to the seven days for all they could see.”
passages.vernacular: 六天嘅車夫都對我講同樣嘅話,我存進儲蓄銀行嘅錢都比以前多;至於妻子同細路,先生,嗨,天呀!佢哋睇到嘅一切都唔能夠讓佢哋再回到七天嘅日子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六天的車夫都對我說同樣的話,我存進儲蓄銀行的錢也比以前多;至於妻子和孩子,先生,嗨,天哪!他們看到的一切都不能讓他們再回到七天的日子。」

passages.original: “Oh, very well,” said the gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好好,」嗰位紳士講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,很好,」那位紳士說。

passages.original: “Don't trouble yourself, Mr. Barker, any further.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好再費心喇,巴克先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別再費心了,巴克先生。

passages.original: I will inquire somewhere else,” and he walked away.
passages.vernacular: 我去別處問,」佢走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去別處問,」他走開了。

passages.original: “Well,” says Jerry to me, “we can't help it, Jack, old boy; we must have our Sundays.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」傑瑞對我講,「我哋都冇辦法,傑克,老夥計;我哋必須有我哋嘅星期日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」傑瑞對我說,「我們也沒辦法,傑克,老夥計;我們必須有我們的星期日。」

passages.original: “Polly!” he shouted, “Polly! come here.”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗!」佢喊道,「波麗!過嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗!」他喊道,「波麗!過來。」

passages.original: She was there in a minute.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉眼就到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她轉眼就到了。

passages.original: “What is it all about, Jerry?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係點回事,傑瑞?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是怎麼回事,傑瑞?」

passages.original: “Why, my dear, Mr. Briggs wants me to take Mrs. Briggs to church every Sunday morning.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,親愛嘅,布里格斯先生要我每個星期日早晨送布里格斯太太去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,親愛的,布里格斯先生要我每個星期日早晨送布里格斯太太去教堂。

passages.original: I say I have only a six-days' license.
passages.vernacular: 我講我只有六天嘅執照。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說我只有六天的執照。

passages.original: He says, 'Get a seven-days' license, and I'll make it worth your while;' and you know, Polly, they are very good customers to us.
passages.vernacular: 佢講:『領一個七天嘅執照,我會讓你值得。』你知道,波麗,佢哋對我哋係好好嘅顧客。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:『領一個七天的執照,我會讓你值得。』你知道,波麗,他們對我們是很好的顧客。

passages.original: Mrs. Briggs often goes out shopping for hours, or making calls, and then she pays down fair and honorable like a lady; there's no beating down or making three hours into two hours and a half, as some folks do; and it is easy work for the horses; not like tearing along to catch trains for people that are always a quarter of an hour too late; and if I don't oblige her in this matter it is very likely we shall lose them altogether.
passages.vernacular: 布里格斯太太常出去購物幾個小時,或拜訪,然後佢像個女士一樣公道誠實地付錢;佢唔會討價仲價,或把三個小時講成兩個半小時,像有些人嗰樣;對馬來講都係輕鬆嘅活;不像為嗰啲總是遲到一刻鐘嘅人猛衝去趕火車;如果我喺呢件事上不遷就佢,我哋好可能完全失去佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布里格斯太太常出去購物幾個小時,或拜訪,然後她像個女士一樣公道誠實地付錢;她不會討價還價,或把三個小時說成兩個半小時,像有些人那樣;對馬來說也是輕鬆的活;不像為那些總是遲到一刻鐘的人猛衝去趕火車;如果我在這件事上不遷就她,我們很可能完全失去他們。

passages.original: What do you say, little woman?”
passages.vernacular: 你講呢,小女人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說呢,小女人?」

passages.original: “I say, Jerry,” says she, speaking very slowly, “I say, if Mrs. Briggs would give you a sovereign every Sunday morning, I would not have you a seven-days' cabman again.
passages.vernacular: 「我講,傑瑞,」佢講,講得好慢,「我講,即使布里格斯太太每個星期日早晨畀你一個金鎊,我都唔好你再做七天嘅車夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,傑瑞,」她說,說得非常慢,「我說,即使布里格斯太太每個星期日早晨給你一個金鎊,我也不要你再做七天的車夫。

passages.original: We have known what it was to have no Sundays, and now we know what it is to call them our own.
passages.vernacular: 我哋知道冇星期日係乜嘢樣,而家我哋知道把佢哋叫作自己嘅係乜嘢滋味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們知道沒有星期日是什麼樣,現在我們知道把它們叫作自己的是什麼滋味。

passages.original: Thank God, you earn enough to keep us, though it is sometimes close work to pay for all the oats and hay, the license, and the rent besides; but Harry will soon be earning something, and I would rather struggle on harder than we do than go back to those horrid times when you hardly had a minute to look at your own children, and we never could go to a place of worship together, or have a happy, quiet day.
passages.vernacular: 感謝上帝,你賺嘅夠養活我哋,雖然有時要支付所有燕麥同乾草、執照同房租都好緊;但哈里不久就會賺點乜嘢,我寧願比而家更辛苦地奮鬥,都唔願回到嗰啲可怕嘅日子,你幾乎冇一分鐘睇睇你自己嘅細路,我哋都從唔能夠一起去禮拜嘅地方,或者度過快樂安靜嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感謝上帝,你賺的夠養活我們,雖然有時要支付所有燕麥和乾草、執照和房租也很緊;但哈里不久就會賺點什麼,我寧願比現在更辛苦地奮鬥,也不願回到那些可怕的日子,你幾乎沒有一分鐘看看你自己的孩子,我們也從不能一起去禮拜的地方,或者度過快樂安靜的一天。

passages.original: God forbid that we should ever turn back to those times; that's what I say, Jerry.”
passages.vernacular: 上帝禁止我哋再回到嗰啲日子;呢個就係我要講嘅,傑瑞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝禁止我們再回到那些日子;這就是我要說的,傑瑞。」

passages.original: “And that is just what I told Mr. Briggs, my dear,” said Jerry, “and what I mean to stick to.
passages.vernacular: 「呢正是我對布里格斯先生講嘅,親愛嘅,」傑瑞講,「都係我打算堅持嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這正是我對布里格斯先生說的,親愛的,」傑瑞說,「也是我打算堅持的。

passages.original: So don't go and fret yourself, Polly” (for she had begun to cry); “I would not go back to the old times if I earned twice as much, so that is settled, little woman.
passages.vernacular: 所以唔好去煩惱,波麗」(因為佢開始哭喇);「即使我賺兩倍多,我都唔願回到老日子,所以呢件事定喇,小女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以別去煩惱,波麗」(因為她開始哭了);「即使我賺兩倍多,我也不願回到老日子,所以這件事定了,小女人。

passages.original: Now, cheer up, and I'll be off to the stand.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,振作起嚟,我要去停靠站喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,振作起來,我要去停靠站了。」

passages.original: Three weeks had passed away after this conversation, and no order had come from Mrs. Briggs; so there was nothing but taking jobs from the stand.
passages.vernacular: 呢次談話後過咗三個星期,布里格斯太太嗰邊冇任何訂單;所以只有從停靠站接活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次談話後過了三個星期,布里格斯太太那邊沒有任何訂單;所以只有從停靠站接活。

passages.original: Jerry took it to heart a good deal, for of course the work was harder for horse and man.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞好放喺心上,因為當然馬同人嘅活都更辛苦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞很放在心上,因為當然馬和人的活都更辛苦了。

passages.original: But Polly would always cheer him up, and say, “Never mind, father, never, mind.
passages.vernacular: 但波麗總是讓佢振作起嚟,講:「別在意,爸爸,別在意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但波麗總是讓他振作起來,說:「別在意,爸爸,別在意。

passages.original: “'Do your best, And leave the rest, 'Twill all come right Some day or night.'”
passages.vernacular: 『盡你所能,其餘嘅別管,總有一天一個晚上,一切都會好。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『盡你所能,其餘的別管,總有一天一個晚上,一切都會好。』」

passages.original: It soon became known that Jerry had lost his best customer, and for what reason.
passages.vernacular: 好快人哋就知道咗傑瑞失去咗佢最好嘅顧客,以及點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快人們就知道了傑瑞失去了他最好的顧客,以及為什麼。

passages.original: Most of the men said he was a fool, but two or three took his part.
passages.vernacular: 大多數人講佢係個傻瓜,但有兩三個站喺佢一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數人說他是個傻瓜,但有兩三個站在他一邊。

passages.original: “If workingmen don't stick to their Sunday,” said Truman, “they'll soon have none left; it is every man's right and every beast's right.
passages.vernacular: 「如果工人不堅持佢哋嘅星期日,」特魯曼講,「佢哋好快就冇喇;呢個係每個人嘅權利,都係每頭牲口嘅權利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果工人不堅持他們的星期日,」特魯曼說,「他們很快就沒有了;這是每個人的權利,也是每頭牲口的權利。

passages.original: By God's law we have a day of rest, and by the law of England we have a day of rest; and I say we ought to hold to the rights these laws give us and keep them for our children.”
passages.vernacular: 按上帝嘅律法我哋有一個休息日,按英國嘅法律我哋有一個休息日;我講我哋應該堅持呢啲律法賦予我哋嘅權利,並為我哋嘅細路保住佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按上帝的律法我們有一個休息日,按英國的法律我們有一個休息日;我說我們應該堅持這些律法賦予我們的權利,並為我們的孩子保住它們。」

passages.original: “All very well for you religious chaps to talk so,” said Larry; “but I'll turn a shilling when I can.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋呢啲虔誠嘅人咁樣講當然好,」拉里講;「但我能賺一先令就賺一先令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們這些虔誠的人這樣說當然好,」拉里說;「但我能賺一先令就賺一先令。

passages.original: I don't believe in religion, for I don't see that your religious people are any better than the rest.”
passages.vernacular: 我不信宗教,因為我睇不出你哋虔誠嘅人比其他人好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不信宗教,因為我看不出你們虔誠的人比其他人好。」

passages.original: “If they are not better,” put in Jerry, “it is because they are not religious.
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢哋不更好,」傑瑞插話講,「嗰個係因為佢哋不虔誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他們不更好,」傑瑞插話說,「那是因為他們不虔誠。

passages.original: You might as well say that our country's laws are not good because some people break them.
passages.vernacular: 你都不妨講我哋國家嘅法律不好,因為有些人違反佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也不妨說我們國家的法律不好,因為有些人違反它們。

passages.original: If a man gives way to his temper, and speaks evil of his neighbor, and does not pay his debts, he is not religious, I don't care how much he goes to church.
passages.vernacular: 如果一個人放縱脾氣,講鄰居壞話,不還債,佢就不虔誠,我不在乎佢去教堂多少次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一個人放縱脾氣,說鄰居壞話,不還債,他就不虔誠,我不在乎他去教堂多少次。

passages.original: If some men are shams and humbugs, that does not make religion untrue.
passages.vernacular: 如果有些人係假貨同騙子,嗰唔能夠使宗教不真實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有些人是假貨和騙子,那不能使宗教不真實。

passages.original: Real religion is the best and truest thing in the world, and the only thing that can make a man really happy or make the world we live in any better.”
passages.vernacular: 真正嘅宗教係世上最好、最真實嘅嘢,都係唯一能使人真正快樂或使我哋生活嘅世界變得更好嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真正的宗教是世上最好、最真實的東西,也是唯一能使人真正快樂或使我們生活的世界變得更好的東西。」

passages.original: “If religion was good for anything,” said Jones, “it would prevent your religious people from making us work on Sundays, as you know many of them do, and that's why I say religion is nothing but a sham; why, if it was not for the church and chapel-goers it would be hardly worth while our coming out on a Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 「如果宗教有任何用處,」瓊斯講,「佢就會阻止你哋虔誠嘅人讓我哋星期日幹活,你知道佢哋中許多人咁樣做,呢個就係我講宗教不過係騙局嘅原因;嗨,如果唔係去教堂同禮拜堂嘅人,我哋星期日幾乎不值得出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果宗教有任何用處,」瓊斯說,「它就會阻止你們虔誠的人讓我們星期日幹活,你知道他們中許多人這樣做,這就是我說宗教不過是騙局的原因;嗨,如果不是去教堂和禮拜堂的人,我們星期日幾乎不值得出來。

passages.original: But they have their privileges, as they call them, and I go without.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋有佢哋嘅特權,像佢哋所講嘅,我則冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們有他們的特權,像他們所說的,我則沒有。

passages.original: I shall expect them to answer for my soul, if I can't get a chance of saving it.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我得唔到拯救自己靈魂嘅機會,我會期待佢哋為我嘅靈魂負責。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我得不到拯救自己靈魂的機會,我會期待他們為我的靈魂負責。」

passages.original: Several of the men applauded this, till Jerry said:
passages.vernacular: 有幾個人為此鼓掌,直到傑瑞講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾個人為此鼓掌,直到傑瑞說:

passages.original: “That may sound well enough, but it won't do; every man must look after his own soul; you can't lay it down at another man's door like a foundling and expect him to take care of it; and don't you see, if you are always sitting on your box waiting for a fare, they will say, 'If we don't take him some one else will, and he does not look for any Sunday.'
passages.vernacular: 「嗰聽起嚟或者不錯,但行不通;每個人必須照顧自己嘅靈魂;你唔能夠把佢像棄嬰一樣放喺別人嘅門口,指望佢照顧;你冇睇見嗎,如果你總是坐喺車座上等客,佢哋會講:『如果我哋不乘佢嘅,別人都會乘,佢都不期待乜嘢星期日。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那聽起來也許不錯,但行不通;每個人必須照顧自己的靈魂;你不能把它像棄嬰一樣放在別人的門口,指望他照顧;你沒看見嗎,如果你總是坐在車座上等客,他們會說:『如果我們不乘他的,別人也會乘,他也不期待什麼星期日。』

passages.original: Of course, they don't go to the bottom of it, or they would see if they never came for a cab it would be no use your standing there; but people don't always like to go to the bottom of things; it may not be convenient to do it; but if you Sunday drivers would all strike for a day of rest the thing would be done.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢哋冇追根究底,否則佢哋會睇到,如果佢哋從不嚟叫車,你站喺嗰度都冇用;但人哋並不總是鍾意追根究底;或者不方便;但如果你哋星期日嘅車夫都為一天嘅休息罷工,事情就辦成喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,他們沒有追根究底,否則他們會看到,如果他們從不來叫車,你站在那裡也沒用;但人們並不總是喜歡追根究底;也許不方便;但如果你們星期日的車夫都為一天的休息罷工,事情就辦成了。」

passages.original: “And what would all the good people do if they could not get to their favorite preachers?” said Larry.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰所有好人如果去不咗佢哋最鍾意嘅牧師嗰度點算?」拉里講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那所有好人如果去不了他們最喜歡的牧師那裡怎麼辦?」拉里說。
