passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高貴的老傢伙,是很好的伴。

passages.original: I never thought that he would have to leave his home and go down the hill; but his turn came, and this was how it happened.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇想過佢必須離開家、走下坡路;可佢嘅輪次到喇,係咁樣發生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒想過他必須離開家、走下坡路;可他的輪次到了,是這樣發生的。

passages.original: I was not there, but I heard all about it.
passages.vernacular: 我不喺嗰度,但我聽講咗一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在那裡,但我聽說了一切。

passages.original: He and Jerry had taken a party to the great railway station over London Bridge, and were coming back, somewhere between the bridge and the monument, when Jerry saw a brewer's empty dray coming along, drawn by two powerful horses.
passages.vernacular: 佢同傑瑞載咗一夥人去倫敦橋對面嘅大火車站,正在回嚟,喺橋同紀念碑之間嘅某處,傑瑞睇見一輛啤酒商嘅空載重貨車沿路而嚟,由兩匹強壯嘅馬拉住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他和傑瑞載了一夥人去倫敦橋對面的大火車站,正在回來,在橋和紀念碑之間的某處,傑瑞看見一輛啤酒商的空載重貨車沿路而來,由兩匹強壯的馬拉著。

passages.original: The drayman was lashing his horses with his heavy whip; the dray was light, and they started off at a furious rate; the man had no control over them, and the street was full of traffic.
passages.vernacular: 車夫正用佢嘅重鞭抽打佢嘅馬;車好輕,佢哋以狂暴嘅速度出發;嗰人無法控制佢哋,而街上滿係車輛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 車夫正用他的重鞭抽打他的馬;車很輕,它們以狂暴的速度出發;那人無法控制它們,而街上滿是車輛。

passages.original: One young girl was knocked down and run over, and the next moment they dashed up against our cab; both the wheels were torn off and the cab was thrown over.
passages.vernacular: 一個年輕女孩被撞倒並壓過,下一刻佢哋衝撞上咗我哋嘅出租車;兩個輪子都被撕掉,車被掀翻喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個年輕女孩被撞倒並壓過,下一刻它們衝撞上了我們的出租車;兩個輪子都被撕掉,車被掀翻了。

passages.original: Captain was dragged down, the shafts splintered, and one of them ran into his side.
passages.vernacular: 船長被拖倒,轅桿裂成碎片,其中一根刺進咗佢嘅側身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 船長被拖倒,轅桿裂成碎片,其中一根刺進了他的側身。

passages.original: Jerry, too, was thrown, but was only bruised; nobody could tell how he escaped; he always said 'twas a miracle.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞都被甩出去,但只受咗擦傷;冇人能講佢點逃脫嘅;佢總講嗰個係奇蹟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞也被甩出去,但只受了擦傷;沒人能說他怎麼逃脫的;他總說那是奇蹟。

passages.original: When poor Captain was got up he was found to be very much cut and knocked about.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅船長被扶起嚟時,發現被割傷同撞傷得好厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的船長被扶起來時,發現被割傷和撞傷得很厲害。

passages.original: Jerry led him home gently, and a sad sight it was to see the blood soaking into his white coat and dropping from his side and shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞輕輕地把佢牽回家,睇到血浸透佢嘅白毛,從佢嘅身側同肩膀滴下嚟,係令人悲傷嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞輕輕地把他牽回家,看到血浸透他的白毛,從他的身側和肩膀滴下來,是令人悲傷的景象。

passages.original: The drayman was proved to be very drunk, and was fined, and the brewer had to pay damages to our master; but there was no one to pay damages to poor Captain.
passages.vernacular: 車夫被證明飲得爛醉,被罰款,啤酒商要向我哋主人賠償損失;但冇人賠償可憐嘅船長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 車夫被證明喝得爛醉,被罰款,啤酒商要向我們主人賠償損失;但沒有人賠償可憐的船長。

passages.original: The farrier and Jerry did the best they could to ease his pain and make him comfortable.
passages.vernacular: 蹄鐵匠同傑瑞盡其所能減輕佢嘅痛苦,讓佢舒適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蹄鐵匠和傑瑞盡其所能減輕他的痛苦,讓他舒適。

passages.original: The fly had to be mended, and for several days I did not go out, and Jerry earned nothing.
passages.vernacular: 輕便馬車需要修理,好幾天我冇出去,傑瑞乜嘢都冇賺到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕便馬車需要修理,好幾天我沒有出去,傑瑞什麼也沒賺到。

passages.original: The first time we went to the stand after the accident the governor came up to hear how Captain was.
passages.vernacular: 事故後我哋第一次去停靠站,老大過嚟聽船長點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事故後我們第一次去停靠站,老大過來聽船長怎麼樣。

passages.original: “He'll never get over it,” said Jerry, “at least not for my work, so the farrier said this morning.
passages.vernacular: 「佢永遠好不咗喇,」傑瑞講,「至少對我嘅工作來講,今日早晨蹄鐵匠咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他永遠好不了了,」傑瑞說,「至少對我的工作來說,今天早晨蹄鐵匠這麼說。

passages.original: He says he may do for carting, and that sort of work.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢或者可以做拉貨嘅工作,嗰類活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他也許可以做拉貨的工作,那類活。

passages.original: It has put me out very much.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓我好煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓我非常煩惱。

passages.original: Carting, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 拉貨,確實!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉貨,確實!

passages.original: I've seen what horses come to at that work round London.
passages.vernacular: 我見過馬幹嗰種活喺倫敦周圍嘅下場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我見過馬幹那種活在倫敦周圍的下場。

passages.original: I only wish all the drunkards could be put in a lunatic asylum instead of being allowed to run foul of sober people.
passages.vernacular: 我只希望所有嘅酒鬼都被關進瘋人院,而唔係被允許撞上清醒嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只希望所有的酒鬼都被關進瘋人院,而不是被允許撞上清醒的人。

passages.original: If they would break their own bones, and smash their own carts, and lame their own horses, that would be their own affair, and we might let them alone, but it seems to me that the innocent always suffer; and then they talk about compensation!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋摔斷自己嘅骨頭,砸碎自己嘅車,弄瘸自己嘅馬,嗰個係佢哋自己嘅事,我哋可以不管佢哋,但喺我睇來無辜嘅人總是受苦;然後佢哋仲講乜嘢賠償!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們摔斷自己的骨頭,砸碎自己的車,弄瘸自己的馬,那是他們自己的事,我們可以不管他們,但在我看來無辜的人總是受苦;然後他們還說什麼賠償!

passages.original: You can't make compensation; there's all the trouble, and vexation, and loss of time, besides losing a good horse that's like an old friend--it's nonsense talking of compensation!
passages.vernacular: 你無法賠償;有所有嘅麻煩、煩惱同時間損失,仲失去一匹像老朋友一樣嘅好馬——談賠償係胡扯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你無法賠償;有所有的麻煩、煩惱和時間損失,還失去一匹像老朋友一樣的好馬——談賠償是胡扯!

passages.original: If there's one devil that I should like to see in the bottomless pit more than another, it's the drink devil.”
passages.vernacular: 如果有一個魔鬼我比別嘅更想睇佢進無底坑,嗰個就係酒魔。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有一個魔鬼我比別的更想看他進無底坑,那就是酒魔。」

passages.original: “I say, Jerry,” said the governor, “you are treading pretty hard on my toes, you know; I'm not so good as you are, more shame to me; I wish I was.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,傑瑞,」老大講,「你相當重地踩住我嘅腳趾,你知道;我不像你咁好,我更該羞愧;我真希望我係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,傑瑞,」老大說,「你相當重地踩著我的腳趾,你知道;我不像你那麼好,我更該羞愧;我真希望我是。」

passages.original: “Well,” said Jerry, “why don't you cut with it, governor?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」傑瑞講,「你點解不戒掉佢,老大?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」傑瑞說,「你為什麼不戒掉它,老大?

passages.original: You are too good a man to be the slave of such a thing.”
passages.vernacular: 你係個太好嘅人,不該做呢種嘢嘅奴隸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個太好的人,不該做這種東西的奴隸。」

passages.original: “I'm a great fool, Jerry, but I tried once for two days, and I thought I should have died; how did you do?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係個大傻瓜,傑瑞,但我試過一次兩天,我以為我會死;你係點做嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是個大傻瓜,傑瑞,但我試過一次兩天,我以為我會死;你是怎麼做的?」

passages.original: “I had hard work at it for several weeks; you see I never did get drunk, but I found that I was not my own master, and that when the craving came on it was hard work to say 'no'.
passages.vernacular: 「我努力咗好幾個星期;你睇我從冇飲醉過,但我發現我唔係自己嘅主人,當渴望襲嚟時,講『不』好難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我努力了好幾個星期;你看我從沒喝醉過,但我發現我不是自己的主人,當渴望襲來時,說『不』很難。

passages.original: I saw that one of us must knock under, the drink devil or Jerry Barker, and I said that it should not be Jerry Barker, God helping me; but it was a struggle, and I wanted all the help I could get, for till I tried to break the habit I did not know how strong it was; but then Polly took such pains that I should have good food, and when the craving came on I used to get a cup of coffee, or some peppermint, or read a bit in my book, and that was a help to me; sometimes I had to say over and over to myself, 'Give up the drink or lose your soul!
passages.vernacular: 我睇出我哋中嘅一個必須屈服,酒魔或傑瑞·巴克,我講絕不該係傑瑞·巴克,願上帝幫助我;但嗰個係一場掙扎,我需要我能得到嘅所有幫助,因為直到我試住戒掉呢個習慣,我才知道佢有多強;但波麗咁費心讓我有好嘅食物,渴望襲嚟時我就飲一杯咖啡,或食點薄荷,或喺我嘅書裡讀啲,嗰對我係幫助;有時我必須一遍又一遍地對自己講:『戒酒,否則失去你嘅靈魂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看出我們中的一個必須屈服,酒魔或傑瑞·巴克,我說絕不該是傑瑞·巴克,願上帝幫助我;但那是一場掙扎,我需要我能得到的所有幫助,因為直到我試著戒掉這個習慣,我才知道它有多強;但波麗那麼費心讓我有好的食物,渴望襲來時我就喝一杯咖啡,或吃點薄荷,或在我的書裡讀一點,那對我是幫助;有時我必須一遍又一遍地對自己說:『戒酒,否則失去你的靈魂!

passages.original: Give up the drink or break Polly's heart!'
passages.vernacular: 戒酒,否則讓波麗心碎!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戒酒,否則讓波麗心碎!』

passages.original: But thanks be to God, and my dear wife, my chains were broken, and now for ten years I have not tasted a drop, and never wish for it.”
passages.vernacular: 但感謝上帝,同我親愛嘅妻子,我嘅鎖鏈斷喇,而家十年喇,我冇嘗過一滴,都從唔想佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但感謝上帝,和我親愛的妻子,我的鎖鏈斷了,現在十年了,我沒嘗過一滴,也從不想它。」

passages.original: “I've a great mind to try at it,” said Grant, “for 'tis a poor thing not to be one's own master.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好想試試,」格蘭特講,「因為唔係自己嘅主人係件可憐嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很想試試,」格蘭特說,「因為不是自己的主人是件可憐的事。」

passages.original: “Do, governor, do, you'll never repent it, and what a help it would be to some of the poor fellows in our rank if they saw you do without it.
passages.vernacular: 「試吧,老大,試吧,你永遠唔會後悔,而且如果我哋隊列裡嘅可憐夥計哋睇到你不飲酒,嗰會係多大嘅幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「試吧,老大,試吧,你永遠不會後悔,而且如果我們隊列裡的可憐夥計們看到你不喝酒,那會是多大的幫助。

passages.original: I know there's two or three would like to keep out of that tavern if they could.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道有兩三個人想,如果能嘅話,不進嗰間酒館。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道有兩三個人想,如果能的話,不進那間酒館。」

passages.original: At first Captain seemed to do well, but he was a very old horse, and it was only his wonderful constitution, and Jerry's care, that had kept him up at the cab work so long; now he broke down very much.
passages.vernacular: 起初船長似乎好好,但佢係匹好老嘅馬,只係佢奇妙嘅體質同傑瑞嘅照顧,才使佢能喺出租車工作中堅持咁久;而家佢垮得好厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初船長似乎很好,但他是匹非常老的馬,只是他奇妙的體質和傑瑞的照顧,才使他能在出租車工作中堅持這麼久;現在他垮得很厲害。

passages.original: The farrier said he might mend up enough to sell for a few pounds, but Jerry said, no! a few pounds got by selling a good old servant into hard work and misery would canker all the rest of his money, and he thought the kindest thing he could do for the fine old fellow would be to put a sure bullet through his head, and then he would never suffer more; for he did not know where to find a kind master for the rest of his days.
passages.vernacular: 蹄鐵匠講佢或者能好到足夠賣幾英鎊,但傑瑞講,不!靠把一個好老僕人賣去幹苦活受苦得嚟嘅幾英鎊,會腐蝕佢其餘嘅所有錢,佢認為佢能為呢位高貴嘅老夥計做嘅最仁慈嘅事,係用一顆穩妥嘅子彈打穿佢嘅頭,咁樣佢就再都唔會受苦;因為佢唔知道邊度能為佢嘅餘生找到一個好主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蹄鐵匠說他也許能好到足夠賣幾英鎊,但傑瑞說,不!靠把一個好老僕人賣去幹苦活受苦得來的幾英鎊,會腐蝕他其餘的所有錢,他認為他能為這位高貴的老夥計做的最仁慈的事,是用一顆穩妥的子彈打穿他的頭,這樣他就再也不會受苦;因為他不知道哪裡能為他的餘生找到一個好主人。

passages.original: The day after this was decided Harry took me to the forge for some new shoes; when I returned Captain was gone.
passages.vernacular: 決定呢件事嘅第二天,哈里帶我去鐵匠鋪釘新蹄鐵;我回嚟時船長已經走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 決定這件事的第二天,哈里帶我去鐵匠鋪釘新蹄鐵;我回來時船長已經走了。

passages.original: I and the family all felt it very much.
passages.vernacular: 我同一家人都好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和一家人都非常難過。

passages.original: Jerry had now to look out for another horse, and he soon heard of one through an acquaintance who was under-groom in a nobleman's stables.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞而家得另找一匹馬,佢好快通過一個熟人聽講咗一匹,嗰人係一位貴族馬廄嘅副馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞現在得另找一匹馬,他很快通過一個熟人聽說了一匹,那人是一位貴族馬廄的副馬夫。

passages.original: He was a valuable young horse, but he had run away, smashed into another carriage, flung his lordship out, and so cut and blemished himself that he was no longer fit for a gentleman's stables, and the coachman had orders to look round, and sell him as well as he could.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係匹寶貴嘅年輕馬,但佢跑掉喇,撞上咗另一輛馬車,把勳爵甩咗出去,自己被割傷、留下瑕疵,唔再適合紳士嘅馬廄,車夫奉命四處找人,盡可能賣掉佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是匹寶貴的年輕馬,但他跑掉了,撞上了另一輛馬車,把勳爵甩了出去,自己被割傷、留下瑕疵,不再適合紳士的馬廄,車夫奉命四處找人,盡可能賣掉他。

passages.original: “I can do with high spirits,” said Jerry, “if a horse is not vicious or hard-mouthed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我能對付精神旺盛嘅馬,」傑瑞講,「只要馬不凶狠或嘴硬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能對付精神旺盛的馬,」傑瑞說,「只要馬不凶狠或嘴硬。」

passages.original: “There is not a bit of vice in him,” said the man; “his mouth is very tender, and I think myself that was the cause of the accident; you see he had just been clipped, and the weather was bad, and he had not had exercise enough, and when he did go out he was as full of spring as a balloon.
passages.vernacular: 「佢啲惡習都冇,」嗰人講;「佢嘅嘴好嬌嫩,我自己認為嗰個係事故嘅原因;你睇佢剛被剪過毛,天氣不好,佢運動唔夠,出去時佢像氣球一樣充滿彈跳力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他一點惡習也沒有,」那人說;「他的嘴很嬌嫩,我自己認為那是事故的原因;你看他剛被剪過毛,天氣不好,他運動不夠,出去時他像氣球一樣充滿彈跳力。

passages.original: Our governor (the coachman, I mean) had him harnessed in as tight and strong as he could, with the martingale, and the check-rein, a very sharp curb, and the reins put in at the bottom bar.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅老大(我係講車夫)把佢套得盡可能緊、盡可能結實,用咗胸帶、止韁繩,一個好銳利嘅鏈嚼子,韁繩穿喺底下嘅橫槓上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的老大(我是說車夫)把他套得盡可能緊、盡可能結實,用了胸帶、止韁繩,一個非常銳利的鏈嚼子,韁繩穿在底下的橫槓上。

passages.original: It is my belief that it made the horse mad, being tender in the mouth and so full of spirit.”
passages.vernacular: 我相信嗰使馬發瘋喇,嘴嬌嫩又精神咁足。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信那使馬發瘋了,嘴嬌嫩又精神那麼足。」

passages.original: “Likely enough; I'll come and see him,” said Jerry.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能;我嚟睇睇佢,」傑瑞講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能;我來看看他,」傑瑞說。

passages.original: The next day Hotspur, that was his name, came home; he was a fine brown horse, without a white hair in him, as tall as Captain, with a very handsome head, and only five years old.
passages.vernacular: 第二天,霍特斯珀,嗰個係佢嘅名字,嚟喇;佢係匹漂亮嘅棕色馬,冇一根白毛,同船長一樣高,頭好漂亮,才五歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,霍特斯珀,那是他的名字,來了;他是匹漂亮的棕色馬,沒有一根白毛,和船長一樣高,頭很漂亮,才五歲。

passages.original: I gave him a friendly greeting by way of good fellowship, but did not ask him any questions.
passages.vernacular: 我友好地問候佢,作為同伴嘅禮貌,但冇問佢任何問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我友好地問候他,作為同伴的禮貌,但沒有問他任何問題。

passages.original: The first night he was very restless.
passages.vernacular: 第一晚佢好不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一晚他非常不安。

passages.original: Instead of lying down, he kept jerking his halter rope up and down through the ring, and knocking the block about against the manger till I could not sleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢不躺下,而係不停地把籠頭繩上下拽過環,把木塊喺槽邊敲嚟敲去,吵得我瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不躺下,而是不停地把籠頭繩上下拽過環,把木塊在槽邊敲來敲去,吵得我睡不著。

passages.original: However, the next day, after five or six hours in the cab, he came in quiet and sensible.
passages.vernacular: 不過,第二天,喺出租車裡五六個小時後,佢回嚟時安靜而懂事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,第二天,在出租車裡五六個小時後,他回來時安靜而懂事。

passages.original: Jerry patted and talked to him a good deal, and very soon they understood each other, and Jerry said that with an easy bit and plenty of work he would be as gentle as a lamb; and that it was an ill wind that blew nobody good, for if his lordship had lost a hundred-guinea favorite, the cabman had gained a good horse with all his strength in him.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞拍佢、同佢講咗好多話,好快佢哋就彼此了解,傑瑞講用一個輕柔嘅嚼子同大量嘅活,佢會像羔羊一樣溫和;講壞風唔會對邊個都冇好處,因為如果勳爵失去咗一匹值一百畿尼嘅寵物,車夫卻得到咗一匹力氣十足嘅好馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞拍他、同他說了很多話,很快他們就彼此了解,傑瑞說用一個輕柔的嚼子和大量的活,他會像羔羊一樣溫和;說壞風不會對誰都沒好處,因為如果勳爵失去了一匹值一百畿尼的寵物,車夫卻得到了一匹力氣十足的好馬。

passages.original: Hotspur thought it a great come-down to be a cab-horse, and was disgusted at standing in the rank, but he confessed to me at the end of the week that an easy mouth and a free head made up for a great deal, and after all, the work was not so degrading as having one's head and tail fastened to each other at the saddle.
passages.vernacular: 霍特斯珀認為當出租車馬係個大跌落,對站喺隊列裡好反感,但一個星期結束時,佢向我承認,輕柔嘅嘴同自由嘅頭彌補咗好多,而且畢竟呢活冇把頭同尾巴喺鞍子處綁喺一起咁羞辱人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 霍特斯珀認為當出租車馬是個大跌落,對站在隊列裡很反感,但一個星期結束時,他向我承認,輕柔的嘴和自由的頭彌補了很多,而且畢竟這活沒有把頭和尾巴在鞍子處綁在一起那麼羞辱人。

passages.original: In fact, he settled in well, and Jerry liked him very much.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,佢安頓得好好,傑瑞好鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,他安頓得很好,傑瑞非常喜歡他。

chapters.title: Part III · 45 Jerry's New Year 第三部·45 傑瑞的新年

passages.original: CH For some people Christmas and the New Year are very merry times; but for cabmen and cabmen's horses it is no holiday, though it may be a harvest.
passages.vernacular: 對有些人來講,聖誕節同新年係好快樂嘅時候;但對出租車夫同出租車馬來講,唔係假日,雖然可能係收穫期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對有些人來說,聖誕節和新年是非常快樂的時候;但對出租車夫和出租車馬來說,不是假日,雖然可能是收穫期。

passages.original: There are so many parties, balls, and places of amusement open that the work is hard and often late.
passages.vernacular: 有咁多聚會、舞會同開放嘅娛樂場所,活好辛苦,常常好晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼多聚會、舞會和開放的娛樂場所,活很辛苦,常常很晚。

passages.original: Sometimes driver and horse have to wait for hours in the rain or frost, shivering with the cold, while the merry people within are dancing away to the music.
passages.vernacular: 有時車夫同馬必須喺雨中或霜凍中等好幾個小時,冷得發抖,而裡面快樂嘅人哋隨住音樂跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時車夫和馬必須在雨中或霜凍中等好幾個小時,冷得發抖,而裡面快樂的人們隨著音樂跳舞。

passages.original: I wonder if the beautiful ladies ever think of the weary cabman waiting on his box, and his patient beast standing, till his legs get stiff with cold.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道嗰啲美麗嘅女士係咪曾想過疲憊嘅車夫等喺佢嘅車座上,同佢耐心嘅牲口站住,直到腿被凍僵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道那些美麗的女士是否曾想過疲憊的車夫等在他的車座上,和他耐心的牲口站著,直到腿被凍僵。

passages.original: I had now most of the evening work, as I was well accustomed to standing, and Jerry was also more afraid of Hotspur taking cold.
passages.vernacular: 我而家做大部分晚間嘅活,因為我好習慣站住,傑瑞都更怕霍特斯珀住涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在做大部分晚間的活,因為我很習慣站著,傑瑞也更怕霍特斯珀著涼。

passages.original: We had a great deal of late work in the Christmas week, and Jerry's cough was bad; but however late we were, Polly sat up for him, and came out with a lantern to meet him, looking anxious and troubled.
passages.vernacular: 聖誕週我哋有好多晚間嘅活,傑瑞咳嗽得好厲害;但不管我哋多晚,波麗都為佢熬夜,提住燈籠出嚟迎佢,神情焦慮不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖誕週我們有很多晚間的活,傑瑞咳嗽得很厲害;但不管我們多晚,波麗都為他熬夜,提著燈籠出來迎他,神情焦慮不安。

passages.original: On the evening of the New Year we had to take two gentlemen to a house in one of the West End Squares.
passages.vernacular: 新年嗰天晚上,我哋得載兩位紳士去西區一個廣場嘅一座房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新年那天晚上,我們得載兩位紳士去西區一個廣場的一座房子。

passages.original: We set them down at nine o'clock, and were told to come again at eleven, “but,” said one, “as it is a card party, you may have to wait a few minutes, but don't be late.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋九點鐘放下佢哋,被告知十啲再嚟,「不過,」一個講,「呢個係個牌局,你可能要等幾分鐘,但別遲到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們九點鐘放下他們,被告知十一點再來,「不過,」一個說,「這是個牌局,你可能要等幾分鐘,但別遲到。」

passages.original: As the clock struck eleven we were at the door, for Jerry was always punctual.
passages.vernacular: 鐘敲十啲時我哋已喺門口,因為傑瑞總是準時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐘敲十一點時我們已在門口,因為傑瑞總是準時。

passages.original: The clock chimed the quarters, one, two, three, and then struck twelve, but the door did not open.
passages.vernacular: 鐘報咗一刻、兩刻、三刻,然後敲十二點,門仲冇開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐘報了一刻、兩刻、三刻,然後敲十二點,門還沒有開。

passages.original: The wind had been very changeable, with squalls of rain during the day, but now it came on sharp, driving sleet, which seemed to come all the way round; it was very cold, and there was no shelter.
passages.vernacular: 風一直好多變,白天有陣陣雨,但而家颳起咗尖利嘅、猛烈嘅雨夾雪,好像從四面八方嚟;好冷,冇遮蔽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風一直很多變,白天有陣陣雨,但現在颳起了尖利的、猛烈的雨夾雪,好像從四面八方來;很冷,沒有遮蔽。

passages.original: Jerry got off his box and came and pulled one of my cloths a little more over my neck; then he took a turn or two up and down, stamping his feet; then he began to beat his arms, but that set him off coughing; so he opened the cab door and sat at the bottom with his feet on the pavement, and was a little sheltered.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞下咗車座,過嚟把我嘅一塊毯子往我脖子上拉咗拉;然後佢嚟回走咗一兩圈,跺住腳;然後佢開始拍打手臂,但呢使佢咳嗽起嚟;所以佢打開車門,坐喺底部,腳踩喺人行道上,稍有遮蔽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞下了車座,過來把我的一塊毯子往我脖子上拉了拉;然後他來回走了一兩圈,跺著腳;然後他開始拍打手臂,但這使他咳嗽起來;所以他打開車門,坐在底部,腳踩在人行道上,稍有遮蔽。

passages.original: Still the clock chimed the quarters, and no one came.
passages.vernacular: 鐘仍報住刻,冇人嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐘仍報著刻,沒有人來。

passages.original: At half-past twelve he rang the bell and asked the servant if he would be wanted that night.
passages.vernacular: 十二點半佢按鈴,問僕人今晚係咪仲需要佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二點半他按鈴,問僕人今晚是否還需要他。

passages.original: “Oh, yes, you'll be wanted safe enough,” said the man; “you must not go, it will soon be over,” and again Jerry sat down, but his voice was so hoarse I could hardly hear him.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,肯定需要你,」嗰人講;「你唔能夠走,好快就結束喇,」傑瑞又坐下,但佢嘅聲音咁嘶啞,我幾乎聽唔見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,肯定需要你,」那人說;「你不能走,很快就結束了,」傑瑞又坐下,但他的聲音那麼嘶啞,我幾乎聽不見。

passages.original: At a quarter past one the door opened, and the two gentlemen came out; they got into the cab without a word, and told Jerry where to drive, that was nearly two miles.
passages.vernacular: 啲一刻,門開喇,兩位紳士走出嚟;佢哋一言不發地上咗車,告訴傑瑞駕往邊度,嗰將近兩英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一點一刻,門開了,兩位紳士走出來;他們一言不發地上了車,告訴傑瑞駕往哪裡,那將近兩英里。

passages.original: My legs were numb with cold, and I thought I should have stumbled.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅腿冷得發麻,我想我會絆倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的腿冷得發麻,我想我會絆倒。

passages.original: When the men got out they never said they were sorry to have kept us waiting so long, but were angry at the charge; however, as Jerry never charged more than was his due, so he never took less, and they had to pay for the two hours and a quarter waiting; but it was hard-earned money to Jerry.
passages.vernacular: 兩人下車時從冇講過抱歉讓我哋等咗咁久,而係對車費生氣;不過,因為傑瑞從不多收超過應得嘅,所以都從不少收,佢哋唔得不付兩小時一刻鐘嘅等候費;但嗰對傑瑞係辛苦錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人下車時從沒說過抱歉讓我們等了這麼久,而是對車費生氣;不過,因為傑瑞從不多收超過應得的,所以也從不少收,他們不得不付兩小時一刻鐘的等候費;但那對傑瑞是辛苦錢。

passages.original: At last we got home; he could hardly speak, and his cough was dreadful.
passages.vernacular: 終於我哋回家喇;佢幾乎講不出話,咳嗽得可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於我們回家了;他幾乎說不出話,咳嗽得可怕。

passages.original: Polly asked no questions, but opened the door and held the lantern for him.
passages.vernacular: 波麗乜嘢都冇問,開咗門,為佢舉住燈籠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗什麼也沒問,開了門,為他舉著燈籠。

passages.original: “Can't I do something?” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「我能做點乜嘢嗎?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能做點什麼嗎?」她說。

passages.original: “Yes; get Jack something warm, and then boil me some gruel.”
passages.vernacular: 「能;畀傑克弄點熱嘅,然後畀我煮點麥片粥。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「能;給傑克弄點熱的,然後給我煮點麥片粥。」

passages.original: This was said in a hoarse whisper; he could hardly get his breath, but he gave me a rub-down as usual, and even went up into the hayloft for an extra bundle of straw for my bed.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係嘶啞地低聲講嘅;佢幾乎喘不過氣,但佢像往常一樣畀我擦洗,甚至上乾草棚去畀我嘅床多攞咗一捆稻草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是嘶啞地低聲說的;他幾乎喘不過氣,但他像往常一樣給我擦洗,甚至上乾草棚去給我的床多拿了一捆稻草。

passages.original: Polly brought me a warm mash that made me comfortable, and then they locked the door.
passages.vernacular: 波麗畀我端嚟一份熱糊,讓我舒服,然後佢哋鎖上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗給我端來一份熱糊,讓我舒服,然後他們鎖上了門。

passages.original: It was late the next morning before any one came, and then it was only Harry.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨好晚才有人嚟,而且只係哈里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨很晚才有人來,而且只是哈里。

passages.original: He cleaned us and fed us, and swept out the stalls, then he put the straw back again as if it was Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀我哋刷洗、餵食,打掃馬棚,然後佢把稻草放回去,好像係星期日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給我們刷洗、餵食,打掃馬棚,然後他把稻草放回去,好像是星期日。

passages.original: He was very still, and neither whistled nor sang.
passages.vernacular: 佢好安靜,既不吹口哨都不唱歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很安靜,既不吹口哨也不唱歌。

passages.original: At noon he came again and gave us our food and water; this time Dolly came with him; she was crying, and I could gather from what they said that Jerry was dangerously ill, and the doctor said it was a bad case.
passages.vernacular: 中午佢又嚟畀我哋送食物同水;呢次多麗同佢一起嚟;佢喺哭,我從佢哋講嘅話中能知道,傑瑞病得好危險,醫生講情況好糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午他又來給我們送食物和水;這次多麗同他一起來;她在哭,我從他們說的話中能知道,傑瑞病得很危險,醫生說情況很糟。

passages.original: So two days passed, and there was great trouble indoors.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣過咗兩天,屋裡有好大嘅煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣過了兩天,屋裡有很大的煩惱。

passages.original: We only saw Harry, and sometimes Dolly.
passages.vernacular: 我哋只睇見哈里,有時睇見多麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們只看見哈里,有時看見多麗。

passages.original: I think she came for company, for Polly was always with Jerry, and he had to be kept very quiet.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢嚟係為了作伴,因為波麗一直同傑瑞喺一起,佢必須保持好安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她來是為了作伴,因為波麗一直同傑瑞在一起,他必須保持非常安靜。

passages.original: On the third day, while Harry was in the stable, a tap came at the door, and Governor Grant came in.
passages.vernacular: 第三天,哈里喺馬廄裡時,有人敲門,老大格蘭特走咗進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第三天,哈里在馬廄裡時,有人敲門,老大格蘭特走了進來。

passages.original: “I wouldn't go to the house, my boy,” he said, “but I want to know how your father is.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想去房子嗰邊,細路,」佢講,「但我想知道你父親點樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想去房子那邊,孩子,」他說,「但我想知道你父親怎麼樣。」

passages.original: “He is very bad,” said Harry, “he can't be much worse; they call it 'bronchitis'; the doctor thinks it will turn one way or another to-night.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢好糟,」哈里講,「唔能夠再糟喇;佢哋叫佢『支氣管炎』;醫生認為今晚會有轉折。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他很糟,」哈里說,「不能再糟了;他們叫它『支氣管炎』;醫生認為今晚會有轉折。」

passages.original: “That's bad, very bad,” said Grant, shaking his head; “I know two men who died of that last week; it takes 'em off in no time; but while there's life there's hope, so you must keep up your spirits.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好糟,好糟,」格蘭特搖住頭講;「我知道上星期有兩個人死於嗰個;佢好快就把人帶走;但有生命就有希望,所以你必須保持精神。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很糟,很糟,」格蘭特搖著頭說;「我知道上星期有兩個人死於那個;它很快就把人帶走;但有生命就有希望,所以你必須保持精神。」

passages.original: “Yes,” said Harry quickly, “and the doctor said that father had a better chance than most men, because he didn't drink.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」哈里好快地講,「醫生講我父親比大多數人機會更好,因為佢不飲酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」哈里很快地說,「醫生說我父親比大多數人機會更好,因為他不喝酒。

passages.original: He said yesterday the fever was so high that if father had been a drinking man it would have burned him up like a piece of paper; but I believe he thinks he will get over it; don't you think he will, Mr. Grant?”
passages.vernacular: 佢尋日講熱度咁高,如果我父親係個飲酒嘅人,會把佢像一張紙一樣燒掉;但我相信佢認為佢會好起嚟;你不認為佢會嗎,格蘭特先生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他昨天說熱度那麼高,如果我父親是個喝酒的人,會把他像一張紙一樣燒掉;但我相信他認為他會好起來;你不認為他會嗎,格蘭特先生?」

passages.original: The governor looked puzzled.
passages.vernacular: 老大顯得困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老大顯得困惑。

passages.original: “If there's any rule that good men should get over these things, I'm sure he will, my boy; he's the best man I know.
passages.vernacular: 「如果有乜嘢規律講好人應該度過呢啲事,我確信佢會,細路;佢係我所知最好嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果有什麼規律說好人應該度過這些事,我確信他會,孩子;他是我所知最好的人。

passages.original: I'll look in early to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽日一早嚟睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明天一早來看看。」

passages.original: Early next morning he was there.
passages.vernacular: 第二天一早佢就嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天一早他就來了。

passages.original: “Well?” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「點樣?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣?」他說。

passages.original: “Father is better,” said Harry.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸好些喇,」哈里講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸好些了,」哈里說。

passages.original: “Mother hopes he will get over it.”
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽希望佢能好起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽希望他能好起來。」

passages.original: “Thank God!” said the governor, “and now you must keep him warm, and keep his mind easy, and that brings me to the horses; you see Jack will be all the better for the rest of a week or two in a warm stable, and you can easily take him a turn up and down the street to stretch his legs; but this young one, if he does not get work, he will soon be all up on end, as you may say, and will be rather too much for you; and when he does go out there'll be an accident.”
passages.vernacular: 「感謝上帝!」老大講,「而家你必須讓佢保暖,讓佢心裡輕鬆,呢就講到馬喇;你睇傑克休息一兩個星期,待喺暖同嘅馬廄裡,會好得多,你可以輕易地牽佢喺街上嚟回走走伸展腿;但呢匹年輕嘅,如果佢冇活幹,佢好快就會暴躁起嚟,像人哋講嘅,對你太難應付;佢出去時會出事故。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「感謝上帝!」老大說,「現在你必須讓他保暖,讓他心裡輕鬆,這就說到馬了;你看傑克休息一兩個星期,待在暖和的馬廄裡,會好得多,你可以輕易地牽他在街上來回走走伸展腿;但這匹年輕的,如果他沒有活幹,他很快就會暴躁起來,像人們說的,對你太難應付;他出去時會出事故。」

passages.original: “It is like that now,” said Harry.
passages.vernacular: 「而家就係咁樣,」哈里講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在就是這樣,」哈里說。

passages.original: “I have kept him short of corn, but he's so full of spirit I don't know what to do with him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我讓佢少食穀物,但佢精神咁足,我唔知道該攞佢點算。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我讓他少吃穀物,但他精神那麼足,我不知道該拿他怎麼辦。」

passages.original: “Just so,” said Grant.
passages.vernacular: 「正是,」格蘭特講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正是,」格蘭特說。

passages.original: “Now look here, will you tell your mother that if she is agreeable I will come for him every day till something is arranged, and take him for a good spell of work, and whatever he earns, I'll bring your mother half of it, and that will help with the horses' feed.
passages.vernacular: 「而家聽住,你能告訴你母親,如果佢同意,我每天嚟牽佢,直到事情安排好,帶佢好好幹一陣活,佢賺多少,我就帶畀你母親一半,呢會有助於馬嘅飼料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在聽著,你能告訴你母親,如果她同意,我每天來牽他,直到事情安排好,帶他好好幹一陣活,他賺多少,我就帶給你母親一半,這會有助於馬的飼料。

passages.original: Your father is in a good club, I know, but that won't keep the horses, and they'll be eating their heads off all this time; I'll come at noon and hear what she says,” and without waiting for Harry's thanks he was gone.
passages.vernacular: 你父親喺一個好嘅互助會,我知道,但嗰養不咗馬,佢哋呢段時間會食垮;我中午嚟聽佢點講,」不等哈里道謝佢就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你父親在一個好的互助會,我知道,但那養不了馬,它們這段時間會吃垮;我中午來聽她怎麼說,」不等哈里道謝他就走了。

passages.original: At noon I think he went and saw Polly, for he and Harry came to the stable together, harnessed Hotspur, and took him out.
passages.vernacular: 中午我想佢去睇咗波麗,因為佢同哈里一起嚟到馬廄,畀霍特斯珀套上挽具,牽佢出去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午我想他去看了波麗,因為他和哈里一起來到馬廄,給霍特斯珀套上挽具,牽他出去了。

passages.original: For a week or more he came for Hotspur, and when Harry thanked him or said anything about his kindness, he laughed it off, saying it was all good luck for him, for his horses were wanting a little rest which they would not otherwise have had.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟牽咗霍特斯珀一個星期多,哈里謝佢或講乜嘢關於佢善意嘅話時,佢一笑置之,講呢對佢係好運,因為佢嘅馬需要啲休息,不然佢哋得唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來牽了霍特斯珀一個星期多,哈里謝他或說什麼關於他善意的話時,他一笑置之,說這對他是好運,因為他的馬需要一點休息,不然它們得不到。

passages.original: Jerry grew better steadily, but the doctor said that he must never go back to the cab work again if he wished to be an old man.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞穩步好轉,但醫生講,如果佢想活到老,就絕唔能夠再回去幹出租車嘅活喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞穩步好轉,但醫生說,如果他想活到老,就絕不能再回去幹出租車的活了。

passages.original: The children had many consultations together about what father and mother would do, and how they could help to earn money.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋一起商量咗許多次,爸爸媽媽會做乜嘢,佢哋點樣能幫忙賺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們一起商量了許多次,爸爸媽媽會做什麼,他們怎樣能幫忙賺錢。

passages.original: One afternoon Hotspur was brought in very wet and dirty.
passages.vernacular: 一天下午,霍特斯珀被牽進嚟時又濕又髒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天下午,霍特斯珀被牽進來時又濕又髒。

passages.original: “The streets are nothing but slush,” said the governor; “it will give you a good warming, my boy, to get him clean and dry.”
passages.vernacular: 「街上全係爛泥,」老大講;「畀佢刷乾淨弄乾,會讓你好好暖同一下,細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「街上全是爛泥,」老大說;「給他刷乾淨弄乾,會讓你好好暖和一下,孩子。」

passages.original: “All right, governor,” said Harry, “I shall not leave him till he is; you know I have been trained by my father.”
passages.vernacular: 「好嘅,老大,」哈里講,「佢冇弄好我唔會離開佢;你知道我係被我父親訓練過嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好的,老大,」哈里說,「他沒弄好我不會離開他;你知道我是被我父親訓練過的。」

passages.original: “I wish all the boys had been trained like you,” said the governor.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望所有男孩都像你咁樣被訓練,」老大講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望所有男孩都像你這樣被訓練,」老大說。

passages.original: While Harry was sponging off the mud from Hotspur's body and legs Dolly came in, looking very full of something.
passages.vernacular: 哈里正在用海綿擦霍特斯珀身上同腿上嘅泥時,多麗進嚟,睇起嚟滿懷心事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里正在用海綿擦霍特斯珀身上和腿上的泥時,多麗進來,看起來滿懷心事。

passages.original: “Who lives at Fairstowe, Harry?
passages.vernacular: 「邊個住喺費爾斯托,哈里?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰住在費爾斯托,哈里?

passages.original: Mother has got a letter from Fairstowe; she seemed so glad, and ran upstairs to father with it.”
passages.vernacular: 媽媽收到一封費爾斯托嚟嘅信;佢好像好高興,攞住跑上樓去畀爸爸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 媽媽收到一封費爾斯托來的信;她好像很高興,拿著跑上樓去給爸爸。」

passages.original: “Don't you know?
passages.vernacular: 「你唔知道嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不知道嗎?

passages.original: Why, it is the name of Mrs. Fowler's place--mother's old mistress, you know--the lady that father met last summer, who sent you and me five shillings each.”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,嗰個係福勒太太嘅地方——媽媽嘅老女主人,你知道——去年夏天爸爸遇到嘅嗰位女士,畀你同我每人五先令。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,那是福勒太太的地方——媽媽的老女主人,你知道——去年夏天爸爸遇到的那位女士,給你和我每人五先令。」

passages.original: “Oh!
Mrs. Fowler.
passages.vernacular: 福勒太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福勒太太。

passages.original: Of course, I know all about her.
passages.vernacular: 當然,我全知道佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,我全知道她。

passages.original: I wonder what she is writing to mother about.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢畀媽媽寫乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道她給媽媽寫什麼。」

passages.original: “Mother wrote to her last week,” said Harry; “you know she told father if ever he gave up the cab work she would like to know.
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽上星期畀佢寫咗信,」哈里講;「你知道佢告訴爸爸,如果佢放棄咗出租車嘅活,佢想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽上星期給她寫了信,」哈里說;「你知道她告訴爸爸,如果他放棄了出租車的活,她想知道。

passages.original: I wonder what she says; run in and see, Dolly.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢講乜嘢;跑進去睇睇,多麗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道她說什麼;跑進去看看,多麗。」

passages.original: Harry scrubbed away at Hotspur with a huish! huish! like any old hostler.
passages.vernacular: 哈里像個老馬夫嗰樣,噓、噓地用力刷霍特斯珀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里像個老馬夫那樣,噓、噓地用力刷霍特斯珀。

passages.original: In a few minutes Dolly came dancing into the stable.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,多麗蹦蹦跳跳地進咗馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,多麗蹦蹦跳跳地進了馬廄。

passages.original: “Oh!
Harry, there never was anything so beautiful; Mrs. Fowler says we are all to go and live near her.
passages.vernacular: 哈里,從冇咁美好嘅事;福勒太太講我哋都去住喺佢附近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里,從沒有這麼美好的事;福勒太太說我們都去住在她附近。

passages.original: There is a cottage now empty that will just suit us, with a garden and a henhouse, and apple-trees, and everything! and her coachman is going away in the spring, and then she will want father in his place; and there are good families round, where you can get a place in the garden or the stable, or as a page-boy; and there's a good school for me; and mother is laughing and crying by turns, and father does look so happy!”
passages.vernacular: 而家有一間空住嘅小屋正適合我哋,有花園、雞舍同蘋果樹,一切都有!佢嘅車夫春天要走,嗰時佢要爸爸去接替佢嘅位置;周圍有好人家,你可以喺花園或馬廄找到工作,或當侍童;仲有一所好學校畀我;媽媽又笑又哭,爸爸睇起嚟咁高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在有一間空著的小屋正適合我們,有花園、雞舍和蘋果樹,一切都有!她的車夫春天要走,那時她要爸爸去接替他的位置;周圍有好人家,你可以在花園或馬廄找到工作,或當侍童;還有一所好學校給我;媽媽又笑又哭,爸爸看起來那麼高興!」

passages.original: “That's uncommon jolly,” said Harry, “and just the right thing, I should say; it will suit father and mother both; but I don't intend to be a page-boy with tight clothes and rows of buttons.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太好喇,」哈里講,「正是合適嘅事,我該講;佢對爸爸媽媽都合適;但我不打算當穿緊身衣服、一排排鈕扣嘅侍童。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太好了,」哈里說,「正是合適的事,我該說;它對爸爸媽媽都合適;但我不打算當穿緊身衣服、一排排鈕扣的侍童。

passages.original: I'll be a groom or a gardener.”
passages.vernacular: 我要當馬夫或園丁。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要當馬夫或園丁。」

passages.original: It was quickly settled that as soon as Jerry was well enough they should remove to the country, and that the cab and horses should be sold as soon as possible.
passages.vernacular: 好快決定,等傑瑞好得足夠,佢哋就搬到鄉下去,出租車同馬要盡快賣掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快決定,等傑瑞好得足夠,他們就搬到鄉下去,出租車和馬要盡快賣掉。

passages.original: This was heavy news for me, for I was not young now, and could not look for any improvement in my condition.
passages.vernacular: 呢對我係沉重嘅消息,因為我而家不年輕喇,唔能夠指望我嘅處境改善。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對我是沉重的消息,因為我現在不年輕了,不能指望我的處境改善。

passages.original: Since I left Birtwick I had never been so happy as with my dear master Jerry; but three years of cab work, even under the best conditions, will tell on one's strength, and I felt that I was not the horse that I had been.
passages.vernacular: 自從離開伯特威克,我從冇像同親愛嘅主人傑瑞喺一起嗰樣快樂;但三年嘅出租車工作,即使喺最好嘅條件下,都會損害人嘅力量,我覺得我唔再係以前嘅馬喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從離開伯特威克,我從沒像同親愛的主人傑瑞在一起那樣快樂;但三年的出租車工作,即使在最好的條件下,也會損害人的力量,我覺得我不再是以前的馬了。

passages.original: Grant said at once that he would take Hotspur, and there were men on the stand who would have bought me; but Jerry said I should not go to cab work again with just anybody, and the governor promised to find a place for me where I should be comfortable.
passages.vernacular: 格蘭特即刻講佢要霍特斯珀,停靠站上都有人願意買我;但傑瑞講我不該再隨便跟邊個去拉出租車,老大答應為我找一個我會舒適嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格蘭特馬上說他要霍特斯珀,停靠站上也有人願意買我;但傑瑞說我不該再隨便跟誰去拉出租車,老大答應為我找一個我會舒適的地方。

passages.original: The day came for going away.
passages.vernacular: 離開嘅日子到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離開的日子到了。

passages.original: Jerry had not been allowed to go out yet, and I never saw him after that New Year's eve.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑞仲不被允許出門,從嗰個除夕夜後我再都冇見過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑞還不被允許出門,從那個除夕夜後我再也沒見過他。

passages.original: Polly and the children came to bid me good-by.
passages.vernacular: 波麗同細路哋嚟同我告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗和孩子們來同我告別。

passages.original: “Poor old Jack! dear old Jack!
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅老傑克!親愛嘅老傑克!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的老傑克!親愛的老傑克!

passages.original: I wish we could take you with us,” she said, and then laying her hand on my mane she put her face close to my neck and kissed me.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我哋能帶你一起走,」佢講,然後把手放喺我嘅鬃毛上,把臉貼近我嘅脖子吻咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我們能帶你一起走,」她說,然後把手放在我的鬃毛上,把臉貼近我的脖子吻了我。

passages.original: Dolly was crying and kissed me too.
passages.vernacular: 多麗喺哭,都吻咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多麗在哭,也吻了我。

passages.original: Harry stroked me a great deal, but said nothing, only he seemed very sad, and so I was led away to my new place.
passages.vernacular: 哈里撫摸咗我好久,但乜嘢都冇講,只係顯得好悲傷,就咁樣我被牽走去我嘅新地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里撫摸了我很久,但什麼也沒說,只是顯得很悲傷,就這樣我被牽走去我的新地方。

chapters.title: Part IV · 46 Jakes and the Lady 第四部·46 傑克斯與女士

passages.original: CH I was sold to a corn dealer and baker, whom Jerry knew, and with him he thought I should have good food and fair work.
passages.vernacular: 我被賣畀咗一個穀物商同麵包師,傑瑞認識佢,佢認為喺佢嗰度我會有好食物同公平嘅活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被賣給了一個穀物商和麵包師,傑瑞認識他,他認為在他那裡我會有好食物和公平的活。

passages.original: In the first he was quite right, and if my master had always been on the premises I do not think I should have been overloaded, but there was a foreman who was always hurrying and driving every one, and frequently when I had quite a full load he would order something else to be taken on.
passages.vernacular: 第啲佢完全對,如果我嘅主人一直在場,我想我唔會被超載,但有一個領班總是催促同驅趕每個人,常常喺我已經裝咗滿滿一車時,佢仲命令再裝上別嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一點他完全對,如果我的主人一直在場,我想我不會被超載,但有一個領班總是催促和驅趕每個人,常常在我已經裝了滿滿一車時,他還命令再裝上別的東西。

passages.original: My carter, whose name was Jakes, often said it was more than I ought to take, but the other always overruled him.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅車夫名叫傑克斯,常講呢比我該拉嘅多,但領班總是推翻佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的車夫名叫傑克斯,常說這比我該拉的多,但領班總是推翻他。

passages.original: “'Twas no use going twice when once would do, and he chose to get business forward.”
passages.vernacular: 「一次能完成嘅事走兩次冇用,佢選擇把生意向前推進。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一次能完成的事走兩次沒用,他選擇把生意向前推進。」

passages.original: Jakes, like the other carters, always had the check-rein up, which prevented me from drawing easily, and by the time I had been there three or four months I found the work telling very much on my strength.
passages.vernacular: 傑克斯同其他車夫一樣,總把止韁繩勒得高高嘅,呢使我難以輕鬆拉車,我喺嗰度三四個月後,發現呢活對我嘅力氣影響好大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑克斯同其他車夫一樣,總把止韁繩勒得高高的,這使我難以輕鬆拉車,我在那裡三四個月後,發現這活對我的力氣影響很大。

passages.original: One day I was loaded more than usual, and part of the road was a steep uphill.
passages.vernacular: 有一天我裝得比平常多,路嘅一部分係陡峭嘅上坡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我裝得比平常多,路的一部分是陡峭的上坡。

passages.original: I used all my strength, but I could not get on, and was obliged continually to stop.
passages.vernacular: 我用盡全力,但走不上去,唔得不不斷停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用盡全力,但走不上去,不得不不斷停下。

passages.original: This did not please my driver, and he laid his whip on badly.
passages.vernacular: 呢不讓我嘅車夫高興,佢狠狠地用鞭子抽我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不讓我的車夫高興,他狠狠地用鞭子抽我。

passages.original: “Get on, you lazy fellow,” he said, “or I'll make you.”
passages.vernacular: 「走,你呢懶傢伙,」佢講,「否則我逼你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走,你這懶傢伙,」他說,「否則我逼你。」

passages.original: Again I started the heavy load, and struggled on a few yards; again the whip came down, and again I struggled forward.
passages.vernacular: 我又拉起嗰沉重嘅貨,掙扎住走咗幾碼;鞭子又落下嚟,我又掙扎住向前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我又拉起那沉重的貨,掙扎著走了幾碼;鞭子又落下來,我又掙扎著向前。

passages.original: The pain of that great cart whip was sharp, but my mind was hurt quite as much as my poor sides.
passages.vernacular: 嗰條大貨車鞭子嘅疼痛係尖銳嘅,但我嘅心受嘅傷同我可憐嘅兩肋一樣重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那條大貨車鞭子的疼痛是尖銳的,但我的心受的傷和我可憐的兩肋一樣重。

passages.original: To be punished and abused when I was doing my very best was so hard it took the heart out of me.
passages.vernacular: 我盡咗全力卻仲被懲罰同虐待,太難受喇,把我嘅精神都抽走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我盡了全力卻還被懲罰和虐待,太難受了,把我的精神都抽走了。

passages.original: A third time he was flogging me cruelly, when a lady stepped quickly up to him, and said in a sweet, earnest voice:
passages.vernacular: 佢第三次殘忍地抽打我時,一位女士快步走到佢面前,用甜美懇切嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他第三次殘忍地抽打我時,一位女士快步走到他面前,用甜美懇切的聲音說:

passages.original: “Oh! pray do not whip your good horse any more; I am sure he is doing all he can, and the road is very steep; I am sure he is doing his best.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦!請唔好再鞭打你嘅好馬喇;我確信佢喺盡其所能,而且路好陡;我確信佢喺盡力。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!請不要再鞭打你的好馬了;我確信他在盡其所能,而且路很陡;我確信他在盡力。」

passages.original: “If doing his best won't get this load up he must do something more than his best; that's all I know, ma'am,” said Jakes.
passages.vernacular: 「如果盡力都拉不上呢貨,佢就得做比盡力更多嘅事;我只知道呢個,夫人,」傑克斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果盡力也拉不上這貨,他就得做比盡力更多的事;我只知道這個,夫人,」傑克斯說。

passages.original: “But is it not a heavy load?” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「可嗰貨係唔係太重喇?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可那貨是不是太重了?」她說。

passages.original: “Yes, yes, too heavy,” he said; “but that's not my fault; the foreman came just as we were starting, and would have three hundredweight more put on to save him trouble, and I must get on with it as well as I can.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係嘅,太重喇,」佢講;「但嗰唔係我嘅錯;領班喺我哋剛要出發時嚟喇,為了省麻煩要再加三百磅,我只好盡我所能拉住走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是的,太重了,」他說;「但那不是我的錯;領班在我們剛要出發時來了,為了省麻煩要再加三百磅,我只好盡我所能拉著走。」

passages.original: He was raising the whip again, when the lady said:
passages.vernacular: 佢又舉起鞭子,女士講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又舉起鞭子,女士說:

passages.original: “Pray, stop; I think I can help you if you will let me.”
passages.vernacular: 「請停下;我想如果你讓我,我可以幫你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請停下;我想如果你讓我,我可以幫你。」

passages.original: The man laughed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人笑了。

passages.original: “You see,” she said, “you do not give him a fair chance; he cannot use all his power with his head held back as it is with that check-rein; if you would take it off I am sure he would do better--do try it,” she said persuasively, “I should be very glad if you would.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,」佢講,「你冇畀佢公平嘅機會;佢嘅頭被止韁繩咁樣向後勒住,唔能夠使出全部力量;如果你把佢取下嚟,我確信佢會做得更好——試試吧,」佢勸講道,「如果你肯,我會好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,」她說,「你沒有給他公平的機會;他的頭被止韁繩這樣向後勒著,不能使出全部力量;如果你把它取下來,我確信他會做得更好——試試吧,」她勸說道,「如果你肯,我會很高興。」

passages.original: “Well, well,” said Jakes, with a short laugh, “anything to please a lady, of course.
passages.vernacular: 「好,好,」傑克斯短促地笑咗一聲講,「當然要討女士歡心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,好,」傑克斯短促地笑了一聲說,「當然要討女士歡心。

passages.original: How far would you wish it down, ma'am?”
passages.vernacular: 您希望放低多少,夫人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您希望放低多少,夫人?」

passages.original: “Quite down, give him his head altogether.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全放下,把佢嘅頭完全放開。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全放下,把他的頭完全放開。」

passages.original: The rein was taken off, and in a moment I put my head down to my very knees.
passages.vernacular: 韁繩取下喇,一瞬間我把頭低到咗膝蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 韁繩取下了,一瞬間我把頭低到了膝蓋。

passages.original: What a comfort it was!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係多大嘅舒適啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是多大的舒適啊!

passages.original: Then I tossed it up and down several times to get the aching stiffness out of my neck.
passages.vernacular: 然後我把佢上下甩咗幾次,把脖子裡酸痛嘅僵硬甩掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我把它上下甩了幾次,把脖子裡酸痛的僵硬甩掉。

passages.original: “Poor fellow! that is what you wanted,” said she, patting and stroking me with her gentle hand; “and now if you will speak kindly to him and lead him on I believe he will be able to do better.”
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅傢伙!呢個就係你想要嘅,」佢講,用佢溫柔嘅手拍住、撫摸住我;「而家如果你對佢講句好話,領佢走,我相信佢能做得更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的傢伙!這就是你想要的,」她說,用她溫柔的手拍著、撫摸著我;「現在如果你對他說句好話,領他走,我相信他能做得更好。」

passages.original: Jakes took the rein.
passages.vernacular: 傑克斯攞起韁繩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑克斯拿起韁繩。

passages.original: “Come on, Blackie.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟吧,黑黑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來吧,黑黑。」

passages.original: I put down my head, and threw my whole weight against the collar; I spared no strength; the load moved on, and I pulled it steadily up the hill, and then stopped to take breath.
passages.vernacular: 我低下頭,把全部重量壓向頸圈;我毫不保留力氣;貨車動喇,我穩穩地把佢拉上坡,然後停下喘口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我低下頭,把全部重量壓向頸圈;我毫不保留力氣;貨車動了,我穩穩地把它拉上坡,然後停下喘口氣。

passages.original: The lady had walked along the footpath, and now came across into the road.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位女士一直沿住人行道走,而家穿過嚟到路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位女士一直沿著人行道走,現在穿過來到路上。

passages.original: She stroked and patted my neck, as I had not been patted for many a long day.
passages.vernacular: 佢撫摸、拍住我嘅脖子,像許多日子冇人拍過我嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她撫摸、拍著我的脖子,像許多日子沒有人拍過我那樣。

passages.original: “You see he was quite willing when you gave him the chance; I am sure he is a fine-tempered creature, and I dare say has known better days.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,你畀佢機會時佢係完全願意嘅;我確信佢係個脾氣好好嘅生靈,我敢講佢曾有過更好嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,你給他機會時他是完全願意的;我確信他是個脾氣很好的生靈,我敢說他曾有過更好的日子。

passages.original: You won't put that rein on again, will you?” for he was just going to hitch it up on the old plan.
passages.vernacular: 你唔會再把嗰根韁繩套上喇,係吧?」因為佢正要按老辦法把佢掛上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會再把那根韁繩套上了,是吧?」因為他正要按老辦法把它掛上去。

passages.original: “Well, ma'am, I can't deny that having his head has helped him up the hill, and I'll remember it another time, and thank you, ma'am; but if he went without a check-rein I should be the laughing-stock of all the carters; it is the fashion, you see.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,夫人,我唔能夠否認讓佢自由頭部幫佢上咗坡,我下次會記住嘅,謝謝您,夫人;但如果佢不戴止韁繩,我會成為所有車夫嘅笑柄;呢個係時尚,您知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,夫人,我不能否認讓他自由頭部幫他上了坡,我下次會記住的,謝謝您,夫人;但如果他不戴止韁繩,我會成為所有車夫的笑柄;這是時尚,您知道。」

passages.original: “Is it not better,” she said, “to lead a good fashion than to follow a bad one?
passages.vernacular: 「領頭做一個好嘅時尚,不比跟隨一個壞嘅更好嗎?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「領頭做一個好的時尚,不比跟隨一個壞的更好嗎?」她說。

passages.original: A great many gentlemen do not use check-reins now; our carriage horses have not worn them for fifteen years, and work with much less fatigue than those who have them; besides,” she added in a very serious voice, “we have no right to distress any of God's creatures without a very good reason; we call them dumb animals, and so they are, for they cannot tell us how they feel, but they do not suffer less because they have no words.
passages.vernacular: 「而家許多紳士唔使止韁繩喇;我哋嘅馬車馬十五年嚟冇戴過,比戴嘅嗰啲幹活嘅疲勞少得多;此外,」佢用好嚴肅嘅聲音補充,「我哋冇權利無充足理由使上帝嘅任何生靈受苦;我哋叫佢哋啞巴動物,佢哋確實係,因為佢哋唔能夠告訴我哋佢哋嘅感覺,但佢哋不因冇言語而少受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在許多紳士不用止韁繩了;我們的馬車馬十五年來沒戴過,比戴的那些幹活的疲勞少得多;此外,」她用非常嚴肅的聲音補充,「我們沒有權利無充足理由使上帝的任何生靈受苦;我們叫它們啞巴動物,它們確實是,因為它們不能告訴我們它們的感覺,但它們不因沒有言語而少受苦。

passages.original: But I must not detain you now; I thank you for trying my plan with your good horse, and I am sure you will find it far better than the whip.
passages.vernacular: 但我而家唔能夠耽擱你喇;我感謝你用我嘅辦法試你嘅好馬,我確信你會發現佢比鞭子好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我現在不能耽擱你了;我感謝你用我的辦法試你的好馬,我確信你會發現它比鞭子好得多。

passages.original: Good-day,” and with another soft pat on my neck she stepped lightly across the path, and I saw her no more.
passages.vernacular: 再見,」又喺我脖子上輕輕拍咗一下,佢輕快地走過人行道,我再冇見到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,」又在我脖子上輕輕拍了一下,她輕快地走過人行道,我再沒見到她。

passages.original: “That was a real lady, I'll be bound for it,” said Jakes to himself; “she spoke just as polite as if I was a gentleman, and I'll try her plan, uphill, at any rate;” and I must do him the justice to say that he let my rein out several holes, and going uphill after that, he always gave me my head; but the heavy loads went on.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係位真正嘅女士,我敢打賭,」傑克斯自言自語;「佢講話咁有禮貌,好像我係位紳士,我至少上坡時會試試佢嘅辦法;」我必須公平地講,佢把我嘅韁繩放長咗好幾個孔,此後上坡時,佢總是讓我嘅頭自由;但沉重嘅貨仍喺繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是位真正的女士,我敢打賭,」傑克斯自言自語;「她說話那麼有禮貌,好像我是位紳士,我至少上坡時會試試她的辦法;」我必須公平地說,他把我的韁繩放長了好幾個孔,此後上坡時,他總是讓我的頭自由;但沉重的貨仍在繼續。

passages.original: Good feed and fair rest will keep up one's strength under full work, but no horse can stand against overloading; and I was getting so thoroughly pulled down from this cause that a younger horse was bought in my place.
passages.vernacular: 好嘅飼料同公平嘅休息可以喺滿負荷嘅工作下保持力量,但冇馬能經受過載;由於呢個原因,我被拖垮得如此徹底,買咗一匹更年輕嘅馬嚟替代我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好的飼料和公平的休息可以在滿負荷的工作下保持力量,但沒有馬能經受過載;由於這個原因,我被拖垮得如此徹底,買了一匹更年輕的馬來替代我。

passages.original: I may as well mention here what I suffered at this time from another cause.
passages.vernacular: 我不妨喺呢度提一下我此時由於另一原因遭受嘅苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不妨在這裡提一下我此時由於另一原因遭受的苦。

passages.original: I had heard horses speak of it, but had never myself had experience of the evil; this was a badly-lighted stable; there was only one very small window at the end, and the consequence was that the stalls were almost dark.
passages.vernacular: 我聽馬講過,但自己從冇體驗過呢種害處;呢個係一個光線不好嘅馬廄;只有盡頭一扇好小嘅窗子,結果馬棚幾乎一片黑暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽馬說過,但自己從沒體驗過這種害處;這是一個光線不好的馬廄;只有盡頭一扇很小的窗子,結果馬棚幾乎一片黑暗。

passages.original: Besides the depressing effect this had on my spirits, it very much weakened my sight, and when I was suddenly brought out of the darkness into the glare of daylight it was very painful to my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 除咗呢對我精神嘅壓抑作用,佢都大大削弱咗我嘅視力,當我突然從黑暗中被牽出到日光嘅刺眼中時,對我嘅眼睛好疼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這對我精神的壓抑作用,它也大大削弱了我的視力,當我突然從黑暗中被牽出到日光的刺眼中時,對我的眼睛非常疼。

passages.original: Several times I stumbled over the threshold, and could scarcely see where I was going.
passages.vernacular: 有好幾次我喺門檻上絆倒,幾乎睇唔見要去邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有好幾次我在門檻上絆倒,幾乎看不見要去哪裡。

passages.original: I believe, had I stayed there very long, I should have become purblind, and that would have been a great misfortune, for I have heard men say that a stone-blind horse was safer to drive than one which had imperfect sight, as it generally makes them very timid.
passages.vernacular: 我相信,如果我喺嗰度待得好久,我會變成半盲,嗰將係個好大嘅不幸,因為我聽人講,一匹全盲嘅馬駕駛起嚟比視力不全嘅馬更安全,因為後者通常使馬好膽小。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信,如果我在那裡待得很久,我會變成半盲,那將是個很大的不幸,因為我聽人說,一匹全盲的馬駕駛起來比視力不全的馬更安全,因為後者通常使馬非常膽小。

passages.original: However, I escaped without any permanent injury to my sight, and was sold to a large cab owner.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我視力冇受到永久傷害就逃出嚟喇,被賣畀咗一個大出租車老闆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我視力沒有受到永久傷害就逃出來了,被賣給了一個大出租車老闆。

chapters.title: Part IV · 47 Hard Times 第四部·47 艱難時世

passages.original: CH My new master I shall never forget; he had black eyes and a hooked nose, his mouth was as full of teeth as a bull-dog's, and his voice was as harsh as the grinding of cart wheels over graveled stones.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅新主人我永遠唔會忘記;佢有一雙黑眼睛同一個鷹鉤鼻,嘴裡嘅牙齒多得像鬥牛犬,聲音像貨車輪喺碎石上碾過嘅刺耳聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的新主人我永遠不會忘記;他有一雙黑眼睛和一個鷹鉤鼻,嘴裡的牙齒多得像鬥牛犬,聲音像貨車輪在碎石上碾過的刺耳聲。

passages.original: His name was Nicholas Skinner, and I believe he was the man that poor Seedy Sam drove for.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字叫尼古拉斯·斯金納,我相信佢就係可憐嘅落魄山姆為佢駕車嘅嗰個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的名字叫尼古拉斯·斯金納,我相信他就是可憐的落魄山姆為他駕車的那個人。

passages.original: I have heard men say that seeing is believing; but I should say that feeling is believing; for much as I had seen before, I never knew till now the utter misery of a cab-horse's life.
passages.vernacular: 我聽人講眼見為實;但我該講親身感受才為實;因為雖然我之前見過許多,直到而家我才知道出租車馬生活嘅徹底悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽人說眼見為實;但我該說親身感受才為實;因為雖然我之前見過許多,直到現在我才知道出租車馬生活的徹底悲慘。

passages.original: Skinner had a low set of cabs and a low set of drivers; he was hard on the men, and the men were hard on the horses.
passages.vernacular: 斯金納有一批低等嘅出租車同一批低等嘅車夫;佢對人好苛刻,人對馬好苛刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯金納有一批低等的出租車和一批低等的車夫;他對人很苛刻,人對馬很苛刻。

passages.original: In this place we had no Sunday rest, and it was in the heat of summer.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢個地方我哋冇星期日嘅休息,而且正值酷暑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這個地方我們沒有星期日的休息,而且正值酷暑。

passages.original: Sometimes on a Sunday morning a party of fast men would hire the cab for the day; four of them inside and another with the driver, and I had to take them ten or fifteen miles out into the country, and back again; never would any of them get down to walk up a hill, let it be ever so steep, or the day ever so hot--unless, indeed, when the driver was afraid I should not manage it, and sometimes I was so fevered and worn that I could hardly touch my food.
passages.vernacular: 有時星期日早晨,一夥飛揚跋扈嘅人整天租呢輛車;四個喺裡面,另一個同車夫坐喺一起,我得載佢哋到鄉下十到十五英里,再回嚟;佢哋中冇一個會下車步行上坡,不管多陡、天多熱——除非車夫怕我拉不動,有時我熱得疲憊不堪,幾乎食不下嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時星期日早晨,一夥飛揚跋扈的人整天租這輛車;四個在裡面,另一個和車夫坐在一起,我得載他們到鄉下十到十五英里,再回來;他們中沒有一個會下車步行上坡,不管多陡、天多熱——除非車夫怕我拉不動,有時我熱得疲憊不堪,幾乎吃不下東西。

passages.original: How I used to long for the nice bran mash with niter in it that Jerry used to give us on Saturday nights in hot weather, that used to cool us down and make us so comfortable.
passages.vernacular: 我幾咁想念傑瑞喺炎熱天氣嘅星期六晚上畀我哋嘅加咗硝石嘅好麩皮糊,佢使我哋降溫,讓我哋咁舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多麼想念傑瑞在炎熱天氣的星期六晚上給我們的加了硝石的好麩皮糊,它使我們降溫,讓我們那麼舒服。

passages.original: Then we had two nights and a whole day for unbroken rest, and on Monday morning we were as fresh as young horses again; but here there was no rest, and my driver was just as hard as his master.
passages.vernacular: 然後我哋有兩個晚上同整整一天不間斷嘅休息,星期一早晨我哋又像年輕嘅馬一樣精神;但喺呢度冇休息,我嘅車夫同佢嘅主人一樣苛刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我們有兩個晚上和整整一天不間斷的休息,星期一早晨我們又像年輕的馬一樣精神;但在這裡沒有休息,我的車夫和他的主人一樣苛刻。

passages.original: He had a cruel whip with something so sharp at the end that it sometimes drew blood, and he would even whip me under the belly, and flip the lash out at my head.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一條殘忍嘅鞭子,末端有乜嘢嘢咁尖,有時會抽出血嚟,佢甚至會喺我肚子底下抽我,並把鞭梢甩向我嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一條殘忍的鞭子,末端有什麼東西那麼尖,有時會抽出血來,他甚至會在我肚子底下抽我,並把鞭梢甩向我的頭。

passages.original: Indignities like these took the heart out of me terribly, but still I did my best and never hung back; for, as poor Ginger said, it was no use; men are the strongest.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣嘅屈辱可怕地讓我喪氣,但我仍盡力而為,從不退縮;因為,像可憐嘅金姐講嘅,冇用;人最強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣的屈辱可怕地讓我喪氣,但我仍盡力而為,從不退縮;因為,像可憐的金姐說的,沒有用;人最強。

passages.original: My life was now so utterly wretched that I wished I might, like Ginger, drop down dead at my work and be out of my misery, and one day my wish very nearly came to pass.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅生活而家如此徹底悲慘,我希望像金姐嗰樣喺幹活時倒地而死,結束我嘅苦難,有一天我嘅願望差點實現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的生活現在如此徹底悲慘,我希望像金姐那樣在幹活時倒地而死,結束我的苦難,有一天我的願望差點實現了。

passages.original: I went on the stand at eight in the morning, and had done a good share of work, when we had to take a fare to the railway.
passages.vernacular: 我早晨八點上咗停靠站,已經幹咗好多活,呢陣我哋得載一個客人去火車站。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早晨八點上了停靠站,已經幹了很多活,這時我們得載一個客人去火車站。

passages.original: A long train was just expected in, so my driver pulled up at the back of some of the outside cabs to take the chance of a return fare.
passages.vernacular: 一列長長嘅火車剛要進站,所以我嘅車夫喺啲外面嘅出租車後面停下,等住碰碰運氣找回程客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一列長長的火車剛要進站,所以我的車夫在一些外面的出租車後面停下,等著碰碰運氣找回程客人。

passages.original: It was a very heavy train, and as all the cabs were soon engaged ours was called for.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一列好滿嘅火車,所有嘅出租車好快都被雇走喇,我哋嘅都被叫去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一列非常滿的火車,所有的出租車很快都被雇走了,我們的也被叫去。

passages.original: There was a party of four; a noisy, blustering man with a lady, a little boy and a young girl, and a great deal of luggage.
passages.vernacular: 係一夥四個人;一個吵鬧、盛氣凌人嘅男人,帶住一位女士、一個小男孩同一個年輕女孩,仲有大量行李。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是一夥四個人;一個吵鬧、盛氣凌人的男人,帶著一位女士、一個小男孩和一個年輕女孩,還有大量行李。

passages.original: The lady and the boy got into the cab, and while the man ordered about the luggage the young girl came and looked at me.
passages.vernacular: 女士同男孩上咗車,男人指揮行李時,年輕女孩走過嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女士和男孩上了車,男人指揮行李時,年輕女孩走過來看我。

passages.original: “Papa,” she said, “I am sure this poor horse cannot take us and all our luggage so far, he is so very weak and worn up.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸,」佢講,「我確信呢匹可憐嘅馬載不動我哋同所有行李走咁遠,佢好虛弱疲憊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸,」她說,「我確信這匹可憐的馬載不動我們和所有行李走那麼遠,他非常虛弱疲憊。

passages.original: Do look at him.”
passages.vernacular: 睇睇佢吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看他吧。」

passages.original: “Oh! he's all right, miss,” said my driver, “he's strong enough.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦!佢冇問題,小姐,」我嘅車夫講,「佢夠強壯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!他沒問題,小姐,」我的車夫說,「他夠強壯。」

passages.original: The porter, who was pulling about some heavy boxes, suggested to the gentleman, as there was so much luggage, whether he would not take a second cab.
passages.vernacular: 喺拖動啲重箱子嘅搬運工向紳士建議,既然行李咁多,係咪另叫一輛出租車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在拖動一些重箱子的搬運工向紳士建議,既然行李這麼多,是否另叫一輛出租車。

passages.original: “Can your horse do it, or can't he?” said the blustering man.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅馬行定係不行?」嗰盛氣凌人嘅男人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的馬行還是不行?」那盛氣凌人的男人說。

passages.original: “Oh! he can do it all right, sir; send up the boxes, porter; he could take more than that;” and he helped to haul up a box so heavy that I could feel the springs go down.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!佢完全行,先生;把箱子搬上嚟,搬運工;佢能載比呢更多;」佢幫住拖上一個咁重嘅箱子,我能感到彈簧壓咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!他完全行,先生;把箱子搬上來,搬運工;他能載比這更多;」他幫著拖上一個那麼重的箱子,我能感到彈簧壓了下去。

passages.original: “Papa, papa, do take a second cab,” said the young girl in a beseeching tone.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸,爸爸,請另叫一輛出租車,」年輕女孩用懇求嘅語氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸,爸爸,請另叫一輛出租車,」年輕女孩用懇求的語氣說。

passages.original: “I am sure we are wrong, I am sure it is very cruel.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確信我哋錯喇,我確信呢個好殘忍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確信我們錯了,我確信這很殘忍。」

passages.original: “Nonsense, Grace, get in at once, and don't make all this fuss; a pretty thing it would be if a man of business had to examine every cab-horse before he hired it--the man knows his own business of course; there, get in and hold your tongue!”
passages.vernacular: 「胡講,格蕾絲,即刻上車,別咁大驚小怪;如果一個做生意嘅人雇馬車前得檢查每匹馬,嗰就好玩喇——嗰人當然知道自己嘅行當;好喇,上車,閉嘴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說,格蕾絲,馬上上車,別這麼大驚小怪;如果一個做生意的人雇馬車前得檢查每匹馬,那就好玩了——那人當然知道自己的行當;好了,上車,閉嘴!」

passages.original: My gentle friend had to obey, and box after box was dragged up and lodged on the top of the cab or settled by the side of the driver.
passages.vernacular: 我溫柔嘅朋友唔得不服從,一個又一個箱子被拖上嚟,放喺車頂上或放喺車夫旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我溫柔的朋友不得不服從,一個又一個箱子被拖上來,放在車頂上或放在車夫旁邊。

passages.original: At last all was ready, and with his usual jerk at the rein and slash of the whip he drove out of the station.
passages.vernacular: 終於一切準備好喇,佢照例猛拉一下韁繩、抽一鞭子,駛出咗車站。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於一切準備好了,他照例猛拉一下韁繩、抽一鞭子,駛出了車站。

passages.original: The load was very heavy and I had had neither food nor rest since morning; but I did my best, as I always had done, in spite of cruelty and injustice.
passages.vernacular: 貨好重,我從早晨起冇食嘢都冇休息;但我像往常一樣盡力,不顧殘忍同不公。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貨很重,我從早晨起沒有吃東西也沒有休息;但我像往常一樣盡力,不顧殘忍和不公。

passages.original: I got along fairly till we came to Ludgate Hill; but there the heavy load and my own exhaustion were too much.
passages.vernacular: 我走得相當好,直到到咗盧德門山;但喺嗰度沉重嘅貨同我自己嘅精疲力竭太過分喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走得相當好,直到到了盧德門山;但在那裡沉重的貨和我自己的精疲力竭太過分了。

passages.original: I was struggling to keep on, goaded by constant chucks of the rein and use of the whip, when in a single moment--I cannot tell how--my feet slipped from under me, and I fell heavily to the ground on my side; the suddenness and the force with which I fell seemed to beat all the breath out of my body.
passages.vernacular: 我正掙扎住繼續前進,被不斷嘅猛拉韁繩同鞭子驅趕住,忽然一瞬間——我講不上點——我嘅蹄子從我底下滑咗出去,我重重地側身摔倒喺地;摔倒嘅突然同力量,好像把我身體裡所有嘅氣都打咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正掙扎著繼續前進,被不斷的猛拉韁繩和鞭子驅趕著,忽然一瞬間——我說不上怎麼——我的蹄子從我底下滑了出去,我重重地側身摔倒在地;摔倒的突然和力量,好像把我身體裡所有的氣都打了出去。

passages.original: I lay perfectly still; indeed, I had no power to move, and I thought now I was going to die.
passages.vernacular: 我完全一動不動地躺住;確實,我已冇力氣動,我想而家我要死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我完全一動不動地躺著;確實,我已沒有力氣動,我想現在我要死了。

passages.original: I heard a sort of confusion round me, loud, angry voices, and the getting down of the luggage, but it was all like a dream.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見四周有一種混亂,大聲憤怒嘅講話聲,行李被搬下嚟嘅聲音,但呢一切像夢一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見四周有一種混亂,大聲憤怒的說話聲,行李被搬下來的聲音,但這一切像夢一樣。

passages.original: I thought I heard that sweet, pitiful voice saying, “Oh! that poor horse! it is all our fault.”
passages.vernacular: 我好像聽到嗰甜美、憐憫嘅聲音講:「哦!嗰可憐嘅馬!都係我哋嘅錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我好像聽到那甜美、憐憫的聲音說:「哦!那可憐的馬!都是我們的錯。」

passages.original: Some one came and loosened the throat strap of my bridle, and undid the traces which kept the collar so tight upon me.
passages.vernacular: 有人過嚟鬆開我轡頭嘅喉帶,解開把頸圈勒得咁緊嘅挽繩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人過來鬆開我轡頭的喉帶,解開把頸圈勒得那麼緊的挽繩。

passages.original: Some one said, “He's dead, he'll never get up again.”
passages.vernacular: 有人講:「佢死喇,再都起不嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說:「他死了,再也起不來了。」

passages.original: Then I could hear a policeman giving orders, but I did not even open my eyes; I could only draw a gasping breath now and then.
passages.vernacular: 然後我聽見一個警察下命令,但我連眼睛都冇睜開;我只能偶爾喘一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我聽見一個警察下命令,但我連眼睛都沒睜開;我只能偶爾喘一口氣。

passages.original: Some cold water was thrown over my head, and some cordial was poured into my mouth, and something was covered over me.
passages.vernacular: 有人往我頭上潑咗些冷水,往我嘴裡灌咗些補藥,仲有乜嘢嘢蓋喺我身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人往我頭上潑了些冷水,往我嘴裡灌了些補藥,還有什麼東西蓋在我身上。

passages.original: I cannot tell how long I lay there, but I found my life coming back, and a kind-voiced man was patting me and encouraging me to rise.
passages.vernacular: 我講不上我喺嗰度躺咗多久,但我發現生命喺回嚟,一個聲音和善嘅人喺拍我、鼓勵我站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不上我在那裡躺了多久,但我發現生命在回來,一個聲音和善的人在拍我、鼓勵我站起來。

passages.original: After some more cordial had been given me, and after one or two attempts, I staggered to my feet, and was gently led to some stables which were close by.
passages.vernacular: 又畀我灌咗啲補藥後,經過一兩次嘗試,我踉蹌地站起嚟,被輕輕地牽到附近嘅啲馬廄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又給我灌了一些補藥後,經過一兩次嘗試,我踉蹌地站起來,被輕輕地牽到附近的一些馬廄。

passages.original: Here I was put into a well-littered stall, and some warm gruel was brought to me, which I drank thankfully.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度我被放進一個墊草好多嘅馬棚,有人畀我端嚟溫麥片粥,我感激地飲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡我被放進一個墊草很多的馬棚,有人給我端來溫麥片粥,我感激地喝了。

passages.original: In the evening I was sufficiently recovered to be led back to Skinner's stables, where I think they did the best for me they could.
passages.vernacular: 傍晚我恢復得足夠被牽回斯金納嘅馬廄,我想佢哋喺嗰度盡力為我做咗最好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傍晚我恢復得足夠被牽回斯金納的馬廄,我想他們在那裡盡力為我做了最好的。

passages.original: In the morning Skinner came with a farrier to look at me.
passages.vernacular: 早晨斯金納帶住一個蹄鐵匠嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨斯金納帶著一個蹄鐵匠來看我。

passages.original: He examined me very closely and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢好仔細地檢查咗我,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常仔細地檢查了我,說:

passages.original: “This is a case of overwork more than disease, and if you could give him a run off for six months he would be able to work again; but now there is not an ounce of strength left in him.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係過勞,而唔係疾病,如果你能讓佢放牧六個月,佢就能再幹活;但而家佢身上連啲力氣都冇喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是過勞,而不是疾病,如果你能讓他放牧六個月,他就能再幹活;但現在他身上連一點力氣都沒有了。」

passages.original: “Then he must just go to the dogs,” said Skinner.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢就只有去餵狗喇,」斯金納講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那他就只有去餵狗了,」斯金納說。

passages.original: “I have no meadows to nurse sick horses in--he might get well or he might not; that sort of thing don't suit my business; my plan is to work 'em as long as they'll go, and then sell 'em for what they'll fetch, at the knacker's or elsewhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇草地養病馬——佢可能好都可能不好;嗰種事不適合我嘅生意;我嘅辦法係讓佢哋幹到走不動,然後賣掉,賣多少算多少,賣畀屠宰場或別處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有草地養病馬——他可能好也可能不好;那種事不適合我的生意;我的辦法是讓它們幹到走不動,然後賣掉,賣多少算多少,賣給屠宰場或別處。」

passages.original: “If he was broken-winded,” said the farrier, “you had better have him killed out of hand, but he is not; there is a sale of horses coming off in about ten days; if you rest him and feed him up he may pick up, and you may get more than his skin is worth, at any rate.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢係呼吸壞喇,」蹄鐵匠講,「你最好當場殺咗佢,但佢唔係;大約十天後有一場馬拍賣;你如果讓佢休息、餵飽佢,佢可能恢復,你至少能得到比佢皮更值錢嘅價錢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他是呼吸壞了,」蹄鐵匠說,「你最好當場殺了他,但他不是;大約十天後有一場馬拍賣;你如果讓他休息、餵飽他,他可能恢復,你至少能得到比他皮更值錢的價錢。」

passages.original: Upon this advice Skinner, rather unwillingly, I think, gave orders that I should be well fed and cared for, and the stable man, happily for me, carried out the orders with a much better will than his master had in giving them.
passages.vernacular: 聽咗呢個建議,斯金納,我想相當不情願地,下令好好餵我、照顧我,馬廄嘅人,幸運地對我,比佢主人下令時帶住好得多嘅意願執行咗命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽了這個建議,斯金納,我想相當不情願地,下令好好餵我、照顧我,馬廄的人,幸運地對我,比他主人下令時帶著好得多的意願執行了命令。

passages.original: Ten days of perfect rest, plenty of good oats, hay, bran mashes, with boiled linseed mixed in them, did more to get up my condition than anything else could have done; those linseed mashes were delicious, and I began to think, after all, it might be better to live than go to the dogs.
passages.vernacular: 十天完全嘅休息,大量好燕麥、乾草、加咗煮亞麻籽嘅麩皮糊,比任何別嘅方法都更有助於恢復我嘅狀態;嗰啲亞麻籽糊太好食喇,我開始想,畢竟活住可能比去餵狗好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十天完全的休息,大量好燕麥、乾草、加了煮亞麻籽的麩皮糊,比任何別的方法都更有助於恢復我的狀態;那些亞麻籽糊太好吃了,我開始想,畢竟活著可能比去餵狗好。

passages.original: When the twelfth day after the accident came, I was taken to the sale, a few miles out of London.
passages.vernacular: 事故後嘅第十二天到喇,我被帶去拍賣,喺倫敦外幾英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事故後的第十二天到了,我被帶去拍賣,在倫敦外幾英里。

passages.original: I felt that any change from my present place must be an improvement, so I held up my head, and hoped for the best.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得從我而家嘅地方換到任何地方一定係改善,所以我昂起頭,抱住最好嘅希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得從我現在的地方換到任何地方一定是改善,所以我昂起頭,抱著最好的希望。

chapters.title: Part IV · 48 Farmer Thoroughgood and His Grandson Willie 第四部·48 桑魯古德農夫與他的孫子威利

passages.original: CH At this sale, of course I found myself in company with the old broken-down horses--some lame, some broken-winded, some old, and some that I am sure it would have been merciful to shoot.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢次拍賣上,我當然發現自己同老嘅、垮掉嘅馬喺一起——有些瘸喇,有些呼吸壞喇,有些老喇,有些我確信槍斃佢哋才係仁慈嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這次拍賣上,我當然發現自己和老的、垮掉的馬在一起——有些瘸了,有些呼吸壞了,有些老了,有些我確信槍斃它們才是仁慈的。

passages.original: The buyers and sellers, too, many of them, looked not much better off than the poor beasts they were bargaining about.
passages.vernacular: 買家同賣家都一樣,許多睇起嚟並不比佢哋討價仲價嘅可憐牲口好多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 買家和賣家也一樣,許多看起來並不比他們討價還價的可憐牲口好多少。

passages.original: There were poor old men, trying to get a horse or a pony for a few pounds, that might drag about some little wood or coal cart.
passages.vernacular: 有可憐嘅老人,試圖花幾英鎊買一匹馬或小馬,能拖點小柴車或煤車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有可憐的老人,試圖花幾英鎊買一匹馬或小馬,能拖點小柴車或煤車。

passages.original: There were poor men trying to sell a worn-out beast for two or three pounds, rather than have the greater loss of killing him.
passages.vernacular: 有窮人試圖以兩三英鎊賣掉一匹累垮嘅牲口,而唔願承受殺掉佢嘅更大損失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有窮人試圖以兩三英鎊賣掉一匹累垮的牲口,而不願承受殺掉它的更大損失。

passages.original: Some of them looked as if poverty and hard times had hardened them all over; but there were others that I would have willingly used the last of my strength in serving; poor and shabby, but kind and human, with voices that I could trust.
passages.vernacular: 有些人睇起嚟像貧窮同艱難嘅日子把佢哋整個都磨硬喇;但都有些人,我願意用盡我最後嘅力氣為佢哋服務;窮而破舊,但善良而有人性,聲音我可以信任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人看起來像貧窮和艱難的日子把他們整個都磨硬了;但也有些人,我願意用盡我最後的力氣為他們服務;窮而破舊,但善良而有人性,聲音我可以信任。

passages.original: There was one tottering old man who took a great fancy to me, and I to him, but I was not strong enough--it was an anxious time!
passages.vernacular: 有一個搖搖晃晃嘅老人好鍾意我,我都鍾意佢,但我唔夠強壯——嗰個係焦慮嘅時刻!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個搖搖晃晃的老人非常喜歡我,我也喜歡他,但我不夠強壯——那是焦慮的時刻!

passages.original: Coming from the better part of the fair, I noticed a man who looked like a gentleman farmer, with a young boy by his side; he had a broad back and round shoulders, a kind, ruddy face, and he wore a broad-brimmed hat.
passages.vernacular: 從集市較好嘅一邊走嚟,我注意到一個睇起嚟像鄉紳農場主嘅人,身邊有一個小男孩;佢背寬肩圓,有一張善良紅潤嘅臉,戴住寬邊帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從集市較好的一邊走來,我注意到一個看起來像鄉紳農場主的人,身邊有一個小男孩;他背寬肩圓,有一張善良紅潤的臉,戴著寬邊帽子。

passages.original: When he came up to me and my companions he stood still and gave a pitiful look round upon us.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到我同我嘅同伴哋跟前時,站住喇,憐憫地環顧我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走到我和我的同伴們跟前時,站住了,憐憫地環顧我們。

passages.original: I saw his eye rest on me; I had still a good mane and tail, which did something for my appearance.
passages.vernacular: 我睇見佢嘅目光落喺我身上;我仲有好好嘅鬃毛同尾巴,呢為我嘅外表增色咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見他的目光落在我身上;我還有很好的鬃毛和尾巴,這為我的外表增色了一些。

passages.original: I pricked my ears and looked at him.
passages.vernacular: 我豎起耳朵,睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我豎起耳朵,看著他。

passages.original: “There's a horse, Willie, that has known better days.”
passages.vernacular: 「威利,嗰個係匹有過更好日子嘅馬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「威利,那是匹有過更好日子的馬。」

passages.original: “Poor old fellow!” said the boy, “do you think, grandpapa, he was ever a carriage horse?”
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅老傢伙!」男孩講,「爺爺,你認為佢曾係匹馬車馬嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的老傢伙!」男孩說,「爺爺,你認為他曾是匹馬車馬嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes! my boy,” said the farmer, coming closer, “he might have been anything when he was young; look at his nostrils and his ears, the shape of his neck and shoulder; there's a deal of breeding about that horse.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅!細路,」農夫講,走近咗啲,「佢年輕時可能係任何嘢;睇佢嘅鼻孔同耳朵,脖子同肩膀嘅形狀;嗰匹馬有好好嘅血統。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的!孩子,」農夫說,走近了一些,「他年輕時可能是任何東西;看他的鼻孔和耳朵,脖子和肩膀的形狀;那匹馬有很好的血統。」

passages.original: He put out his hand and gave me a kind pat on the neck.
passages.vernacular: 佢伸出手,親切地喺我脖子上拍咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他伸出手,親切地在我脖子上拍了一下。

passages.original: I put out my nose in answer to his kindness; the boy stroked my face.
passages.vernacular: 我伸出鼻子回應佢嘅善意;男孩撫摸我嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我伸出鼻子回應他的善意;男孩撫摸我的臉。

passages.original: “Poor old fellow! see, grandpapa, how well he understands kindness.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅老傢伙!睇,爺爺,佢幾咁懂得善意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的老傢伙!看,爺爺,他多麼懂得善意。

passages.original: Could not you buy him and make him young again as you did with Ladybird?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠買下佢,像你對待小瓢蟲嗰樣讓佢變年輕嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能買下他,像你對待小瓢蟲那樣讓他變年輕嗎?」

passages.original: “My dear boy, I can't make all old horses young; besides, Ladybird was not so very old, as she was run down and badly used.”
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅細路,我唔能夠把所有老馬都變年輕;再講,小瓢蟲並冇咁老,佢係累垮咗又被虐待。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的孩子,我不能把所有老馬都變年輕;再說,小瓢蟲並沒有那麼老,她是累垮了又被虐待。」

passages.original: “Well, grandpapa, I don't believe that this one is old; look at his mane and tail.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,爺爺,我不相信呢匹老;睇佢嘅鬃毛同尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,爺爺,我不相信這匹老;看他的鬃毛和尾巴。

passages.original: I wish you would look into his mouth, and then you could tell; though he is so very thin, his eyes are not sunk like some old horses'.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你睇睇佢嘅嘴,嗰樣你就能講喇;雖然佢好瘦,佢嘅眼睛不像啲老馬嗰樣凹陷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你看看他的嘴,那樣你就能說了;雖然他很瘦,他的眼睛不像一些老馬那樣凹陷。」

passages.original: The old gentleman laughed.
passages.vernacular: 老先生笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老先生笑了。

passages.original: “Bless the boy! he is as horsey as his old grandfather.”
passages.vernacular: 「保佑呢細路!佢同佢老爺爺一樣懂馬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「保佑這孩子!他和他老爺爺一樣懂馬。」

passages.original: “But do look at his mouth, grandpapa, and ask the price; I am sure he would grow young in our meadows.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過睇睇佢嘅嘴吧,爺爺,問問價錢;我確信佢喺我哋嘅草地上會變年輕嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是看看他的嘴吧,爺爺,問問價錢;我確信他在我們的草地上會變年輕的。」

passages.original: The man who had brought me for sale now put in his word.
passages.vernacular: 帶我嚟賣嘅嗰人呢陣插話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶我來賣的那人這時插話了。

passages.original: “The young gentleman's a real knowing one, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「呢位小少爺真係個內行,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這位小少爺真是個內行,先生。

passages.original: Now the fact is, this 'ere hoss is just pulled down with overwork in the cabs; he's not an old one, and I heerd as how the vetenary should say, that a six months' run off would set him right up, being as how his wind was not broken.
passages.vernacular: 事實係,呢匹馬只係喺出租車上過勞累垮喇;佢不老,我聽嗰獸醫講,六個月嘅放牧能讓佢完全好起嚟,因為佢嘅呼吸冇壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實是,這匹馬只是在出租車上過勞累垮了;他不老,我聽那獸醫說,六個月的放牧能讓他完全好起來,因為他的呼吸沒壞。

passages.original: I've had the tending of him these ten days past, and a gratefuller, pleasanter animal I never met with, and 'twould be worth a gentleman's while to give a five-pound note for him, and let him have a chance.
passages.vernacular: 過去呢十天我一直照顧佢,我從冇遇到過更感恩、更好脾氣嘅牲口,一位紳士花一張五鎊鈔票買佢,畀佢一個機會,係值得嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過去這十天我一直照顧他,我從沒遇到過更感恩、更好脾氣的牲口,一位紳士花一張五鎊鈔票買他,給他一個機會,是值得的。

passages.original: I'll be bound he'd be worth twenty pounds next spring.”
passages.vernacular: 我敢講佢明年春天值二十鎊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說他明年春天值二十鎊。」

passages.original: The old gentleman laughed, and the little boy looked up eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 老先生笑喇,小男孩急切地抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老先生笑了,小男孩急切地抬起頭。

passages.original: “Oh, grandpapa, did you not say the colt sold for five pounds more than you expected?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,爺爺,你唔係講嗰匹小馬駒賣嘅比你預期嘅多五鎊嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,爺爺,你不是說那匹小馬駒賣的比你預期的多五鎊嗎?

passages.original: You would not be poorer if you did buy this one.”
passages.vernacular: 你買呢匹都唔會更窮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你買這匹也不會更窮。」

passages.original: The farmer slowly felt my legs, which were much swelled and strained; then he looked at my mouth.
passages.vernacular: 農夫慢慢地摸咗我嘅腿,佢哋腫得好厲害,勞損喇;然後佢睇咗睇我嘅嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 農夫慢慢地摸了我的腿,它們腫得很厲害,勞損了;然後他看了看我的嘴。

passages.original: “Thirteen or fourteen, I should say; just trot him out, will you?”
passages.vernacular: 「我該講十三或十四歲;小跑畀我睇睇,好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我該說十三或十四歲;小跑給我看看,好嗎?」

passages.original: I arched my poor thin neck, raised my tail a little, and threw out my legs as well as I could, for they were very stiff.
passages.vernacular: 我拱起我可憐瘦削嘅脖子,稍微抬起尾巴,盡我所能甩開腿,因為佢哋好僵硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拱起我可憐瘦削的脖子,稍微抬起尾巴,盡我所能甩開腿,因為它們很僵硬。

passages.original: “What is the lowest you will take for him?” said the farmer as I came back.
passages.vernacular: 「你最低要多少錢?」我回嚟時農夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最低要多少錢?」我回來時農夫說。

passages.original: “Five pounds, sir; that was the lowest price my master set.”
passages.vernacular: 「五鎊,先生;嗰個係我主人定嘅最低價。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五鎊,先生;那是我主人定的最低價。」

passages.original: “'Tis a speculation,” said the old gentleman, shaking his head, but at the same time slowly drawing out his purse, “quite a speculation!
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係一場投機,」老先生搖住頭講,同時慢慢地掏出佢嘅錢包,「真係投機!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是一場投機,」老先生搖著頭說,同時慢慢地掏出他的錢包,「真是投機!

passages.original: Have you any more business here?” he said, counting the sovereigns into his hand.
passages.vernacular: 你喺呢度仲有別嘅事嗎?」佢講,把金幣數喺手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在這裡還有別的事嗎?」他說,把金幣數在手裡。

passages.original: “No, sir, I can take him for you to the inn, if you please.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,先生,您願意嘅話,我可以替您把佢牽到客棧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,先生,您願意的話,我可以替您把他牽到客棧。」

passages.original: “Do so, I am now going there.”
passages.vernacular: 「就咁樣,我而家正要去嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就這樣,我現在正要去那裡。」

passages.original: They walked forward, and I was led behind.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走喺前面,我被牽喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們走在前面,我被牽在後面。

passages.original: The boy could hardly control his delight, and the old gentleman seemed to enjoy his pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 男孩幾乎控制不住佢嘅喜悅,老先生似乎享受佢嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩幾乎控制不住他的喜悅,老先生似乎享受他的快樂。

passages.original: I had a good feed at the inn, and was then gently ridden home by a servant of my new master's, and turned into a large meadow with a shed in one corner of it.
passages.vernacular: 我喺客棧食咗一頓好嘅,然後被我新主人嘅一個僕人輕輕騎住回家,放進一片大草地,草地一角有個棚子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在客棧吃了一頓好的,然後被我新主人的一個僕人輕輕騎著回家,放進一片大草地,草地一角有個棚子。

passages.original: Mr. Thoroughgood, for that was the name of my benefactor, gave orders that I should have hay and oats every night and morning, and the run of the meadow during the day, and, “you, Willie,” said he, “must take the oversight of him; I give him in charge to you.”
passages.vernacular: 桑魯古德先生,嗰個係我嘅恩人嘅名字,下令我每天早晚有乾草同燕麥,白天可以喺草地上活動,「你,威利,」佢講,「必須負責照睇佢;我把佢託付畀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桑魯古德先生,那是我的恩人的名字,下令我每天早晚有乾草和燕麥,白天可以在草地上活動,「你,威利,」他說,「必須負責照看他;我把他託付給你。」

passages.original: The boy was proud of his charge, and undertook it in all seriousness.
passages.vernacular: 男孩為佢負責嘅事自豪,嚴肅地承擔起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩為他負責的事自豪,嚴肅地承擔起來。

passages.original: There was not a day when he did not pay me a visit; sometimes picking me out from among the other horses, and giving me a bit of carrot, or something good, or sometimes standing by me while I ate my oats.
passages.vernacular: 冇一天佢不嚟睇我;有時從其他馬中把我挑出嚟,畀我一小塊胡蘿蔔或別嘅好嘢,有時我食燕麥時佢站喺我旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一天他不來看我;有時從其他馬中把我挑出來,給我一小塊胡蘿蔔或別的好東西,有時我吃燕麥時他站在我旁邊。

passages.original: He always came with kind words and caresses, and of course I grew very fond of him.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是帶住好話同撫摸嚟,當然我變得好鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是帶著好話和撫摸來,當然我變得很喜歡他。

passages.original: He called me Old Crony, as I used to come to him in the field and follow him about.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫我老夥計,因為我常喺田裡走向佢、跟住佢到處走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他叫我老夥計,因為我常在田裡走向他、跟著他到處走。

passages.original: Sometimes he brought his grandfather, who always looked closely at my legs.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢帶佢爺爺嚟,爺爺總是仔細地睇我嘅腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他帶他爺爺來,爺爺總是仔細地看我的腿。

passages.original: “This is our point, Willie,” he would say; “but he is improving so steadily that I think we shall see a change for the better in the spring.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我哋嘅關鍵,威利,」佢會講;「但佢進步得咁穩,我想春天我哋會睇到好轉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我們的關鍵,威利,」他會說;「但他進步得這麼穩,我想春天我們會看到好轉。」

passages.original: The perfect rest, the good food, the soft turf, and gentle exercise, soon began to tell on my condition and my spirits.
passages.vernacular: 完全嘅休息、好食物、柔軟嘅草皮同輕柔嘅運動,好快開始對我嘅狀態同精神起作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 完全的休息、好食物、柔軟的草皮和輕柔的運動,很快開始對我的狀態和精神起作用。

passages.original: I had a good constitution from my mother, and I was never strained when I was young, so that I had a better chance than many horses who have been worked before they came to their full strength.
passages.vernacular: 我從母親嗰度得到咗好體質,年輕時從冇勞損過,所以我比許多喺完全長成之前就被使喚嘅馬有更好嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從母親那裡得到了好體質,年輕時從沒勞損過,所以我比許多在完全長成之前就被使喚的馬有更好的機會。

passages.original: During the winter my legs improved so much that I began to feel quite young again.
passages.vernacular: 冬天裡我嘅腿好咗好多,我開始覺得自己又年輕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天裡我的腿好了很多,我開始覺得自己又年輕了。

passages.original: The spring came round, and one day in March Mr. Thoroughgood determined that he would try me in the phaeton.
passages.vernacular: 春天到喇,三月嘅一天,桑魯古德先生決定試試用我拉四輪敞篷馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 春天到了,三月的一天,桑魯古德先生決定試試用我拉四輪敞篷馬車。

passages.original: I was well pleased, and he and Willie drove me a few miles.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興,佢同威利駕住我走咗幾英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興,他和威利駕著我走了幾英里。

passages.original: My legs were not stiff now, and I did the work with perfect ease.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅腿而家不僵硬喇,我輕鬆自如地完成咗呢活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的腿現在不僵硬了,我輕鬆自如地完成了這活。

passages.original: “He's growing young, Willie; we must give him a little gentle work now, and by mid-summer he will be as good as Ladybird.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺變年輕,威利;我哋而家必須畀佢啲輕鬆嘅活,到仲夏佢就會像小瓢蟲一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他在變年輕,威利;我們現在必須給他一點輕鬆的活,到仲夏他就會像小瓢蟲一樣好。

passages.original: He has a beautiful mouth and good paces; they can't be better.”
passages.vernacular: 佢有一張漂亮嘅嘴同好嘅步伐;唔可能更好喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一張漂亮的嘴和好的步伐;不可能更好了。」

passages.original: “Oh, grandpapa, how glad I am you bought him!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,爺爺,我真高興你買咗佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,爺爺,我真高興你買了他!」

passages.original: “So am I, my boy; but he has to thank you more than me; we must now be looking out for a quiet, genteel place for him, where he will be valued.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,細路;但佢得感謝你比感謝我多;我哋而家必須為佢物色一個安靜、體面嘅地方,喺嗰度佢會被珍視。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,孩子;但他得感謝你比感謝我多;我們現在必須為他物色一個安靜、體面的地方,在那裡他會被珍視。」

chapters.title: Part IV · 49 My Last Home 第四部·49 我最後的家

passages.original: CH One day during this summer the groom cleaned and dressed me with such extraordinary care that I thought some new change must be at hand; he trimmed my fetlocks and legs, passed the tarbrush over my hoofs, and even parted my forelock.
passages.vernacular: 呢個夏天嘅一天,馬夫畀我刷洗、打扮得咁格外用心,我以為一定有乜嘢新變化要嚟喇;佢修剪咗我嘅蹄距毛同腿,喺我嘅蹄子上刷咗焦油,甚至把我嘅額毛分咗縫。
