passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個夏天的一天,馬夫給我刷洗、打扮得那麼格外用心,我以為一定有什麼新變化要來了;他修剪了我的蹄距毛和腿,在我的蹄子上刷了焦油,甚至把我的額毛分了縫。

passages.original: I think the harness had an extra polish.
passages.vernacular: 我想挽具都格外擦亮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想挽具也格外擦亮了。

passages.original: Willie seemed half-anxious, half-merry, as he got into the chaise with his grandfather.
passages.vernacular: 威利同佢爺爺上輕便馬車時,似乎半係焦慮、半係快活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威利和他爺爺上輕便馬車時,似乎半是焦慮、半是快活。

passages.original: “If the ladies take to him,” said the old gentleman, “they'll be suited and he'll be suited.
passages.vernacular: 「如果女士哋鍾意佢,」老先生講,「佢哋就合適,佢都合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果女士們喜歡他,」老先生說,「她們就合適,他也合適。

passages.original: We can but try.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋只能試試。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們只能試試。」

passages.original: At the distance of a mile or two from the village we came to a pretty, low house, with a lawn and shrubbery at the front and a drive up to the door.
passages.vernacular: 離村子一兩英里嘅地方,我哋嚟到一座漂亮嘅低矮房子,前面有草坪同灌木叢,有車道通到門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離村子一兩英里的地方,我們來到一座漂亮的低矮房子,前面有草坪和灌木叢,有車道通到門口。

passages.original: Willie rang the bell, and asked if Miss Blomefield or Miss Ellen was at home.
passages.vernacular: 威利按咗鈴,問布洛姆菲爾德小姐或埃倫小姐係咪喺家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威利按了鈴,問布洛姆菲爾德小姐或埃倫小姐是否在家。

passages.original: Yes, they were.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們在。

passages.original: So, while Willie stayed with me, Mr. Thoroughgood went into the house.
passages.vernacular: 於是,威利同我留喺呢兒,桑魯古德先生進咗屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,威利和我留在這兒,桑魯古德先生進了屋。

passages.original: In about ten minutes he returned, followed by three ladies; one tall, pale lady, wrapped in a white shawl, leaned on a younger lady, with dark eyes and a merry face; the other, a very stately-looking person, was Miss Blomefield.
passages.vernacular: 大約好鐘後佢回嚟喇,後面跟住三位女士;一位高個子嘅蒼白女士,裹住白披肩,靠喺一位年輕些嘅女士身上,佢有黑眼睛同快活嘅臉;另一位,好端莊嘅人,係布洛姆菲爾德小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約十分鐘後他回來了,後面跟著三位女士;一位高個子的蒼白女士,裹著白披肩,靠在一位年輕些的女士身上,她有黑眼睛和快活的臉;另一位,非常端莊的人,是布洛姆菲爾德小姐。

passages.original: They all came and looked at me and asked questions.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都過嚟睇我,問問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們都過來看我,問問題。

passages.original: The younger lady--that was Miss Ellen--took to me very much; she said she was sure she should like me, I had such a good face.
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅女士——嗰個係埃倫小姐——好鍾意我;佢講佢確信佢會鍾意我,我有一張咁好嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的女士——那是埃倫小姐——非常喜歡我;她說她確信她會喜歡我,我有一張這麼好的臉。

passages.original: The tall, pale lady said that she should always be nervous in riding behind a horse that had once been down, as I might come down again, and if I did she should never get over the fright.
passages.vernacular: 高個子嘅蒼白女士講,佢坐喺一匹曾經摔倒過嘅馬後面,總會緊張,因為我可能再摔倒,如果我摔喇,佢永遠從驚嚇中恢復不過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高個子的蒼白女士說,她坐在一匹曾經摔倒過的馬後面,總會緊張,因為我可能再摔倒,如果我摔了,她永遠從驚嚇中恢復不過來。

passages.original: “You see, ladies,” said Mr. Thoroughgood, “many first-rate horses have had their knees broken through the carelessness of their drivers without any fault of their own, and from what I see of this horse I should say that is his case; but of course I do not wish to influence you.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋瞧,女士哋,」桑魯古德先生講,「許多一流嘅馬因為駕車人嘅粗心而摔破咗膝蓋,唔係佢哋自己嘅錯,從我睇呢匹馬嘅情況,我該講佢就係咁樣;不過當然我唔想左右你哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們瞧,女士們,」桑魯古德先生說,「許多一流的馬因為駕車人的粗心而摔破了膝蓋,不是它們自己的錯,從我看這匹馬的情況,我該說他就是這樣;不過當然我不想左右你們。

passages.original: If you incline you can have him on trial, and then your coachman will see what he thinks of him.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋傾向,可以試用佢,然後你哋嘅車夫會睇佢認為點樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們傾向,可以試用他,然後你們的車夫會看他認為怎麼樣。」

passages.original: “You have always been such a good adviser to us about our horses,” said the stately lady, “that your recommendation would go a long way with me, and if my sister Lavinia sees no objection we will accept your offer of a trial, with thanks.”
passages.vernacular: 「你一向係我哋選馬嘅好顧問,」端莊嘅女士講,「你嘅推薦對我好有分量,如果我妹妹拉維妮婭冇反對意見,我哋就接受你試用嘅提議,並表示感謝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一向是我們選馬的好顧問,」端莊的女士說,「你的推薦對我很有分量,如果我妹妹拉維妮婭沒有反對意見,我們就接受你試用的提議,並表示感謝。」

passages.original: It was then arranged that I should be sent for the next day.
passages.vernacular: 然後安排第二天派人嚟接我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後安排第二天派人來接我。

passages.original: In the morning a smart-looking young man came for me.
passages.vernacular: 早晨一個精明嘅年輕人嚟牽我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨一個精明的年輕人來牽我。

passages.original: At first he looked pleased; but when he saw my knees he said in a disappointed voice:
passages.vernacular: 起初佢顯得高興;但佢睇見我嘅膝蓋時,用失望嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初他顯得高興;但他看見我的膝蓋時,用失望的聲音說:

passages.original: “I didn't think, sir, you would have recommended my ladies a blemished horse like that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇想到,先生,您會向我嘅女主人哋推薦咁一匹有瑕疵嘅馬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒想到,先生,您會向我的女主人們推薦這麼一匹有瑕疵的馬。」

passages.original: “'Handsome is that handsome does',” said my master; “you are only taking him on trial, and I am sure you will do fairly by him, young man.
passages.vernacular: 「『行動好才係真好睇』,」我嘅主人講;「你只係試用佢,我確信你會公平地對待佢,年輕人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『行動好才是真好看』,」我的主人說;「你只是試用他,我確信你會公平地對待他,年輕人。

passages.original: If he is not as safe as any horse you ever drove send him back.”
passages.vernacular: 如果佢不像你駕過嘅任何馬一樣安全,就把佢送回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他不像你駕過的任何馬一樣安全,就把他送回來。」

passages.original: I was led to my new home, placed in a comfortable stable, fed, and left to myself.
passages.vernacular: 我被領到新家,安置喺一個舒適嘅馬廄,餵咗料,就留畀自己喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被領到新家,安置在一個舒適的馬廄,餵了料,就留給自己了。

passages.original: The next day, when the groom was cleaning my face, he said:
passages.vernacular: 第二天,馬夫畀我擦臉時講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,馬夫給我擦臉時說:

passages.original: “That is just like the star that 'Black Beauty' had; he is much the same height, too.
passages.vernacular: 「呢正像『黑神駒』嘅嗰顆星;佢哋身高都差不多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這正像『黑神駒』的那顆星;他們身高也差不多。

passages.original: I wonder where he is now.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢而家喺邊度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道他現在在哪裡。」

passages.original: A little further on he came to the place in my neck where I was bled and where a little knot was left in the skin.
passages.vernacular: 再往下走啲,佢嚟到我脖子上被放過血、皮膚上留咗一個小結嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再往下走一點,他來到我脖子上被放過血、皮膚上留了一個小結的地方。

passages.original: He almost started, and began to look me over carefully, talking to himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎一驚,開始仔細地打量我,自言自語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他幾乎一驚,開始仔細地打量我,自言自語。

passages.original: “White star in the forehead, one white foot on the off side, this little knot just in that place;” then looking at the middle of my back--“and, as I am alive, there is that little patch of white hair that John used to call 'Beauty's three-penny bit'.
passages.vernacular: 「額頭上嘅白星,右側一隻白蹄子,呢個小結正好喺嗰個地方;」然後睇我背中間——「天呀,有嗰小塊白毛,約翰過去叫佢『神駒嘅三便士』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「額頭上的白星,右側一隻白蹄子,這個小結正好在那個地方;」然後看我背中間——「天哪,有那小塊白毛,約翰過去叫它『神駒的三便士』。

passages.original: It must be 'Black Beauty'!
passages.vernacular: 一定係『黑神駒』!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一定是『黑神駒』!

passages.original: Why, Beauty!
passages.vernacular: 嗨,神駒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,神駒!

passages.original: Beauty! do you know me?--little Joe Green, that almost killed you?”
passages.vernacular: 神駒!你認識我嗎?——小喬·格林,差點害死你嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 神駒!你認識我嗎?——小喬·格林,差點害死你的?」

passages.original: And he began patting and patting me as if he was quite overjoyed.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始一下又一下地拍我,好像欣喜若狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始一下又一下地拍我,好像欣喜若狂。

passages.original: I could not say that I remembered him, for now he was a fine grown young fellow, with black whiskers and a man's voice, but I was sure he knew me, and that he was Joe Green, and I was very glad.
passages.vernacular: 我講不上我記得佢,因為而家佢係個魁梧嘅年輕人,有黑鬍鬚同男人嘅聲音,但我確信佢認識我,佢係喬·格林,我好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不上我記得他,因為現在他是個魁梧的年輕人,有黑鬍鬚和男人的聲音,但我確信他認識我,他是喬·格林,我非常高興。

passages.original: I put my nose up to him, and tried to say that we were friends.
passages.vernacular: 我把鼻子伸向佢,試住講我哋係朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把鼻子伸向他,試著說我們是朋友。

passages.original: I never saw a man so pleased.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過一個人咁高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過一個人那麼高興。

passages.original: “Give you a fair trial!
passages.vernacular: 「畀你公平嘅試用!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給你公平的試用!

passages.original: I should think so indeed!
passages.vernacular: 我想當然會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想當然會!

passages.original: I wonder who the rascal was that broke your knees, my old Beauty! you must have been badly served out somewhere; well, well, it won't be my fault if you haven't good times of it now.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道弄破你膝蓋嘅係邊個惡棍,我嘅老神駒!你一定喺某處被糟蹋得好慘;好吧,好吧,如果你而家冇好日子過,嗰就唔係我嘅錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道弄破你膝蓋的是哪個惡棍,我的老神駒!你一定在某處被糟蹋得很慘;好吧,好吧,如果你現在沒有好日子過,那就不是我的錯了。

passages.original: I wish John Manly was here to see you.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望約翰·曼利喺呢度睇到你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望約翰·曼利在這裡看到你。」

passages.original: In the afternoon I was put into a low park chair and brought to the door.
passages.vernacular: 下午我被套進一輛低矮嘅公園椅式馬車,牽到門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午我被套進一輛低矮的公園椅式馬車,牽到門口。

passages.original: Miss Ellen was going to try me, and Green went with her.
passages.vernacular: 埃倫小姐要試我,格林同佢一起去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 埃倫小姐要試我,格林同她一起去。

passages.original: I soon found that she was a good driver, and she seemed pleased with my paces.
passages.vernacular: 我好快發現佢係個好駕車人,佢似乎對我嘅步伐好滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很快發現她是個好駕車人,她似乎對我的步伐很滿意。

passages.original: I heard Joe telling her about me, and that he was sure I was Squire Gordon's old “Black Beauty”.
passages.vernacular: 我聽見喬告訴佢我嘅事,佢確信我係戈登鄉紳嘅老「黑神駒」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽見喬告訴她我的事,他確信我是戈登鄉紳的老「黑神駒」。

passages.original: When we returned the other sisters came out to hear how I had behaved myself.
passages.vernacular: 我哋回嚟時,其他姐妹哋出嚟聽我表現得點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們回來時,其他姐妹們出來聽我表現得怎麼樣。

passages.original: She told them what she had just heard, and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢剛聽到嘅告訴咗佢哋,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把她剛聽到的告訴了她們,說:

passages.original: “I shall certainly write to Mrs. Gordon, and tell her that her favorite horse has come to us.
passages.vernacular: 「我一定要畀戈登太太寫信,告訴佢,佢最鍾意嘅馬到我哋呢兒嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一定要給戈登太太寫信,告訴她,她最喜歡的馬到我們這兒來了。

passages.original: How pleased she will be!”
passages.vernacular: 佢會多高興啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會多高興啊!」

passages.original: After this I was driven every day for a week or so, and as I appeared to be quite safe, Miss Lavinia at last ventured out in the small close carriage.
passages.vernacular: 此後大約一個星期,我每天被駕駛,既然我顯得相當安全,拉維妮婭小姐終於冒險坐進咗嗰輛小嘅封閉馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後大約一個星期,我每天被駕駛,既然我顯得相當安全,拉維妮婭小姐終於冒險坐進了那輛小的封閉馬車。

passages.original: After this it was quite decided to keep me and call me by my old name of “Black Beauty”.
passages.vernacular: 此後完全決定留下我,並叫我我嘅老名字「黑神駒」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後完全決定留下我,並叫我我的老名字「黑神駒」。

passages.original: I have now lived in this happy place a whole year.
passages.vernacular: 我而家喺呢個快樂嘅地方已經住咗整整一年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在在這個快樂的地方已經住了整整一年。

passages.original: Joe is the best and kindest of grooms.
passages.vernacular: 喬係最好、最善良嘅馬夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬是最好、最善良的馬夫。

passages.original: My work is easy and pleasant, and I feel my strength and spirits all coming back again.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅工作輕鬆愉快,我感到我嘅力氣同精神都喺恢復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的工作輕鬆愉快,我感到我的力氣和精神都在恢復。

passages.original: Mr. Thoroughgood said to Joe the other day:
passages.vernacular: 桑魯古德先生前幾天對喬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桑魯古德先生前幾天對喬說:

passages.original: “In your place he will last till he is twenty years old--perhaps more.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺你呢度,佢能活到二十歲——或者更久。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在你這裡,他能活到二十歲——也許更久。」

passages.original: Willie always speaks to me when he can, and treats me as his special friend.
passages.vernacular: 威利只要能,總會同我講話,把我當作佢特別嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威利只要能,總會同我說話,把我當作他特別的朋友。

passages.original: My ladies have promised that I shall never be sold, and so I have nothing to fear; and here my story ends.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅女士哋答應過永遠不賣我,所以我冇乜嘢好怕嘅;我嘅故事就喺呢度結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的女士們答應過永遠不賣我,所以我沒有什麼好怕的;我的故事就在這裡結束。

passages.original: My troubles are all over, and I am at home; and often before I am quite awake, I fancy I am still in the orchard at Birtwick, standing with my old friends under the apple-trees.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅苦難都過去喇,我回到咗家;常常喺我仲冇完全醒嚟時,我幻想自己仍喺伯特威克嘅果園裡,同我嘅老朋友哋站喺蘋果樹下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的苦難都過去了,我回到了家;常常在我還沒完全醒來時,我幻想自己仍在伯特威克的果園裡,同我的老朋友們站在蘋果樹下。
